\label{thm:F30}
Let \(H\) be a history space with base readout \(b:H\to B\),
explanation readout \(e:H\to E\), target readout \(t:H\to T\),
continuation \(\kappa:H\to H'\), later explanation
\(e':H'\to E'\), and later target \(t':H'\to T'\).  Assume \(b\)
and \(e\) are surjective.  Define
\[
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}
  :=
  \{(h,h')\in H^2:b(h)=b(h')\ \text{and}\ e(h)\ne e(h')\},
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{tgt}}
  :=
  \{(h,h')\in H^2:e(h)=e(h')\ \text{and}\ t(h)\ne t(h')\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{ExactExplanation}(b,e,t)
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}=\emptyset
  \wedge
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{tgt}}=\emptyset\\
  &\iff
  \exists\,\alpha:B\to E,\ \exists\,\beta:E\to T,\
    \alpha\circ b=e\ \text{and}\ \beta\circ e=t,\\
  \operatorname{StrictCompression}(b,e)
  &\iff
  \exists\,\alpha:B\to E,\ \alpha\circ b=e
  \ \text{and}\ 
  \neg\exists\,\delta:E\to B,\ \delta\circ e=b.
\end{align*}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:F31}
Let \(q:H\to Q\) be a context quotient, let
\(\alpha:A\to\bar A\) be an intervention abstraction, let
\(\operatorname{Adm}:H\times A\to\mathrm{Prop}\) be admissibility, let
\(\Gamma:H\times A\to H'\) be a counterfactual route, let
\(q':H'\to R\) be a target quotient, and let
\(\tau:H'\to\mathrm{Bool}\) be target truth.  Define
\[
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{adm}}
  :=
  \{((h,a),(h',a')) :
    q(h)=q(h'),\ \alpha(a)=\alpha(a'),\
    \operatorname{Adm}(h,a)\not\leftrightarrow
    \operatorname{Adm}(h',a')\},
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{cf}}
  :=
  \left\{
  \begin{array}{l}
    ((h,a),(h',a')) :
    q(h)=q(h'),\ \alpha(a)=\alpha(a'),\\
    \operatorname{Adm}(h,a),\ \operatorname{Adm}(h',a'),\\
    \tau(\Gamma(h,a))\ne\tau(\Gamma(h',a'))
  \end{array}
  \right\}.
\]
Write \(\operatorname{CFL}\) for the counterfactual-legitimacy
predicate for this data.  Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{CFL}(q,\alpha,\operatorname{Adm},\Gamma,q',\tau)
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{adm}}=\emptyset
  \wedge
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{cf}}=\emptyset\\
  &\iff
  \begin{gathered}
    \exists\,\bar\tau:Q\times\bar A\to\mathrm{Bool}
    \ \text{such that}\\
    \bar\tau(q(h),\alpha(a))=\tau(\Gamma(h,a))
    \ \text{for all admissible }(h,a).
  \end{gathered}
\end{align*}

Let \(H\) be a set of histories with an interior--exterior
decomposition \(H \cong I \times E\), and define
\[

surjective, and let \(t:I\times E\to T\) be a declared target readout.

\begin{align*}

    \bar t\circ\pi=t .
\end{align*}
For a family \((t_\sigma)_{\sigma\in\Sigma}\), horizon sufficiency is
the pointwise conjunction of these equivalent conditions for every
\(\sigma\in\Sigma\).

\begin{theorem}[Information Loss Normal Form]\label{thm:F34}
Let \(H_0,H_1\) be source and later carriers with transport
\(\tau:H_0\to H_1\). Let \(\sigma:H_0\to I\) be source information,
\(\rho:H_1\to R\) a recovery quotient, \(q_0:H_0\to Q_0\) a source
quotient, \(q_1:H_1\to Q_1\) a later quotient, and
\(s:H_0\to S\) a declared signature. Assume that
\(\rho\circ\tau\), \(q_0\), and \(q_1\circ\tau\) are surjective onto
their images. Define
\[
  \mathcal O_\rho
  =\{(h,h'):\rho(\tau h)=\rho(\tau h')\ \text{and}\
      \sigma(h)\ne\sigma(h')\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{Recoverable}(\sigma,\tau,\rho)
  &\iff \mathcal O_\rho=\emptyset\\
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar\sigma:R\to I\ \text{ such that }\
    \bar\sigma\circ\rho\circ\tau=\sigma .
\end{align*}
Information loss is legitimate exactly when every declared later
identification made by \(\rho\circ\tau\) is invisible to \(\sigma\).
\end{theorem}
\footnote{\raggedright Verified in Lean as
\texttt{SelfReferenceLimits.\allowbreak{}InformationLoss.\allowbreak{}information\_loss\_normal\_form};
see \Cref{app:formalization}.}
\begin{proof}
Assume the named maps and the surjectivity of \(\rho\circ\tau\). If
\(\sigma=\bar\sigma\circ\rho\circ\tau\), then
\[
  \rho(\tau h)=\rho(\tau h')
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \sigma(h)=\bar\sigma(\rho(\tau h))
           =\bar\sigma(\rho(\tau h'))=\sigma(h'),
\]
so \(\mathcal O_\rho=\emptyset\). Conversely assume
\(\mathcal O_\rho=\emptyset\). For \(r\in R\) in the image of
\(\rho\circ\tau\), choose \(h\) with \(\rho(\tau h)=r\) and define
\[
  \bar\sigma(r):=\sigma(h).
\]
If \(h'\) is another choice, then \((h,h')\notin\mathcal O_\rho\), so
\(\sigma(h)=\sigma(h')\); hence \(\bar\sigma\) is well-defined and
\(\bar\sigma\circ\rho\circ\tau=\sigma\). If
\(\mathcal O_\rho\ne\emptyset\), some pair \(h,h'\) has the same
recovered class but different source information, which is precisely
loss across an access class.
\end{proof}

The famous physical instance is the black-hole information paradox
posed in \citet{Hawking1976BHThermodynamics}; the layer-agnostic
statement above records the descent obstruction abstracted from
that substrate.

\label{thm:F35}
Let \(H\) be a carrier with consecutive scale quotients
\(q_n:H\to Q_n\) and \(q_{n+1}:H\to Q_{n+1}\). Let
\(c:Q_n\to Q_{n+1}\) be a surjective coarsening with
\[
  c\circ q_n=q_{n+1},
\]
and let \(t:H\to T\) be a target law. Put
\[
  \mathcal O_n(t)=
  \{(h,h'):q_n(h)=q_n(h')\ \text{and}\ t(h)\ne t(h')\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  t \text{ descends to } Q_n
  &\iff \mathcal O_n(t)=\emptyset\\
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar t_n:Q_n\to T\ \text{ such that }\
    \bar t_n\circ q_n=t .
\end{align*}
The renormalized law at scale \(Q_{n+1}\) exists exactly when
\(\bar t_n\) is constant on the fibers of \(c\).

\label{thm:F36}
Let \(P\) be a set of limiting processes, let \(\ell:P\to\widehat Q\)
be a surjective limit quotient, let \(j:Q\to\widehat Q\) be a
completion map, let \(u:P\to\widehat T\) be the target-limit readout,
let \(\sigma:P\to\widehat S\) be a declared signature-limit readout,
let \(u^{\mathrm{ren}}:P\to\widehat T^{\mathrm{ren}}\) be a declared
renormalized target-limit readout, and let \(p_0\in P\) be a selected
process.  Define the singular target obstruction
\[
  \mathcal O_{\ell}(u)
  =\{(p_1,p_2)\in P^2:
      \ell(p_1)=\ell(p_2)\ \text{and}\ u(p_1)\ne u(p_2)\}
\]
and the corresponding family obstruction
\(\mathcal O_{\ell}(\sigma)\).  Write
\[
  \rho_{u,\ell}:P\to\widehat Q\times\widehat T,
  \qquad
  \rho_{u,\ell}(p):=(\ell(p),u(p)),
\]
for the joint \((\ell,u)\) refinement, and let
\(\operatorname{Current}_{j}(\ell,p_0)\) abbreviate
\(\exists c\in Q,\ j(c)=\ell(p_0)\).  Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{Completed}(u,\ell)
  &\iff \mathcal O_{\ell}(u)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{Completed}(u,\ell)
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar u:\widehat Q\to\widehat T,\ \bar u\circ\ell=u,\\
  \operatorname{Completed}(\sigma,\ell)
  &\iff \mathcal O_{\ell}(\sigma)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{PathDependent}(u,\ell)
  &\iff \neg\operatorname{Completed}(u,\ell),\\
  \operatorname{Removable}(j,\ell,\sigma,p_0)
  &\iff
  \neg\operatorname{Current}_{j}(\ell,p_0)
  \wedge
  \operatorname{Completed}(\sigma,\ell),\\
  &\operatorname{Refines}(\rho_{u,\ell},\ell),\\
  &\operatorname{Completed}(u,\rho_{u,\ell}),\\
  \operatorname{Completed}(u^{\mathrm{ren}},\ell)
  &\iff
  \operatorname{Completed}(u^{\mathrm{ren}},\ell).
\end{align*}
Equivalently, completion is descent of \(u\) through \(\ell\); the
canonical path-memory repair \(\rho_{u,\ell}\) is a refinement of
\(\ell\) that completes \(u\); a renormalized target inherits the
same completion criterion as its raw target.

\label{thm:F36}
Let \(P\) be a set of limiting processes, let \(\ell:P\to\widehat Q\)
be a surjective limit quotient, let \(j:Q\to\widehat Q\) be a
completion map, let \(u:P\to\widehat T\) be the target-limit readout,
let \(\sigma:P\to\widehat S\) be a declared signature-limit readout,
let \(u^{\mathrm{ren}}:P\to\widehat T^{\mathrm{ren}}\) be a declared
renormalized target-limit readout, and let \(p_0\in P\) be a selected
process.  Define the singular target obstruction
\[
  \mathcal O_{\ell}(u)
  =\{(p_1,p_2)\in P^2:
      \ell(p_1)=\ell(p_2)\ \text{and}\ u(p_1)\ne u(p_2)\}
\]
and the corresponding family obstruction
\(\mathcal O_{\ell}(\sigma)\).  Write
\[
  \rho_{u,\ell}:P\to\widehat Q\times\widehat T,
  \qquad
  \rho_{u,\ell}(p):=(\ell(p),u(p)),
\]
for the joint \((\ell,u)\) refinement, and let
\(\operatorname{Current}_{j}(\ell,p_0)\) abbreviate
\(\exists c\in Q,\ j(c)=\ell(p_0)\).  Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{Completed}(u,\ell)
  &\iff \mathcal O_{\ell}(u)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{Completed}(u,\ell)
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar u:\widehat Q\to\widehat T,\ \bar u\circ\ell=u,\\
  \operatorname{Completed}(\sigma,\ell)
  &\iff \mathcal O_{\ell}(\sigma)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{PathDependent}(u,\ell)
  &\iff \neg\operatorname{Completed}(u,\ell),\\
  \operatorname{Removable}(j,\ell,\sigma,p_0)
  &\iff
  \neg\operatorname{Current}_{j}(\ell,p_0)
  \wedge
  \operatorname{Completed}(\sigma,\ell),\\
  &\operatorname{Refines}(\rho_{u,\ell},\ell),\\
  &\operatorname{Completed}(u,\rho_{u,\ell}),\\
  \operatorname{Completed}(u^{\mathrm{ren}},\ell)
  &\iff
  \operatorname{Completed}(u^{\mathrm{ren}},\ell).
\end{align*}
Equivalently, completion is descent of \(u\) through \(\ell\); the
canonical path-memory repair \(\rho_{u,\ell}\) is a refinement of
\(\ell\) that completes \(u\); a renormalized target inherits the
same completion criterion as its raw target.

\label{thm:F37}
Let \(H\) be a carrier with two access quotients
\(q_A:H\to Q_A\) and \(q_B:H\to Q_B\). A joint access is a quotient
\(j:H\to J\) together with maps \(a:J\to Q_A\) and \(b:J\to Q_B\)
satisfying
\[
  a\circ j=q_A,\qquad b\circ j=q_B .
\]
Assume \(q_A\) and \(q_B\) are separately admissible. Then
\begin{align*}
  q_A \perp_{\mathrm{acc}} q_B
  \iff
  \neg\exists (J: \mathrm{Type})(j:H\to J)(a:J\to Q_A)(b:J\to Q_B),\
  a\circ j=q_A\ \wedge\ b\circ j=q_B .
\end{align*}
Thus complementarity is precisely non-existence of an admissible joint
quotient carrying both accesses.

\label{thm:F38}
Let \(H_s,H_t\) be source and target history sets with continuation
\(\kappa:H_s\to H_t\). Let \(r_s:H_s\to R_s\) and
\(r_t:H_t\to R_t\) be surjective record quotients, and let
\(s_s:R_s\to S\), \(s_t:R_t\to S\) be status readouts into a preorder
\((S,\le_S)\). Then
\begin{align*}
  r_t\circ\kappa \text{ descends through } r_s
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar\kappa:R_s\to R_t\ \text{ such that }\
    \bar\kappa\circ r_s=r_t\circ\kappa,\\
  \operatorname{Arrow}(\kappa)
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar\kappa:R_s\to R_t,\
  \bar\kappa\circ r_s=r_t\circ\kappa
  \ \wedge\
  \forall x\in R_s,\ s_s(x)\le_S s_t(\bar\kappa x).
\end{align*}
The arrow is the monotone direction of the descended record transport.

\label{thm:F39}
Let \(q:H\to Q\) be a surjective access quotient with target readout
\(t:H\to T\).  Let \(q_F:H\to Q_F\) be a finer quotient and
\(q_C:H\to Q_C\) a coarsening, related by a factorization
\(c:Q_F\to Q_C\) with
\[
  c\circ q_F=q_C.
\]
Let \((\mathcal E,\le_E)\) be a preorder of entropy values, and let
\[
  E:\{\,q':H\to Q'\,\}\longrightarrow \mathcal E
\]
be an entropy functional assigning a fiber-volume value to every
declared quotient.  Suppose the apparatus declares a mixing
functional \(m\) and a combiner
\(\odot:\mathcal E\times\mathcal E\to\mathcal E\) satisfying the
chain-rule identity
\[
  E(q_C)=E(q_F)\odot m(q_F,q_C)
\]
and the combine-monotonicity condition
\[
  \forall a,b\in\mathcal E,\quad a\le_E a\odot b.
\]
Define the raw split-pair and target obstructions
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal O_q^{\mathrm{raw}}
  &:=
  \{(h,h')\in H^2:q(h)=q(h')\ \text{and}\ h\ne h'\},\\
  \mathcal O_q(t)
  &:=
  \{(h,h')\in H^2:q(h)=q(h')\ \text{and}\ t(h)\ne t(h')\}.
\end{align*}
Then
\begin{align*}
  E(q)=0
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_q^{\mathrm{raw}}=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{TargetEntropyZero}(q,t)
  &\iff
  t\ \text{descends through}\ q,\\
  \operatorname{TargetUnresolved}(q,t)
  &\iff
  \neg(t\ \text{descends through}\ q),\\
  \forall b\in Q_C,\ \forall h\in H,\quad
  q_C(h)=b
  &\iff
  \exists a\in Q_F,\ c(a)=b\ \wedge\ q_F(h)=a,\\
  E(q_F)
  &\le_E
  E(q_C).
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F42}
Let \(H\) be a set of objects with base map \(b:H\to B\), compression
map \(e:H\to E\), target readout \(t:H\to T\), and route updates
\(r_\gamma:H\to H\) for \(\gamma\in\Gamma\). Let
\(\operatorname{cost}:E\to C\) take values in a strict preorder
\((C,<)\). A compression \(e\) is closed for \(h\in H\) when \(t\) and
all \(e\circ r_\gamma\) descend through the \(e\)-class of \(h\). Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{ClosedCompression}(e,h)
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_t(e,h)=\emptyset
  \ \wedge\
  \forall\gamma\in\Gamma,\ \mathcal O_\gamma(e,h)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{Irreducible}(h)
  &\iff
  \neg\exists e'\!,\
  \operatorname{ClosedCompression}(e',h)
  \ \wedge\
  \operatorname{cost}(e')<\operatorname{cost}(e(h)).
\end{align*}
Irreducibility is therefore absence of a shorter closed description.

\label{thm:F44}
Let \(\mathcal C\) be a control space with quotient
\(c:\mathcal C\to C\), phase readout \(\varphi:\mathcal C\to\Phi\),
formedness predicate \(F:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Prop}\), and
neighborhood relation \(N(x,U,y)\). Let
\(S,M,U,R:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Prop}\) denote, respectively,
status-change, margin-vanishing, non-uniform response, and
residuals-statused. For a readout \(r:\mathcal C\to V\), define
\[
  \mathcal O_c(r)=
  \{(x,y):c(x)=c(y)\ \text{and}\ r(x)\ne r(y)\}.
\]
Then, for \(x,\ell,r_0\in\mathcal C\),
\begin{align*}
  r \text{ descends through }c
  &\iff \mathcal O_c(r)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{PhaseTransition}(\ell,r_0)
  &\iff \varphi(\ell)\ne\varphi(r_0),\\
  \operatorname{PhaseBoundary}(x)
  &\iff F(x)\ \wedge\
    \neg\exists U,\ \forall y,\ N(x,U,y)\Rightarrow \varphi(y)=\varphi(x),\\
  \operatorname{Critical}(x)
  &\iff \operatorname{PhaseBoundary}(x)\wedge (M(x)\vee U(x))\wedge R(x).
\end{align*}

Let \(H\) be a history set with local quotient \(\ell:H\to L\),
target readout \(t:H\to T\), signature \(\sigma:H\to\Sigma\), update

\begin{align*}

  \operatorname{DynamicLocality}(\ell,u,q')

  &\iff \operatorname{TargetFamilyLocal}(\ell,\sigma)\ \wedge\\
  &\qquad
  \neg\exists \ell',\ \ell'\!<\ell\ \wedge\
  \operatorname{TargetFamilyLocal}(\ell',\sigma).
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F47}
Let \(M\) be a moduli space, \(r:M\to V\) a readout, and
\(T:V\to\mathrm{Prop}\) a target-region predicate.  Let
\(\mathcal M\) be the carrier type of measure-record values, let
\(\mu:\mathrm{Pow}(M)\to\mathcal M\) be a measure record on subsets
of \(M\), let \(\mu_{\mathrm{tot}}\in\mathcal M\) be the total
measure, let \(\theta\) be a threshold, and let
\(\odot:\Theta\times\mathcal M\to\mathcal M\) be the declared
threshold scaling.  Let \(\operatorname{Pos}:\mathcal M\to
\mathrm{Prop}\) and \({\le_{\mathcal M}}\subseteq
\mathcal M\times\mathcal M\) be the declared positivity and order
predicates on the measure record.  Let \(\mathrm{sel}\in M\) be a
selected modulus, let \(\mathsf{selDec}\) be a selector-declared
predicate, and let
\(\mathsf{modDec},\mathsf{tgtDec},\mathsf{meaDec},\mathsf{thrDec},
\mathsf{presStat}\) be the five required apparatus-declaration
predicates.  Define the selector region
\[
  \Sigma(r,T):=\{m\in M:T(r(m))\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  m\in\Sigma(r,T)
  &\iff
  T(r(m)),\\
  \operatorname{Small}(\Sigma(r,T))
  &\iff
  \operatorname{Pos}(\mu(\Sigma(r,T)))
  \wedge
  \mu(\Sigma(r,T))\le_{\mathcal M}\theta\odot\mu_{\mathrm{tot}},\\
  \operatorname{Realized}(\Sigma(r,T),\mathrm{sel},\mathsf{selDec})
  &\iff
  \mathsf{selDec}
  \wedge
  \mathrm{sel}\in\Sigma(r,T)
  \wedge
  \operatorname{Small}(\Sigma(r,T)),\\
  \operatorname{TargetImpossible}(\Sigma(r,T))
  &\Longrightarrow
  \neg\operatorname{Realized}(\Sigma(r,T),\mathrm{sel},\mathsf{selDec}),\\
  \operatorname{WellTyped}
  &\iff
  \mathsf{modDec}\wedge\mathsf{tgtDec}\wedge\mathsf{meaDec}
  \wedge\mathsf{thrDec}\wedge\mathsf{presStat}.
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F48}
Let \(G\) be a set of global states with gluing quotient
\(\gamma:G\to\Gamma\), readout \(r:G\to V\), transport
\(\tau:G\to G'\), and target gluing quotient \(\gamma':G'\to\Gamma'\).
Assume \(\gamma\) is surjective, and define
\[
  \mathcal O_\gamma(r)=
  \{(g,g'):\gamma(g)=\gamma(g')\ \text{and}\ r(g)\ne r(g')\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{TopologicalReadout}(r)
  &\iff \mathcal O_\gamma(r)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{CompleteInvariant}(r)
  &\iff \operatorname{TopologicalReadout}(r)\wedge
    \forall g,g',\ r(g)=r(g')\Rightarrow \gamma(g)=\gamma(g'),\\
  \operatorname{CoarseInvariant}(r)
  &\iff \operatorname{TopologicalReadout}(r)\wedge
    \exists g,g',\gamma(g)\ne\gamma(g')\wedge r(g)=r(g'),\\
  \operatorname{TransportDescends}(\tau)
  &\iff
    \exists\,\bar\tau:\Gamma\to\Gamma'\ \text{ with }\
    \bar\tau\circ\gamma=\gamma'\circ\tau .
\end{align*}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The famous physical instance of correlations that admit no local
common-source explanation is the Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen / Bell
situation \citep{Bell1964EPR}; the layer-agnostic statement below
records the descent-to-common-source obstruction abstracted from
that substrate.

\begin{theorem}[Common-Source / Nonlocal Correlation Normal Form]\label{thm:F49}
Let \(H\) be a history space with source quotient \(\sigma:H\to S\),
shared interface \(\iota:H\to I\), access quotients
\(q_A:H\to L_A\), \(q_B:H\to L_B\), and readouts
\(r_A:H\to A\), \(r_B:H\to B\). Let
\(\kappa:H\to K\) be the correlation readout. Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{CommonSource}(\sigma)
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar r_A:S\to A,\bar r_B:S\to B,\
    \bar r_A\circ\sigma=r_A\ \wedge\ \bar r_B\circ\sigma=r_B,\\
  \operatorname{InterfaceFactorization}(\iota)
  &\iff
  \exists\,\hat r_A:I\to A,\hat r_B:I\to B,\
    \hat r_A\circ\iota=r_A\ \wedge\ \hat r_B\circ\iota=r_B,\\
  \operatorname{LocallyExplainable}(\kappa)
  &\iff \operatorname{CommonSource}(\sigma)
    \vee \operatorname{InterfaceFactorization}(\iota).
\end{align*}
If neither disjunct holds, the correlation is a statused nonlocal
residual.
\end{theorem}
\footnote{\raggedright Verified in Lean as
\texttt{SelfReferenceLimits.\allowbreak{}CommonSourceNonlocal.\allowbreak{}common\_source\_nonlocal\_correlation};
see \Cref{app:formalization}.}
\begin{proof}
Assume the source quotient \(\sigma\), interface \(\iota\), accesses
\(q_A,q_B\), and readouts \(r_A,r_B,\kappa\). If
\(\bar r_A\circ\sigma=r_A\) and \(\bar r_B\circ\sigma=r_B\), then both
local readouts depend only on the shared source class:
\[
  \sigma(h)=\sigma(h')\Rightarrow
  r_A(h)=r_A(h')\ \wedge\ r_B(h)=r_B(h').
\]
This is a common-source explanation. The interface case is identical
with \(\iota\) replacing \(\sigma\). Conversely, any explanation by a
common source or interface gives exactly such descended readouts. Thus
there are two local-explanation cases,
\[
  \operatorname{CommonSource}(\sigma)
  \quad\text{or}\quad
  \operatorname{InterfaceFactorization}(\iota),
\]
and failure of both leaves the correlation as a nonlocal residual.
\end{proof}

\label{thm:F50}
Let \(\mathcal X\) be a closure space with moduli quotient
\(\mu:\mathcal X\to M\), raw background \(b_0:\mathcal X\to B\),
descended background \(b:M\to B\), target \(t:M\to T\), and vacuum
criterion \(V\subseteq M\). Assume \(\mu\) is surjective. Then
\begin{align*}
  b_0 \text{ descends through }\mu
  &\iff
  \exists\,b:M\to B\ \text{ with } b\circ\mu=b_0,\\
  \operatorname{NecessaryBackground}(b)
  &\iff \forall m,m'\in M,\ b(m)=b(m'),\\
  \operatorname{BackgroundModuli}(b)
  &\iff \exists m,m'\in M,\ b(m)\ne b(m'),\\
  \operatorname{Vacuum}(m_\ast)
  &\iff V=\{m_\ast\}\ \wedge\ t(m_\ast)\ \text{is formed}.
\end{align*}
The necessary/moduli alternatives are exhaustive and disjoint.

\label{thm:F51}
Let \(\mathcal C_U,\mathcal C_A,\mathcal C_B\) be parent and child
closures with quotients \(q_U:\mathcal C_U\to Q_U\),
\(q_A:\mathcal C_A\to Q_A\), and \(q_B:\mathcal C_B\to Q_B\). Let
\(\iota_A:\mathcal C_U\to\mathcal C_A\) and
\(\iota_B:\mathcal C_U\to\mathcal C_B\) be interpretations, and let
\(\pi_A:Q_U\to Q_A\), \(\pi_B:Q_U\to Q_B\) be quotient projections.
For claim sets \(K_A,K_B,K_U\), lifts
\(\lambda_A:K_A\to K_U\), \(\lambda_B:K_B\to K_U\), and status maps
\(s_A,s_B,s_U\), unification is equivalent to
\begin{align*}
  \pi_A\circ q_U=q_A\circ\iota_A
  &\quad\wedge\quad
  \pi_B\circ q_U=q_B\circ\iota_B,\\
  \pi_A\circ R_U^A=R_A\circ\pi_A
  &\quad\wedge\quad
  \pi_B\circ R_U^B=R_B\circ\pi_B,\\
  s_U(\lambda_A k)=\alpha_A(s_A k)
  &\quad\wedge\quad
  s_U(\lambda_B \ell)=\alpha_B(s_B \ell)
  \quad\text{for all }k\in K_A,\ell\in K_B .
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F52}
Let \(R\) be a residual type with predicates
\(\operatorname{hasStatus}:R\to\mathrm{Prop}\) and
\(\operatorname{adequate}:R\to\mathrm{Prop}\). Let \(D\) be a direction
type with predicates \(\operatorname{inScope}:D\to\mathrm{Prop}\),
\(\operatorname{claimed}:D\to\mathrm{Prop}\), and
\(\operatorname{namedOutside}:D\to\mathrm{Prop}\), and let
\[
  v\in\{\operatorname{accepted},\operatorname{open},\operatorname{refused}\}
\]
be a meta-audit verdict. Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{ResidualCoverage}
  &\iff
  \forall r\in R,\ \operatorname{hasStatus}(r)\wedge\operatorname{adequate}(r),\\
  \operatorname{MetaCovered}(v)
  &\iff v=\operatorname{accepted},\\
  \operatorname{ScopedClosureComplete}
  &\iff
  \operatorname{formed}\wedge\operatorname{scopeDeclared}\wedge
  \operatorname{ResidualCoverage}\\
  &\qquad\wedge\
  \forall d\in D,\ \operatorname{claimed}(d)\Rightarrow
    \bigl(\operatorname{inScope}(d)\vee\operatorname{namedOutside}(d)\bigr),\\
  \operatorname{MetaComplete}
  &\iff \operatorname{ScopedClosureComplete}\wedge\operatorname{MetaCovered}(v).
\end{align*}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:CER-direct-no-go}
Let \(\mathfrak S\) be a declared scope, let \(\mathcal C\) be a
class of carriers, let
\(\operatorname{BareReal}_{\mathfrak S}:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Prop}\)
be bare physical realisability, and let
\(\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak S}:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C\) be the formal
closure operator over \(\mathfrak S\).  Under the reduct-obstruction
hypothesis there exists a carrier \(C\in\mathcal C\) such that
\[
  \operatorname{BareReal}_{\mathfrak S}(C)
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  C\ne \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak S}(C).
\]
Equivalently, the direct CER implication
\[
  \operatorname{BareReal}_{\mathfrak S}(C)
  \Longrightarrow
  C=\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak S}(C)
\]
fails in general.

conclusion: The structural laws of the Six Birds corpus through Foundations IV are stated from the standpoint of an external theorist: the theorist declares a lens, detects an obstruction, installs a repair, prices a residual, and runs the audit. This paper makes the closure apparatus part of the carrier. An endogenous closure system carries its own instruments, ledgers, repair generator, boundary records, and re-audit loop, and its claims of self-repair are admitted only when the relevant records are produced by its own transitions under a closed-loop source policy. Six definitions (D1–D6) and sixteen laws (E1–E16) give the resulting catalog: endogenous repair, bounded reflexivity, self-maintenance, repair compilation and collapse; priced exposure, alarm, control prices, and probe acquisition; stack rewrite, individuation, and repair transport; and reconsolidation, offline reclosure, and adaptability. The laws are carrier-side and substrate-independent. Living, cognitive, and social systems therefore enter on equal terms: physiological regulation and organismal maintenance, agent-side learning and control, and institutional reproduction and rewrite are distinct realizations of the same typed hypotheses, not metaphors for one another. Each law is stated in the six-part normal form inherited from Foundations IV, with an obstruction or falsifier, an exactly-one status partition where applicable, a proof spine, interaction discipline, and explicit nonclaims. D1–D6 and the core E1–E16 laws are represented in the companion Lean 4 development and finite Repair-World/law-specific campaign; two named interpretive corollaries, Alarm Fatigue and Operational Selfhood, remain unformalized and are marked accordingly. The finite campaign contains 348 preregistered comparisons across fifteen law-specific result artifacts, all passing. Existing particle and neural substrate experiments supply life-facing null, drive, maintenance, motif, and intervention evidence under explicit nonclaims, while an unrun planarian-regeneration protocol states a concrete biological promotion target and its falsifiers. No definition of biological life, consciousness, death, welfare, or autonomous evolution is claimed.

\paragraph{D1 cases.}
If one input quotient already refines the other, their repair join is
fiber-equivalent to the finer input.  The join of a constant quotient with
\(r\) is \(r\); the join with a discrete quotient is discrete; and on an
empty carrier the universal property holds vacuously.  Presentations with
different or even non-isomorphic codomains are compared only by their fiber
relations.  These cases also fix the order convention: under the
finer-to-coarser order, the operation named \(\vee\) in this corpus is
meet-shaped.  Most importantly, D1 constructs the unrestricted common
refinement; it does \emph{not} prove that this joint access is in an admissible
access class.  The Foundations IV F37 obstruction remains a separate gate.

Full output equality is required. A carried record with the right type but the wrong value cannot witness maintenance. [Proof of Theorem ] -level fixed point. E3_TwoLevelFixedPoint combines an object fixed-point certificate, object-record coherence, a carried maintenance-operator occurrence, exact reinstatement, a supplied maintained-closure status occurrence with exact operator and reinstatement links, empty maintenance obstruction, no subsidy, and conditional regress-stop evidence. Its ApparatusMaintainedStep field in challenge-free operation requires apparatus distance at most . Under an apparatus challenge it instead requires a linked E1-style repair occurrence with defect, generated move, join/install evidence, kernel transition, and re-audit. Thus approximate stability and challenged repair are two branches of one maintained-step predicate, not interchangeable observations. The theorem packages the two-level fixed point and MaintainedClosureHolds; it does not synthesize the maintained status from object stability, reinstatement, empty obstruction, and completeness alone.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:e4}
A lawful compilation candidate
\(R\leadsto K_{\ell}^{\rm compiled}\) requires a certified top-down channel,
a passing memory-only comparator, saturation strictness, and a carried
annotation or decompilation record.  The \texttt{compiled} case additionally
carries independent descent and post-compilation silence certificates.
Within the trained class those certificates remove the per-episode repair
demand:
\[
 \Delta(Q_{\ell}^{\rm compiled},F_{\mathcal C},r)=\varnothing.
\]
Outside that class, a compiled gate can create split-pair obstructions that
defeat descent on a supplied witness.  The formal theorem makes no
counterfactual claim that the formerly exposed repair would have statused or
avoided them.  Compilation may therefore trade recurrent audit cost for
scope-dependent brittleness when the declared out-of-class witness is
present.

candidate, lawfulness, verified in-class descent, silence of the formerly
exposed higher invocation, and the priority exclusions.  The theorem
\texttt{E4\_Compilation} is a packaging wrapper: it takes a carried status
occurrence tagged \texttt{compiled} and an already supplied full

refinement.  The result is intentionally verification-shaped: the
top-down channel and descent certificates are host inputs checked by their
interfaces; Lean proves that the complete certificate entails the status and

It is irreversibly collapsed when, in addition, the repair generator is unreachable, the apparatus-level viability kernel is empty, and the reachability/kernel grades are certified coherent. conclusion: Failure to prove irreversibility alone does not prove recoverability.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:e5}]
Completeness turns the universal phrase ``no admissible carried move'' into a
finite inventory statement.  If an in-budget linked candidate descends, the
definition supplies a collapse falsifier, and the falsifier theorem shows
collapsed core is false.  If none exists,
collapsed core holds.  Coherent unreachability of both repair generator and
apparatus viability kernel in a supplied
\texttt{IrreversibleCollapseInput} selects irreversible collapse.  The
recoverable branch requires its own \texttt{RecoverableCollapseInput}:
coherent evidence of self-reachability, external-only reachability, or a
nonempty kernel, together with explicit negation of the irreversible input.
Failure to prove irreversibility alone does not prove recoverability.  A fully linked external descent is
classified by the subsidy witness before either collapsed branch only when
the witness's no-internal-rescue condition and priority exclusions hold;
external descent alone is insufficient.  Intact apparatus plus
gated-off operations selects suspension.  A later internal rescue with a new
lineage selects revival.  The evidence-priority definitions make these
branches pairwise disjoint, and occurrence completeness supplies existence
and same-claim status-kind uniqueness.
\end{proof}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The source catalog records a further consequence that is not part of the E7
Lean module.  Suppose viability-coupled positive excess persists across a
declared horizon, the preemption channel has finite carried capacity, and
the total discharge available to that channel is insufficient for the
credited alarm demand.  Then continued treatment of every occurrence as a
fresh currentization cannot remain a free operation.  The source program
allows three audited outcomes: the preemption channel saturates; the system
performs a carried threshold or constraint-set repair; or excess remains as
a statused pathology.  Threshold raising is lawful only when it is charged
to the carried ledger and the original threshold lineage remains available
to audit.  Otherwise the move is indistinguishable from E8.1 budget
inflation, where the report improves while the original-lineage blind spot
does not.

This corollary connects two already named limits without identifying them.
E2 bounds the depth and footprint of carried audit, while E7.1 concerns the
capacity of the preemption channel that acts on viability-coupled excess.
A general theorem translating the E2 carrier-capacity bound into the E7.1
discharge bound remains open.  The corollary is therefore
\emph{interpretation-grade}: its inputs and three outcomes are the
source-program statement, but no theorem in
\path|Laws.E7Alarm| proves their exhaustive partition.

to audit.  Otherwise the move is indistinguishable from E8.1 budget
inflation, where the report improves while the original-lineage blind spot
does not.

discharge bound remains open.  The corollary is therefore
\emph{interpretation-grade}: its inputs and three outcomes are the
source-program statement, but no theorem in
\path|Laws.E7Alarm| proves their exhaustive partition.

\paragraph{Layer-specific bridge obligations.}
\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=2.4em]
\item[Living systems.]
A transcriptional, immune, bioelectric, or metabolic package qualifies only
when perturbing that carried package changes the organism's own future
support and strictly discharges the named viability obstruction.  A
biomarker readable by an experimenter supplies only the correlate branch.
This application is structural and empirical-candidate grade; it makes no
consciousness claim.
\item[Cognitive systems.]
A plan, working-memory state, or learned controller must restrict or orient
action before the outcome under matched controls.  Goals additionally
survive route substitution.  These are direct operational instantiations,
conditional on the comparator and inventory certificates.
\item[Social and economic systems.]
A decision rule, policy package, or governance procedure qualifies only
when its carried invocation changes admissible organizational action and
repairs the declared class.  Minutes or labels that merely predict later
behavior remain correlates; externally installed compliance machinery is
scaffolding unless and until its source status changes.
\end{description}

Fix a complete matched comparison.  If a linked structural effect exists,
the accepted channel supplies difference-making for that exact pair, and
the concrete comparator supplies either a support witness $(z,z')$ or
closure inequality.  Empty $\Delta_{\rm stack}$ excludes reproduction of
the outcome on unrevised support.  If a carried E11-local

the constitutive case holds.  This is an E4-shaped interface, not an import of
the actual E4 theorem or record type; the general E4-to-E11 bridge remains
open.  If no such evidence exists, the comparison-wide negation in
\texttt{StackActiveEvidence} gives the stack-active case.

A selfhood claim fails if the proposed L_S is not carried, if one declared domain does not factor through it, if a cross-domain repair borrows an external or wrong-lineage record, or if fragmentation is claimed without a literal split pair between two of the declared future readouts. Conversely, a common database identifier is insufficient unless the same carried ledger actually supports the role, memory, action, and viability probes. A perfectly integrated ledger can also fail E12 individuation when its budget, boundary, or repair apparatus is maintained by another carrier. This is an interpretation-grade corollary and is not part of |Laws.E12Individuation|. The current development has no theorem constructing L_S , no exhaustive inventory of cognitive domains, and no consciousness consequence. E12.1 is not used by a later proof
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{rem:e12-selfhood}
At the cognitive scale, take role, memory, action, and viability as the
declared domains whose future probes must be jointly supported.  The source
program calls a \emph{self} the private common repair ledger \(L_S\) through
which those cross-domain probes jointly descend.  ``Private'' here means
carried by the selected system and available to its own repair interfaces;
it does not mean phenomenally private or inaccessible in principle.  The
object of the claim is the ledger and its factorization property, not an
inner observer.

The specialization turns the Foundations IV F17 common-quotient idea
inward.  F17 compares observations across public viewpoints; E12.1 compares
the system's own role, record, action, and viability interfaces.  When one
versioned ledger supplies the distinctions used by all four interfaces, the
same repair occurrence can be traced across them.  When the ledger is lost
or fragmented, histories may remain equal under an action quotient while
their memory or role futures differ, or equal under a role quotient while
their viability futures differ.  Those are ordinary cross-domain split
pairs, not a metaphysical failure of identity.

The corresponding falsifier is therefore operational.  A selfhood claim
fails if the proposed \(L_S\) is not carried, if one declared domain does not
factor through it, if a cross-domain repair borrows an external or
wrong-lineage record, or if fragmentation is claimed without a literal
split pair between two of the declared future readouts.  Conversely, a
common database identifier is insufficient unless the same carried ledger
actually supports the role, memory, action, and viability probes.  A
perfectly integrated ledger can also fail E12 individuation when its budget,
boundary, or repair apparatus is maintained by another carrier.

This is an interpretation-grade corollary and is not part of
\path|Laws.E12Individuation|.  The current development has no theorem
constructing \(L_S\), no exhaustive inventory of cognitive domains, and no
consciousness consequence.  E12.1 is not used by a later proof.

\end{aligned}

&\mathsf{BoundaryApparatus}(I,B_I,A_t)\\
&{}\land\mathsf{MaintenanceReinstatementFor}
  (t,A_t,A_{t+1},m,R)\\
&{}\land I(R.\mathsf{sourceState}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Merely locating a membrane, API, or legal perimeter does not prove this
clause.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The bridge is not an analyst's pairing of two time series.  It carries a
joint bridge record, a linked defect, source and target ledger entries, and
a shared discharge-comparator certificate, with the appropriate occurrence
carried by each system.  Challenge alignment is taxonomy-relative:
\[
\mathsf{SameTransportChallengeClass}(C_A,C_B)
\iff
\begin{cases}
C_A,C_B\text{ occur in one carried declared taxonomy},\\
\mathsf{taxonomyId}(C_A)=\mathsf{taxonomyId}(C_B),\\
\mathsf{classId}(C_A)=\mathsf{classId}(C_B).
\end{cases}
\]
Matching two informal names is insufficient.

For the receiver repair, let $q_B^-$ and $q_B^+$ be the before and installed
after quotients.  The linked reduction predicate is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf{TransportDeltaReduction}\iff{}&
\Delta(q_B^+,F_C,r_B)
\subseteq\Delta(q_B^-,F_C,r_B)\\
&{}\land
\exists x,x',\
\Delta(q_B^-,F_C,r_B;x,x')
\land\neg\Delta(q_B^+,F_C,r_B;x,x')\\
&{}\land
q_B^+\text{ is installed by the carried target move}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, receiver improvement on another class or after an unrelated
move cannot be borrowed by the transport claim.

repair-capacity distributions that survives all declared controls and is not
already an outstanding E15 residue.  Such a record has two consequences:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item the endpoints satisfy the exact
  \(\mathsf{CurrentEventEquiv}\) relation; and
  \item the exact claim-linked records report unequal future repair
  probabilities despite matched current endpoints.
\end{enumerate}
A currentizable residue is legible slack, not adaptability; a residue erased
by lawful continuation is dissipative memory; an equal claim-linked pair is
flat.

conclusion: It is the finite-inventory limitation that prevents the paper from claiming robustness against every latent variable.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
One negative governance result is especially important.  An undeclared
proxy cannot be detected by a classifier whose complete universe does not
contain it; the mechanical fixture can retain coherent status until the
proxy is declared and the support controls are rerun.  This is not evidence
that the proxy is harmless.  It is the finite-inventory limitation that
prevents the paper from claiming robustness against every latent variable.
The nine discipline checks record actual-scope, no-hardcoding,
off-inventory-dissipation, predictive-reveal, administrative-rejection,
wrong-claim-E15, same-ID content mutation, same-ID perturbation mutation, and
pair-local flatness isolation.

The catalog is intentionally incomplete.  The following candidates have
recognizable shapes but do not yet possess a distinct theorem, obstruction
set, and recognition interface.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Global or conscious access.} Simultaneous descent into
  memory, action, and report may combine E6, E7, E12, and E13 without adding
  a new law.  Phenomenality is outside the present apparatus.
  \item \textbf{Play or sandboxed obstruction sampling.} This currently
  appears to be E9 under a gated risk budget unless transfer from sandbox to
  live repair supplies a new obstruction.
  \item \textbf{Boundary discovery dynamics.} E12 classifies a candidate
  boundary; it does not state how a carrier searches the boundary lattice.
  \item \textbf{Transported gates and norms.} E13 transports repair.  A
  separate P2-transport theorem may be needed for norms, standards, and
  regulatory gates.
  \item \textbf{Distributed exposure and price discovery.} A multi-carrier
  E6/E9 system may model markets or collective sensing, but standard
  aggregation results must not be merely renamed.
  \item \textbf{Reproduction, heredity, and evolutionary closure.} The
  E-series treats repair and adaptation of a declared carrier.  Replication,
  heritable variation, population selection, ecological inheritance, and
  open-ended lineage innovation require additional carrier and source
  machinery.  The life-focused substrate paper likewise separates bounded
  competencies from autonomous open-ended evolution
  \citep{Tsiokos2026Life}.
  \item \textbf{Abiogenesis and origin-of-life transitions.} No theorem here
  selects the first E-system from nonliving chemistry or proves that the
  D1--D6 package is necessary and sufficient for life.
\end{itemize}

footprints.  The appendix does not claim that a proof of an implication
constructs an honest biological instrument or a complete empirical catalog.

conclusion: The Six Birds corpus through certifies states: each of its laws fixes a single map, quotient, package, or declared finite family and proves a static classification about it. Nothing in the corpus certifies runs — liveness (every orbit eventually earns a certificate), amortized or transfinite cost over unbounded time, covers that must move with their targets, obstructions that grow, react, or are manufactured by the system's own history, route defects that integrate into potentials, transport that emerges from substrate dynamics, or content that persists through repeated loss. This paper is the catalog of exactly those laws: dynamical structural laws (G1–G13), organized in clusters, each stated in the six-part normal form inherited verbatim from and each carrying a temporal quantifier that no static row possesses. The laws were mined from eccentric mathematical problems — Collatz, Goodstein, Egyptian fractions, reverse-and-add, Recam\'an, the angel problem, sandpiles, rule 184, Ducci, aperiodic tilings, Hadwiger–Nelson, Apollonian packings — treated as theorem detectors: each problem's folklore almost-proof names a promoted object, the object's lawful descended certificate fixes a boundary expression, and the residual surviving comparison against every existing law is the law seed. All thirteen laws are mechanized in Mathlib-free Lean 4 with per-declaration kernel-axiom audits; six laws are full theorem-grade rows and one splits into an unconditional theorem and a schema, four are schema-grade with named boxed hypotheses, and three are calibration-anchored schemas discharged end-to-end by solved classical instances. The paper solves no open problem and claims none: Collatz, Erd o s–Straus, Lychrel, Recam\'an, the Langton's-ant highway, Gilbreath, and the exact chromatic number of the plane all remain open, and each law's nonclaims say so explicitly.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Needles, membranes, and lawful repairs.} A \emph{needle} is a localized obstruction
surviving all native-layer probes; the corpus discipline prices needles against a declared budget,
dissolves them by promotion, or confines them by duality \citep{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}. A
\emph{membrane} is a budget condition holding at every accepted stage, and its failure is a critical
pair with exactly five lawful repairs (declared nonclaim, raised budget, rewritten carrier/audit,
genuinely new probes, completed transport family) --- same-package repetition is not a repair. In the
corpus every needle, budget, and probe family is declared up front and static; Clusters B and D live
precisely in the gap this leaves (history-generated needles, adversarial needles, and needles whose
survival is a positive certificate).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{The catalog form, status tags, and discharge vocabulary.} Foundations~IV presents its
fifty-two laws in a six-part normal form --- Setup, Theorem, Proof spine, Case enumeration,
Interaction status, Nonclaims --- each with five worked layer instantiations
\citep{Tsiokos2026FoundIV}; this paper adopts the template verbatim. One verified fact about that
catalog does structural work everywhere here: every F-IV Setup names fixed, singular data --- one
map, one quotient pair, one declared finite patch system --- and every F-IV theorem is a static
classification of that fixed data; no row contains a step-indexed quantifier, a growing family, an
adversary, a rate comparison, or an emergence-over-time claim. The temporal quantifier is therefore
the novelty axis of every G-law, and each law's Setup states it explicitly. Status tags are
three-valued and typographically fixed: \texttt{theorem} (the abstract implication is proved),
\texttt{schema} (named hypotheses carry the implication; no concrete instance is asserted to satisfy
them until discharged), and \texttt{calibration-anchored schema} (a schema whose mechanism is fully
discharged by a recognized solved classical instance). Residual accounting uses the AOR status
vocabulary \citep{Tsiokos2026AOR}, including the four asymptotic statuses recalled in
\Cref{sec:currency-taxonomy}, and the corpus nonclaim register is in force throughout --- most
prominently: route mismatch never implies drive content (G8's bridge is conditional on its named
hypotheses, which is legal); local admissibility never implies global admissibility without
exhaustion data (G4, G11); no same-level self-certification (G6, G7 are theorist-side); and promoted
support is never literalized at the native layer (all of Cluster A)
\citep{Tsiokos2026FoundIII}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
This section has no counterpart in Foundations~IV, and the addition is deliberate: the catalog's laws were
not invented and then illustrated, they were \emph{mined}, and the mining procedure is a first-class
contribution of this paper. The raw material is the class of eccentric problems --- Collatz,
Goodstein, Erd\H{o}s--Straus, Lychrel, Recam\'an, the angel problem, sandpiles, Langton's ant, Ducci,
Gilbreath, aperiodic tilings, Hadwiger--Nelson, Apollonian packings --- problems that are easy to
state, resistant in a characteristic way, and each equipped with a folklore argument that everyone
reaches for and that fails. The thesis of the method is that the folklore argument's failure is
structured: what it illegitimately assumes is a \emph{promoted object}, and what would repair it is a
\emph{descended certificate}, and the gap between the two, once it survives comparison against every
existing law of the corpus, is a new law.

For each problem, in order:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Identify the tempting almost-proof} --- the argument everyone reaches for that fails.
    The almost-proof reveals the illegal overread.
  \item \textbf{Name the promoted object the almost-proof secretly uses} --- an invariant measure on a
    completion, a fixed finite certificate package, a well-founded escrow. Typically the object does
    not descend to the native carrier.
  \item \textbf{State what a lawful descended certificate would be.} This fixes the boundary
    expression: the native, checkable assertion that promoted support is allowed to purchase
    (\Cref{sec:apparatus}).
  \item \textbf{Isolate the residual that survives every existing law.} Run the candidate against the
    full Foundations~IV catalog (exact statements, not summaries), the Foundations~V laws, the
    nonclaim register, and the AOR status list. What remains unhandled is the law seed --- and this
    step kills candidates as often as it produces them.
  \item \textbf{Find the siblings.} The seed is a law only if the same residual shape appears in at
    least three independent domains, at least one of them solved (the calibration instance).
    Otherwise it is a substrate observation, not a law.
\end{enumerate}
Admission then passes four further gates inherited from the corpus's discipline: a precise recognition
source making every Setup datum definite; a rebadge test requiring the candidate to differ from every
existing law on at least one declared axis --- for all thirteen laws here the differentiating axis is
the same, a step-indexed, growing, adversarial, or rate-comparison witness schema that no static
catalog row possesses, which is why an editing pass that accidentally deletes a temporal quantifier
from a law's statement collapses the law into its cousin and fails the gate; nonclaim compatibility
(a law that needs an unconditional version of a forbidden inference is dead); and a replication
ladder on the instantiation table (at least one solved calibration plus at least one instance with
genuine engagement beyond citation). The remainder of this section runs the protocol on four seeds:
two that became laws, and two that the protocol correctly killed.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The corpus is rich in currencies --- constraints, ledgers, potentials, duals --- but every one of them
is checked at an instant or across one declared comparison. What it lacks are the \emph{temporal}
currencies: the solvency question (does an unbounded run eventually earn a native descent
certificate?), the escrow question (can a changing presentation be audited by strict descent in a
well-founded carrier?), and the credit question (when does a supplied potential bound the total cost of
every finite prefix?). The three laws of this cluster record those currencies. Hidden Amortized Solvency (G1) is the
liveness law and the flagship of the catalog: it splits the eventual-solvency question into an
unconditional reduction and a conditional discharge schema whose named hypotheses are exactly what
remains open for Collatz. Transfinite Escrow (G2) is the termination law for stage-indexed runs, with
Goodstein sequences discharging the full transfinite mechanism. Amortized Potential Currency (G3) is the safety law:
the classical potential-method telescoping identity, stated as a currency with an explicit legality
gate.

\label{thm:G1b}
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G1-ghost-convergence]} for a computable neighborhood system $U_h(\Gamma)$ in
    $\widehat{X}$ with $\bigcap_h U_h(\Gamma) = \Gamma$: every infinite bad thread based at a
    nonterminal native point has a limit in $\widehat{X}$, every such limit lies in $\Gamma$, and
    hence for every $h$ the thread is eventually in $U_h(\Gamma)$;
  \item \textup{[H-G1-separation]} for every nonterminal native point $x$ there are computable
    $h(x)$ and $K(x)$, established by native certificates only, with
    \[
      T^{t}(x) \notin U_{h(x)}(\Gamma) \qquad \text{for every } t \ge K(x).
    \]
\end{itemize}
Then $\bigcap_k N_k = \varnothing$; by Part~(a), every nonterminal native point is live, and for each
fixed $x$ the bad-tail predicate $x \in N_k$ is eventually false. For Collatz both hypotheses are
unproved: they are named obligations, not evidence that the conjecture has been settled.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\subsection*{Layer instantiations}\label{layer-inst:G1}
\begin{description}
  \item[Collatz accelerated odd map --- conjectural flagship.] The affine ledger, the $2$-adic ghost
    $-1$, the $2^{L}-1$ shadowing family, and the cycle integrality condition are verified algebraic
    facts; liveness remains open because both boxed hypotheses are unproved
    \citep{Lagarias1985,Lagarias2010,Tao2019Collatz}.
  \item[Binary-counter increment --- calibration of the currency mechanism.] With $\Phi$ the number of
    $1$-bits, an increment across $r$ trailing ones costs $r + 1$, changes potential by $1 - r$, and
    is exactly solvent at every step; this calibrates the solvency currency, not the ghost mechanism
    \citep{Tarjan1985,CormenEtAl}.
  \item[Size-change and ranking-function termination --- calibration.] Termination analysis discharges
    local non-descent by a hidden well-founded ranking certificate --- ``promoted ledger gives native
    liveness'' as solved technology, without a Collatz-style ghost \citep{LeeJonesBenAmram2001}.
  \item[Aliquot dynamics --- conjectural folded instance.] For $s(n) = \sigma(n) - n$ the
    Catalan--Dickson question is open, and the natural currency is the whole factorization/divisor
    ledger rather than a scalar valuation --- G1 ledgers need not be one-dimensional
    \citep{GuySelfridge1975,GuyUnsolved}.
  \item[Switched and probabilistic termination certificates --- structural.] Average-dwell-time and
    ranking-supermartingale methods separate hidden average certificates from pointwise native
    progress; they become G1 instances only with an exact boundary certificate and pointwise residual
    \citep{Liberzon2003,AgrawalChatterjeeNovotny2017}.
\end{description}

\label{thm:G3}
For every finite run prefix $s_0 \to \cdots \to s_n$,
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i
  \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{n} \widehat{a}_i + \Phi(s_0) - \Phi(s_n)
  \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^{n} \widehat{a}_i + \Phi(s_0),
\]
the inequality because $\Phi(s_n) \ge 0$. Consequently, if a declared class of runs has
$\widehat{a}_i \le B$ for every step, then every length-$n$ prefix satisfies
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i \;\le\; n B + \Phi(s_0).
\]

\label{thm:G3}
For every finite run prefix $s_0 \to \cdots \to s_n$,
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i
  \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{n} \widehat{a}_i + \Phi(s_0) - \Phi(s_n)
  \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^{n} \widehat{a}_i + \Phi(s_0),
\]
the inequality because $\Phi(s_n) \ge 0$. Consequently, if a declared class of runs has
$\widehat{a}_i \le B$ for every step, then every length-$n$ prefix satisfies
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i \;\le\; n B + \Phi(s_0).
\]

\label{thm:G5}
\textbf{No-go schema.} Assume
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G5-unbounded-horizon]} for every fixed depth $m$ there are a step $j$ and states
    $y, z$ in the declared carrier with $q_m(y) = q_m(z)$ but different declared future probe values
    --- a nonempty step-indexed split-pair obstruction $\Delta(q_m, R_b^{\,j}, r_j) \neq \varnothing$.
\end{itemize}
Then no fixed-depth quotient $q_m$ is future-sufficient for the declared unbounded run: for every
$m$, the future probe fails to factor through $q_m$.

\textbf{Confinement schema.} Assume
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G5-closed-pattern]} a declared regular or automatic language $\mathcal{P}$
    satisfies $R_b(\mathcal{P}) \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ (cyclically $R_b(P_i) \subseteq P_{i+1}$ when
    phase-indexed, with $\mathcal{P} = \bigcup_i P_i$), and no member of $\mathcal{P}$ satisfies the
    target predicate.
\end{itemize}
Then if some iterate $R_b^{\,N}(x)$ lies in $\mathcal{P}$, no later iterate satisfies the target:
closure gives $R_b^{\,N+t}(x) \in \mathcal{P}$ for every $t \ge 0$, and target-freeness gives
$\lnot\,\mathrm{Pal}_b(R_b^{\,N+t}(x))$ for every $t \ge 0$.

Both halves are conditional: the no-go does not by itself prove escape from the target, and the
confinement applies only after a concrete target-free closed language has been verified.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The calibration is the solved base-2 instance: the orbit of $22 = 10110_2$ never reaches a binary
palindrome. Directly, $10110 \to 100011 \to 1010100 \to 1101001 \to 10110100$, and from there the
orbit enters a four-phase regular family, defined for $r \ge 2$ by
\[
  P_0(r) = 10\,1^r\,01\,0^r, \quad
  P_1(r) = 11\,0^{r-2}\,1\,000\,1^{r-2}\,01, \quad
  P_2(r) = 10\,1^r\,01\,0^{r+1}, \quad
  P_3(r) = 11\,0^r\,10\,1^{r-1}\,01,
\]
with the phase cycle, verified by binary addition with carries,
\[
  R(P_0(r)) = P_1(r), \qquad
  R(P_1(r)) = P_2(r), \qquad
  R(P_2(r)) = P_3(r), \qquad
  R(P_3(r)) = P_0(r+1).
\]
No string in the family is a palindrome: $P_0$ and $P_2$ begin with $1$ and end with $0$; $P_1$ and
$P_3$ begin with $11$ and end with $01$, so second and penultimate digits differ. The four pre-entry
strings are also non-palindromic, so the whole orbit is certified target-free --- discharging
\textup{[H-G5-closed-pattern]} with the full four-phase family as the invariant (note the closure is
cyclic phase-to-phase; the frequently quoted pattern $10\,1^k\,01\,0^k$ recurs under $R^4$, every
fourth iterate, not under single steps).\footnote{The base-2 result is recorded at OEIS A060382 and
attributed to Kevin Brown's MathPages note; no peer-reviewed publication of the proof was located, so
the attribution is informally sourced --- and this Kevin Brown is distinct from the Cornell
topologist Kenneth~S.~Brown, with whom secondary discussions sometimes conflate him
\citep{OEIS-A060382,Brown-MathPages}.} For base 10, no analogous certificate is known: $196$ remains
open, and finite searches, however deep, are bounded evidence only \citep{Walker-Fourmilab}.

\label{thm:G6}
\textbf{Covering schema.} Assume
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G6-dominant-pressure]} there are a finite exception set $E \subseteq X$, a cofinal
    exhaustion $W_1 \subseteq W_2 \subseteq \cdots$ with $\bigcup_M W_M = X \setminus E$, and for
    each $M$ a finite block decomposition of times after some $N_M$ such that whenever $H_n(W_M)$ is
    nonempty at the start of a block $I$, the audited inequality
    \[
      \sum_{i \in I} \rho_i(W_M) \;\ge\; 1 + \sum_{i \in I} \gamma_i(W_M)
    \]
    holds and the excess is charged to at least one distinct first visit in $H_n(W_M)$ during $I$.
\end{itemize}
Then every point of $X \setminus E$ is eventually visited: the orbit is cofinite-covering relative to
$E$.

\textbf{Hole-forming schema.} Assume
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G6-dominant-obstruction]} there are a target $y \in X$, a time $N$ with
    $y \notin V_N$, and a declared sequence of separating cuts $C_n(y)$ such that for every
    $n \ge N$ every legal path from $(x_n, S_n)$ to $y$ crosses $S_n$ or a certified blocked cut,
    with the quantitative excess $\sum_{i \in I} \gamma_i(C_i(y)) > \sum_{i \in I} \rho_i(C_i(y))$ on
    every later audit block, tied to the displayed cut rather than inferred from density.
\end{itemize}
Then $y$ is a permanent hole: $y \notin V_n$ for all $n \ge N$.

Both directions are schemas: no concrete system satisfies either hypothesis until its rate ledger and
witness cuts are supplied, and the two hypotheses can only conflict on a single target if the audit
record itself is inconsistent.

\label{thm:G8}
Let $(C, V, \{m_v\}, L)$ be a move system with initial configuration $x$, and assume:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G8]} (abelian compatibility) for every configuration $c$ and all \emph{distinct}
    sites $v \neq w$: if $L_v(c)$ and $L_w(c)$ both hold, then firing either move preserves legality
    of the other, the two composites agree,
    \[
      m_w(m_v(c)) \;=\; m_v(m_w(c)),
    \]
    and both two-step routes record the same counter increment $e_v + e_w$. The case $v = w$ is
    outside the scope of this hypothesis: \textup{[H-G8]} does not require a move to preserve its own
    legality after firing.
  \item \textup{[termination at $x$]} every maximal legal run from $x$ terminates.
\end{itemize}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Order-independent stabilization.} All legal terminating runs from $x$ end at the same
    stable configuration $x^{\circ}$.
  \item \emph{Odometer invariance.} All legal terminating runs from $x$ have the same counter vector
    $u_x \in \mathbb{N}^{V}$.
\end{enumerate}
If, in addition,
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G8-mono]} (least-action monotonicity) the move system carries a declared comparison
    structure under which stabilizing scripts are compared pointwise, legal move maps are compatible
    with the comparison, and adding available resource or delaying commuting legal moves cannot make a
    genuinely necessary firing disappear from every stabilizing script,
\end{itemize}
then the odometer is pointwise minimal among legally sufficient scripts: for every $n \in
\mathbb{N}^{V}$ whose prescribed multiset of moves is realized by some legal admissible stabilizing
order from $x$,
\[
  u_x(v) \;\le\; n(v) \qquad \text{for every } v \in V.
\]
This is a legal-versus-legal least-action statement. It does not compare the odometer against the
fully general Fey--Levine--Peres class of arbitrary nonnegative stabilizing scripts, which includes
force-firing scripts passing through illegal intermediate configurations.

In interaction terms, G8 turns P3 route data into P6 audit content through a P2 conservation gate: the
legal firing order is route data, the counter vector is bookkeeping, and \textup{[H-G8]} is the gate
that makes the bookkeeping conserved across all legal routes. The claim is conditional on that gate
and on termination; it is not an unconditional inference from route mismatch to potential. The
computational record exercises both sides. Lab G8-L1 ran $500$ seeded random stabilizations on square
sandpile grids of sizes $10, 20, 30, 40, 50$ ($100$ random legal orders per configuration) and found
every run agreeing with the deterministic baselines in both final configuration and odometer vector.
Lab G8-L2 sampled $1000$ random legal orders of the case~(b) witness: every run reached $N$, and
exactly three distinct counter vectors appeared --- confluence without a canonical ledger, as the law
predicts.

\label{thm:G9}
Let a run of an extended local system carry the setup data above.

\textbf{Positive schema.} Assume:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G9-census]} the run carries an exact defect ledger, and there is a finite $N$ such
    that for all $n \ge N$ the unresolved defect measure is non-increasing after accounting for bound
    and absorbed defects: $|\mathrm{unresolved}_{n+1}| \le |\mathrm{unresolved}_n|$.
  \item \textup{[H-G9-absorb]} there are finite constants $N, T$ and a finite family of transporter
    records $\{R_j\}$ such that every defect still unresolved for $T$ steps after time $N$ is
    annihilated, bound into a finite non-moving composite, or assigned by the ledger to exactly one
    transporter record.
\end{itemize}
If the transporter-assigned persistent-defect set is nonempty and at least one assigned transporter
has displacement $d \neq 0$, then the run enters a certified transport regime: there is a finite time
$t_0$ and a finite nonempty family of transporter records covering every transporter-assigned
persistent defect after $t_0$, each record satisfying its recurrence-with-displacement equality on its
declared support. Persistent defects bound into stationary residue may coexist; the transport
certification rests on the moving subset. In the single-transporter or common-velocity case the
conclusion is eventual spatio-temporal periodicity modulo translation:
\[
  c_{\,t+\tau}\big|_{W+d} \;=\; \mathrm{shift}_d\!\left(c_t\big|_{W}\right)
  \qquad \text{for all certified } t \ge t_0.
\]
If instead all defects are eventually annihilated or resolved, with no persistent transporter-assigned
defect, the run is cleared or quiescent --- not transport-certified.

\textbf{Negative schema.} Separately, if the ledger exhibits unbounded unresolved creation ---
$\sup_n |\mathrm{unresolved}_n| = \infty$, or infinitely many creation events remain forever unmatched
by annihilation, binding, or absorption --- then the positive transport claim is blocked by the
proliferation ledger itself. Equivalently, such a ledger is incompatible with
\textup{[H-G9-census]}, so the positive schema's census obligation cannot be discharged; no
recurrence-with-displacement record may be inferred from finite local motion or holonomy language
alone.

\subsection*{Layer instantiations}\label{layer-inst:G9}
\begin{description}
  \item[Rule 184 and traffic cellular automata --- calibration.] The solved density regimes above are
    the calibration instance discharging the census-to-transport mechanism
    \citep{Fuks1997,Nagel1996,ChowdhurySantenSchadschneider2000}.
  \item[Langton's ant --- conjectural.] The highway conjecture --- that every finite initial
    configuration reaches the $104$-step highway --- remains open; the standard ant is due to
    \citet{Langton1986}. What \emph{is} proved is trajectory unboundedness, due to
    \citet{BunimovichTroubetzkoy1992}; the rival ``Cohen--Kong theorem'' attribution circulating in
    popular accounts is flagged as incorrect by the specialist literature and is not used here. The
    unboundedness fragment is a nonclaim-scoped citation: G9's theorem and lab are carried by rule
    184, not by the ant.
  \item[Excitable-media automata --- structural.] Greenberg--Hastings-style systems produce discrete
    waves and spiral cores, but an instance requires an explicit defect census and transporter
    recurrence record for a specific model \citep{Greenberg1978,DurrettGriffeath}.
  \item[Cellular-automata glider ecology --- structural.] Life gliders and one-dimensional CA
    particles are direct recurrence-with-displacement objects once the period/displacement equality is
    checked on finite support; arbitrary debris-to-glider emergence remains model-specific
    \citep{Gardner1970,Pivato}.
  \item[Queue clearing and traffic shock waves --- structural.] Kinematic-wave and cell-transmission
    models supply moving jam and clearing-front analogues; an instance requires a discrete event
    ledger matching creation, annihilation, and absorption of queue defects
    \citep{LighthillWhitham1955,Richards1956,Daganzo1994}.
\end{description}

\subsection*{Layer instantiations}\label{layer-inst:G9}
\begin{description}
  \item[Rule 184 and traffic cellular automata --- calibration.] The solved density regimes above are
    the calibration instance discharging the census-to-transport mechanism
    \citep{Fuks1997,Nagel1996,ChowdhurySantenSchadschneider2000}.
  \item[Langton's ant --- conjectural.] The highway conjecture --- that every finite initial
    configuration reaches the $104$-step highway --- remains open; the standard ant is due to
    \citet{Langton1986}. What \emph{is} proved is trajectory unboundedness, due to
    \citet{BunimovichTroubetzkoy1992}; the rival ``Cohen--Kong theorem'' attribution circulating in
    popular accounts is flagged as incorrect by the specialist literature and is not used here. The
    unboundedness fragment is a nonclaim-scoped citation: G9's theorem and lab are carried by rule
    184, not by the ant.
  \item[Excitable-media automata --- structural.] Greenberg--Hastings-style systems produce discrete
    waves and spiral cores, but an instance requires an explicit defect census and transporter
    recurrence record for a specific model \citep{Greenberg1978,DurrettGriffeath}.
  \item[Cellular-automata glider ecology --- structural.] Life gliders and one-dimensional CA
    particles are direct recurrence-with-displacement objects once the period/displacement equality is
    checked on finite support; arbitrary debris-to-glider emergence remains model-specific
    \citep{Gardner1970,Pivato}.
  \item[Queue clearing and traffic shock waves --- structural.] Kinematic-wave and cell-transmission
    models supply moving jam and clearing-front analogues; an instance requires a discrete event
    ledger matching creation, annihilation, and absorption of queue defects
    \citep{LighthillWhitham1955,Richards1956,Daganzo1994}.
\end{description}

\label{thm:currency-bridge}
\textbf{(A) C7 solvency.} Fix the G1 data $(T, <, A)$ and a nonterminal point $x$, and let
$\mathrm{badtail}_j(x) \in \{0, 1\}$ indicate membership $x \in N_j$ in the $j$-th bad-tail
membrane. Then pointwise liveness at $x$ --- some $k \ge 1$ with $V_k(x) > 0$ --- holds if and only
if $\mathrm{badtail}_j(x)$ is \textit{eventual\_zero}. Globalized over nonterminal points, this is
the status-language reading of \Cref{thm:G1}.

\textbf{(B) C6 transfinite escrow.} Fix the G2 data and a run satisfying the stage-coherence audit
over a well-founded escrow carrier, and let $\mathrm{notdone}_k \in \{0, 1\}$ indicate that no stage
$i \le k$ has reached the terminal set. Then --- classically, or constructively once a concrete
terminal witness is extracted --- there is a finite stage $K$ reaching the terminal set, and
$\mathrm{notdone}$ is \textit{eventual\_zero}.

\textbf{(C) C5 amortized potential.} Fix a G3-style run with nonnegative actual costs $a_i$,
nonnegative amortized costs $\widehat{a}_i$, nonnegative potential $\Phi$, and write
$A_n = \sum_{i \le n} a_i$, $H_n = \sum_{i \le n} \widehat{a}_i$, $\Phi_0 = \Phi(s_0)$, so that
$A_n \le H_n + \Phi_0$ by \Cref{thm:G3}. Then the status of the amortized-cost sequence converts
into a total-actual-cost bound:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textit{asymptotic\_budgeted} ($\widehat{a}_i \le B$ for $i \ge J_0$) gives, for every
    $n \ge J_0$, $A_n \le \Phi_0 + H_{\mathrm{head}} + B\,(n - J_0 + 1)$ where
    $H_{\mathrm{head}} = \sum_{i < J_0} \widehat{a}_i$; in particular $A_n = O(n)$;
  \item \textit{summable} ($\sum_i \widehat{a}_i = S < \infty$) gives the uniform bound
    $A_n \le S + \Phi_0$ for every $n$: total actual cost over the infinite run is finite;
  \item \textit{contractive} reduces to the summable case by the geometric tail bound, with the
    explicit constant $A_n \le \Phi_0 + \sum_{i < J} \widehat{a}_i + \widehat{a}_J / (1 - q)$;
  \item \textit{eventual\_zero} ($\widehat{a}_i = 0$ for $i \ge J_0$) gives the fixed finite bound
    $A_n \le \Phi_0 + \sum_{i < J_0} \widehat{a}_i$ for every $n$.
\end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Conditionality where the register demands it.} Each law is exactly as conditional as the
corpus's nonclaim register requires, and several hypotheses are load-bearing by design. G8's abelian
compatibility is named and non-negotiable --- terminating confluence alone determines no canonical
counter ledger (the case-(b) witness), and Part~B's least action is the legal-versus-legal
comparison only. G9's transport is certified by recurrence-with-displacement records, never by
holonomy or visual motion; nothing in G8 or G9 is a drive, arrow, or entropy-production claim, and
that vocabulary stays reserved. G4 and G11 are conditional on their exhaustion and per-period
certificate data --- local admissibility never globalizes for free, and G11 supplies no algorithm
against Berger's undecidability. G5's no-go half is not an escape certificate; its confinement half
requires a verified target-free closed language. G6 and G7 are theorist-side throughout: the system
never certifies itself, and the adversary's strategy space is always declared --- no hidden-oracle
devil. G6's two rate hypotheses are proposed formalizations that later labs may refine, and its
designed-variant calibrations deliberately do not upgrade its grade. G7's thresholds are board- and
rule-relative; its finite-board lab is an exhibit, not infinite-board evidence. G10 does not
contradict the corpus's information-loss results and reconstructs nothing lost; its hypotheses must
be proved, not observed empirically. G12's compactness bridge is a purchased set-theoretic
commitment, recorded, and choice sensitivity in plane-coloring questions is a real warning; the
826-vertex lab witness is solver-verified UNSAT without an independent proof-checked certificate,
as its provenance record states. G13's status ceiling is \texttt{schema}; ``thin'' and ``thick''
carry only their strict technical senses, and congruence admissibility is local and incomplete ---
the 2024 reciprocity obstruction shows exactly that. Throughout Cluster A, promoted objects
(ledgers, escrows, completions, ghosts) are never literalized at the native layer; only boundary
certificates descend.

conclusion: Six Birds theory studies finite systems observed through deterministic coarse-grainings (``lenses'') using a small audited vocabulary of primitives. This paper proves eight no-go theorems that constrain when common emergence narratives can be made honest in a finite, checkable setting. For a finite Markov system and horizon T , define an arrow audit as the Kullback–Leibler divergence between the observed path law and its time reversal. We prove a deterministic data-processing inequality: observation cannot increase arrow. As a consequence, any reversible system started in stationarity has zero observed arrow, even when the observation supports nontrivial protocol structure. Further results give graph-theoretic obstructions for force-like antisymmetric drives (exactness on forests and zero cycle sums), a finite variational identity for best macro-kernels and closure deficit, and a bounded-interface saturation theorem that prevents unbounded laddering. Together these theorems delimit what can and cannot be certified as emergent from audited primitives in finite models.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
All results are stated for finite systems and deterministic lenses.
The theorem statements are collected in Section~\ref{sec:main-results}, and the later theorem-front sections refer back to those labels.
In one line each, the fronts are:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Arrow/DPI:} deterministic observation cannot increase forward--reverse path-space KL; equality holds for identity observation. (\Cref{thm:NG_ARROW_DPI})
  \item \emph{Protocol trap:} holonomy can produce apparent protocol structure without honest entropy production, under a stationary initialization scope. (\Cref{thm:NG_PROTOCOL_TRAP})
  \item \emph{Force implies cycles:} nontrivial force-like structure requires non-forest support (positive cycle rank). (\Cref{thm:NG_FORCE_FOREST})
  \item \emph{Null force under exactness:} if the log-ratio 1-form is exact (potential), cycle affinities vanish. (\Cref{thm:NG_FORCE_NULL})
  \item \emph{Closure deficit:} coarse closure deficit is a conditional-information obstruction characterized by a finite variational best macro kernel. (\Cref{thm:NG_MACRO_CLOSURE_DEFICIT})
  \item \emph{Objecthood (bounded):} strict contraction implies at most one fixed distribution; the theorem front addresses uniqueness and separation in the contractive total-variation regime. (\Cref{thm:NG_OBJECT_CONTRACTIVE})
  \item \emph{Idempotence no-ladder:} idempotent packaging stabilizes after one step (no iterate ladder). (\Cref{thm:NG_LADDER_IDEM})
  \item \emph{Bounded-interface no-ladder:} with a fixed finite interface, definability is bounded by $2^{|\mathrm{im}(f)|}$ and no unbounded predicate ladder can arise without leaving the interface scope. (\Cref{thm:NG_LADDER_BOUNDED_INTERFACE})
\end{itemize}

  \item \emph{Arrow/DPI:} deterministic observation cannot increase forward--reverse path-space KL; equality holds for identity observation. (\thmNGArrowDPI)
  \item \emph{Protocol trap:} holonomy can produce apparent protocol structure without honest entropy production, under a stationary initialization scope. (\thmNGProtocolTrap)
  \item \emph{Force implies cycles:} nontrivial force-like structure requires non-forest support (positive cycle rank). (\thmNGForceForest)
  \item \emph{Null force under exactness:} if the log-ratio 1-form is exact (potential), cycle affinities vanish. (\thmNGForceNull)
  \item \emph{Closure deficit:} coarse closure deficit is a conditional-information obstruction characterized by a finite variational best macro kernel. (\thmNGMacroClosureDeficit)
  \item \emph{Objecthood (bounded):} strict contraction implies at most one fixed distribution; the theorem front addresses uniqueness and separation in the contractive total-variation regime. (\thmNGObjectContractive)
  \item \emph{Idempotence no-ladder:} idempotent packaging stabilizes after one step (no iterate ladder). (\thmNGLadderIdem)
  \item \emph{Bounded-interface no-ladder:} with a fixed finite interface, definability is bounded by $2^{|\mathrm{im}(f)|}$ and no unbounded predicate ladder can arise without leaving the interface scope. (\thmNGLadderBoundedInterface)
\end{itemize}

\label{thm:NG_ARROW_DPI}
Let $\mu\in\Delta(\mathsf{X})$, let $P:\mathsf{X}\times\mathsf{X}\to[0,1]$ be row-stochastic, and let $T\ge 1$. Define the micro path law on $\mathsf{X}^{T+1}$ by \[\mathbf{P}^{(T)}_{\mu,P}(x_{0:T})=\mu(x_0)\prod_{t=0}^{T-1}P(x_t,x_{t+1}).\] Let $\mathrm{rev}_T(x_{0:T})=(x_T,\dots,x_0)$ and let $\ell:\mathsf{X}\to\mathsf{Y}$ be deterministic with pointwise extension $\ell^{(T)}(x_{0:T})=(\ell(x_0),\dots,\ell(x_T))$. Then \[\mathrm{KL}\!\Big((\ell^{(T)})_{\#}\mathbf{P}^{(T)}_{\mu,P}\ \Big\|\ (\mathrm{rev}_T)_{\#}(\ell^{(T)})_{\#}\mathbf{P}^{(T)}_{\mu,P}\Big)\ \le\ \mathrm{KL}\!\Big(\mathbf{P}^{(T)}_{\mu,P}\ \Big\|\ (\mathrm{rev}_T)_{\#}\mathbf{P}^{(T)}_{\mu,P}\Big).\]

\label{thm:NG_FORCE_FOREST}
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite undirected forest. Let $a$ be an antisymmetric function on oriented edges, so that $a(u,v)=-a(v,u)$ and $a(u,v)=0$ whenever $\{u,v\}\notin E$. Then there exists a potential $\phi:V\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for every oriented edge $(u,v)$, \[ a(u,v)=\phi(v)-\phi(u).\]

For each $x\in\mathsf{X}$, define the packaged future law \[ p_x^{(\tau)}(y') := \Pr_{\mu,P}[\Pi(X_{t+\tau})=y' \mid X_t=x].\] For a candidate macro kernel $K:\mathsf{Y}\times\mathsf{Y}\to[0,1]$, define \[ \mathcal{L}_\tau(K) := \sum_{x\in \mathsf{X}} \mu(x)\,\mathrm{KL}\!\big(p_x^{(\tau)} \mid K_{\Pi(x)}\big).\] Define the closure deficit by \[ \mathrm{CD}_\tau(\Pi) := I\!\big(X_t;\Pi(X_{t+\tau})\,\big|\,\Pi(X_t)\big).\] Then the kernel \[ K^\star_y(y') := \Pr_{\mu,P}[\Pi(X_{t+\tau})=y' \mid \Pi(X_t)=y] \] satisfies \[ \mathrm{CD}_\tau(\Pi)=\min_K \mathcal{L}_\tau(K)=\mathcal{L}_\tau(K^\star).\] Moreover, if there exist $x,x'\in\mathsf{X}$ with $\Pi(x)=\Pi(x')$, $\mu(x)>0$, $\mu(x')>0$, and $p_x^{(\tau)}\neq p_{x'}^{(\tau)}$, then $\mathrm{CD}_\tau(\Pi)>0$.

\label{thm:NG_LADDER_BOUNDED_INTERFACE}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:NG_ARROW_DPI}]
Fix $T\ge 0$ and abbreviate $P := P_T^{\mu,K}\in\Delta(X^{T+1})$ and $Q := P_T^{\mu,K,\mathrm{rev}} = \mathrm{rev}_{\#}P$.
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:deterministic_dpi_kl} to $\Omega=X^{T+1}$, $\Omega'=Y^{T+1}$ and $g=f^{(T)}$:
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\big(f^{(T)}_{\#}P \,\|\, f^{(T)}_{\#}Q\big)
\le
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\,\|\,Q).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:rev_pushforward_commute}, $f^{(T)}_{\#}P = P_T^{\mu,K,f}$ and $f^{(T)}_{\#}Q = P_T^{\mu,K,f,\mathrm{rev}}$.
Therefore the left-hand side equals $\mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K;f)$ and the right-hand side equals $\mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K)$, proving
$\mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K;f)\le \mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K)$ as claimed.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:NG_ARROW_DPI}]
Fix $T\ge 0$ and abbreviate $P := P_T^{\mu,K}\in\Delta(X^{T+1})$ and $Q := P_T^{\mu,K,\mathrm{rev}} = \mathrm{rev}_{\#}P$.
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:deterministic_dpi_kl} to $\Omega=X^{T+1}$, $\Omega'=Y^{T+1}$ and $g=f^{(T)}$:
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\big(f^{(T)}_{\#}P \,\|\, f^{(T)}_{\#}Q\big)
\le
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\,\|\,Q).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:rev_pushforward_commute}, $f^{(T)}_{\#}P = P_T^{\mu,K,f}$ and $f^{(T)}_{\#}Q = P_T^{\mu,K,f,\mathrm{rev}}$.
Therefore the left-hand side equals $\mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K;f)$ and the right-hand side equals $\mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K)$, proving
$\mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K;f)\le \mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K)$ as claimed.
\end{proof}

Let $w=(v_0,v_1,\dots,v_k)$ be a finite walk with $v_k=v_0$ and
$\{v_i,v_{i+1}\}\in E$ for all $i$.
The \emph{closed-walk sum} of $a$ along $w$ is
\[
S_a(w)\;=\;\sum_{i=0}^{k-1} a(v_i,v_{i+1}).
\]
When $a$ is a log-ratio $1$-form, $S_a(w)$ is the (log) cycle affinity.
This is the standard cycle-affinity language for finite Markov networks \citep{Schnakenberg1976}.

If $K$ is a Markov kernel on a finite state space with bidirected support graph $G$,
a common affinity $1$-form is the log-ratio
\[
a_K(u,v)=\log\frac{K(u,v)}{K(v,u)}
\qquad\text{on each bidirected edge.}
\]
This is antisymmetric on $\vec E$. Theorems~\ref{thm:NG_FORCE_FOREST} and
\ref{thm:NG_FORCE_NULL} show that (i) on forest support every such antisymmetric form
is potential-generated, and (ii) any potential-generated form has zero closed-walk sums,
so every cycle affinity vanishes.
