\label{lem:closure_kl_mixture}
Let $(w_i)_{i\in I}$ be nonnegative weights on a finite index set $I$, not all zero,
and let $(P_i)_{i\in I}$ be probability laws on a finite set $\Omega$.
Define
\[
W := \sum_{i\in I} w_i,
\qquad
R := \frac{1}{W}\sum_{i\in I} w_i P_i.
\]
Then for every probability law $Q$ on $\Omega$,
\[
\sum_{i\in I} w_i\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_i\,\middle\|\,Q\right)
=
\sum_{i\in I} w_i\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_i\,\middle\|\,R\right)
+
W\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(R\,\middle\|\,Q\right).
\]
In particular, $Q=R$ is a minimizer, and the minimum value is
\[
\sum_{i\in I} w_i\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_i\,\middle\|\,R\right).
\]

conclusion: Many mathematical frameworks come with audit data alongside their main objects: source ledgers, route registries, residual budgets, status annotations, nonclaim boundaries, and meta-audit records. Audited Operational Realisability (AOR) is the meta-theory of typed carriers that close as audit systems within a declared scope. A PreSB carrier is a typed carrier together with this audit data; it is an AOR carrier when every declared audit obligation is discharged inside the scope. We show that every PreSB carrier _ S admits a canonical completion into the full subcategory of AOR carriers via a reflection obtained as a monotone Knaster–Tarski saturation on the complete lattice of AOR-extending operations. The reflection is developed in four parts: the closure-completion construction and its universal property; the eight-stratum decomposition of the structural defect ; the thirteen-type residual atlas, with reciprocal local and global mismatch types, its discharge cascades, and cascade-stable AOR; and refinement chains with asymptotic statuses, yielding the hierarchy . The development is meta-theoretic and carries no PDE-specific worked example; concrete AOR-instance applications belong to consumer manuscripts that cite this meta-theory at paper level. Two scope disclosures apply. The cascade-confluence theorem uses Newman's lemma as a classical body input after proving the local diamond property and the well-founded discharge relation; Appendix D records the corresponding formal companion row as partial. The hierarchy is exhibited via named witness carriers and their typed obstruction markers; full predicate-level non-membership proofs at every level remain framework future work.

Many mathematical frameworks come with audit data alongside their
main objects: source ledgers, route registries, residual budgets,
status annotations, nonclaim boundaries, and meta-audit records.
\emph{Audited Operational Realisability} (AOR) is the meta-theory of
typed carriers that close as audit systems within a declared scope.
A \emph{PreSB carrier} is a typed carrier together with this audit
data; it is an \emph{AOR carrier} when every declared audit
obligation is discharged inside the scope.  We show that every PreSB
carrier \(\PreSB_{\mathfrak S}\) admits a canonical completion into
the full subcategory of AOR carriers via a reflection
\(\ClSB\dashv\iota\) obtained as a monotone Knaster--Tarski
saturation on the complete lattice of AOR-extending operations.  The
reflection is developed in four parts: the closure-completion
construction and its universal property; the eight-stratum
decomposition of the structural defect \(\XiSB\); the thirteen-type
residual atlas, with reciprocal local and global mismatch types, its
discharge cascades, and cascade-stable AOR; and refinement chains with asymptotic
statuses, yielding the hierarchy
\(\RefStableAOR\subseteq\CascadeStableAOR\subseteq\AOR\).  The
development is meta-theoretic and carries no PDE-specific worked
example; concrete AOR-instance applications belong to consumer
manuscripts that cite this meta-theory at paper level.  Two scope
disclosures apply.  The cascade-confluence theorem uses Newman's lemma
as a classical body input after proving the local diamond property and
the well-founded discharge relation; Appendix~D records the corresponding
formal companion row as partial.  The hierarchy is exhibited via named
witness carriers and their typed obstruction markers; full predicate-level
non-membership proofs at every level remain framework future work.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Fix a scope record \(\mathfrak S\) declaring the admissible
carrier-class, source ledger, interface family, and route registry.
The category \(\PreSB_{\mathfrak S}\) consists of typed carriers
equipped with declared audit data over \(\mathfrak S\) --- observation,
stage, constraint, rewrite, holonomy, residual, status, nonclaim, and
meta-audit registries --- together with morphisms preserving the
scoped package.  Its full subcategory \(\AOR_{\mathfrak S}\) contains
the audit-closed carriers, those whose declared records, routes,
residuals, nonclaims, and meta-audits have all been typed, registered,
statused, or discharged inside \(\mathfrak S\).  The central question
is the corresponding closure problem: when does an arbitrary object of
\(\PreSB_{\mathfrak S}\) admit a canonical completion into
\(\AOR_{\mathfrak S}\), and what is the structure of that completion?

conclusion: It has eight named strata: observation, stage, constraint, rewrite, holonomy, residual, nonclaim, and meta-audit.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The first diagnostic device is the structural defect \(\Xi_{SB}\).  For a
PreSB carrier, \(\Xi_{SB}\) measures the aggregate failure of audit
closure.  It has eight named strata: observation, stage, constraint,
rewrite, holonomy, residual, nonclaim, and meta-audit.  AOR membership
therefore decomposes: it holds exactly when every stratum is empty.  The
residual stratum is refined further by a thirteen-type residual atlas:
descent, transport, interface, local mismatch, global mismatch,
presentation, source admission, horizon, scale, limit, symmetry, role,
and target typing.
Residual atoms carry statuses drawn from the AOR-8 catalogue and may
generate downstream obligations, so audit closure is also an
operational question about how discharge propagates.

conclusion: it is accompanied by records of which probes are native, which routes are legal, which residuals remain unpaid, which statements are explicitly outside scope, and which bookkeeping obligations have been accepted.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The framework developed here abstracts an audit discipline that
already appears in the formed-layer membrane theory of
\citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}.  In that setting the mathematical
object of interest is never just a bare carrier; it is accompanied by
records of which probes are native, which routes are legal, which
residuals remain unpaid, which statements are explicitly outside
scope, and which bookkeeping obligations have been accepted.  We do
not rederive that membrane theory, but isolate the meta-theoretic
pattern behind it: a carrier can be meaningfully used only after its
record layer has been audited inside a declared scope.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The adequacy-residual calculus of \citet{Tsiokos2026XiCompanion}
supplies a second motivating source.  There the central object is the
Schur-complement residual \(\Xi_C(D\mid L)\), measuring what a
dissolving probe family \(D\) cannot explain through a native probe
family \(L\) under an audit operator \(C\).  The calculus distinguishes
native explanation from leftover residual, exact adequacy from
defective adequacy, and lawful promotion from blind-spot failure.
AOR neither imports those theorems nor depends on them; it abstracts
the surrounding bookkeeping question: once a residual, route, status,
or nonclaim has been declared, what does it mean for the whole
carrier to be audit-closed?

conclusion: The fieldwise meet of any family keeps precisely the data common to all packages, and the fieldwise generated join adjoins the union of all carrier, route, residual, nonclaim, and meta-audit data while retaining only well-typed scope-compatible entries.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
Fix the scope \(\mathfrak S\) and a seed carrier \(\mathsf C\).  Let
\(\mathcal L_{\mathfrak S}(\mathsf C)\) be the poset of AOR-extending
operation packages over \(\mathsf C\), ordered by subcarrier inclusion and
typed-field extension.  The fieldwise meet of any family keeps precisely the
data common to all packages, and the fieldwise generated join adjoins the
union of all carrier, route, residual, nonclaim, and meta-audit data while
retaining only well-typed scope-compatible entries.  These operations give a
complete lattice.  The saturation endomap \(S\) sends a package to the same
package together with the minimal operations forced by its currently missing
AOR obligations.  If \(X\le Y\), then every obligation visible in \(X\) is
also visible in \(Y\), and every operation forced over \(X\) is included
among the operations forced over \(Y\); hence \(S(X)\le S(Y)\).

Knaster--Tarski \citep{TarskiFixedPoint1955} now gives a least fixed
point \(\mathrm{lfp}(S)\).  This object contains the seed package,

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
The minimal operation \(\sigma\) adds exactly one of the audit-completion
data types used by the saturation map: typed-record data, route audits,
residual statuses, nonclaim entries, or meta-audit discharge records.  In
each case, the AOR-extending datum of \(\sigma\) is the smallest typed
completion of \(X\) that closes the obligation \(\sigma\) addresses.  The
map \(g_X\) sends the fields already present in \(X\) to a typed
configuration in \(\mathsf D\).  Because \(\mathsf D\) is AOR, the
corresponding obligation is already discharged in \(\iota\mathsf D\), so
the image of the new completion datum is forced.  This defines
\(\widetilde g_\sigma\).

The first diagnostic layer is the structural defect \(\Xi_{SB}\): the
aggregate record of ways in which a scoped PreSB carrier has not yet
closed as an AOR carrier.  Splitting the defect into strata keeps the
failure mode visible, in the spirit of typed fault-and-failure
taxonomies in the dependable-computing literature
\citep{Avizienis2004Dependability}.  A missing observation typing, an
undeclared stage law, an unwitnessed constraint, an unannotated
rewrite, a missing holonomy transport, an unstatused residual, an
unregistered nonclaim, and an undischarged meta-audit obligation are
different audit failures, even when they all obstruct the same
conclusion that the carrier is audit-closed.  Strata are recorded as
finite multisets in the sense of \citet{Blizard1989Multiset}, so a
record may appear with multiplicity matching the carrier-field data
that creates it.

\begin{definition}[Structural defect $\Xi_{SB}$]\label{def:aor:xi-sb}
The \emph{structural defect} $\Xi_{SB}(\mathsf C)$ of a PreSB carrier
$\mathsf C$ is the disjoint sum of its eight defect strata,
\begin{align*}
  \Xi_{SB}(\mathsf C)
  \;=\;& \Sigma_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{stage}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{constraint}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{rewrite}}(\mathsf C) \\
  & {} \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{holonomy}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{residual}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{nonclaim}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{meta}}(\mathsf C),
\end{align*}
with the strata defined in \Cref{def:aor:sigma-obs}--\Cref{def:aor:sigma-meta}.
The carrier is AOR exactly when every stratum is empty.
\end{definition}

source_wording_tex:
The first diagnostic layer is the structural defect \(\XiSB\): the
aggregate record of ways in which a scoped PreSB carrier has not yet
closed as an AOR carrier.  Splitting the defect into strata keeps the
failure mode visible, in the spirit of typed fault-and-failure
taxonomies in the dependable-computing literature
\citep{Avizienis2004Dependability}.  A missing observation typing, an
undeclared stage law, an unwitnessed constraint, an unannotated
rewrite, a missing holonomy transport, an unstatused residual, an
unregistered nonclaim, and an undischarged meta-audit obligation are
different audit failures, even when they all obstruct the same
conclusion that the carrier is audit-closed.  Strata are recorded as
finite multisets in the sense of \citet{Blizard1989Multiset}, so a
record may appear with multiplicity matching the carrier-field data
that creates it.

\begin{definition}[Structural defect $\XiSB$]\label{def:aor:xi-sb}
The \emph{structural defect} $\XiSB(\mathsf C)$ of a PreSB carrier
$\mathsf C$ is the disjoint sum of its eight defect strata,
\begin{align*}
  \XiSB(\mathsf C)
  \;=\;& \Sigobs(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigstage(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigconstr(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigrewrite(\mathsf C) \\
  & {} \sqcup \Sighol(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigres(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Signon(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigmeta(\mathsf C),
\end{align*}
with the strata defined in \Cref{def:aor:sigma-obs}--\Cref{def:aor:sigma-meta}.
The carrier is AOR exactly when every stratum is empty.
\end{definition}

conclusion: A missing observation typing, an undeclared stage law, an unwitnessed constraint, an unannotated rewrite, a missing holonomy transport, an unstatused residual, an unregistered nonclaim, and an undischarged meta-audit obligation are different audit failures, even when they all obstruct the same conclusion that the carrier is audit-closed.

conclusion: The field that creates it also determines its stratum: an observation record belongs to Sigma_ obs , a stage entry to Sigma_ stage , a constraint or budget entry to Sigma_ constraint , a rewrite record to Sigma_ rewrite , a holonomy or route memory record to Sigma_ holonomy , a residual record to Sigma_ residual , an implicit exclusion to Sigma_ nonclaim , and a meta-audit obligation to Sigma_ meta .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
Each defect record is created from a typed field of the carrier.  The field
that creates it also determines its stratum: an observation record belongs
to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{obs}}\), a stage entry to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{stage}}\), a constraint or budget entry
to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{constraint}}\), a rewrite record to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{rewrite}}\), a holonomy or route
memory record to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{holonomy}}\), a residual record to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{residual}}\), an implicit
exclusion to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nonclaim}}\), and a meta-audit obligation to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{meta}}\).  These
field tags are disjoint by construction, so the structural defect is the
coproduct of the eight typed collections.  Computability is simply the
fieldwise scan of the carrier: inspect each declared record, test whether
the corresponding required annotation is present, and emit the uniquely
tagged defect record exactly when it is absent.

conclusion: The residual stratum Sigma_ residual tracks unpaid mathematical content rather than missing record syntax. It is refined here along three axes: primary type, atom refinement, and product behavior. We call the resulting classification the thirteen-type atlas. The local and global mismatch residuals are distinct primary types, linked by reciprocal forced-secondary rules; they are not counted as a single type. [Thirteen residual types] The residual stratum Sigma_ residual is partitioned by thirteen disjoint residual types: Delta_ descent (legal-quotient descent failure), Delta_ transport (route map failure), Delta_ interface (bounded-interface failure), Delta_ local (local mismatch), Delta_ global (global mismatch), Delta_ presentation (normalization mismatch), Delta_ source (source-admission failure), Delta_ horizon (carrier-class horizon failure), Delta_ scale (stage-law failure), Delta_ limit (asymptotic failure), Delta_ sym (symmetry/equivariance failure), Delta_ role (role-typing failure), and Delta_ target (response-target failure). Every Sigma_ residual entry has a unique primary type from this list.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The residual stratum \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{residual}}\) tracks unpaid mathematical content
rather than missing record syntax.  It is refined here along three
axes: primary type, atom refinement, and product behavior.  We call
the resulting classification the thirteen-type atlas.  The local and
global mismatch residuals are distinct primary types, linked by
reciprocal forced-secondary rules; they are not counted as a single
type.

\begin{definition}[Thirteen residual types]\label{def:aor:residual-types-twelve}
The residual stratum $\Sigma_{\mathrm{residual}}$ is partitioned by thirteen disjoint
\emph{residual types}: $\Delta_{\mathrm{descent}}$ (legal-quotient descent failure),
$\Delta_{\mathrm{transport}}$ (route map failure), $\Delta_{\mathrm{interface}}$ (bounded-interface
failure), $\Delta_{\mathrm{local}}$ (local mismatch), $\Delta_{\mathrm{global}}$ (global mismatch),
$\Delta_{\mathrm{presentation}}$ (normalization mismatch), $\Delta_{\mathrm{source}}$ (source-admission
failure), $\Delta_{\mathrm{horizon}}$ (carrier-class horizon failure), $\Delta_{\mathrm{scale}}$
(stage-law failure), $\Delta_{\mathrm{limit}}$ (asymptotic failure), $\Delta_{\mathrm{sym}}$
(symmetry/equivariance failure), $\Delta_{\mathrm{role}}$ (role-typing failure), and
$\Delta_{\mathrm{target}}$ (response-target failure).  Every $\Sigma_{\mathrm{residual}}$ entry has a
unique primary type from this list.
\end{definition}

rather than missing record syntax.  It is refined here along three
axes: primary type, atom refinement, and product behavior.  We call
the resulting classification the thirteen-type atlas.  The local and
global mismatch residuals are distinct primary types, linked by

type.

\begin{definition}[Thirteen residual types]\label{def:aor:residual-types-twelve}

\emph{residual types}: $\Ddescent$ (legal-quotient descent failure),
$\Dtransport$ (route map failure), $\Dinterface$ (bounded-interface
failure), $\Dlocal$ (local mismatch), $\Dglobal$ (global mismatch),
$\Dpresentation$ (normalization mismatch), $\Dsource$ (source-admission
failure), $\Dhorizon$ (carrier-class horizon failure), $\Dscale$
(stage-law failure), $\Dlimit$ (asymptotic failure), $\Dsym$
(symmetry/equivariance failure), $\Drole$ (role-typing failure), and
$\Dtarget$ (response-target failure).  Every $\Sigres$ entry has a
unique primary type from this list.
\end{definition}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{lem:aor:cost-table-admissibility}
The base cost table of \Cref{def:aor:cost-table}, together with the
asymptotic companion rows used for refinement-chain discharge, satisfies
two admissibility properties:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Strict descent.}  For every cost-table or asymptotic companion row
  \(\mathrm{Down}(a,s)=w\), the output multiset \(w\) is strictly less
  than the singleton multiset \(\{(a,s)\}\) in the Dershowitz--Manna
  multiset extension \citep{DershowitzManna1979Multiset} of the
  well-founded order on the status coordinate, where base statuses are
  ordered by the rank of \Cref{def:aor:aor-8-statuses}, \texttt{zero} is the unique
  minimum and \texttt{contractive}, \texttt{eventual\_zero},
  \texttt{summable}, and \texttt{asymptotic\_budgeted} ordered above
  \texttt{zero} but below the base non-terminal statuses \texttt{budgeted},
  \texttt{bridged}, \texttt{hidden}, \texttt{moduli}, \texttt{selected},
  \texttt{probabilistic}, \texttt{out\_of\_scope}, \texttt{nonclaim},
  \texttt{blocked}, \texttt{approved\_other}, with
  \texttt{summable}<\texttt{asymptotic\_budgeted} inside the asymptotic
  tier.  Concretely, every output element \((t',s')\in w\) satisfies
  \(s'<s\) in this status order; the primary type coordinate is
  unconstrained.
  \item \emph{Local diamond.}  For every record \(r\) with two distinct
  cost-table moves \(r\to r_1\) and \(r\to r_2\), there exists a common
  cost-table-reachable record \(r_*\) with \(r_1\to^* r_*\) and
  \(r_2\to^* r_*\).
\end{enumerate}

multiset whose elements are all at status \texttt{zero}.  Since

conclusion: The preceding sections develop AOR as a meta-theory of audit-closed carriers. Its formal objects are scope records, PreSB carriers, closure completion, defect strata, residual atoms, discharge cascades, and refinement chains; they are not a direct model of any particular analytic problem. Downstream AOR-instance manuscripts may consume the meta-theory developed here, but they are not theorem-level dependencies of it. [No strong-realism reading of AOR] Membership in AOR_ S is not a metaphysical or philosophical realism claim about the carrier's underlying domain. It is a record-level audit predicate: every declared record is typed, every cited route is audited, every residual is statused, and every nonclaim is registered, within the declared scope S . Any extra-scope interpretation requires its own audit and is outside the present framework.

conclusion: The central result of this paper is a closure theorem for typed audit carriers. Every carrier in PreSB_ S admits a completion into the audit-closed full subcategory through the reflection Cl_ SB . The construction does not merely adjoin missing data; it makes audit closure a structural operation, so that records, routes, residuals, statuses, nonclaims, and meta-audits remain visible as typed fields rather than being collapsed into an external well-formedness assertion. In that setting, the chain AOR^ ref ⊆AOR^ casc ⊆AOR organizes ordinary record-level audit closure, finite cascade closure, and closure stable under refinement limits. The framework comprises four layers. The first is the closure-completion reflection and its universal property. The second is the eight-stratum decomposition of the structural defect Xi_ SB , which turns failure of audit closure into typed diagnostic data. The third is the residual layer: the thirteen-type atlas, with reciprocal local and global mismatch types, together with the status catalogue, cost records, downstream obligations, and cascade graphs tracing how residual atoms are paid. The fourth is the refinement layer, where directed chains and asymptotic statuses distinguish finite discharge from discharge that only closes at a limit. Together they form a self-contained meta-theory of audit-closed carriers.

residual atoms are paid.  The fourth is the refinement
layer, where directed chains and asymptotic statuses distinguish
finite discharge from discharge that only closes at a limit.

\Cref{sec:aor-methods} constructs \(\mathrm{Cl}_{SB}\) by applying a monotone
saturation operation to a scoped PreSB carrier.  The reproducibility
object is the complete lattice of AOR-extending operations over the
fixed scope \(\mathfrak S\).  An element of this lattice is a candidate
audit extension of the seed carrier: it adds typed record data, route
audits, residual statuses, nonclaim entries, and meta-audit discharge
records, but it does not change the declared scope.  The order is
fieldwise extension, so meets and joins are computed by fieldwise
intersection and generated union subject to scope compatibility.

conclusion: Accounting-style inequalities are central in Six Birds Theory, but they do not by themselves rule out catastrophic extremes: highly localized ``needle'' probes can satisfy global budgets while producing large peaks. We ask when packaging plus accounting forces anti-localization, and propose Reflexive SBT: a capacity-based audit of the packaged artifacts (subspaces, feasibility dictionaries, and route ladders). We define a localization metric _j at cell scale 2^ -j , compute it via an eigenvalue method, and upper-bound it using three auditable capacities: subspace trace/diagonal dispersion, sparse feasibility conditioning on small supports, and a route-union ledger charging multi-route inflation. We find three controlled separations: (i) shift-invariant channels (Fourier/circulant) have uniform projector diagonals and _j follows the deterministic m/2^j bound, while diagonal disorder drives _j rapidly toward 1 compared with full-noise perturbations; (ii) feasibility-level needles arise exactly when small-support conditioning collapses ( sigma_ → 0 ) and are absent in random baselines; (iii) for spectral packaging, route mismatch spikes only at degenerate cutoffs and is eliminated by a canonical tie-break, with remaining route effects captured by the union ledger. This turns the anti-localization hinge into a reproducible checklist and yields a conditional theorem: vanishing capacity implies _j→ 0 along a ladder. We are explicit that Reflexive SBT is not proven here to universally drive capacities to zero; we prove the capacity implies anti-localization implications and provide auditable closure evidence on canonical failure and repair modes.

conclusion: What this paper does not claim.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{What this paper does not claim.}
We do \emph{not} prove that Reflexive SBT necessarily drives these capacities to zero for every admissible packaging ladder.
Instead, we give (a) theorem-quality implications of the form \emph{capacity} \(\Rightarrow\) \emph{anti-localization}, (b) counterexamples showing the capacities are not optional, and (c) an auditable Reflexive SBT loop (closure tests and primitive-move analogues) whose trajectories empirically reduce the relevant capacities on canonical obstructions.
Proving capacity decay as a consequence of SBT minimality/closure principles is a natural next-paper target; this paper supplies the clean capacity objects that such a theorem must control.

\label{lem:shift-commute-constant-diag}
Let \(S\) be the cyclic shift on \(\mathbb{C}^N\) defined by \(Se_i=e_{i+1}\) (indices mod \(N\)).
If an orthogonal projector \(P\) satisfies \(PS=SP\), then its diagonal is constant: \(P_{ii}=P_{00}\) for all \(i\).

\label{lem:shift-commute-constant-diag}
Let \(S\) be the cyclic shift on \(\mathbb{C}^N\) defined by \(Se_i=e_{i+1}\) (indices mod \(N\)).
If an orthogonal projector \(P\) satisfies \(PS=SP\), then its diagonal is constant: \(P_{ii}=P_{00}\) for all \(i\).
Consequently, if \(\mathrm{tr}(P)=m\) then \(P_{ii}=m/N\) for all \(i\).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Symmetry breaking is not unique: diagonal disorder behaves differently than full noise.}
A key open-minded finding of the Reflexive SBT scans is that ``breaking symmetry'' can occur in qualitatively different ways.
In the eigenchannel pipeline (extracting packaged channels as eigenvectors of a perturbed operator), diagonal disorder (Anderson-style \cite{anderson1958}) rapidly increases localization at fine scales, while full Wigner-type noise \cite{wigner1958_roots} does not in the same parameter range.
This suggests that diagonal non-uniformity is a more direct driver of trace capacity than generic non-commutation alone.
We emphasize that we do not claim a general theorem of the form ``small symmetry defect \(\Rightarrow\) approximately constant diagonal'' without additional hypotheses; instead we treat diagonal-dispersion bounds as the audit-friendly capacity proxy.

source_wording_digest: Canonical tie-break repairs degeneracy. A Reflexive SBT interpretation is that packaging must include a canonicalization step (P5): when a cutoff eigenspace is degenerate, select a canonical m -dimensional subspace inside the degenerate block. In our experiments, a canonical tie-break that minimizes a symmetry-defect proxy produces a unique, reproducible choice and restores route stability: Scope of canonicalization. Our canonical tie-break is a deterministic rule that operates within an (approximately) degenerate eigenspace using symmetry-defect proxies (e.g.\ diagonal dispersion / shift-commutation surrogates). We do not claim that all packaging families admit such a canonicalizer, nor that canonicalization is unique; we present it as one explicit, auditable choice that removes degeneracy-driven non-uniqueness in the spectral setting.

conclusion: Formal incompleteness explains why no sufficiently expressive effective theory captures all arithmetic truth, but it does not by itself provide a structural language for comparing theory growth. This paper develops such a language by treating a formal theory as a packaged closure object evaluated on a frozen ledger. First, a fixed idempotent package saturates under iteration: repeated closure does not sustain persistent strict growth. Hence genuine growth requires package change. Second, on a frozen slice with fixed yield, cost, and support data, efficiency transfers across cone-equivalent representatives, yielding a restricted alignment theorem. Third, these internal results combine with an explicit external dependency contract to give a conditional arithmetic lift: if the required canonical-family-on-cone assumptions are discharged from the arithmetic literature, then frontier-efficient extension operators admit canonical representatives on the relevant comparison cone. The result reframes incompleteness and axiom choice in package language. G\"odel becomes the canonical fixed-package failure mode, while new axioms appear as controlled package changes evaluated under a frozen regime. Vendor-backed PICA evidence is used only to discipline primitive roles and scope, not as proof support.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Definition (closure package).}
A \emph{closure package} is a pair
\[
\mathrm{pkg}=(X,\operatorname{op})
\]
where $\operatorname{op}\colon X\to X$ is idempotent:
\[
\operatorname{op}(\operatorname{op}(x))=\operatorname{op}(x)\qquad \text{for all }x\in X.
\]
The package is the theorem-track realization of the fixed \(P5\) object. When the package is held fixed, repeated application of $\operatorname{op}$ remains inside the same closure regime.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Definition (package change).}
Given two closure packages
\[
\mathrm{pkg}=(X,\operatorname{op}), \qquad \mathrm{pkg}'=(X,\operatorname{op}'),
\]
a \emph{package change} from $\mathrm{pkg}$ to $\mathrm{pkg}'$ is any replacement for which
\[
\operatorname{op}\neq \operatorname{op}'
\]
as endomaps on $X$. A \emph{package-change witness} is a point $x\in X$ such that
\[
\operatorname{op}(x)\neq \operatorname{op}'(x).
\]
The present paper does not formalize the full internal mechanics of such changes. Instead it records the structural fact that genuine strict growth cannot be attributed to a fixed package once idempotent saturation has been proved. Package change is therefore the theorem-track locus at which \(P1/P2\) enter.

Instead it records the structural fact that genuine strict growth cannot be attributed to a fixed package once idempotent saturation has been proved. Package change is therefore the theorem-track locus at which \(P1/P2\) enter.

conclusion: The proof-carrying core of the manuscript is already visible in Sections – . Those sections define the theorem objects, state the internal theorem ladder, and culminate in the conditional arithmetic lift. The vendor-backed material does not bear theorem-level weight in that route. It supports primitive-role discipline, scope discipline, and the refusal to collapse richer interaction structure into a single proxy, but it does not discharge any theorem in Sections – . For that reason the paper is theorem-led conditional rather than hybrid-led. A hybrid-led presentation would misplace the proof burden by making the empirical material constitutive of the central theorem package. That is not the structure of the manuscript. The theorem package stands on its internal proofs together with the explicit external assumptions in the conditional arithmetic lift.

conclusion: The Zermelo–Fraenkel axioms are usually presented as a flat list, adopted because they work. We show that the list factors, theorem by theorem, through a single staged construction discipline—packaging under a membership lens, audited by rank. We then read, at discussion grade, G\"odel incompleteness and Cohen independence as the saturation and extension faces of that discipline. Over finite well-founded membership presentations, the Mostowski collapse is an idempotent packaging map whose fixed points are canonically bijective with the hereditarily finite sets, and the closure of the empty family under finite packaging is exactly —a model of ZF minus Infinity with each axiom witnessed by a named clause or the rank audit. The four infinitary commitments enter only through an explicit assumption box of priced hypotheses: Infinity as inductive-stage completion, Power set as full subpackage completion, Replacement as unbounded descent transport, and Choice as canonical-lift existence. Separately, rank-erasure is shown to be a lossless flattening of the finite staged hierarchy. Under that box, and named classical imports, the rank-erased shadow satisfies ZF(C) conditionally; countermodels guard each commitment's non-redundancy. The centerpiece discharges an analogy the framework had only named: we characterize the density defects of the finite Cohen poset exactly and show that the finite forcing lemma is precisely their measure. Over an infinite index set these defects vanish, so Cohen genericity is non-definability from the ground lens and the generic extension is a strict theory extension. Read through the imported classical forcing facts, independence is the visible footprint of lawful theory extension, with the continuum hypothesis appearing as lens relativity. Selected finite and structural cores are mechanized in Lean on a \ propext , Quot.sound \ axiom base with the Axiom of Choice absent throughout; the finite lift used to price choice is verified without using choice. We make no consistency claims, claim no new independence results, and treat every infinitary commitment as a named, priced hypothesis. Read structurally, a set-theoretic foundation is an audited ledger: what the chosen membership instrument supplies, what must be purchased, and why the open questions are open.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
We prove that no finitely generated
completion rule, iterated from any hereditarily finite seed, contains an inductive object
(Theorem~\ref{thm:nonattain}). Infinity is therefore not a stronger way of iterating; it is a
\emph{package change}. This is the saturation pattern at the scale of $\mathrm{HF}$; the later
comparison with G\"odel is a meta-grade reading, not an added theorem.

conclusion: We do not claim that ZFC is the unique or most natural promoted set layer—the continuum-hypothesis instance is precisely an argument that it is not.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
We state the perimeter once, here, and again in \S\ref{sec:scope}. We do \emph{not} derive
$\mathsf{ZF}$ or $\mathsf{ZFC}$ from finite principles; the infinitary content enters only
through the priced assumption box. We prove \emph{no} consistency statement, relative or
absolute, beyond what we explicitly import. We claim \emph{no} new independence result; the
forcing section reorganizes classical theorems, it does not reprove or extend them. We do
\emph{not} claim that $\mathsf{ZFC}$ is the unique or most natural promoted set layer---the
continuum-hypothesis instance is precisely an argument that it is not. And the reading of all
this as an answer to ``where does mathematics come from,'' developed in
\S\ref{sec:discussion}, is offered at the grade of discussion, after the theorems, never as
one of them.

conclusion: A theory package is a tuple (Z, f, E, A) consisting of a carrier Z ; a lens f: Z→ X recording what an observer sees of a carrier object (its definability content is the family of predicates constant on the fibers of f ); a completion (or packaging) endomap E: Z→ Z , typically idempotent, whose fixed points are the objects the package recognizes; and an audit A , a monotone certificate.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:presentation}
A \emph{finite pointed membership presentation} is a triple $P=(V,\to,v)$ where $V$ is a
finite set of nodes, ${\to}\subseteq V\times V$ is acyclic, and $v\in V$ is a distinguished
\emph{point}. We read $u\to w$ as ``$w$ is a member-candidate of $u$,'' and write
$\Ch_P(u):=\{w: u\to w\}$. The carrier $Z$ is the set of all finite pointed membership
presentations.

A \emph{finite pointed membership presentation} is a triple $P=(V,\to,v)$ where $V$ is a
finite set of nodes, ${\to}\subseteq V\times V$ is acyclic, and $v\in V$ is a distinguished
\emph{point}. We read $u\to w$ as ``$w$ is a member-candidate of $u$,'' and write
$\Ch_P(u):=\{w: u\to w\}$. The carrier $Z$ is the set of all finite pointed membership
presentations.

membership structures of \citet{Aczel1988}; here, on well-founded graphs, it is the assignment
collapsed by the Mostowski lemma.}

Lemma~\ref{lem:L2} says precisely that the extensional identification is a \emph{genuine
quotient of presentation volume}: node names, the multiplicity of a presentation route, and
graph shape above a fixed profile are \emph{hidden volume} for this instrument. Two
presentations of $\{\varnothing\}$, one with a duplicated childless node, have the same
profile and are identified. Extensionality, on this reading, is not forced by anything; it is
the decision to look only through $f$. We return to this in the countermodel atlas
(\S\ref{sec:atlas}, \gradetag{guard}) and prove there that a different instrument may lawfully
distinguish what $f$ blurs.

\label{thm:p5}
The packaging map $E\colon Z\to Z$ of Definition~\ref{def:E} is idempotent, and
\[
  \operatorname{Fix}(E)\;=\;\operatorname{im}(E)\;=\;\{C(a): a\in\mathrm{HF}\}.
\]
The restricted lens $f\!\upharpoonright\!\operatorname{Fix}(E)\colon \operatorname{Fix}(E)\to\mathrm{HF}$ is a bijection, with inverse
$a\mapsto C(a)$. Writing $i\colon\operatorname{Fix}(E)\hookrightarrow Z$ for the inclusion and
$r\colon Z\to\operatorname{Fix}(E)$, $r(P):=E(P)$, one has
\[
  r\circ i=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Fix}(E)},\qquad i\circ r=E,
\]
so $\operatorname{Fix}(E)$ canonically realizes the lens quotient $Z/{\sim}$, with $E$ the packaging map and
$C(\cdot)$ the selected representative.

conclusion: Theorem is not merely analogous to how set theory is formally built; it is that construction. The standard mechanized development of the set-theoretic universe [] Mathlib2020 defines a set as an equivalence class of pre-sets—finitely or transfinitely branching membership trees—under extensional equivalence, i.e.\ as the quotient of presentations by the lens relation . The fixed-point/representative picture of Theorem is the finite instance of that quotient. What is standardly built as ``the universe of sets'' is thus the packaging quotient of the membership instrument.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{rem:mathlib}
Theorem~\ref{thm:p5} is not merely analogous to how set theory is formally built; it is that
construction. The standard mechanized development of the set-theoretic universe
\citep[e.g.\ the \texttt{PSet}/\texttt{ZFSet} construction of][]{Mathlib2020} defines a set
as an equivalence class of \emph{pre-sets}---finitely or transfinitely branching membership
trees---under extensional equivalence, i.e.\ as the quotient of presentations by the lens
relation $\sim$. The fixed-point/representative picture of Theorem~\ref{thm:p5} is the finite
instance of that quotient. What is standardly built as ``the universe of sets'' is thus the
packaging quotient of the membership instrument.

\label{def:F}
For $A\subseteq\mathrm{HF}$ let
\[
  \begin{aligned}
  F(A):={}&\{\varnothing\}\cup A

  &\cup\;\underbrace{\{h[a]:a\in A,\ h\colon a\to A\}}_{\text{transport (P1)}},
  \end{aligned}
\]

$h$ is admissible: at a finite carrier the constraint and transport roles carry no definability
restriction. (The definable-gate refinement is exactly what reappears, and matters, at the
forcing tier, \S\ref{sec:forcing}.)

\label{lem:closure}
$\mathrm{HF}$ is $F$-closed, so for each $A\subseteq\mathrm{HF}$ the least $F$-closed superset
$\operatorname{cl}_F(A)=\bigcap\{B\supseteq A: F(B)\subseteq B\}$ exists, and $\operatorname{cl}_F$ is a closure operator in
the order-theoretic sense---extensive, monotone, and idempotent
\citep{DaveyPriestley2002,Tarski1955}. No choice principle is used: the operations build finite
sets, and the intersection is over a family of subsets of the countable lattice $\mathcal{P}(\mathrm{HF})$.

conclusion: the first place the construction must be told to continue—it is a change of rule, not a stronger use of the old one. This is the saturation reading of S realized at the scale of HF ; the comparison with incompleteness remains meta-grade framing
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Theorem~\ref{thm:hfsat} left exactly one $\mathsf{ZF}$ axiom out of the free column: Infinity. We
now show this is not an accident of bookkeeping but a theorem. The boundary of the free part is
sharp from the inside: \emph{no} fixed finite packaging rule, however many times it is iterated
from a hereditarily finite seed, reaches an infinite set. Infinity is therefore the first place
the construction must be \emph{told to continue}---it is a change of rule, not a stronger use of
the old one. This is the saturation reading of \S\ref{sec:intro} realized at the scale of
$\mathrm{HF}$; the comparison with incompleteness remains meta-grade framing.

conclusion: Corollary is one instance of a general anti-laddering discipline: a fixed completion under a bounded generation budget cannot produce unbounded object growth by self-iteration. Read against incompleteness, the resonance is deliberate. G\"odel's theorems say a fixed, sufficiently expressive deductive apparatus does not exhaust arithmetic truth and cannot, by iterating its own moves, reach its own consistency. Theorem says a fixed finite packaging apparatus does not reach the infinite and cannot, by iterating, get there; omega lies outside and must be adjoined. Same shape: a closed apparatus, run to saturation, with the novelty placed deliberately out of reach. The other half of the shape—what adjoining actually does—is the subject of S . We flag this as structural framing, not a metatheorem ( meta ); each half is a theorem, the kinship between them is a reading.

conclusion: Theorem licenses the one-sorted bookkeeping of the rest of the paper: when we speak of the membership shadow ``satisfying ZF ,'' no staging content has been silently dropped. It also explains why ZFC can afford to be flat: the staging is not external scaffolding but internally recoverable data—the one-sorted derivation of the axioms from the stage picture is the classical complement of this recovery . The infinitary analogue, the definability of the von Neumann rank in ZF , is standard . The losslessness is special to the canonical, rank labeling and is not a claim about arbitrary stage maps. A uniform first-order recovery exists for rank; it cannot exist for every labeling, by cardinality—there are only countably many formulas (even with finitely many parameters), but uncountably many maps HF→Ord_ fin . So some staging would be genuinely lost under erasure; the point is that the set-theoretic staging is exactly the one that is not.

conclusion: (Finite tier, A_FIN.) Every surjection f: Z→ X between finite sets admits a section, constructed without any choice principle (the least-index preimage); a section of f is the same datum as a prototype family for the lens. (Metatheory.) Over ZF , the following are equivalent: (1) the Axiom of Choice; (2) every surjection of sets admits a section; (3) every fibered lens admits a canonical-lift prototype family; (4) every product of nonempty sets is nonempty.

conclusion: Theorem is the positive form of one of our non-claims. We do not claim ZFC is the unique or canonical promoted set layer; the continuum hypothesis is precisely a place where two completions of the same substrate disagree, and Cohen's mechanism (S ) supplies the disagreement on the generic side. The pluralist reading of such disagreements as distinct, equally legitimate universes is the set-theoretic multiverse of ; the opposing universe view (e.g.\ ) holds that one of them is correct. We construct no model, reprove no independence result, and adjudicate nothing between the completions: which packaging, if any, is ``correct'' is not a question this paper takes a position on. Independence is, on this reading, the expected signature of a foundation that grows by lawful extension—the footprint, at the scale of set theory, of the extension law.

conclusion: What we do not claim. We do not claim ZFC is the unique or most natural promoted set layer.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{What we do \emph{not} claim.}
\begin{enumerate}\itemsep0pt
  \item We do not derive $\mathsf{ZF}$ or $\mathsf{ZFC}$ from finite principles. The infinitary
  content enters only through the priced assumption box; the four commitments are named
  hypotheses, never conclusions.
  \item We prove no consistency statement, relative or absolute, beyond the classical results we
  explicitly import. Nothing here bears on the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.
  \item We claim no new independence result. The forcing section reorganizes classical theorems
  into the framework's vocabulary; it reproves and extends nothing. No model is constructed.
  \item We do not claim $\mathsf{ZFC}$ is the unique or most natural promoted set layer. The
  continuum-hypothesis instance (\S\ref{sec:ch}) is an argument to the contrary, and structural or
  alternative set theories remain available.
  \item We make no metaphysical claim about the existence of a set-theoretic universe. ``Set'' is
  used as a package; ``$\in$'' as a lens; the readings are structural.
  \item The interpretation of all this as an account of where mathematics comes from
  (\S\ref{sec:discussion}) is offered at the grade of discussion (\gradetag{meta}), after the theorems, and
  is never used as a premise for any of them.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: A foundation that grows by lawful extension must have undecided questions: they are the predicates not yet definable from the current lens, the places where extension is still available. The continuum hypothesis is the canonical such place (S ): the same substrate admits an inner-model packaging where it holds and a generic-extension packaging where it fails, and the ground lens does not adjudicate. Independence is the footprint of the extension law—the formal signature of a foundation that is still, lawfully, being written. A foundation with no independent questions would be one that had saturated completely, and by the saturation law no sufficiently expressive one ever does.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{description}[style=multiline,leftmargin=!,labelwidth=0.31\textwidth,labelsep=0.8em,itemsep=3pt]
\item[Theory package.] A carrier, lens, packaging endomap, and audit
$(Z,f,E,\mathcal A)$; see Convention~\ref{conv:package}. In this paper the package is used only
as an organizing instrument for set-theoretic constructions.
\item[Finite membership presentation.] A finite pointed acyclic graph
$(V,\to,v)$ read as a membership presentation; see Definition~\ref{def:presentation}.
\item[Membership-profile lens.] The map $f\colon Z\to\mathrm{HF}$ sending a presentation to the
decoration of its point; see Definition~\ref{def:lens}. Its definability content is what the
instrument can see.
\item[Packaging map.] The endomap $E(P)=C(f(P))$ that forgets accidental presentation shape and
reinstantiates the profile canonically; see Definition~\ref{def:E}.
\item[Rank audit.] The certificate $\rho(P)=\operatorname{rank}(f(P))$, decreasing along membership edges; see
Definition~\ref{def:rank} and Lemma~\ref{lem:L3}.
\item[Finite packaging operator.] The operator $F$ on subfamilies of $\mathrm{HF}$ generated by empty
set, pairing, flattening, finite gates, and finite transport; see Definition~\ref{def:F}.
\item[Finitely generated completion rule.] A completion rule that adds only finite sets whose
members are drawn from the current family and the transitive closures of its members; see
Definition~\ref{def:fg}.
\item[Rank-erased shadow.] The one-sorted membership structure obtained from the staged
two-sorted presentation by forgetting the explicit stage sort; see Definition~\ref{def:staged}.
\item[Assumption box.] The four named infinitary commitments
\textbf{C-INF}, \textbf{C-POW}, \textbf{C-REPL}, and \textbf{C-SEL}; see
\S\ref{ssec:box}. They are hypotheses, not conclusions.
\item[Strict theory extension.] A package change whose new object map does not factor through the
old ground object; in this paper it is instantiated by Theorem~\ref{thm:nonfactor}.
\item[Ground lens.] The countable ground model read through its coded reals
$\Sig_M=2^\omega\cap M$; see Definition~\ref{def:groundlens}.
\end{description}

\begin{description}[style=multiline,leftmargin=!,labelwidth=0.31\textwidth,labelsep=0.8em,itemsep=3pt]
\item[Theory package.] A carrier, lens, packaging endomap, and audit
$(Z,f,E,\mathcal A)$; see Convention~\ref{conv:package}. In this paper the package is used only
as an organizing instrument for set-theoretic constructions.
\item[Finite membership presentation.] A finite pointed acyclic graph
$(V,\to,v)$ read as a membership presentation; see Definition~\ref{def:presentation}.
\item[Membership-profile lens.] The map $f\colon Z\to\HF$ sending a presentation to the
decoration of its point; see Definition~\ref{def:lens}. Its definability content is what the
instrument can see.
\item[Packaging map.] The endomap $E(P)=C(f(P))$ that forgets accidental presentation shape and
reinstantiates the profile canonically; see Definition~\ref{def:E}.
\item[Rank audit.] The certificate $\rho(P)=\rank(f(P))$, decreasing along membership edges; see
Definition~\ref{def:rank} and Lemma~\ref{lem:L3}.
\item[Finite packaging operator.] The operator $F$ on subfamilies of $\HF$ generated by empty
set, pairing, flattening, finite gates, and finite transport; see Definition~\ref{def:F}.
\item[Finitely generated completion rule.] A completion rule that adds only finite sets whose
members are drawn from the current family and the transitive closures of its members; see
Definition~\ref{def:fg}.
\item[Rank-erased shadow.] The one-sorted membership structure obtained from the staged
two-sorted presentation by forgetting the explicit stage sort; see Definition~\ref{def:staged}.
\item[Assumption box.] The four named infinitary commitments
\textbf{C-INF}, \textbf{C-POW}, \textbf{C-REPL}, and \textbf{C-SEL}; see
\S\ref{ssec:box}. They are hypotheses, not conclusions.
\item[Strict theory extension.] A package change whose new object map does not factor through the
old ground object; in this paper it is instantiated by Theorem~\ref{thm:nonfactor}.
\item[Ground lens.] The countable ground model read through its coded reals
$\Sig_M=2^\omega\cap M$; see Definition~\ref{def:groundlens}.
\end{description}

conclusion: Many ``higher'' mathematical objects are introduced as definitions (limits, completions, analytic continuations), but it is often unclear when a large discrete protocol admits a stable continuous closure and how to test that stability without overclaiming. This question matters because premature or untested closure claims can propagate errors through dependent results. We instantiate the Six-Birds Theory ( ) framework of —which provides a general audit methodology for validating compressions of discrete data into continuous or idealized objects—as a closure-and-audit method for mathematics: a discrete substrate is staged by refinement, compressions are assessed by an explicit defect ledger, and a packaged object is accepted only when defects shrink or stabilize under refinement. Operationally, we (i) formalize two anchor statements in Lean/mathlib —the exact finite-difference Leibniz identity with its explicit remainder term and an algebraic uniqueness anchor for derivations on R[X] —and (ii) implement falsification-first Python diagnostics that compare competing closure routes under matched controls and an artifact contract (tables and macros are generated from snapshot-visible pointer JSONs). Across four exhibits we observe controlled, checkable separations. First, stability-only stencil filtering selects order- 0 closures, while adding a Leibniz-defect gate selects derivative-like order- 1 closures. Second, route mismatch (RM, measuring disagreement between closure paths) under a small coordinate change decays with refinement (power-law fit exponent p 1.46 ). Third, for prime-based closures in a convergence control regime (s)>1 , route mismatch RM_2 decreases with sample size N (e.g.\ RM_2(800) 5 10^ -2 ), whereas the same diagnostic in the critical strip exhibits mismatch growth by many orders of magnitude under naive staging (e.g.\ RM_2(800) 5 10^ 12 ). Fourth, in a self-dual toy family, tightening a positivity constraint sharply confines zeros to the symmetry locus (mean radial deviation drops from 0.87 to 3 10^ -4 ). These results provide a reproducible methodology to separate feasible closures from protocol artifacts and to compare closure proposals across regimes. We emphasize that this paper does not establish new theorems about or zero distributions; we report audit-style diagnostics under explicit controls and document the upgrade points required for stronger claims.

\label{rem:six-primitives}
Fix a space $\mathcal P$ of protocol objects (discrete descriptions) equipped with a refinement chain, modeled as a family of equivalences $\sim_j$ indexed by a stage parameter $j$ (or, in analysis notation, by a step size $h\downarrow 0$).
Write $\Pi_j:\mathcal P\to \mathcal P/\!\sim_j$ for the quotient/packaging map.
Then the six primitives may be read as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{P5}\ (Packaging). Each equivalence $\sim_j$ yields a quotient/packaging map $\Pi_j$ and induces an idempotent saturation on predicates/events via
  \[
    \mathrm{cl}_j(A)\;:=\;\Pi_j^{-1}(\Pi_j(A)).
  \]
  This is a standard closure-operator construction in order/lattice settings; see e.g.\ \cite{DaveyPriestley2002}.
  In analytic instantiations, $\Pi_j$ is a limit/identification map (``equal up to $o(1)$ as $h\to 0$''); in algebraic instantiations it is a literal quotient by a congruence.

  \item \textbf{P6}\ (Accounting). The refinement order on quotients induces a preorder and monotone defect/audit quantities (e.g.\ $j\mapsto \mathrm{Def}(j)$ or $h\mapsto \mathrm{Err}(h)$).
  In this mathematics instantiation, ``accounting'' is a feasibility ledger (error control), not a directionality certificate.

  \item \textbf{P4}\ (Staging). The refinement chain generates the stage index $j$ (or $h$).
  Nontrivial staging corresponds to strict refinement at some scale (a genuine increase in resolution rather than a reparameterization).

  \item \textbf{P2}\ (Constraints). Feasible macrostates at depth $j$ are those representable as images under $\Pi_j$.
  Concretely, this is where invariances (translation/rotation/scale), locality, linearity, and algebra-compatibility are imposed as coherence conditions on the packaged layer.

  \item \textbf{P1}\ (Operator rewrite). Fix a micro-update or micro-operator $F:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P$.
  The induced macro-update $F^\sharp([p]) := [F(p)]$ on $\mathcal P/\!\sim_j$ is well-defined iff
  \[
    p\sim_j q \ \Rightarrow\ F(p)\sim_j F(q).
  \]
  When this fails, one must either refine the lens (change $\sim_j$), modify/extend $F$ (renormalize / rescale / rewrite it), or accept that no closed macro dynamics exists at depth $j$.

  \item \textbf{P3}\ (Protocol / holonomy). When there exist two admissible closure/evolution routes with the same input/output type (e.g.\ ``refine then apply'' versus ``apply then refine''), their discrepancy defines a holonomy-like diagnostic.
  In normed instantiations we measure this by a route-mismatch quantity $\mathrm{RM}$: a number that should decay under refinement in stable regimes.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: The framework packages an instantiation as a theory package: a carrier (micro) space, a lens of observation, a completion/packaging rule, and an audit/defect principle . For the mathematics instantiation we use the same shape, with ``audit'' interpreted as a nonnegative defect ledger (error and mismatch diagnostics). [Mathematics theory package] A mathematics theory package is a tuple T = (Z,\ f,\ Sigma_f,\ E,\ D) where: Z is a carrier of discrete protocol objects at a chosen stage (e.g.\ grid functions, truncated sums/products, finite compositions, Cauchy sequences of rationals). f:Z→ X is a lens (a coarse description map). The induced definability structure Sigma_f is the family of predicates on Z that are visible through f (equivalently: constant on fibers of f ). E: V→ V is a completion/packaging endomap on a chosen description space V associated to Z (often idempotent or approximately idempotent in a specified norm). The fixed points of E are the internally complete objects recognized by the theory at the chosen scale. D is a defect ledger: a designated family of nonnegative diagnostics (error bounds, residual norms, route mismatch statistics) together with a monotonicity principle under refinement/coarsening. In this mathematics instantiation, D records feasibility (stability under refinement), not a thermodynamic arrow-of-time.

A \emph{mathematics theory package} is a tuple
\[
\mathcal T \;=\; (Z,\ f,\ \Sigma_f,\ E,\ \mathcal D)
\]

\begin{itemize}
  \item $Z$ is a carrier of discrete protocol objects at a chosen stage (e.g.\ grid functions, truncated sums/products, finite compositions, Cauchy sequences of rationals).

  \item $E:\mathcal V\to\mathcal V$ is a \emph{completion/packaging endomap} on a chosen description space $\mathcal V$ associated to $Z$ (often idempotent or approximately idempotent in a specified norm). The fixed points of $E$ are the internally complete objects recognized by the theory at the chosen scale.
  \item $\mathcal D$ is a \emph{defect ledger}: a designated family of nonnegative diagnostics (error bounds, residual norms, route mismatch statistics) together with a monotonicity principle under refinement/coarsening. In this mathematics instantiation, $\mathcal D$ records feasibility (stability under refinement), not a thermodynamic arrow-of-time.
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

\label{def:math-theory-package}
A \emph{mathematics theory package} is a tuple
\[
\mathcal T \;=\; (Z,\ f,\ \Sigma_f,\ E,\ \mathcal D)
\]
where:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $Z$ is a carrier of discrete protocol objects at a chosen stage (e.g.\ grid functions, truncated sums/products, finite compositions, Cauchy sequences of rationals).
  \item $f:Z\to X$ is a \emph{lens} (a coarse description map). The induced definability structure $\Sigma_f$ is the family of predicates on $Z$ that are visible through $f$ (equivalently: constant on fibers of $f$).
  \item $E:\mathcal V\to\mathcal V$ is a \emph{completion/packaging endomap} on a chosen description space $\mathcal V$ associated to $Z$ (often idempotent or approximately idempotent in a specified norm). The fixed points of $E$ are the internally complete objects recognized by the theory at the chosen scale.
  \item $\mathcal D$ is a \emph{defect ledger}: a designated family of nonnegative diagnostics (error bounds, residual norms, route mismatch statistics) together with a monotonicity principle under refinement/coarsening. In this mathematics instantiation, $\mathcal D$ records feasibility (stability under refinement), not a thermodynamic arrow-of-time.
\end{itemize}

\label{lem:finite-diff-leibniz}
Let $F$ be a field, let $h\in F$ with $h\neq 0$, and let $f,g:F\to F$.
Define $\delta_h f(x):=(f(x+h)-f(x))/h$.
Then for all $x\in F$,

\delta_h(fg)(x)
\;=\;
\delta_h f(x)\, g(x)
\;+
\;f(x)\, \delta_h g(x)
\;+

\]

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:derivation-determined-by-X}
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring and let $A:=R[X]$ be the polynomial ring.
An $R$-derivation $D:\mathrm{Derivation}(R,A,A)$ is uniquely determined by its value on the indeterminate $X\in A$.
Equivalently, evaluation on $X$ induces an $R$-linear equivalence
\[
\mathrm{Derivation}(R,R[X],R[X]) \;\simeq_{\ell[R]}\; R[X],
\qquad
D \longmapsto D(X),
\]
with inverse given (schematically) by ``multiply the formal derivative by a polynomial''.

conclusion: We present a reproducible computational framework—with Lean 4 mechanized proofs and deterministic Python simulations—that treats multi-scale model reduction as a closure-audit calculus: each ``physics theory'' is a packaging operator built from a lens (retained macro information), a completion (canonical reconstruction), and diagnostics that certify when the reduced description is self-consistent. We instantiate the Six-Birds lens/completion/closure dictionary as a multi-scale layer template, centering three cross-domain certificates: closure coherence (idempotence), audit monotonicity (data-processing inequality), and route mismatch (noncommutation of coarse-graining with dynamics). We operationalize this calculus via a reproducible workflow (Python artifacts + Lean-certified lemmas) and demonstrate it on four instantiations: quantum dephasing, discrete BGK-like kinetic closure, filtered Burgers (LES), and nonlinear averaging (backreaction). Under null conditions (no coarse-graining, zero heterogeneity, or exact projections), idempotence defects and route mismatches are 0 ; under controlled interventions they separate cleanly. Dephasing is exactly idempotent; sampled CPTP channels satisfy quantum relative-entropy DPI with no violations beyond tolerance; unitary evolution produces nonzero mismatch that grows with dephasing strength. In the BGK model, packaging coherence improves as collision strength increases, with explicit failure modes when the equilibrium family or retained moments are misspecified. In LES and averaging models, mismatch grows with filter width or heterogeneity and yields canonical subgrid/backreaction correction terms. This reframes ``physics theories'' as comparable closure layers and localizes which effective terms are forced by a chosen scale and audit. We do not derive continuum theories or prove analytic bounds; we report Lean-certified algebraic facts and numerical certificates under stated controls.

Under null conditions (no coarse-graining, zero heterogeneity, or exact projections), idempotence defects and route mismatches are 0 ; under controlled interventions they separate cleanly. Dephasing is exactly idempotent; sampled CPTP channels satisfy quantum relative-entropy DPI with no violations beyond tolerance; unitary evolution produces nonzero mismatch that grows with dephasing strength. In the BGK model, packaging coherence improves as collision strength increases, with explicit failure modes when the equilibrium family or retained moments are misspecified. In LES and averaging models, mismatch grows with filter width or heterogeneity and yields canonical subgrid/backreaction correction terms. This reframes ``physics theories'' as comparable closure layers and localizes which effective terms are forced by a chosen scale and audit. We do not derive continuum theories or prove analytic bounds; we report Lean-certified algebraic facts and numerical certificates under stated controls.

conclusion: Quantum relative entropy S(rho\|sigma) is the canonical audit for distinguishability of quantum states. A foundational monotonicity principle states that for any CPTP map Phi , S(rho\|sigma) S(Phi(rho)\|Phi(sigma)). This is the quantum data processing inequality (DPI): applying a channel cannot increase distinguishability. We cite standard sources for DPI and its variants . We stress that DPI itself is a standard theorem; our numerical suite is a regression test for the correctness and numerical stability of our implementations of quantum relative entropy and channel application (Appendix records the default trial counts and tolerances). The repository includes a numerical audit suite that samples random density matrices and random CPTP channels (mixtures of dephasing, depolarizing, and random Kraus families), and records the differences S(rho\|sigma) - S(Phi(rho)\|Phi(sigma)). Figure shows the distribution of these differences across random trials, and Table summarizes the experiment across dimensions.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Quantum relative entropy
\[
  S(\rho\|\sigma)
\]
is the canonical audit for distinguishability of quantum states. A foundational monotonicity principle states that for any CPTP map $\Phi$,
\[
  S(\rho\|\sigma) \ge S(\Phi(\rho)\|\Phi(\sigma)).
\]
This is the quantum data processing inequality (DPI): applying a channel cannot increase distinguishability.
We cite standard sources for DPI and its variants \citep{lindblad1975,petz1986,wilde2017}.
We stress that DPI itself is a standard theorem; our numerical suite is a regression test for the correctness and numerical stability of our implementations of quantum relative entropy and channel application (Appendix~\ref{app:sims} records the default trial counts and tolerances).

The repository includes a numerical audit suite that samples random density matrices and random CPTP channels (mixtures of dephasing, depolarizing, and random Kraus families), and records the differences
\[
  S(\rho\|\sigma) - S(\Phi(\rho)\|\Phi(\sigma)).
\]
Figure~\ref{fig:quantum-dpi-hist} shows the distribution of these differences across random trials, and Table~\ref{tab:quantum-dpi-summary} summarizes the experiment across dimensions.

conclusion: Many of the objects mathematics uses to solve problems do not live in the layer where the problem is posed. Imaginary numbers are not real, infinitesimals are not real scalars, roots of irreducible polynomials need not lie in the base field, and cohomology classes are not vertex potentials. We study this pattern by separating a lower layer, where a problem and its accepted answers are stated, from a promoted layer, where additional objects may be available. We define theory layers, promotion bridges, audited descending expressions, and the Strict Audited Utility (SAU) certificate, and we show that the certificate is extracted from strict useful traces rather than stipulated. The main results are an essential boundary necessity theorem, which forces hidden non-descent together with an audited lower-layer boundary expression; a boundary normal form; a partial converse closing the circle from trace to validated certificate to accepted lower-layer answer; a soundness theorem specifying what an accepted certificate licenses; a classification of primitive boundary heads; four canonical witnesses—imaginary numbers, dual numbers, Galois roots, and graph cohomology—each instantiating a distinct minimal or universal profile; and a transfer theorem showing that a validated profile is portable under matching audit hypotheses while not identifying objects across domains. Together these results show that, in finite typed audited promoted-use traces, strict mathematical usefulness forces hidden non-descent paired with audited boundary descent. The scope is intentionally narrow. The paper concerns strict useful promoted-use traces, not mathematical practice in general; it does not assert that every promoted extension is useful, that hidden promoted objects are lower-layer content, or novelty for the classical constructions themselves. A companion Lean development supplies substantive proofs for selected direct, computational, and definitional fragments and records the remaining theorems as proof-carrying traceability records.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The main claim is that, in finite typed audited promoted-use traces, strict
mathematical usefulness---what we call \emph{Strict Audited Utility} (SAU),
formally defined in \Cref{sec:layers}---forces hidden non-descent paired with
audited boundary descent.  An \emph{audit} here is an explicit checkable
derivation connecting a promoted-layer computation back to a lower-layer
answer; a \emph{boundary} is the single derivation step at which descent
takes place.  We extract this pairing from strict useful traces rather than
posit it.

\Cref{sec:necessity} develops the necessity side.  An essential boundary
necessity theorem shows that any strict useful trace forces a non-descending
support and an audited descent expression at its boundary.  A boundary normal
form theorem shows that the boundary expression has a canonical reduced
shape: one primitive head and a defined support set.  A partial converse then
closes the loop, taking the extracted package back to a validated SAU
certificate and to an accepted lower-layer claim.  Read together, these
results show that SAU is the normal form of strict audited promoted use, not
a name chosen to make the central theorem true.

\label{def:sau-promoted-use-trace}
A finite promoted-use trace for a lower problem profile \(\mathfrak P_0\) is a tuple
\[
\mathfrak T=(D,V,E,r,o,\lambda,\upsilon,\mathcal B,A_{\mathfrak T},\mathcal N,v_\ast),
\]
where:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(D=(V,E)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph.  An edge \(u\to v\) means that the node \(v\) depends on the node \(u\).
\item \(r\) records the rule, operation, bridge, or audit step used at each non-input node.
\item \(o(v)\) is the mathematical object, assertion, certificate, or intermediate expression carried by \(v\).
\item \(\lambda(v)\in\{0,1\}\) is the declared layer label: \(0\) for lower-layer nodes and \(1\) for promoted-layer nodes.
\item \(\upsilon(v)\in\{\texttt{visible},\texttt{suppressed},\texttt{outside},\texttt{unknown}\}\) is the visibility status under the declared instrument.
\item \(\mathcal B\) is the finite family of declared bridge or descent steps used by the trace.
\item \(A_{\mathfrak T}\) is the finite audit/provenance/replay record for the trace.
\item \(\mathcal N\) is the nonclaim register.
\item \(v_\ast\in V\) is the final answer node, whose object is denoted
\[
a^\sharp_{\mathfrak T}:=o(v_\ast).
\]
\end{enumerate}
The trace is typed: every edge and every rule application must respect the source and target layers recorded by \(\lambda\), the visibility status recorded by \(\upsilon\), and the bridge permissions recorded by \(\mathcal B\).

source_wording_tex:
\label{def:sau-promoted-use-trace}
A finite promoted-use trace for a lower problem profile \(\mathfrak P_0\) is a tuple
\[
\mathfrak T=(D,V,E,r,o,\lambda,\upsilon,\mathcal B,A_{\mathfrak T},\mathcal N,v_\ast),
\]
where:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(D=(V,E)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph.  An edge \(u\to v\) means that the node \(v\) depends on the node \(u\).
\item \(r\) records the rule, operation, bridge, or audit step used at each non-input node.
\item \(o(v)\) is the mathematical object, assertion, certificate, or intermediate expression carried by \(v\).
\item \(\lambda(v)\in\{0,1\}\) is the declared layer label: \(0\) for lower-layer nodes and \(1\) for promoted-layer nodes.
\item \(\upsilon(v)\in\{\texttt{visible},\texttt{suppressed},\texttt{outside},\texttt{unknown}\}\) is the visibility status under the declared instrument.
\item \(\mathcal B\) is the finite family of declared bridge or descent steps used by the trace.
\item \(A_{\mathfrak T}\) is the finite audit/provenance/replay record for the trace.
\item \(\mathcal N\) is the nonclaim register.
\item \(v_\ast\in V\) is the final answer node, whose object is denoted
\[
a^\sharp_{\mathfrak T}:=o(v_\ast).
\]
\end{enumerate}
The trace is typed: every edge and every rule application must respect the source and target layers recorded by \(\lambda\), the visibility status recorded by \(\upsilon\), and the bridge permissions recorded by \(\mathcal B\).

The ancestor cone of a node v is Anc(v)=\ u∈ V:u v by a directed path, including possibly u=v\ . The essential hidden cone of the final answer is Hid_ ( T)=Hid_1( T) Anc(v_ ).

\label{def:sau-trace-visible-hidden}
Let \(\mathfrak T\) be a finite promoted-use trace.  A node \(v\in V\) is
lower-visible when either \(\lambda(v)=0\), or \(v\) is the target of an
audited bridge in \(\mathcal B\) whose output is accepted by the lower
instrument.  Write
\[
\Vis_0(\mathfrak T)=\{v\in V:v\text{ is lower-visible}\}.
\]
A node is hidden promoted support when it is promoted-layer content not
accepted as lower-visible:
\[
\Hid_1(\mathfrak T)=\{v\in V:\lambda(v)=1\text{ and }v\notin \Vis_0(\mathfrak T)\}.
\]
The ancestor cone of a node \(v\) is
\[
\operatorname{Anc}(v)=\{u\in V:u\leadsto v\text{ by a directed path, including possibly }u=v\}.
\]
The essential hidden cone of the final answer is
\[
\Hid_\ast(\mathfrak T)=\Hid_1(\mathfrak T)\cap \operatorname{Anc}(v_\ast).
\]

\label{def:sau-strict-essential-trace}
An accepted trace \(\mathfrak T\) is strict, written
\[
\operatorname{StrictTrace}(\mathfrak T),
\]
when its promoted interface separates content collapsed by its lower interface.
Concretely, there exist comparison states or trace presentations \(s,s'\) such
that
\[
\pi_0(s)=\pi_0(s')
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\pi_1(s)\neq \pi_1(s'),
\]
or equivalently
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing.
\]
It is essentially promoted, written
\[
\operatorname{EssProm}(\mathfrak T),
\]
when the final accepted answer depends on hidden promoted support in a way that
cannot be removed or replaced by lower-visible data while preserving the same
lower interface, the same final answer, the same admissible lower rules, and
the same audit status.  Equivalently for the finite trace calculus used here,
there exists
\[
h\in \Hid_\ast(\mathfrak T)
\]
such that every audit-preserving deletion or lower-visible replacement of the
dependency of \(v_\ast\) on \(h\) either changes the final answer, invalidates a
rule application, changes the lower interface, or fails the declared audit.

\label{thm:sau-essential-boundary-necessity}

\[
H\not\downarrow_{\mathcal T_0},
\qquad
C_H(H)\downarrow_B b^\sharp.
\]
Moreover, \(b^\sharp\) lies in the lower dependency cone of the final answer; hence there is a lower-visible audited continuation from \(b^\sharp\) to the final answer \(a^\sharp_{\mathfrak T}\).

\begin{definition}[SAU boundary normal form]
\label{def:sau-boundary-normal-form}
An accepted trace is in SAU boundary normal form when, after deleting irrelevant nodes outside the dependency cone of the final answer, it has the schematic shape
\[
\mathcal T_0
\xleftarrow{\ q\ }
\mathcal T_1,
\qquad
\left[U\not\downarrow_q,
\quad
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp\right],
\]
possibly followed by a lower-visible verifier from \(a^\sharp\) to the final accepted answer.  In a multi-generator case this becomes
\[
\left[\vec U\not\downarrow_q,
\quad
\vec C(\vec U)\downarrow_B \vec a^\sharp\right].
\]
Write
\[
\NF_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak T)
\]
for the boundary normal form obtained by contracting hidden promoted support and retaining the first audited lower-visible boundary.
\end{definition}

\label{thm:sau-soundness}
Let \(\mathfrak C\) be a validated raw SAU proof package for
\((\mathfrak P_0,B_{0\to1},U,C,a^\sharp)\).  Then the following instrument-indexed claim is accepted:
\[
\Gamma;\mathcal T_0\leadsto\mathcal T_1;I_B
\vdash
\operatorname{Useful}(B_{0\to1},P):\texttt{accepted}.
\]
More explicitly, the accepted claim has the following content:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Lower-layer saturation.} No candidate at the fixed lower interface solves the problem:
\[
\forall s\in\mathsf{Cand}_0(P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(s))\neq\texttt{pass}.
\]
\item \textbf{Promoted answer.} The promoted calculation supplies a lower-layer accepted answer:
\[
a^\sharp\in\mathsf{Ans}_0(P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(a^\sharp))=\texttt{pass}.
\]
\item \textbf{Strictness.} The promoted interface is not a relabeling of the lower interface:
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing,
\]
with explicit witness pair
\[
(s,s')\in\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1).
\]
\item \textbf{Non-descent of the promoted structure.} The promoted structure itself is not accepted as lower-layer content:
\[
U\not\downarrow_q.
\]
\item \textbf{Audited descent of the selected expression.} The expression selected from the promoted structure descends under the bridge:
\[
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp.
\]
\item \textbf{No overreading.} The accepted claim asserts only the audited lower descendant \(a^\sharp\), not the whole hidden promoted structure \(U\), at the lower layer.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, \(B_{0\to1}\) is a strictly useful promoted extension of \(\mathcal T_0\) for \(P\) in the sense recorded by the canonical useful-extension definition in \Cref{app:definitions}.

\label{def:sau-failure-fields}
For a raw candidate package
\[
\mathfrak C=(\mathfrak P_0,B_{0\to1},U,C,a^\sharp;

F_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathfrak C)=
\begin{cases}
\varnothing,&\operatorname{Sat}(\mathfrak P_0),\\
\{\star\},&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
\[
F_{\mathrm{strict}}(\mathfrak C)=
\begin{cases}
\varnothing,&\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing,\\
\{\star\},&\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)=\varnothing,
\end{cases}
\]
\[
F_{\mathrm{nondesc}}(\mathfrak C)=
\begin{cases}
\varnothing,&U\not\downarrow_q,\\
\{\star\},&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
\[
F_{\mathrm{desc}}(\mathfrak C)=
\begin{cases}
\varnothing,&C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp,\\
\{\star\},&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
\[
F_{\mathrm{solve}}(\mathfrak C)=
\begin{cases}
\varnothing,&a^\sharp\in\mathsf{Ans}_0(P)
\text{ and }\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(a^\sharp))=\texttt{pass},\\
\{\star\},&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}

and

\{\star\},&\text{otherwise}.

\]

\]
when all six components are empty.

\label{def:sau-counterfeit-patterns}
A candidate bridge has one of the following counterfeit profiles when it resembles SAU informally but lacks a required field:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Ornamental extension:}
\[
\operatorname{Strict}(B),\quad U\not\downarrow_q,
\quad\text{but}\quad C(U)\not\downarrow_B a^\sharp.
\]
The promoted layer is richer but unreturned.
\item \textbf{Mere notation:}
\[
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp,
\quad\text{but}\quad
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)=\varnothing.
\]
The promoted expression descends, but no strictness has been shown.
\item \textbf{Irrelevant descent:}
\[
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp,
\quad\text{but}\quad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(a^\sharp))\neq\texttt{pass}.
\]
The descendant exists but does not answer the problem.
\item \textbf{Smuggled proof:}
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{nosmuggle}}(B)\neq\varnothing.
\]
The proof uses content not admitted by the bridge.
\item \textbf{Literalized hidden object:}
\[
U\not\downarrow_q
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Lit_0(U)
\]
without an independent bridge for \(U\).
\end{enumerate}

\label{def:sau-boundary-head}
Let \(C(U)\) be the selected expression in a reduced boundary trace.  Its head constructor is the outermost audit-relevant operation used to turn the hidden support into a lower-descending expression.  It is denoted
\[
\Head(C).
\]
The head is typed.  For example, a power constructor \(U\mapsto U^n\), a coefficient constructor \(F(\eta)\mapsto[\eta]F(\eta)\), a fixed-point constructor \(x\mapsto x^G\), and a quotient-class constructor \(a\mapsto[a]\) have different sorts even if their descended values happen to be represented by the same set-theoretic object.
