\label{def:sau-basic-audit-grammar}
The basic SAU audit grammar \(\mathcal G_{\operatorname{Basic}}\) is the typed grammar whose primitive boundary constructors are the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Composite or power constructor:}
\[
C(U)=U^n\quad(n\ge2)
\]
or, more generally, a finite composite of a hidden update whose selected composite descends.
\item \textbf{Coefficient or standard-part constructor:}
\[
C(U)=\kappa(\Phi(U)),
\]
where \(\kappa\) is a coefficient, jet, residue, leading-term, or standard-part audit map.
\item \textbf{Projection or shadow constructor:}
\[
C(U)=q(U),
\]
where \(q\) is a declared shadow, real-part, observable, quotient, or forgetful projection.
\item \textbf{Invariant or fixed-point constructor:}
\[
C(U)\in \Inv_G(\mathcal T_1)\quad\text{or}\quad C(U)\in \operatorname{Fix}(G),
\]
where a promoted symmetry action makes the selected expression invariant and hence lower-descending.
\item \textbf{Trace, norm, or symmetric aggregation constructor:}
\[
C(U)=\sum_{g\in G}gU,
\qquad
C(U)=\prod_{g\in G}gU,
\]
or another declared finite symmetric aggregation of a promoted orbit.
\item \textbf{Quotient or obstruction-class constructor:}
\[
C(U)=[U]\in M/N,
\]
where \(N\) is the subobject declared exact, trivial, gauge, globally generated, or lower-null.
\end{enumerate}
The grammar is closed under finite products, finite sums, ordered tuples, and composition with already accepted lower-layer verifiers.  It is not closed under arbitrary informal analogy, undeclared semantic interpretation, or unaudited transfer.

\label{def:sau-basic-profile-registry}
The basic profile registry is
\[
\mathcal R_{\operatorname{Basic}}
=\{\mathsf{RootComp},\mathsf{Coeff},\mathsf{ProjShad},\mathsf{InvDesc},\mathsf{AggInv},\mathsf{ObsLed}\}.
\]
The four canonical case-study profiles are the subregistry
\[
\mathcal R_{4}
=\{\mathsf{RootComp},\mathsf{Coeff},\mathsf{InvDesc},\mathsf{ObsLed}\}.
\]
The registry map
\[
\rho_{\operatorname{Basic}}:\mathcal G_{\operatorname{Basic}}\longrightarrow\mathcal R_{\operatorname{Basic}}
\]
is defined on primitive heads by
\[
\rho_{\operatorname{Basic}}(U\mapsto U^n)=\mathsf{RootComp},
\]
\[
\rho_{\operatorname{Basic}}(\kappa\circ\Phi)=\mathsf{Coeff},
\]
\[
\rho_{\operatorname{Basic}}(q)=\mathsf{ProjShad},
\]
\[
\rho_{\operatorname{Basic}}(\Inv_G\text{ or }\operatorname{Fix}(G))=\mathsf{InvDesc},
\]
\[
\rho_{\operatorname{Basic}}(\sum_G,\prod_G,\text{symmetric aggregation})=\mathsf{AggInv},
\]
\[
\rho_{\operatorname{Basic}}(U\mapsto[U]\in M/N)=\mathsf{ObsLed}.
\]
For composite boundary expressions, \(\rho_{\operatorname{Basic}}\) returns the finite ordered list or product of primitive profile labels appearing in the reduced expression.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
There are \(|Y|^{|Y|}=3^3=27\) candidates in \(\operatorname{End}(Y)\).  Suppose one of
them satisfies \(H^2=F\).  Since \(F\) is bijective, \(H^2\) is bijective; on
a finite set this forces \(H\) itself to be bijective.  Thus the original
27-case check reduces to the six permutations of \(Y\).  Now \(F\) is the
transposition exchanging \(1\) and \(-1\) while fixing \(0\), so \(F\) is odd.
But the square of any permutation is even, because
\[
\operatorname{sgn}(H^2)=\operatorname{sgn}(H)^2=1.
\]
Hence no permutation \(H\) can satisfy \(H^2=F\), and therefore no endomorphism
of \(Y\) can do so.  A full enumeration of the original 27 candidates is
deferred to \Cref{app:methods}; the same finite check is verified in Lean as
a faithful computational proof (\Cref{app:formalization}).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
In the declared real-shadow problem, \(Y=\{-1,0,1\}\), so any surjection
\(q:X\twoheadrightarrow Y\) has \(|X|\geq 3\).  If \(|X|=3\) then \(q\) is
bijective, in which case every update \(G:X\to X\) descends via

\Cref{lem:imag-G2-descends} gives \(G^2\downarrow_q F\).  The full
small-cardinality enumeration is deferred to \Cref{app:methods}.
\end{proof}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:imag-minimal-real-linear-completion}
Let \(J\) be a real-linear hidden half-step satisfying
\[
J^2=-I.
\]
The minimal nonzero real-linear package carrying such a \(J\) is two-dimensional.  In that package, the real algebra generated by \(J\) is
\[
\mathbb R[J]=\{aI+bJ:a,b\in\mathbb R\},
\]
with multiplication
\[
(aI+bJ)(cI+dJ)=(ac-bd)I+(ad+bc)J.
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathbb R[J]\cong \mathbb C
\]
under the map
\[
a+bi\longmapsto aI+bJ.
\]

\[
\mathbb R[\eta]\cong \mathbb R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2).

\end{proposition}

\label{thm:jet-sau-certificate}
The first-order dual-number package supplies a Strict Audited Utility certificate for the value-only derivative-extraction problem:
\[
\mathsf{Jet}\models\mathsf{SAU}.
\]
More explicitly, with
\[
\pi_0=\ev_x,
\qquad
\pi_1=j_x^1,
\qquad
U=\varepsilon,
\qquad
C(U;f)=[\varepsilon]f(x+\varepsilon),
\qquad
 a^\sharp=D_x,
\]
the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the lower profile is saturated:
\[
\operatorname{Sat}(\mathfrak P_{\mathsf{Jet},0});
\]
\item the promotion is strict:
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing;
\]
\item the promoted direction is non-descending:
\[
\varepsilon\notin\mathbb R,
\qquad
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\operatorname{st},\id_{\mathbb R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)})\neq\varnothing;
\]
\item the selected expression descends by coefficient audit:
\[
[\varepsilon]\circ j_x^1=D_x;
\]
\item the descended answer solves the lower problem:
\[
D_x\in\mathsf{Ans}_0(P_{\mathsf{Jet}});
\]
\item the nonclaim register blocks the overread that \(\varepsilon\) is a real scalar or that the derivative was obtained from value alone.
\end{enumerate}

explicit refusal to infer \(\alpha\in K\) from these descended invariant data.
\end{proof}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:coh-period-audit}
A directed closed walk or cycle \(\gamma\) determines a signed sum of oriented edges.  For \(a\in C^1(\Gamma;k)\), define the period of \(a\) around \(\gamma\) by
\[
\oint_\gamma a
=
\sum_{e\in \gamma}\epsilon_e a(e),
\]
where \(\epsilon_e=1\) if \(\gamma\) traverses \(e\) in the chosen orientation and \(\epsilon_e=-1\) if it traverses \(e\) in the opposite orientation.  The period audit is the map
\[
\operatorname{Per}(a):Z_1(\Gamma;k)\to k,
\qquad
\operatorname{Per}(a)(\gamma)=\oint_\gamma a,
\]
where \(Z_1(\Gamma;k)\) is the cycle space of the graph.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:sau-canonical-witness-vector}
The canonical witness vector is the ordered family
\[
\mathfrak W_{4}
=
(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Imag}},\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Jet}},\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Gal}},\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Coh}}),
\]
where:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Imag}}\) is the root-composite witness built from the four-phase carrier \(C_4=\{1,i,-1,-i\}\), the real-shadow lens \(q:C_4\to\{-1,0,1\}\), the quarter-turn \(G(z)=iz\), and the descending square \(G^2\).
\item \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Jet}}\) is the coefficient witness built from the dual-number algebra \(\mathbb R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\), the non-real nilpotent \(\varepsilon\), the first-jet expression \(f(x+\varepsilon)\), and the coefficient audit \([\varepsilon]f(x+\varepsilon)=f'(x)\).
\item \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Gal}}\) is the invariant-descent witness built from a finite Galois splitting field \(L/K\), a non-descending root \(\alpha\notin K\), and descending invariant audits such as elementary symmetric functions, \(L^{\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)}=K\), \(\Tr_{L/K}\), and \(\Nm_{L/K}\).
\item \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Coh}}\) is the obstruction-ledger witness built from a finite connected graph \(\Gamma\), local edge data \(a\in C^1(\Gamma;k)\), the global-potential descent question \(a=d_0\phi\), and the obstruction class \([a]\in H^1(\Gamma;k)\).
\end{enumerate}
Each component of \(\mathfrak W_4\) is understood with its declared lower problem profile, promotion bridge, audit channels, and nonclaim register from the corresponding theorem sheet.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{lem:sau-cross-imag-fields}
The witness \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Imag}}\) is SAU-complete.  Its six-field projection is:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf{SatW}:& \text{no same-layer }H:\{-1,0,1\}\to\{-1,0,1\}\text{ satisfies }H^2(y)=-y,\\[2mm]
\mathsf{StrictW}:& \delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(q,\operatorname{id}_{C_4})\neq\varnothing\text{, witnessed by }(i,-i),\\[2mm]
\mathsf{NonDescW}:& G\not\downarrow_q,\\[1mm]
\mathsf{DescW}:& G^2\downarrow_q F\text{, where }F(y)=-y,\\[1mm]
\mathsf{SolveW}:& F\text{ is the lower reversal required by the half-step problem},\\[1mm]
\mathsf{AuditW}:& q\text{, conjugation, norm, and the nonclaim }G\in\mathcal T_0\text{ is not asserted}.
\end{array}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathsf{Imag}\models\mathsf{SAU}.
\]

\label{thm:sau-transfer-profile-theorem}
Mathematical transfer at SAU strength is possible exactly at the profile level: a successful source case may suggest a reusable skeleton \(\mathfrak p\), but a target case becomes accepted only when it independently validates an instance of \(\mathfrak p\). \label{thm:sau-transfer-profile-theorem}
Mathematical transfer at SAU strength is possible exactly at the profile level: a successful source case may suggest a reusable skeleton \(\mathfrak p\), but a target case becomes accepted only when it independently validates an instance of \(\mathfrak p\).  Formally, for a source \(\mathfrak C_s\), target \(\mathfrak C_t\), and profile \(\mathfrak p\),
\[
\Inst_{\SAU}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_s)
+\Inst_{\SAU}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_t)
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\Use(B_s,P_s):\texttt{accepted}
\text{ and }
\Use(B_t,P_t):\texttt{accepted}.
\]
But
\[
\Inst_{\SAU}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_s)
+\Inst(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_t)
\]
without target validation does not license \(\Use(B_t,P_t):\texttt{accepted}\).

\[

conclusion: The results give a theorem-grade normal form for strict mathematical usefulness in finite typed audited promoted-use traces: when a saturated lower problem is solved or certified by essentially using promoted-only structure, the trace forces hidden non-descent: a support that does not descend directly, together with an audited boundary expression that does descend. The four canonical witnesses—imaginary numbers, dual numbers, Galois roots, and graph cohomology—instantiate distinct minimal or universal profiles, and the necessity–soundness chain extracts SAU from strict useful traces rather than stipulating it. The no-overreading discipline blocks the literalization of hidden promoted objects in the lower layer. The scope is bounded. We address strict useful promoted-use traces, not mathematics in general; not every promoted extension is useful, and the four canonical witnesses are not an exhaustive classification of useful structures. We do not claim novelty for the classical constructions themselves, and hidden promoted objects are not asserted as lower-layer content. The companion Lean development plays a bounded role: it supplies substantive proofs for selected direct, computational, and definitional fragments and records the remaining theorems as proof-carrying traceability records. Source, Lean code, and reproducibility artifacts are hosted at ; see for the discipline that governs which results carry substantive Lean proofs. Foundations I–III provide inherited provenance but are not prerequisites for reading the paper.

Let \(C^\infty_x\) denote the local algebra of smooth germs at \(x\), and let
\[
\mathfrak m_x=\{f\in C^\infty_x:f(x)=0\}

be the maximal ideal of germs vanishing at \(x\).  Then the first-jet algebra
\[
J_x^1=C^\infty_x/\mathfrak m_x^2
\]
is isomorphic, as a real algebra, to \(\mathbb R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\), by
\[
[f]\longmapsto f(x)+f'(x)\varepsilon.
\]

These four examples are classical mathematics; the paper does not claim
novelty for complex numbers, dual numbers, splitting fields, or graph
cohomology themselves.  Their common shape is what matters here: the
calculation uses an object that is useful for a problem about the original
setting, even though the object does not live in that setting, and it pairs
that object with an expression that the original setting can recognize.  The
case studies in \Cref{sec:imaginary,sec:calculus,sec:galois,sec:cohomology}
return to these examples with their full mathematical structure.

\label{def:sau-theory-package}
A theory package is a tuple
\[
\mathcal T=(Z,f,\Sigma_f,E,\mathcal A),
\]
where \(Z\) is a carrier, \(f:Z\to O\) is a lens or interface, \(\Sigma_f\) is the family of distinctions representable through \(f\), \(E\) is a completion or packaging operation when one is present, and \(\mathcal A\) is the inherited package audit functional. In the full finite-lens case,
\[
\Sigma_f=\{f^{-1}(B):B\subseteq \operatorname{im}(f)\}.
\]
The paper may use weaker or profile-specific \(\Sigma_f\), but every use must be declared under the surrounding instrument.

to try, the kind of answer that would count, the defect by which a candidate is
judged, the threshold for passing, and the surrounding nonclaim register.

\label{def:sau-certificate}
Let \(\mathfrak P_0\) be a lower problem profile and \(B_{0\to1}\) a promotion bridge. A Strict Audited Utility certificate, abbreviated
\[
\mathsf{SAU}(\mathfrak P_0,B_{0\to1},U,C,a^\sharp),
\]
is a finite typed record containing the following six fields:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Saturation field:}
\[
\operatorname{Sat}(\mathfrak P_0).
\]
\item \textbf{Strictness field:}
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing.
\]
\item \textbf{Non-descent field:}
\[
U\not\downarrow_q.
\]
\item \textbf{Audited descent field:}
\[
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp.
\]
\item \textbf{Problem-resolution field:}
\[
a^\sharp\in\mathsf{Ans}_0(P)
\]
with \(\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(a^\sharp))=\texttt{pass}\), when the lower problem uses a defect threshold.
\item \textbf{Audit/no-overread/no-smuggling field:}
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{overread}}=\varnothing,
\qquad
\delta_{\mathrm{nosmuggle}}(B)=\varnothing,
\qquad
\delta_{\mathrm{audit}}(B)=\varnothing,
\qquad
\mathsf{AuditGate}_B:\texttt{pass},
\]
with an explicit nonclaim record \(\mathcal N_B\).
\end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:sau-promoted-use-trace}
A finite promoted-use trace for a lower problem profile \(\mathfrak P_0\) is a tuple
\[
\mathfrak T=(D,V,E,r,o,\lambda,\upsilon,\mathcal B,A_{\mathfrak T},\mathcal N,v_\ast),
\]
where:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(D=(V,E)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph.  An edge \(u\to v\) means that the node \(v\) depends on the node \(u\).
\item \(r\) records the rule, operation, bridge, or audit step used at each non-input node.
\item \(o(v)\) is the mathematical object, assertion, certificate, or intermediate expression carried by \(v\).
\item \(\lambda(v)\in\{0,1\}\) is the declared layer label: \(0\) for lower-layer nodes and \(1\) for promoted-layer nodes.
\item \(\upsilon(v)\in\{\texttt{visible},\texttt{suppressed},\texttt{outside},\texttt{unknown}\}\) is the visibility status under the declared instrument.
\item \(\mathcal B\) is the finite family of declared bridge or descent steps used by the trace.
\item \(A_{\mathfrak T}\) is the finite audit/provenance/replay record for the trace.
\item \(\mathcal N\) is the nonclaim register.
\item \(v_\ast\in V\) is the final answer node, whose object is denoted
\[
a^\sharp_{\mathfrak T}:=o(v_\ast).

\label{def:sau-promoted-use-trace}
A finite promoted-use trace for a lower problem profile \(\mathfrak P_0\) is a tuple
\[
\mathfrak T=(D,V,E,r,o,\lambda,\upsilon,\mathcal B,A_{\mathfrak T},\mathcal N,v_\ast),
\]
where:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(D=(V,E)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph.  An edge \(u\to v\) means that the node \(v\) depends on the node \(u\).
\item \(r\) records the rule, operation, bridge, or audit step used at each non-input node.
\item \(o(v)\) is the mathematical object, assertion, certificate, or intermediate expression carried by \(v\).
\item \(\lambda(v)\in\{0,1\}\) is the declared layer label: \(0\) for lower-layer nodes and \(1\) for promoted-layer nodes.
\item \(\upsilon(v)\in\{\texttt{visible},\texttt{suppressed},\texttt{outside},\texttt{unknown}\}\) is the visibility status under the declared instrument.
\item \(\mathcal B\) is the finite family of declared bridge or descent steps used by the trace.
\item \(A_{\mathfrak T}\) is the finite audit/provenance/replay record for the trace.
\item \(\mathcal N\) is the nonclaim register.
\item \(v_\ast\in V\) is the final answer node, whose object is denoted
\[
a^\sharp_{\mathfrak T}:=o(v_\ast).
\]
\end{enumerate}
The trace is typed: every edge and every rule application must respect the source and target layers recorded by \(\lambda\), the visibility status recorded by \(\upsilon\), and the bridge permissions recorded by \(\mathcal B\).

\label{thm:sau-soundness}
Let \(\mathfrak C\) be a validated raw SAU proof package for
\((\mathfrak P_0,B_{0\to1},U,C,a^\sharp)\).  Then the following instrument-indexed claim is accepted:
\[
\Gamma;\mathcal T_0\leadsto\mathcal T_1;I_B
\vdash
\operatorname{Useful}(B_{0\to1},P):\texttt{accepted}.
\]
More explicitly, the accepted claim has the following content:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Lower-layer saturation.} No candidate at the fixed lower interface solves the problem:
\[
\forall s\in\mathsf{Cand}_0(P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(s))\neq\texttt{pass}.
\]
\item \textbf{Promoted answer.} The promoted calculation supplies a lower-layer accepted answer:
\[
a^\sharp\in\mathsf{Ans}_0(P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(a^\sharp))=\texttt{pass}.
\]
\item \textbf{Strictness.} The promoted interface is not a relabeling of the lower interface:
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing,
\]
with explicit witness pair
\[
(s,s')\in\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1).
\]
\item \textbf{Non-descent of the promoted structure.} The promoted structure itself is not accepted as lower-layer content:
\[
U\not\downarrow_q.
\]
\item \textbf{Audited descent of the selected expression.} The expression selected from the promoted structure descends under the bridge:
\[
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp.
\]
\item \textbf{No overreading.} The accepted claim asserts only the audited lower descendant \(a^\sharp\), not the whole hidden promoted structure \(U\), at the lower layer.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, \(B_{0\to1}\) is a strictly useful promoted extension of \(\mathcal T_0\) for \(P\) in the sense recorded by the canonical useful-extension definition in \Cref{app:definitions}.

\label{def:sau-counterfeit-patterns}
A candidate bridge has one of the following counterfeit profiles when it resembles SAU informally but lacks a required field:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Ornamental extension:}
\[
\operatorname{Strict}(B),\quad U\not\downarrow_q,
\quad\text{but}\quad C(U)\not\downarrow_B a^\sharp.
\]
The promoted layer is richer but unreturned.
\item \textbf{Mere notation:}
\[
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp,
\quad\text{but}\quad
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)=\varnothing.
\]
The promoted expression descends, but no strictness has been shown.
\item \textbf{Irrelevant descent:}
\[
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp,
\quad\text{but}\quad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(a^\sharp))\neq\texttt{pass}.
\]
The descendant exists but does not answer the problem.
\item \textbf{Smuggled proof:}
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{nosmuggle}}(B)\neq\varnothing.
\]
The proof uses content not admitted by the bridge.
\item \textbf{Literalized hidden object:}
\[
U\not\downarrow_q
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Lit_0(U)
\]
without an independent bridge for \(U\).
\end{enumerate}

\label{def:sau-basic-audit-grammar}
The basic SAU audit grammar \(\mathcal G_{\operatorname{Basic}}\) is the typed grammar whose primitive boundary constructors are the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Composite or power constructor:}
\[
C(U)=U^n\quad(n\ge2)
\]
or, more generally, a finite composite of a hidden update whose selected composite descends.
\item \textbf{Coefficient or standard-part constructor:}
\[
C(U)=\kappa(\Phi(U)),
\]
where \(\kappa\) is a coefficient, jet, residue, leading-term, or standard-part audit map.
\item \textbf{Projection or shadow constructor:}
\[
C(U)=q(U),
\]
where \(q\) is a declared shadow, real-part, observable, quotient, or forgetful projection.
\item \textbf{Invariant or fixed-point constructor:}
\[
C(U)\in \Inv_G(\mathcal T_1)\quad\text{or}\quad C(U)\in \operatorname{Fix}(G),
\]
where a promoted symmetry action makes the selected expression invariant and hence lower-descending.
\item \textbf{Trace, norm, or symmetric aggregation constructor:}
\[
C(U)=\sum_{g\in G}gU,
\qquad
C(U)=\prod_{g\in G}gU,
\]
or another declared finite symmetric aggregation of a promoted orbit.
\item \textbf{Quotient or obstruction-class constructor:}
\[
C(U)=[U]\in M/N,
\]
where \(N\) is the subobject declared exact, trivial, gauge, globally generated, or lower-null.
\end{enumerate}
The grammar is closed under finite products, finite sums, ordered tuples, and composition with already accepted lower-layer verifiers.  It is not closed under arbitrary informal analogy, undeclared semantic interpretation, or unaudited transfer.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
There are \(|Y|^{|Y|}=3^3=27\) candidates in \(\operatorname{End}(Y)\).  Suppose one of
them satisfies \(H^2=F\).  Since \(F\) is bijective, \(H^2\) is bijective; on
a finite set this forces \(H\) itself to be bijective.  Thus the original
27-case check reduces to the six permutations of \(Y\).  Now \(F\) is the
transposition exchanging \(1\) and \(-1\) while fixing \(0\), so \(F\) is odd.
But the square of any permutation is even, because
\[
\operatorname{sgn}(H^2)=\operatorname{sgn}(H)^2=1.
\]
Hence no permutation \(H\) can satisfy \(H^2=F\), and therefore no endomorphism
of \(Y\) can do so.  A full enumeration of the original 27 candidates is
deferred to \Cref{app:methods}.  The same finite check is verified in Lean as
a faithful computational proof; see also \Cref{app:formalization} for the Lean
traceability.
\end{proof}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
In the declared real-shadow problem, \(Y=\{-1,0,1\}\), so any surjection
\(q:X\twoheadrightarrow Y\) has \(|X|\geq 3\).  If \(|X|=3\), then \(q\) is
bijective.  In that case every update \(G:X\to X\) descends, by defining
\[
G^\sharp=qGq^{-1}:Y\to Y
\]
and observing that \(qG=G^\sharp q\).  This contradicts \(G\not\downarrow_q\).
Thus any such non-descending strict phase promotion has \(|X|\geq 4\).  The
four-phase carrier \(C_4\) has four elements, \Cref{lem:imag-G-nondescends}
gives \(G\not\downarrow_q\), and \Cref{lem:imag-G2-descends} gives
\(G^2\downarrow_q F\).  The full small-cardinality enumeration is deferred to
\Cref{app:methods}.  Lean verifies the no-same-layer-root component, here
corresponding to the lower bound on \(|X|\); the universal \(|X|\geq 4\)
statement is delivered as a paper-side argument.
\end{proof}

\label{thm:imag-minimal-real-linear-completion}
Let \(J\) be a real-linear hidden half-step satisfying
\[
J^2=-I.
\]
The minimal nonzero real-linear package carrying such a \(J\) is two-dimensional.  In that package, the real algebra generated by \(J\) is
\[
\mathbb R[J]=\{aI+bJ:a,b\in\mathbb R\},
\]
with multiplication
\[
(aI+bJ)(cI+dJ)=(ac-bd)I+(ad+bc)J.
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathbb R[J]\cong \mathbb C
\]
under the map
\[
a+bi\longmapsto aI+bJ.
\]

conclusion: Consequently, an element x∈ L descends to the base field exactly when it is fixed by every K -automorphism of L : x∈ K Longleftrightarrow sigma(x)=x for all sigma∈ G.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:gal-fixed-field-audit}
For the finite Galois extension \(L/K\),
\[
L^G=K,
\qquad
G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/K).
\]
Consequently, an element \(x\in L\) descends to the base field exactly when it is fixed by every \(K\)-automorphism of \(L\):
\[
x\in K
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\sigma(x)=x\text{ for all }\sigma\in G.
\]

Saturation is supplied by \Cref{cor:gal-root-saturation}.  Strictness is
\Cref{thm:gal-strictness}, and non-descent of an individual promoted root is
\Cref{lem:gal-root-not-descend}.  The audited descent fields are supplied by the

\Cref{thm:gal-fixed-field-audit}, \Cref{thm:gal-trace-norm-descend}, and
\Cref{cor:gal-orbit-polynomials-descend}.  The nonclaim register is the
explicit refusal to infer \(\alpha\in K\) from those descended invariant data.
Thus the six certificate fields are present for the Galois root package.  The
theorem is tracked by the formalization harness as a projection over the
Galois-case certificate record and its constituent witness fields.
\end{proof}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:coh-period-audit}
A directed closed walk or cycle \(\gamma\) determines a signed sum of oriented edges.  For \(a\in C^1(\Gamma;k)\), define the period of \(a\) around \(\gamma\) by
\[
\oint_\gamma a
=
\sum_{e\in \gamma}\epsilon_e a(e),
\]
where \(\epsilon_e=1\) if \(\gamma\) traverses \(e\) in the chosen orientation and \(\epsilon_e=-1\) if it traverses \(e\) in the opposite orientation.  The period audit is the map
\[
\operatorname{Per}(a):Z_1(\Gamma;k)\to k,
\qquad
\operatorname{Per}(a)(\gamma)=\oint_\gamma a,
\]
where \(Z_1(\Gamma;k)\) is the cycle space of the graph.

\label{def:sau-profile-instance}

\[
\mathfrak C=(\mathfrak P_0,B_{0\to1},U,C,a^\sharp;
\mathsf{SatW},\mathsf{StrictW},\mathsf{NonDescW},\mathsf{DescW},\mathsf{SolveW},\mathsf{AuditW})

\rho:\mathfrak C\longrightarrow\mathfrak p

\[
\operatorname{Inst}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C)
\]
when the typing map is declared and all profile slots are inhabited by concrete witness data.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
The transfer plan gives a validated source instance and a target instance in the
same profile skeleton.  Validation of the target plan is the additional
condition \(\mathbf F_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak C_t)=\varnothing\), so the target has its

validation explains why the profile was a legitimate guide, but it does not
identify the source and target objects.  This theorem is tracked by the
formalization harness as a projection over the transfer-plan and validated-target
records.
\end{proof}

\[

+\Inst_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_t)
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\operatorname{Useful}(B_s,P_s):\texttt{accepted}
\text{ and }
\operatorname{Useful}(B_t,P_t):\texttt{accepted}.
\]

\[
\Inst_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_s)
+\operatorname{Inst}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_t)
\]
without target validation does not license \(\operatorname{Useful}(B_t,P_t):\texttt{accepted}\).

\begin{definition}[Explanatory compression]
\label{def:sau-explanatory-compression}
Suppose a finite registry \(\mathcal R\) SAU-covers a finite problem family \(\mathcal P\).  The registry provides \emph{explanatory compression} when many problem instances are certified by fewer recurring profile skeletons.  A crude count is
\[
\chi_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathcal P,\mathcal R)=|\mathcal P|-|\mathcal R|,
\]
with the understanding that this number is only a bookkeeping index, not an invariant of mathematical depth.
\end{definition}

Within the scope of finite typed audited promoted-use traces, the paper gives a
profile-level explanation of strict mathematical usefulness.  What this unlocks
for further work is not a catalog of future domains, but a disciplined way to ask
whether a family of lower problems is covered by recurring audited profiles.

\begin{definition}[Explanatory compression]
\label{def:sau-explanatory-compression}
Suppose a finite registry \(\mathcal R\) SAU-covers a finite problem family \(\mathcal P\).  The registry provides \emph{explanatory compression} when many problem instances are certified by fewer recurring profile skeletons.  A crude count is
\[
\chi_{\SAU}(\mathcal P,\mathcal R)=|\mathcal P|-|\mathcal R|,
\]
with the understanding that this number is only a bookkeeping index, not an invariant of mathematical depth.
\end{definition}

conclusion: The contribution is a theorem-grade normal form for strict mathematical usefulness in finite typed audited promoted-use traces. When a saturated lower problem is solved or certified by essentially using promoted-only structure, the trace forces hidden support that does not descend directly and an audited boundary expression that does descend. The four canonical witnesses–imaginary numbers, dual numbers, Galois roots, and graph cohomology–instantiate distinct minimal or universal profiles, and the necessity-soundness chain extracts SAU from strict useful traces rather than stipulating it. The no-overreading discipline is part of the contribution: it blocks the literalization of hidden promoted objects in the lower layer. The paper does not claim that all mathematics is useful, that every promoted extension is useful, or that every useful structure has been classified. It does not claim novelty for the classical constructions themselves, and it does not claim that hidden promoted objects literally belong to the lower layer. Foundations I–III supply inherited provenance but are not prerequisites for reading the paper, because the working vocabulary is defined locally. The Lean development also has a bounded role: it supplies substantive proofs for selected direct, computational, and definitional fragments, while projection-over-record theorems are tracked as proof-carrying traceability records.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:sau-strictness-defect}
Given object maps \(\pi_0:S\to O_0\) and \(\pi_1:S\to O_1\), define the factorization defect
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)
=
\{(s,s')\in S\times S:\pi_0(s)=\pi_0(s')\text{ and }\pi_1(s)\neq\pi_1(s')\}.
\]
The promotion is strict when
\[
\operatorname{Strict}(B_{0\to1})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing.
\]

\label{def:sau-strictness-defect}
Given object maps \(\pi_0:S\to O_0\) and \(\pi_1:S\to O_1\), define the factorization defect
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)
=
\{(s,s')\in S\times S:\pi_0(s)=\pi_0(s')\text{ and }\pi_1(s)\neq\pi_1(s')\}.

The promotion is strict when
\[
\operatorname{Strict}(B_{0\to1})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, \(\pi_1\) does not factor through \(\pi_0\). A strict promotion distinguishes something that the lower interface collapses.

A candidate promotion bridge fails to certify strict audited utility if any of the following occur:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{No saturation:} the lower interface already supplies an accepted answer.

\item \textbf{No problem resolution:} the descended output fails the lower problem threshold.
\item \textbf{Audit failure:} the source, audit, visibility, threshold, or replay record fails.
\item \textbf{Smuggling:} \(\delta_{\mathrm{nosmuggle}}(B)\neq\varnothing\).
\item \textbf{Overreading:} the claim asserts hidden promoted content at the lower layer rather than only the audited descendant.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: We propose that to be real is to have closed: that reality is not a substance, a substrate, or a set, but a ledger of survived closures. A thing is real when it is a package that earned its objecthood through audited gates and pays, continuously, to keep it. The proposal is grounded in the Six Birds corpus, which has spent the last years doing something Nietzsche predicted and no one else has attempted: worshipping the stone. The corpus constructs geometry, logic, time, probability, objects, events, agents, institutions, and selves from bare substrates, under explicit audit, with every failure banked and every success priced. The method of this paper is an itemized metaphysics. Every claim is either free, a theorem of the corpus at its stated grade, or purchased, spending one of two named axioms: Ontic Closure Completeness and Substrate Indifference. On this basis we argue that the Born rule's shape is the generic fate of compressed record layers, so that probability is born at the lens; that a simulation which passes a closure's gates is not a simulation of the thing but an instance of it, which is why lattice QCD computes the true proton; that ``matter'' and ``information'' are altitude labels, so that an economy is literally a ghost made of people; that mathematics is closure engineering in vitro, the design of lawful theory extensions ahead of any run, and in practice a map that unfolds only where someone walks; that the explanatory gap of consciousness is a non-descent certificate, predicted rather than embarrassing; that life and intelligence are graded, auditable positions on real axes rather than binaries; that a civilization which learns this grammar crosses into the era of meta-emergence, where creation itself is a wielded power, and that peace is a closure state, an achievement that strengthens rather than dissolves the identities it comprises; and that the great paradoxes (sorites, Theseus, Zeno, Mary's room, the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics, the arrow of time) dissolve under ledger discipline, most of them because they demanded of a layer a certificate that no layer can issue. We close eight old problems and open eight new ones. The last sacrifice is Sacrifice itself.

We close eight old problems and open eight new ones. The last sacrifice is Sacrifice itself.

expanded_source_wording_tex: \textbf{The thin forced skeleton.} Necessity and contingency, in physics, stop being moods and become computed columns. Enumerating nearly twelve thousand chiral gauge structures token-blind, the closure chain forces a thin skeleton: the Standard Model's gauge algebra (conditional on one separation condition), $\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$ at the embedding point, exact proton stability. And it proves other quantities invisible to in-layer law: the generation count, the electroweak scale, the value of the cosmological constant. ``The Standard Model, on this evidence, is not one derivable object. It is a \emph{selection} with a thin forced skeleton --- and the calculus proves both the skeleton and the thinness.'' The laws of nature, like the axioms of set theory \citep{zfc}, factor into a free column and a purchased column. That physics and mathematics have the same receipt structure is the one-grammar thesis in its most compact form.

conclusion: What happens to a civilization after the crossing is an open question, the ninth of this book, and we will not pretend to close it.
expanded_source_wording_tex: What happens to a civilization after the crossing is an open question, the ninth of this book, and we will not pretend to close it. But the grammar constrains the answer's shape. Wielded creation accelerates enablement-time: more strict extensions per generation, more ghosts above and more below. And the corpus's bounded-reflexivity law holds that audit capacity does not scale for free \citep{cognition}. So the era of meta-emergence poses one structural alternative, the same alternative \S\ref{sec:singularities} posed for machine minds, now at the scale of the species: \textbf{either coherence grows with creative power, or the civilization's own creations outrun its audits} and it becomes substrate to ghosts it can no longer read. A civilization past the threshold must evolve toward higher and tighter closure: wider common quotients, faster certificate flow, denser repair transport. Not as moral aspiration. As a viability condition, of the same standing as any other gate.

conclusion: When does prediction become trivial? This paper gives a typed structural answer: within the scope, predictive content collapses when an upstream determining state is exposed to current observation. The load-bearing variable is the visibility coupling predicate ( , ) , which asks whether some polynomial-time current observable factors through the autonomous lift's internal state by a function non-constant on the realized carrier. We state a typed ( ) over the predictive-quotient holonomy carrier on autonomous-lifted polynomial-time substrates. The law has four clauses: dissolution under exposure, preservation under non-exposure, a degenerate clause when there is no predictive witness content, and strength-independence of the coupling function. The is stated at . We also give a granularity-mismatch theorem at : the framework's current and predictive quotients are strictly finer than the standard classes P and NP at the history level, but this strictness can be lost under standard language-level projection.

When does prediction become trivial?  This paper gives a typed
structural answer: within the \CSL{} scope, predictive content
collapses when an upstream determining state is exposed to current
observation.  The
load-bearing variable is the visibility coupling predicate
\(\Exposure(\Lift,\Substrate)\), which asks whether some polynomial-time
current observable factors through the autonomous lift's internal state
by a function non-constant on the realized carrier.  We state a typed
\CSLcore{} (\(\CSL\)) over the predictive-quotient holonomy carrier on
autonomous-lifted polynomial-time substrates.  The law has four clauses:
dissolution under exposure, preservation under non-exposure, a
degenerate clause when there is no predictive witness content, and
strength-independence of the coupling function.  The \CSL{} is stated
at \DiagnosisGrade{}.  We also give a granularity-mismatch theorem at
\RDiagnosis{}: the framework's current and predictive quotients are
strictly finer than the standard classes \(P\) and \(NP\) at the
history level, but this strictness can be lost under standard
language-level projection.

\label{def:autonomous-lift}
Let \(\sigma\) be a computational substrate.  An
\emph{autonomous lift} on \(\sigma\) is a typed object
\[
  L=(\mathrm{gen}_{L},\sigma_{L},\mathrm{replay}_{L})
\]
with the following components:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(\mathrm{gen}_{L}\) is a deterministic polynomial-time
  history-generation procedure.  In plain terms, it is a deterministic
  polynomial-time algorithm that, given the substrate input and the
  prior trace data, extends the computation history by one audited
  step.
  \item \(\sigma_{L}:H_{\sigma}^{L}\to S\) is the internal-state
  readout of the lift, where \(S\) is the lift's finite typed state
  space.  The value \(\sigma_{L}(h)\) records the internal determining
  state of the procedure at the history \(h\).
  \item \(\mathrm{replay}_{L}\) is the all-input replay record for
  \(\mathrm{gen}_{L}\): an audited machine-index and
  time-certificate object that allows the same polynomial-time
  procedure to be reproduced on any input.  This is the audit-side
  bookkeeping supplied by the \(\mathsf{FATCD}\) discipline
  \citep{TsiokosFoundationsII2026}.\footnote{The autonomous lift is
  realized in Lean by the autonomous-lift declaration listed in
  \Cref{app:formalization}; the Lean record exposes additional
  family-characterizing predicates beyond the components named in the
  definition above.  The narrowing-disclosure discipline is recorded in
  \Cref{app:formalization}.}
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: The later csl statement refers to a four-level strength stratification StrengthClass 1 ,\ StrengthClass 2 ,\ StrengthClass 3 ,\ StrengthClass 4 for coupling functions used inside gen_ L . The levels should be read as a graded family of implementation strengths: StrengthClass 1 is trivial or absent coupling, StrengthClass 2 is weak coupling such as linear feedback, StrengthClass 3 is standard cryptographic-strength coupling in the sense of pseudorandom-function families , and StrengthClass 4 is beyond-cryptographic-strength coupling . These labels are not formalized here as complexity classes. They are placeholders for any fixed four-level grading of coupling strength. expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:visibility-coupling}
Let \(\sigma\) be a computational substrate, let \(L\) be an
autonomous lift on \(\sigma\), and write
\(\sigma_{L}:H_{\sigma}^{L}\to S\) for its internal-state readout.
The \emph{visibility coupling predicate}
\(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\) holds if and only if there exist an
observable codomain \(\mathcal O\), a declared polynomial-time current
observable
\[
  \varphi_{Q}:H_{\sigma}^{L}\to\mathcal O,
\]
and a polynomial-time function \(f:S\to\mathcal O\) such that
\[
  \bigl(\exists h,h'\inH_{\sigma}^{L},\,
      f(\sigma_{L}(h))\neq f(\sigma_{L}(h'))\bigr)
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \bigl(\forall h\inH_{\sigma}^{L},\,
      \varphi_{Q}(h)=f(\sigma_{L}(h))\bigr).
\]

\label{lem:csl-core}
Let \(\sigma\) be a computational substrate, let \(L\) be an
autonomous lift on \(\sigma\), and let \(L_{\mathrm{traceFP}}\) be
the trace-fingerprint loop class on \(H_{\sigma}^{L}\).  Assume the six
structural premises (a)--(f) above.  Then the following four clauses
hold.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Dissolution.}  If \(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\) holds
  and \((\sigma,L)\) has predictive witness content, then for
  every loop \(\ell\inL_{\mathrm{traceFP}}\) and every history
  \(h\inH_{\sigma}^{L}\),
  \[
    \Mclass{\ell.h}\neq\Mclass{h}
    \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    \Qclass{\ell.h}\neq\Qclass{h}.
  \]
  Equivalently, the M-vs-Q loop-action asymmetry fails: every
  M-class change is accompanied by a Q-class change.

  \item \emph{Preservation.}  If \(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\) fails
  and \((\sigma,L)\) has predictive witness content, then
  there exist a loop \(\ell\inL_{\mathrm{traceFP}}\) and a history
  \(h\inH_{\sigma}^{L}\) such that
  \[
    \LoopActionQ{\ell}{h}=\Qclass{h}
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \LoopActionM{\ell}{h}\neq\Mclass{h}.
  \]
  The M-vs-Q loop-action asymmetry holds.

  \item \emph{Degenerate.}  If \((\sigma,L)\) has no
  predictive witness content, then \(M_{\sigma}^{L}=Q_{\sigma}^{L}\) on the
  support of \(H_{\sigma}^{L}\), and the M-vs-Q distinction is vacuous.

  \item \emph{Strength-independence.}  Given the value of
  \(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\), the dissolution or preservation
  status of the loop-action asymmetry does not depend on the strength
  class \(\StrengthClass{k}\) of the coupling function used inside
  the lift's generation procedure.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lem:csl-core}
Let \(\Substrate\) be a computational substrate, let \(\Lift\) be an
autonomous lift on \(\Substrate\), and let \(\TraceFPLoopClass\) be
the trace-fingerprint loop class on \(\HistorySpace\).  Assume the six
structural premises (a)--(f) above.  Then the following four clauses
hold.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Dissolution.}  If \(\Exposure(\Lift,\Substrate)\) holds
  and \((\Substrate,\Lift)\) has predictive witness content, then for
  every loop \(\ell\in\TraceFPLoopClass\) and every history
  \(h\in\HistorySpace\),
  \[
    \Mclass{\ell.h}\neq\Mclass{h}
    \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    \Qclass{\ell.h}\neq\Qclass{h}.
  \]
  Equivalently, the M-vs-Q loop-action asymmetry fails: every
  M-class change is accompanied by a Q-class change.

  \item \emph{Preservation.}  If \(\Exposure(\Lift,\Substrate)\) fails
  and \((\Substrate,\Lift)\) has predictive witness content, then
  there exist a loop \(\ell\in\TraceFPLoopClass\) and a history
  \(h\in\HistorySpace\) such that
  \[
    \LoopActionQ{\ell}{h}=\Qclass{h}
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \LoopActionM{\ell}{h}\neq\Mclass{h}.
  \]
  The M-vs-Q loop-action asymmetry holds.

  \item \emph{Degenerate.}  If \((\Substrate,\Lift)\) has no
  predictive witness content, then \(\Mquotient=\Qquotient\) on the
  support of \(\HistorySpace\), and the M-vs-Q distinction is vacuous.

  \item \emph{Strength-independence.}  Given the value of
  \(\Exposure(\Lift,\Substrate)\), the dissolution or preservation
  status of the loop-action asymmetry does not depend on the strength
  class \(\StrengthClass{k}\) of the coupling function used inside
  the lift's generation procedure.
\end{enumerate}

  \citep{BirchSwinnertonDyer1965NotesII}, read here through
  elliptic-curve regulator content
  \citep{Silverman2009ArithmeticEllipticCurves}, admits autonomous
  lifts that are witness-content-exposing.

  \citep{Fefferman2006NavierStokesClay}, read here through
  weak-solution selection content \citep{Leray1934LiquideVisqueux},
  admits autonomous lifts that are witness-content-exposing.

  \citep{Cook2000PNPClay}, read here through satisfying-assignment
  witness content for \(3\)-SAT \citep{Cook1971TheoremProving}, admits
  autonomous lifts that are trace-state-exposing but not
  witness-content-exposing under the polynomial-time current instrument.

  \item \emph{RH substrate.}  The Riemann-hypothesis substrate
  \citep{Bombieri2000RiemannClay}, read here through zeta-zero
  certificate content \citep{Conrey2003RiemannHypothesis}, admits
  autonomous lifts that are trace-state-exposing but not
  witness-content-exposing under the polynomial-time current instrument.
\end{enumerate}
In each case the lift's existence and its classification are
framework-internal facts about the substrate's adequacy-residual
machinery.  The classification records which exposure channel,
witness-content or trace-state, is available under the framework's
lawful instrument.

conclusion: The projection pi_ QP is not a bijection from Q_ sigma ^ L onto the standard class P . The obstruction has three parts. Histories versus languages. A Q_ sigma ^ L -class is a class of histories, possibly over a single bounded instance. A polynomial-time decision predicate is a function on all inputs. A single current class does not by itself define a language predicate over all input strings. Trace observables beyond decision output. The quotient Q_ sigma ^ L identifies histories by equality of all declared polynomial-time current observables, not merely by equality of the decision bit. Two histories computing the same language may still be Q_ sigma ^ L -distinct because their trace, solver-prefix, or audit bookkeeping observables differ. Machine multiplicity. Different polynomial-time machines may decide the same language while producing different Q_ sigma ^ L -observable histories on the same instance. These histories can map to different current classes but to the same language predicate.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:c1-not-bijective}
The projection \(\pi_{QP}\) is not a bijection from \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\) onto
the standard class \(P\).  The obstruction has three parts.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Histories versus languages.}  A \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\)-class is
  a class of histories, possibly over a single bounded instance.  A
  polynomial-time decision predicate is a function on all inputs.  A
  single current class does not by itself define a language predicate
  over all input strings.

  \item \emph{Trace observables beyond decision output.}  The quotient
  \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\) identifies histories by equality of all declared
  polynomial-time current observables, not merely by equality of the
  decision bit.  Two histories computing the same language may still be
  \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\)-distinct because their trace, solver-prefix, or audit
  bookkeeping observables differ.

  \item \emph{Machine multiplicity.}  Different polynomial-time
  machines may decide the same language while producing different
  \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\)-observable histories on the same instance.  These
  histories can map to different current classes but to the same
  language predicate.
\end{enumerate}

source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:c1-not-bijective}
The projection \(\PiQP\) is not a bijection from \(\Qquotient\) onto
the standard class \(P\).  The obstruction has three parts.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Histories versus languages.}  A \(\Qquotient\)-class is
  a class of histories, possibly over a single bounded instance.  A
  polynomial-time decision predicate is a function on all inputs.  A
  single current class does not by itself define a language predicate
  over all input strings.

  \item \emph{Trace observables beyond decision output.}  The quotient
  \(\Qquotient\) identifies histories by equality of all declared
  polynomial-time current observables, not merely by equality of the
  decision bit.  Two histories computing the same language may still be
  \(\Qquotient\)-distinct because their trace, solver-prefix, or audit
  bookkeeping observables differ.

  \item \emph{Machine multiplicity.}  Different polynomial-time
  machines may decide the same language while producing different
  \(\Qquotient\)-observable histories on the same instance.  These
  histories can map to different current classes but to the same
  language predicate.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: Given two probe families on the same finite-dimensional carrier, this paper asks what a dissolving family D measures beyond what a native family L can explain under an audit energy C . Under the standing legal-energy quotient and null-mode legality hypotheses, the adequacy residual _C(D L) is the Schur-complement leftover built from the block currencies K_ LL , K_ DD , K_ DL , and K_ LD . We develop this residual as a calculus: the projection identity identifies it with T_D(I-P_L)T_D^* in energy-scaled coordinates; optimality and exact adequacy characterize Loewner minimality and zero residual; promotion combines native and residual budgets into a dissolving budget; and chain-rule, data-processing, and transfer laws describe native extension, post-processing, coarsening, and exact or defective bridges. The blind-spot witness theorem turns failure of a declared residual budget into an explicit recombination vector with positive excess. The paper does not claim exact adequacy generically, does not classify all probe-family pairs, and does not claim novelty for the classical operator-theoretic constructions it packages. A layer-dissolving use of the calculus is given in .

conclusion: The paper does not claim that every raw substrate sees every dissolving probe, nor that the residual vanishes generically Finally, the paper does not claim novelty for the classical constructions it uses, such as Schur complements, Moore–Penrose pseudoinverses, projection identities, and Douglas-style factorization.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The scope is deliberately narrow.  The paper does not claim that every raw
substrate sees every dissolving probe, nor that the residual vanishes
generically; exact adequacy is a hypothesis to be verified, not a default
state.  It also does not transfer a residual computed from a coarse view to an
intrinsic fine view without an audited bridge: such transfer requires the exact
or defective bridge machinery developed later.  A residual bound at one
accepted finite stage is not treated as predictive adequacy across an indexed
family.  Finally, the paper does not claim novelty for the classical
constructions it uses, such as Schur complements, Moore--Penrose
pseudoinverses, projection identities, and Douglas-style factorization.  The
contribution is one audited residual package: projection, optimality,
exactness, extension, data processing, transfer, and blind-spot witness laws
for the same Schur-complement object.

conclusion: Let E be a finite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert space. An audit energy on E is a self-adjoint positive-semidefinite operator C=C^* 0 on E . The audit cost of a carrier vector u∈ E is the quadratic form u^*Cu , and the kernel Ker C consists of the zero-audit-cost directions.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:xi:audit-energy}
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert space.  An
\emph{audit energy} on \(E\) is a self-adjoint positive-semidefinite operator
\(C=C^*\succeq 0\) on \(E\).  The audit cost of a carrier vector \(u\in E\) is
the quadratic form \(u^*Cu\), and the kernel \(\Ker C\) consists of the
zero-audit-cost directions.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:xi:legal-energy-quotient}
The \emph{legal energy quotient} of \((E,C)\) is the orthogonal complement
\[
  E_C=(\Ker C)^\perp\subseteq E,
\]
together with the restricted audit form
\[
  C_0=C|_{E_C}>0
\]
which is strictly positive on \(E_C\).  The \emph{Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse}
\(C^\dagger\), following
\citet{Penrose1955GeneralizedInverse,BenIsraelGreville2003GeneralizedInverses},
acts as \(C_0^{-1}\) on \(E_C\) and as zero on \(\Ker C\).

For \(z\in Y\), define

conclusion: This section gives the central object of the paper. With the standing hypotheses of and the probe-family currency of in place, the joint native-dissolving currency matrix decomposes into four blocks. The adequacy residual is the Schur complement of the native block : the leftover content of the dissolving block after the native block has explained as much as it can. [Native, dissolving, and joint block currencies] Let L: E→ Y and D: E→ Z be null-legal probe families (in the sense of ), with restrictions L_0,D_0 . The native, dissolving, and cross currencies are K_ LL =L_0C_0^ -1 L_0^*, K_ DL =D_0C_0^ -1 L_0^*, K_ LD =L_0C_0^ -1 D_0^*, K_ DD =D_0C_0^ -1 D_0^*. Here K_ LL =K_F for F=L and K_ DD =K_F for F=D in the probe-family currency of . Equivalently, K_ LL and K_ DD are positive semidefinite operators on Y and Z respectively; K_ DL and K_ LD =K_ DL ^* are the corresponding rectangular cross operators. The joint currency matrix of the combined family (L,D) is K(D,L) = K_ LL K_ LD K_ DL K_ DD .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
This section gives the central object of the paper.  With the standing
hypotheses of \Cref{sec:setup} and the probe-family currency of
\Cref{sec:currency} in place, the joint native-dissolving currency matrix
decomposes into four blocks.  The adequacy residual is the Schur complement of
the native block
\citep{Schur1917Potenzreihen,Haynsworth1968Inertia,Albert1969PSDPartitioned,Cottle1974Manifestations,Zhang2005SchurApplications,HornJohnson2013MatrixAnalysis}:

\begin{definition}[Native, dissolving, and joint block currencies]\label{def:xi:block-currencies}

the sense of \Cref{def:xi:null-legal-probe-family}), with restrictions
\(L_0,D_0\).  The \emph{native, dissolving, and cross currencies} are
\[
  K_{LL}=L_0C_0^{-1}L_0^*,

  K_{DL}=D_0C_0^{-1}L_0^*,
\]
\[
  K_{LD}=L_0C_0^{-1}D_0^*,
  \qquad
  K_{DD}=D_0C_0^{-1}D_0^*.
\]

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The projection theorem gives the geometric meaning of the adequacy residual.
After rescaling by the square root of the audit energy, the native and
dissolving probes become ordinary linear maps in energy-scaled coordinates.  In
those coordinates, the residual is the dissolving readout after projecting away
the part already explained by the native probe range.  Positive
semidefiniteness of \(\Xi_C(D\mid L)\) follows directly from this formulation.

\begin{definition}[Energy-scaled probes and native-explanation projection]\label{def:xi:energy-scaled-probes}
The \emph{energy-scaled native and dissolving probes} are
\[
  T_L=L_0C_0^{-1/2},
  \qquad
  T_D=D_0C_0^{-1/2}.
\]
Here \(C_0^{1/2}\) is the unique positive square root of \(C_0\) on \(E_C\)
\citep{Higham2008Functions,Bhatia2007PositiveDefinite}.  The
\emph{native-explanation projection} \(P_L\) is the orthogonal projection in
\(E_C\) onto
\[
  \Ran(T_L^*)\subseteq E_C,
\]
the native probe range in the energy-scaled coordinate system.
\end{definition}

\label{def:xi:optimal-explanation-map}
Given native and dissolving probe families \(L,D\) and their block currencies
\(K_{LL},K_{DL}\) of \Cref{def:xi:block-currencies}, the \emph{optimal native

\label{def:xi:extended-native-family}
Let \(M\colon E\to W\) be an additional null-legal native probe family.  The
\emph{extended native family} is
\[
  L^+
  =
  \begin{bmatrix}
    L\\
    M
  \end{bmatrix}
  \colon E\to Y\oplus W,
  \qquad
  L^+u=(Lu,Mu),
\]
which is null-legal because \(L\) and \(M\) both vanish on \(\Ker C\).  The
\emph{conditional native currency of \(M\) given \(L\)} is the Schur complement
\[
  K_{MM\mid L}
  =
  K_{MM}-K_{ML}K_{LL}^\dagger K_{LM},
\]
also known as the shorted operator of \(K_{MM}\) by the \(L\)-block
\citep{AndersonWN1971Shorted,AndersonTrapp1975ShortedII}.  The
\emph{conditional dissolving-extension cross currency} is
\[
  K_{DM\mid L}
  =
  K_{DM}-K_{DL}K_{LL}^\dagger K_{LM},
  \qquad
  K_{MD\mid L}=K_{DM\mid L}^*.
\]
The conditional joint currency block is positive semidefinite, so in
particular \(K_{MM\mid L}\succeq 0\) on \(W\); the rectangular cross
block \(K_{DM\mid L}\) is paired with its adjoint \(K_{MD\mid L}\).
\(K_{MM\mid L}\) vanishes precisely when the added probes \(M\) are
already explained by \(L\) on the legal quotient.

\item \emph{Nonclaim or gating} narrows the scope of the claim by excluding
  the offending response direction instead of proving adequacy for it.
\end{enumerate}
Same-family repetition saturates this list: repeating an old probe, or
repackaging the same native data, does not lower the witness because it does
not change \(\Xi_C(D\mid L)\), as shown by
\Cref{cor:xi:same-family-saturation}.  Thus a repair that merely renames the
existing native family is not a residual repair.  This catalog is the dual of
the all-six repair language of \citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}: here the same
distinction is expressed entirely in residual-budget terms.

source_wording_tex:
\item \emph{Nonclaim or gating} narrows the scope of the claim by excluding
  the offending response direction instead of proving adequacy for it.
\end{enumerate}
Same-family repetition saturates this list: repeating an old probe, or
repackaging the same native data, does not lower the witness because it does
not change \(\Xi_C(D\mid L)\), as shown by
\Cref{cor:xi:same-family-saturation}.  Thus a repair that merely renames the
existing native family is not a residual repair.  This catalog is the dual of
the all-six repair language of \citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}: here the same
distinction is expressed entirely in residual-budget terms.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The local mathematical tools are classical.  The construction uses Schur
complements, Moore--Penrose pseudoinverses, the projection identity
\[
  T_L^*(T_LT_L^*)^\dagger T_L
\]
as the orthogonal projection onto \(\Ran(T_L^*)\), and Douglas-style
factorization ideas behind the range-inclusion arguments for faithful
reparameterizations and bridges.  The paper does not claim novelty for those
operator-theoretic ingredients.  Its contribution is the framing: the Schur
complement is treated as an audited residual currency, with projection,
optimality, exactness, extension, data-processing, transfer, and witness laws
all stated against one energy quotient and one null-mode legality discipline.
This is why the object is not merely a block-matrix calculation but a residual
accounting device.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Several scope fences are therefore part of the claim.  The paper does not
assert that every raw substrate sees every dissolving probe, and it does not
assert that \(\Xi_C(D\mid L)=0\) generically; exact adequacy is a hypothesis to
verify, not a default state.  It does not promote a coarse residual view to an
intrinsic fine-grained residual without an audited bridge, and it does not
treat a finite-stage adequacy statement as predictive adequacy across an
indexed family.  Finally, it does not claim novelty for Schur complements,
pseudoinverses, projection identities, or Douglas-style factorization.  The
claim is the residual-calculus packaging under the stated hypotheses.

conclusion: Many obstruction arguments exhibit a localized failure mode that appears irreducible at the layer where it is first visible; this paper studies one audited route by which such needle obstructions cease to be obstructions, namely passage to a higher layer where additional admissible dissolving probes are available. The framework is the formed-layer membrane setting: zero-energy directions are removed by a legal quotient, native probes are assigned a quadratic native currency, unexplained dissolving currency is measured by an adequacy residual, and predictive membranes, dissolving transport records, and the all-six taxonomy control the transfer. The layer-dissolving endpoint theorem shows that, under predictive native bounds, residual bounds, and transport hypotheses, the dissolving currency is bounded uniformly across accepted stages, so no layer-dissolving predictive needles exist within the declared scope. The complementary duality-confinement membrane theorem shows that, under a separating anti-invariant readout and a vanishing-trace sequence of domination records, visible object mass is confined to the fixed locus of the involution. These are framework-bound dissolution results, not a universal singularity-elimination theorem or a claim about any named external problem. The adequacy-residual calculus on which the layer-dissolving endpoint depends is developed in .

irreducible at the layer where it is first visible; this paper studies
one audited route by which such needle obstructions cease to be
obstructions, namely passage to a higher layer where additional
admissible dissolving probes are available.  The framework is the
formed-layer membrane setting: zero-energy directions are removed by a
legal quotient, native probes are assigned a quadratic native currency,
unexplained dissolving currency is measured by an adequacy residual, and
predictive membranes, dissolving transport records, and the all-six

within the declared scope.  The complementary duality-confinement

In many applications the native data is not accepted all at once.  It is
assembled stage by stage: by refinement, enlargement, or passage to an
accepted stage.  At an accepted stage \(j\), we have a stage-local
instance of the framework from \Cref{sec:framework}: a carrier, an audit
energy \(C_j\), an exact package \(\Gamma_j\), a native probe family
\(L_j\) with its response space, and a routing map \(R_j\) into a common
response target.  The predictive currency at stage \(j\) is the
packaged native currency for these data, transported by \(R_j\).

Informally, the predictive currency is
\[
  \widehat K_j
  =R_jL_j\Gamma_j(\Gamma_j^*C_j\Gamma_j)^\dagger
    \Gamma_j^*L_j^*R_j^*.
\]
The middle block
\[
  L_j\Gamma_j(\Gamma_j^*C_j\Gamma_j)^\dagger\Gamma_j^*L_j^*
\]
is the stage-local instance of the packaged native currency
\(\K_{C_j,\Gamma_j}(L_j)\) from \Cref{sec:framework}; the outer
conjugation by \(R_j\) places that currency in the common response
space.  As before, this expression is variationally meaningful only
when \(L_j\Gamma_j\) is null-legal for the packaged audit
\(\Gamma_j^*C_j\Gamma_j\), which is the legal-quotient discipline of
\Cref{sec:framework} applied at stage \(j\).

conclusion: The previous section priced a layer-dissolving probe family against a native one through the adequacy interface. The complementary geometric setting occurs when the layer carries an involutive duality, such as an anti-linear or anti-isometric symmetry, and the question is whether visible object mass is confined to the duality's fixed locus. The framework theorem of this section gives conditions under which anti-invariant membrane collapse implies object-side confinement to that fixed locus. Both main results inhabit the same formed-layer theory; they differ in what is priced and what is confined.

Define P_-:= I- J 2 , psi_-(x):=P_-psi(x). expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:main:involutive-ledger}
An involutive object ledger is a tuple
\[
  \mathfrak X=(X,J,\mu,\psi,Y,\mathcal J),
\]
where:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \(X\) is the visible object space;
\item \(J:X\to X\) is an involution;
\item \(\mu\) is a positive object ledger measure, meaning a positive
  Radon-type measure on \(X\), or a finite positive weight system on
  \(X\);
\item \(Y\) is a real Hilbert response space;
\item \(\mathcal J:Y\to Y\) is a linear isometric involution;
\item \(\psi:X\to Y\) is an equivariant readout:
\[
  \psi(Jx)=\mathcal J\psi(x).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Define
\[
  P_-:=\frac{I-\mathcal J}{2},\qquad \psi_-(x):=P_-\psi(x).
\]
Here \(P_-\) is the spectral projection onto the \(-1\)-eigenspace
of the isometric involution \(\mathcal J\), which is the standard
anti-invariant decomposition for an involution on a Hilbert space
\citep{Conway1990FunctionalAnalysis}.
The anti-invariant object ledger is
\[
  \mathsf A_X:=\int_X \psi_-(x)\psi_-(x)^*\,d\mu(x),
\]
interpreted in the finite-rank or trace-class sense whenever required.

conclusion: retests the same block
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The framework allows only certain repairs to such a failure.  A repair
is lawful if it excludes the offending recombination by a declared
nonclaim, weakens the claim by raising the relevant budget, strengthens
or rewrites the carrier and audit so that the legal quotient has
changed, adds native probes that see the residual direction, or
completes the missing protocol or transport family and then retests the
same block.  These options are deliberately narrow: they change either
the scope of the claim, the budget being asserted, the legal carrier on
which the currency is computed, the probe family available to explain
the residual, or the transfer record that transports the budget.  By
contrast, same-package repetition saturates.  Repeating the same
Schur-block repair with no new probe content, no new audit, and no new
transport data does not change the residual and therefore cannot remove
the critical pair.

conclusion: Across disciplines, stable descriptive layers rely on small sets of variables that budget feasibility, accumulate along protocols, or appear as exchange rates between incompatible objectives. We call such variables currencies. This paper gives a layer-relative definition of currency within the Six Birds closure calculus and proposes a currency–constraint principle: lower-layer currencies become higher-layer constraints because packaged higher-level objects can persist only under bounded lower-layer spending, while higher-layer currencies emerge as the shadow prices of those budgets. In finite Markov laboratories this principle becomes measurable. Path-reversal asymmetry and cycle affinities furnish lower-layer audits; constrained maximum-entropy closure yields dual prices; and across a resolution ladder we observe five robust signatures: honest coarse-grained directionality, monotone price emergence with a slack regime, growth of currency dimension with resolution, failure of proxy currencies under prediction and dual stability, and improved packaging coherence under stronger budget enforcement. A Lean formalization proves deterministic-pushforward monotonicity for a finite KL form, providing a formal anchor for the audit side of the story. The result is a practical and conceptual account of why temperatures, prices, regularizers, and attention weights recur across sciences as the same mathematical kind of object.

conclusion: Scoped event admissibility on fixed support leaves a specific gap for strict tests: the protocol-indexed flagship-seed bridge family realizes the quadratic-levelset and transition-stability slots, but the protocol-indexed readout-agreement slot remains unrealized, so no accepted strict test family is available at the bridge-native event level. This paper asks whether strict-test acceptance is admissible on fixed support without repairing that bridge level. The method is a layer-local, audit-based PICA route: promotion, internalization of protocol coordinates, carrier exactification, and audited source admission produce a carrier substrate above the bridge-native level. On the resulting carriers, the readout-agreement, quadratic-witness, and transition-witness slots are strict-realized natively; the three-slot strict domain closes; and accepted scoped strict test families survive the required control panel. The panel covers null-baseline, memory-only, artifact, boundary, selected-lift, visibility, and claim-boundary checks. The bridge-native level is retained as the : descent from new-layer evidence to old-layer compatibility preserves non-factorization without inducing old-layer strict realization. The final classification is a strict theory extension at the new layer with old-layer real-provisional compatibility intact. The result is bounded: it does not assert event-package construction, shared-event identity, proto-effect or effect-algebra structure, Born valuation, composition readiness, faithful public compression, a lawful public carrier, or canonical selected lifts.

boundary, including the scoped event positives inherited from Paper~8
\cite{Tsiokos2026CarrierToEvent}.  The explicit nonclaims are stronger
structures not asserted here: an event package, a proto-effect fragment, an
effect algebra, a Born valuation, composition readiness, faithful public
compression, a lawful public carrier, and a canonical selected lift.

conclusion: The candidate objects for the PICA route are the three live one-layer-up surfaces retained by the carrier-exactification enumeration . The lifted-package surface records the packaged higher-level lift data; the protocol-indexed higher-witness surface organizes candidate witness data by the protocol coordinates that will remain in scope; and the completion-family surface records the completion-side family structure needed for later carrier formation. These surfaces are also constrained by the internal-structure analysis of . They are named here as methodological inputs, not as already exactified carriers or strict-test evidence. The promotion gate applies the six-criterion test of . In prose, the candidate must be sufficient on the designated observables, induce closure of the update law, remain stable at the second stage under admissible recoarsening, be admissible against the matched controls, preserve protocol honesty by avoiding smuggled claims, and remain legible on at least one designated slice. Each of the lifted-package, protocol-indexed higher-witness, and completion-family surfaces passes all six criteria. The result is the three promoted candidates that proceed to carrier exactification in .

Each exactified carrier carries a carrier-side non-factorization certificate:
its native state space, transport law, and readout law do not factor through the
bridge-native \OldLayer{} description.  Equivalently, the carrier cannot be
reconstructed from old-layer data alone.  This is the carrier-level instance of
the foundations non-factorization condition for a strict extension
\cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII}, applied to the exactified carrier structures
of \cite{Tsiokos2026CarrierExactification}.

The certificate is methodological.  It records why the \NewLayer{} carriers are
not reformulations of bridge-native data and supplies the structural
prerequisite for the final strict-extension verdict of \Cref{sec:final-gate}.
The descent-side statement that this non-factorization is preserved when
new-layer evidence is translated back to old-layer compatibility is separate
and is recorded in \Cref{subsec:non-factorization-preservation}.

Strict-test acceptance certifies that, on each H6 carrier, the family
criteria pass and the controls survive.  It does not provide a packaging
operator over the accepted families, an identification of shared events across
families, or any compositional structure linking the three carriers as a single
algebraic object.  Under the claim/nonclaim discipline of
\cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII}, those are additional structural moves, not
consequences of test-family acceptance.  The event-packaging structures
introduced in \cite{Tsiokos2026LocallyBoolean} and bounded at the event bridge
in \cite{Tsiokos2026CarrierToEvent} therefore remain explicit nonclaims in
Paper~9.

An event package would require a packaging operator that respects
shared-event identification across the three accepted families and remains
audited under the foundations framework.  A shared-event identity claim would
require a verified equivalence among events from different families on a common
comparison base \cite{Tsiokos2026LocallyBoolean}.  Neither structure is
constructed here.  The claim-boundary control of
\Cref{subsec:protocol-honesty-claim-boundary} is the audit-side check that
these structures are not imported into the acceptance result.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The selected-lift discipline of \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII} allows level
crossings to record selected lifts without making any one lift canonical.
Paper~9's strict-extension verdict respects this discipline: it does not
claim that a particular lift is uniquely admissible, and the selected-lift
variation control of \Cref{subsec:selected-lift-visibility-controls} certifies
that the accepted families survive admissible variation.  A canonical selected
lift would assert that one section across the layer transition is privileged;
such a claim would conflict with the descent-and-no-section structure of
\Cref{subsec:non-factorization-baseline,subsec:non-factorization-preservation}.
Non-factorization and selected-lift nonuniqueness are therefore complementary:
the H6 carrier admits no inverse reconstruction, and no particular
lift across the transition is canonical.  The acceptance result lives within
both constraints.  These constraints shape the discussion of
\Cref{sec:discussion}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
This section records the schema-level support behind the gate logic of
Paper~9.  The formal layer consists of theorem schemas that codify the
discipline by which threshold attachment, slot realization, test-family
acceptance, descent compatibility, and the legality constraints of the final
gate are organized.  The schemas are inherited from the foundations layer
\cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII} and follow the convention of Paper~8
\cite{Tsiokos2026CarrierToEvent}: formal support is a typed mirror of the gate
discipline, not an independent derivation of empirical content.

The schemas check legality and gate compatibility.  They do not prove that the
H6 carriers exist, that source-backed threshold evidence is present,
or that the controls pass; those empirical premises are supplied by the methods
and results sections \Cref{sec:methods,sec:primary-results,sec:secondary-results}.
The role of this section is conditional: if the empirical premises hold, then
the resulting claims obey the paper's internal discipline.  The schemas proceed
in order: source-policy admission required for threshold realization
(\Cref{subsec:schema-source-policy-threshold}), promotion versus carrier
exactification (\Cref{subsec:schema-promotion-not-exactification}),
exactified-carrier attachment licensing new-layer slots
(\Cref{subsec:schema-attachment-licenses-slot}), new-layer slots licensing
new-layer test-family reassembly (\Cref{subsec:schema-slots-license-tests}),
the real-provisional old layer blocking old-layer tests but not new-layer tests
(\Cref{subsec:schema-old-blocks-old-only}), unrealized required new-layer slots
blocking accepted new-layer strict tests
(\Cref{subsec:schema-unrealized-blocks-test}), and the boundary on what the
formal layer does not prove (\Cref{subsec:schema-legality-not-existence}).

conclusion: The final gate is an ordered case analysis over the upstream audits from . The principal positive case is reached when the native H6 strict domain closes, the strict test families on the new-layer carrier survive controls, and descent preserves old-layer compatibility without turning H2 into a strict-realized layer. Three weaker positive cases are reserved for incomplete new-layer evidence: a threshold-only case in which the new-layer readout slot is strict-realized but test-family reassembly is unavailable; a real-provisional case in which the route preserves or improves support without a completed threshold-and-slot gate; and a below-threshold or pending case. The same case analysis contains five blocking cases and two terminal negative cases. A blocker case obtains if promotion supplies no surviving object, if promotion survives but carrier exactification does not, if exactified threshold evidence cannot descend compatibly to the old layer, if source-policy admission blocks the source use, or if public-shadow safety blocks the route. A falsification case is legal only when neither old-layer nor new-layer threshold, readout, real-provisional, or below-threshold evidence remains. A separate implementation-failure case is reserved for malformed or unavailable artifacts, not for mathematical absence.

case in which the route preserves or improves support without a completed
threshold-and-slot gate; and a below-threshold or pending case.

The same case analysis contains five blocking cases and two terminal negative
cases.  A blocker case obtains if promotion supplies no surviving object, if
promotion survives but carrier exactification does not, if exactified threshold
evidence cannot descend compatibly to the old layer, if source-policy admission
blocks the source use, or if public-shadow safety blocks the route.  A
falsification case is legal only when neither old-layer nor new-layer threshold,
readout, real-provisional, or below-threshold evidence remains.  A separate
implementation-failure case is reserved for malformed or unavailable artifacts,
not for mathematical absence.

conclusion: The main limitations are structural. The accepted strict test families do not constitute an event package, a proto-effect fragment, an effect algebra, a Born valuation, or a composition-ready structure. Those remain explicit nonclaims, for the reasons given in : each would require additional construction beyond strict-test acceptance. They are future-work targets rather than negative results. Public-shadow nonfaithfulness and selected-lift nonuniqueness also remain part of the result's scope. They are not incidental caveats; they are structural conditions that keep the strict extension from collapsing into a public-shadow or canonical-lift reconstruction, as discussed in . Finally, Paper 9 is scoped to the flagship-only protocol-indexed setting. Global, cross-seed, and full-core test claims are out of scope here. Whether the carrier exactification framework of can be extended to broader support is a methodological question for a successor paper.

conclusion: Earlier fixed-support papers in Six Birds Theory introduced admissible event packages, predictive quotients, and recombination witnesses. They left open whether a recombination-positive witness family supports a genuine promoted package or only a lower-layer summary. We answer that question on a frozen Route A corpus. We define a promotion criterion requiring sufficiency on the designated observable surface, induced update closure, admissible second-stage stability, control admissibility, protocol honesty, and slice legibility. The corpus is exact-finite and controlled: a two-anchor flagship core, four nearby positives, and matched null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls, together with a support-only erasure comparison surface. We replace an earlier vacuous second-stage rule with an admissible surface-coarsening audit and treat the artifact control in paired protocol-aware form. On this pipeline, an intrinsic candidate package survives on both flagship anchors, covers the four nearby positives, preserves the required control contrasts, and remains honest under the paired artifact audit. Two representative-selected route families also survive on the flagship core, but only as secondary evidence: they do not support a unique best strategy and they do not displace the intrinsic survivor. Slice/dual analyses are support-only and the staging–packaging defect atlas is explanatory. A Lean criterion kernel formalizes the promotion vocabulary and the generic implication from the criterion fields to promoted-package status. The resulting claim is narrow: at least one promoted-package candidate survives honestly on fixed support in the Route A flagship family.
