conclusion: We ask whether a recombination-positive witness family supports a genuine promoted package or only a lower-layer summary. This section fixes the criterion vocabulary used throughout. The definitions are intentionally structural and route-family-level; they do not presuppose linearity, additivity, or a unique surviving package. Each individual field of the criterion has a recognizable neighbor in the existing literature; a consolidated positioning statement appears at the end of the section. [Candidate promoted package] Fix a common support surface together with a designated observable family and an admissible family of lower-layer operations. A candidate promoted package is an abstract package-level description intended to summarize lower-layer states or histories on that fixed-support surface. Its purpose is not merely to record a smaller state space but to provide a package on which the designated observables and admissible operations can be read without hidden dependence on arbitrary representatives. A candidate may be intrinsic, representative-selected, protocol-indexed, or otherwise structured, but it is always evaluated on the same frozen corpus and designated slice.

\label{def:promoted-package-criterion}
A candidate package counts as a \emph{promoted package} on the designated corpus and slice only if all of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Sufficiency.} The candidate supports the designated observable family on the frozen corpus.
\item \textbf{Induced closure.} The admissible lower-layer operations descend to a well-defined package-level update law.
\item \textbf{Second-stage stability.} The decisive structure survives admissible further coarse-graining, or else the candidate is rigid-minimal for explicit admissibility reasons rather than vacuous fragility.
\item \textbf{Control admissibility.} The candidate separates the required null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls in the right way.
\item \textbf{No-smuggling.} The candidate's apparent success does not depend on omitted protocol or scheduler variables that should have been internalized.
\item \textbf{Slice legibility.} On at least one designated slice, the candidate is not merely sufficient but distinguished as a frontier-level package.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: The intrinsic route P_ int is the main result because it survives on both flagship anchors, covers the four nearby positives, separates the required controls, and remains honest under the paired artifact audit without requiring representative-selected correction. The representative-selected routes refine that picture rather than replacing it. They show that the surviving-package surface on the flagship core is richer than a single route, but their support remains route-family-level: they do not justify a unique best strategy claim, and they do not displace the intrinsic route. If P_ int had failed and only a representative-selected route had survived, the natural reading would have shifted toward a lift-selected or protocol-indexed package. That is not the current evidential state. Interpreted modestly, this intrinsic-versus-representative asymmetry is closer to familiar contrasts between intrinsic state abstraction, predictive state, and selected refinement than to a claim that one universal abstraction recipe has been proved . The support layers are easier to interpret when kept in their proper place. The slice/dual analysis shows that the surviving-route picture is not exhausted by a single scalar tradeoff ordering: different slices can favor different material route families. This is informative but remains support-only and provisional. The staging–packaging defect atlas contributes explanatory route geometry; it is not a classifier and not even positively ordered in the simplest positive-versus-control way. It sharpens interpretation without entering the claim-bearing pipeline.

conclusion: Six Birds Theory constructs layered descriptions of a stochastic substrate without importing Hilbert space or the Born rule. Earlier papers in the series showed that the substrate supports interference-like recombination structure on fixed support and that at least one promoted package survives on the Route A flagship family, but left open the internal status of that survivor. We classify it here on a frozen exact-finite corpus consisting of two flagship anchors, four nearby positives, matched controls, and one support-only comparison row, comparing intrinsic, sectioned, bundle-section-fiber, and protocol-indexed candidates under descended readout, signature-level descended update, second-stage recoarsening, protocol honesty, invariant validation, and exact-finite quadratic probes. The verdict is an intrinsic package: on the flagship core and required controls the intrinsic nonindexed candidate is the only candidate that combines descended readout, a nontrivial second-stage stability plateau, retained invariant and quadratic families, and protocol honesty. The nearby positives remain anchor-only on the frozen exact readout surface, but carrier diagnostics and family-level quotient evidence support an erased-partner interpretation. Weak primitive-action participation and a flagship-local exact chart are recorded as downstream, non-gating diagnostics.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Scope.}
We classify the internal status of the surviving promoted object on the Route~A flagship family and its fixed comparison surface. conclusion: The intrinsic nonindexed candidate is the only candidate that survives the entire claim-bearing audit stack: the joint descended readout and signature-level update gate ( ), the nontrivial second-stage plateau ( ), and the retained invariant and quadratic families ( ). The sectioned and bundle-section-fiber candidates remain informative—their failure mode is closure ambiguity under section or fiber variation, not readout collapse—but they do not supply a stable promoted object. Dual augmentation adds no decisive improvement, and the protocol-indexed route does not displace the nonindexed intrinsic core. The verdict is the result of elimination on fixed support, not a choice among equally good summaries.

conclusion: Several limitations apply. First, the update surface remains signature-level rather than a full executable promoted dynamics. Second, the nearby-positive readout gap remains real on the current exact frozen readout surface; the erased-partner synthesis explains that gap but does not remove it. Third, no ambient additive or linear carrier model is claimed, and the flagship-local chart is not treated as evidence of such a carrier. Fourth, the bundle/dual and indexed routes remain comparison branches rather than final verdicts. conclusion: Earlier papers in the fixed-support line of Six Birds Theory established admissible event packages, predictive and recombination quotients, a control-stable Route A flagship corpus, promotion criteria, and the intrinsic promoted-package survivor. They left open the internal carrier status of that survivor. We introduce a carrier-level substrate on the same Route A flagship corpus, consisting of three state-like objects and one structural relation. The three objects are a lawful same-branch witness, a refined witness rung on which the same-branch transport and readout law exactifies; a coarse public signature shadow, which retains public signature role but not lawful transport; and a flagship-only protocol-indexed carrier surface, an autonomous lift of the witness on which protocol coordinates are first-class state data. The structural relation is non-faithful public compression: a projection from the witness to the public shadow that preserves public signature role but does not preserve the refined lawful structure. A seven-criterion exactification audit adapted from standard operational-theory methodology—readout sufficiency, transport and readout law, non-reducibility against the lower quotient baselines, section and protocol honesty, denominator and expansion stress, and cross-seed support—together with a refreshed section/protocol honesty rerun on the lifted flagship patch and a controlled adjacent-surface search stabilises the atlas. Three claim-bearing quadratic families and two proto-event/test families survive on the scoped carrier. Carrier law on the public surface, cross-seed carrier exactification, and full-core carrier exactification are not earned; those non-claims are preserved explicitly. A Lean formal layer records the criterion vocabulary and a typed mirror of the final verdict. The carrier atlas, with its scope and compression structure made explicit, is the substrate carried forward.

conclusion: The intrinsic promotion gate decides what kind of survivor the strengthening lane yields. The audited surviving candidate is intrinsic_naked_interface_witness_autonomous_protocol_lift , and its final promotion status is protocol_indexed_only. Two subordinate audits explain why the verdict stops there. The second-stage audit returns identity_only: only the identity proposal survives, and every nonidentity merge proposal collapses deterministic transport or witness retention, so the lane does not earn a deeper promoted object by merging away protocol distinctions. The signature-update audit returns indexed_signature_only, with the strongest blocking reason being that no overlap witness remains separated once coordinate tokens are stripped. The positive evidence disappears when protocol-coordinate indexing is removed.

conclusion: The strongest public, cross-seed, and full-core carrier claim is not licensed. The lawful same-branch witness is licensed. The public signature shadow remains coarse and non-faithfully related to that witness. A flagship-only, protocol-indexed carrier surface is licensed as the strongest survived positive carrier row, with the downstream quadratic and proto-event rows as secondary scoped structures on that same survivor. The final gate is positive but restricted. The scoped verdict is not a weakened version of a larger claim that almost landed. It is the verdict for the artifact surface the repository earned. The lawful witness/public-shadow split is central; the scoped carrier is real but indexed; the nearby positives remain real scope limitations; the stress, honesty, and adjacent-surface panels are part of the verdict; and the secondary quadratic and proto-event rows confirm only that the scoped survivor is nontrivial, not that it globalizes.

conclusion: By the end of Section , the empirical carrier gate is closed. The final verdict, the carrier atlas, the scope limitations, and the claim permissions are artifact-backed results of the pipeline. The formal layer gives a typed vocabulary for the carrier-exactification question, proves a kernel of abstract gating lemmas, mirrors the final scoped verdict in Lean-readable witness data, and separates those formal objects from the empirical rebuild surface. The paper relies on two kinds of support. Lean formalizes the vocabulary and the abstract implication structure of the gate; the canonical pipeline rebuilds or validates the empirical artifact surface. Neither layer is a theorem that the other is correct.

conclusion: A reduction from C to D on the same surface Sigma is a map phi : X_ C → X_ D satisfying, for all admissible arguments, V_ C (x) implies V_ D (phi(x)), rho_ C (s, x) implies rho_ D (s, phi(x)), lambda_ C (x, o) implies lambda_ D (phi(x), o), tau_ C (g, x, y) implies tau_ D (g, phi(x), phi(y)). We write C D when a reduction exists, and say C is non-reducible among a family \ D_i\ _ i ∈ I if C D_i for every i . This is the C3 comparator of Section .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
A \emph{reduction} from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{D}$ on the same surface $\Sigma$
is a map $\phi \colon X_{\mathcal{C}} \to X_{\mathcal{D}}$ satisfying, for all
admissible arguments,
\[
V_{\mathcal{C}}(x) \Rightarrow V_{\mathcal{D}}(\phi(x)), \qquad
\rho_{\mathcal{C}}(s, x) \Rightarrow \rho_{\mathcal{D}}(s, \phi(x)),
\]
\[
\lambda_{\mathcal{C}}(x, o) \Rightarrow \lambda_{\mathcal{D}}(\phi(x), o),
\qquad
\tau_{\mathcal{C}}(g, x, y) \Rightarrow \tau_{\mathcal{D}}(g, \phi(x), \phi(y)).
\]
We write $\mathcal{C} \preceq \mathcal{D}$ when a reduction exists, and say
$\mathcal{C}$ is \emph{non-reducible} among a family
$\{\mathcal{D}_i\}_{i \in I}$ if $\mathcal{C} \not\preceq \mathcal{D}_i$ for every
$i$. This is the C3 comparator of
Section~\ref{sec:candidate-classes-reductions-criteria}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:criterion-implication}
Let $\Sigma$ be a designated surface and $\mathcal{C}$ a carrier candidate on
$\Sigma$, and let $E$ be a full carrier-exactification evidence bundle for
$\mathcal{C}$ with designated seed scope
$\mathcal{S}_{\textup{des}} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$, witness families for section,
protocol, and expansion honesty, a seed-link relation, and a baseline family
$\{\mathcal{D}_i\}$. Then $\mathcal{C}$ satisfies the paper's seven criteria on
$\Sigma$: C1 via $\operatorname{RS}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{S}_{\textup{des}})$; C2
via $\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal{C})$ together with
$\operatorname{RTC}(\mathcal{C})$; C3 via $\mathcal{C} \not\preceq \mathcal{D}_i$
for every $i$; C4 via $\operatorname{SH}(\mathcal{C})$; C5 via
$\operatorname{PH}(\mathcal{C})$; C6 via $\operatorname{EH}(\mathcal{C})$; and C7
via $\operatorname{CS}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{S}_{\textup{des}})$. In addition, the
full evidence bundle yields the stronger transport-exactness predicate
$\operatorname{TE}(\mathcal{C})$.

source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:criterion-implication}
Let $\Sigma$ be a designated surface and $\mathcal{C}$ a carrier candidate on
$\Sigma$, and let $E$ be a full carrier-exactification evidence bundle for
$\mathcal{C}$ with designated seed scope
$\mathcal{S}_{\textup{des}} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$, witness families for section,
protocol, and expansion honesty, a seed-link relation, and a baseline family
$\{\mathcal{D}_i\}$. Then $\mathcal{C}$ satisfies the paper's seven criteria on
$\Sigma$: C1 via $\operatorname{RS}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{S}_{\textup{des}})$; C2
via $\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal{C})$ together with
$\operatorname{RTC}(\mathcal{C})$; C3 via $\mathcal{C} \not\preceq \mathcal{D}_i$
for every $i$; C4 via $\operatorname{SH}(\mathcal{C})$; C5 via
$\operatorname{PH}(\mathcal{C})$; C6 via $\operatorname{EH}(\mathcal{C})$; and C7
via $\operatorname{CS}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{S}_{\textup{des}})$. In addition, the
full evidence bundle yields the stronger transport-exactness predicate
$\operatorname{TE}(\mathcal{C})$.

conclusion: The limitations are structural. The surviving carrier remains flagship-only; protocol indexing remains required; the public surface remains signature_only; cross-seed reach remains partial, and the four nearby positives remain real scope limitations rather than exact transfers; the broader site-not-probe claim fails the honesty audit; route filtering remains unavailable; loop-action asymmetry is not found; C3 blocks strongest-new-carrier language for the richest surviving scoped carrier; no adjacent surface exactifies; and the scoped quadratic and proto-event results do not constitute a general geometry. These are the conditions under which the result is true, not corrections added afterward. How public readout and test structure should be studied from such a scoped carrier is a natural next question but is not taken up here.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The gate vocabulary used in \Cref{sec:final-gate-and-carrier-atlas} is best understood as
a controlled verdict ladder rather than as a single scalar score. At the law layer the
important statuses are \emph{lawful}, \emph{signature-only}, and \emph{collapse}. At the
compression layer the important statuses are \emph{faithful}, \emph{non-faithful}, and
\emph{not applicable}; the present paper uses only
\texttt{non\_faithful\_public\_compression} for the witness-to-public relation. At the
scope layer the main manuscript distinguishes \texttt{flagship\_only},
\texttt{cross\_seed}, \texttt{full\_core}, \texttt{support\_only}, and
\texttt{new\_surface\_candidate} rows.

The verdict layer is intentionally richer than ``carrier'' versus ``no carrier.'' Full
exactification, chart-only survival, descriptor/process-only survival, blocked lanes, and
protocol-indexed-only survival all belong to the same vocabulary. Ticket31 closes with the
verdict \texttt{protocol\_indexed\_carrier\_only}. That verdict should be read together
with the lawful witness row, the signature-only public shadow, the nearby-positive scope
limitations, and the scoped secondary flags. The gate vocabulary therefore preserves two
different kinds of positive statement at once: exactification at the refined witness level
and scoped survival at the lifted protocol-indexed level.

conclusion: Statements.lean and ProofKernel.lean together provide the theorem kernel referenced in Section 12. The kernel proves identity and composition for reductions, reflexive and transitive reducibility, and preservation lemmas for validity, readout, and transport under reduction. On top of that interface, it proves the main evidence-extraction lemmas from both full exactification evidence and protocol-indexed evidence. The theorem layer also encodes the gate's conservative implications. Full exactification evidence implies scoped positivity, transport closure and exactness, section honesty, protocol honesty, expansion honesty, cross-seed support, and non-reducibility. The theorem carrier_exactified_of_evidence packages this into the abstract exactification criterion. The protocol-indexed layer proves that protocol-indexed evidence yields a scoped positive carrier while still blocking any nonindexed promotion. Additional barrier lemmas show that fully exactified conclusions do not follow when cross-seed, section, or protocol barriers remain in force. Finally, CompressionContext supplies the abstract faithfulness implication used to formalize the witness/public-shadow split at theorem level.

conclusion: The preceding carrier-exactification paper established a scoped carrier layer on the Route A flagship support: a lawful same-branch witness, a non-faithful public signature shadow, a protocol-indexed carrier surface, scoped quadratic carrying, and two proto-event and proto-test pilots. We ask whether this carrier structure supports admissible event and test structure on fixed support. The central construct is an event bridge record B_E=(C,P,I,L,V, ,S,A) binding a carrier-side predicate, a public/readout-side predicate, an instrument, a selected lift or forgetting map, a visibility and suppression record, a threshold record, an exact-six role profile, and an audit record. A deterministic artifact pipeline generates candidate events, constructs bridge records, applies an admissibility gate, runs controls, scores layer placement, attempts finite test-family construction, and records the consequences for shared-event identity, proto-effect structure, quadratic alignment, and exact-six bookkeeping. From a pool of seventeen candidates, two inherited scoped positives — a quadratic level-set event and a transition-stability test — are accepted at the event gate and retained under controls as protocol-indexed event-level objects. No finite admissible test family is accepted: the one serious protocol-indexed bridge-family candidate is non-exhaustive because a required readout-agreement slot is unrealized. The scoped quadratic families organize the accepted q-levelset event boundary at event level but not at test level. The resulting classification is accepted scoped protocol-indexed event-level structure without accepted tests, shared-event identity, or proto-effect operations.

\paragraph{Contribution and scope.}
The substrate contributed by this paper is a \emph{carrier-to-event admissibility layer} on fixed support: a record-level discipline in which every candidate event carries an explicit instrument, a selected lift, visibility and suppression data, a threshold record, an exact-six role profile, and an audit trail, and in which tests and higher structure are built only from accepted records of this kind. The admissibility audit that evaluates these records — ten event-level gate checks and the corresponding test-, shared-identity-, and proto-effect-level checks — is adapted from the exact-six admissibility meta-theory of \citet{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII} and the seven-criterion exactification audit of the preceding carrier paper \citep{Tsiokos2026CarrierExactification}, and draws standard operational-measurement vocabulary \citep{DaviesLewis1970,Hardy2001Axioms}. The audit is adapted, not new; the contributions of the present paper are the substrate it stabilizes and the demonstration that the audit lands on that substrate with a specific, bounded verdict. We do not claim an accepted test package, shared-event identity, proto-effect fragment, probability valuation, composition result, lawful public carrier, faithful public compression, cross-seed event package, or full-core event package.

conclusion: The prior carrier-exactification result is deliberately scoped: it is a carrier-exactification statement on the fixed Route A flagship support, not a public event package and not a public carrier theorem. Its lawful object is a refined same-branch witness; its public-side object is a coarse signature shadow. The relationship between the two is non-faithful: public signatures retain operational readout information but do not determine the refined law-bearing carrier data. In standard ontic/epistemic language , the public shadow is an epistemic image of the carrier; in Markov-chain language , the carrier-to-public map is lumpable only in a restricted sense. Throughout this paper we refer to these objects descriptively — the refined witness (lawful, carrier-side), the public signature shadow (coarse, readout-side), and the witness-to-shadow basis that relates them without supplying a faithful inverse. The corresponding machine-readable identifiers are listed once, in Appendix . Consequently the public shadow can supply public/readout-side predicates for later bridge records, but it cannot by itself supply lawful carrier structure or shared-event identity.

expanded_source_wording_tex: Every candidate is then converted into an event bridge record of the form introduced in Section~\ref{sec:bridge-records}. The resulting artifact contains seventeen bridge records, one per candidate, each recording a carrier-side condition, a public/readout-side condition, an instrument, one or more selected lifts or forgetting maps, a visibility and suppression record, a threshold record, a reference to an exact-six skeleton, and an audit record. Each bridge record also annotates the candidate's weaknesses. Public-shadow candidates carry carrier-pullback or fiber-record requirements; they do not assert that public signatures determine refined carrier conditions. Quadratic candidates carry nonclaims against probability and against a global quadratic geometry. Completion candidates carry selected-lift and section-dependence notes. The absent readout-agreement baseline is represented as a negative bridge record rather than silently dropped. The bridge stage therefore establishes representational completeness for later testing, not event acceptance: a complete bridge record is necessary for event acceptance but not sufficient, and the event gate must still check the declared surface, instrument visibility, suppression honesty, selected-lift stability, protocol honesty, threshold activation, controls, layer assignment, exact-six completeness, and claim-boundary compliance.

source_wording_digest: Every candidate is then converted into an event bridge record of the form introduced in Section . The resulting artifact contains seventeen bridge records, one per candidate, each recording a carrier-side condition, a public/readout-side condition, an instrument, one or more selected lifts or forgetting maps, a visibility and suppression record, a threshold record, a reference to an exact-six skeleton, and an audit record. Each bridge record also annotates the candidate's weaknesses. Public-shadow candidates carry carrier-pullback or fiber-record requirements; they do not assert that public signatures determine refined carrier conditions. Quadratic candidates carry nonclaims against probability and against a global quadratic geometry. Completion candidates carry selected-lift and section-dependence notes. The absent readout-agreement baseline is represented as a negative bridge record rather than silently dropped. The bridge stage therefore establishes representational completeness for later testing, not event acceptance: a complete bridge record is necessary for event acceptance but not sufficient, and the event gate must still check the declared surface, instrument visibility, suppression honesty, selected-lift stability, protocol honesty, threshold activation, controls, layer assignment, exact-six completeness, and claim-boundary compliance.

\]
and analogously for the other classifications. The gate classification is a function of accepted-object predicates alone.

The run is therefore not an event-package result.

conclusion: studies strict-test-to-event-package admissibility on fixed support in Six Birds Theory. The starting point is the substrate: accepted new-layer strict tests on support, with the strict-test partition rung valid by inheritance. The paper asks whether this strict-test substrate can be advanced to event-package construction. The method combines identity-lane discipline, a comparison-base attempt, the inherited event-bridge record discipline, and the event-gate threshold and control stages. These steps separate scoped identity evidence from event-level package evidence. The paper obtains two paper-10-new results. First, same-role cross-context edges are accepted at scope, forming a protocol-indexed shared-identity layer. Second, the is identified as the named missing subobject required for event-gate threshold construction; this is a constructive non-definability finding, not a refutation of future construction. The final verdict is the series-canonical : the event-level rung requires further extension, and the verdict is earned by attempting the admissibility chain to the named obstruction. The claim boundary is explicit. Shared-event identity in the strong sense is not claimed; no event-package candidate or proto-effect structures are constructed; and inherited nonclaims from and are preserved. A Lean structural kernel with modules and proof gaps records the formal companion discipline.

expanded_source_wording_tex: The intrinsic identity lane is rejected first.  That lane would have treated the role's carrier-native strict-test content as intrinsically the same across the three H6 PICA carriers, using the inherited role labels from Paper~9 as if they supplied identity by themselves \citep{Tsiokos2026StrictTests}. The candidate triangles therefore remain role-matched probes until a lane supplies that route.  If the intrinsic lane were permitted as a fallback, the paper would erase the distinction between same-role candidacy and accepted protocol-indexed comparison, and the result would drift toward shared-event identity in the strong sense, which Paper~10 does not claim.

conclusion: The downstream structures named at the proto-effect outcome lattice rung are future-work targets in Paper 10, not negative results or hidden refutations. A proto-effect fragment would require accepted packages on which candidate operations can be probed. An effect algebra would require a proto-effect-level operation structure with enough closure and compatibility to support algebraic organization. A Born valuation would require an admissible valuation target over that event/proto-effect structure. Composition readiness would require enough accepted package and operation data to support lawful composition. None of these inputs is supplied by Paper 10, because the event-package candidate stage is upstream-blocked before any such downstream test can begin. The absence of proto-effect, effect-algebra, Born, and composition results is a structural input absence. Proto-effect probes inherit no support because no package is promoted and no accepted package is available as input ( ). These targets sit after accepted event-level records, package candidates, and promotion in the dependency order.

The kernel contains 14 theorem schemas: typed-level statements encoding admissibility discipline, gate consistency, and no-shortcut prohibitions.  A schema states how one typed discipline may be used when its hypotheses are available, or what cannot be inferred from a weaker discipline alone.  Scope is preserved: a statement typed at the strict-test, event-level, old-layer boundary, or formal-companion level cannot be silently retyped as a stronger claim.

The schemas come in two forms.  Positive consistency statements say that if a specified discipline holds at the appropriate typed level, then a corresponding downstream discipline may be stated without changing its type or scope.  No-propagation statements say that a strict-test fact, audit record, identity-lane decision, or proof-gap placeholder does not automatically become an event-level record, package construction, or old-layer transfer.  Whether the inputs satisfy a schema's hypotheses is determined by the audited artifact substrate; \Cref{subsec:proof-gap-ledger} records the places where the structural target is named but the proof is not supplied.

The Lean kernel contains 14 theorem schemas, summarized in the body at \Cref{subsec:theorem-schemas}.  This appendix records their Lean-side form without reproducing all fourteen declarations.  The schemas follow the inherited formal-kernel convention of the series: they state typed conditional structure, not empirical witness existence \citep{Tsiokos2026RecombinationWitnesses}.  The grouping below is therefore representative rather than exhaustive; the unlisted schemas fall into the same three families and differ only in the concrete gate or boundary object they protect.  The first thematic group is definitional.  A representative example is \texttt{strict\_refinement\_witness\_schema}, with input \(w : \texttt{StrictRefinementWitness}\) and output \( \texttt{StrictRefinementExists}\;w \leftrightarrow w.\texttt{coarserIdentifies} \wedge w.\texttt{finerDistinguishes}\).  Its role is positive consistency: the Lean statement says that the strict-refinement witness type and the refinement-existence predicate agree in the specified way.

The second group contains gate-consistency schemas.  A representative example is \texttt{event\_level\_admissibility\_requires\_bridge\_threshold\_controls\_schema}.  Its input types are \(b : \texttt{EventBridgeRecord}\) and \(h : \texttt{AcceptedNewLayerEventLevel}\;b\).  Its output type is the conjunction requiring representation, threshold passage, final event-level controls, final post-control status, and boundary safety for \(b\).  Its role is positive consistency: if the accepted event-level predicate is available at the typed level, then the bridge, threshold, control, and boundary components required by that predicate are available as typed projections.  Related schemas apply the same pattern to package acceptance, promoted-package support, proto-effect probes, final-gate positivity, and retained signatures.  This schema does not assert that any particular paper-10 record satisfies the predicate.

expanded_source_wording_tex: The common proof shape behind the 14 schemas of \Cref{subsec:lean-theorem-schemas} is conditional.  A schema introduces typed inputs, usually a record together with hypotheses about that record, and proves only the implication licensed by those inputs in Lean type theory.  The proof does not import an empirical witness as a theorem and does not assert that a paper-10 artifact satisfies the antecedent.  For example, when a schema takes an accepted event-level predicate as an input, the proof may project the threshold, control, and boundary components required by that predicate; it does not establish that an accepted event-level record exists.  The implication direction is part of the discipline: Lean may consume a typed hypothesis, but it does not manufacture that hypothesis from the artifact ledger.  The antecedent is always typed structural data, not an empirical conclusion smuggled into the kernel.

The Lean development for Paper~10 establishes schema legality and conditional proof structure; it does not establish empirical witness existence.  The empirical content of the paper is supplied by the artifact pipeline: \Cref{sec:methods} records the construction methods and gate attempts, \Cref{sec:primary-results} records the paper-10-new positive construction and constructive non-definability finding, and \Cref{sec:secondary-results} records the audit certificate and bookkeeping coverage.  Lean-level inhabitation, where present, shows that a typed implication or definition is formally well behaved.  It does not by itself show that the corresponding artifact record exists, that a threshold criterion is constructible from the current substrate, or that an event-package object has been produced.

This boundary is protected by the same anti-claim discipline stated methodologically in \Cref{subsec:no-shortcut-discipline} and structurally in \Cref{subsec:no-empirical-hardcoding-discipline}.  Empirical artifacts are not hardcoded as theorems; H2 transfer is not installed as an axiom; and Paper~10 positives are not obtained by silently upgrading Paper~9 results.  These flags make the formal appendix a companion to the manuscript rather than an alternative evidentiary source.  The appendix therefore closes with the same division used throughout the paper: Lean certifies schema form and proof boundaries, while empirical claims rest on audited artifacts and manuscript-level admissibility arguments.

conclusion: We study recombination-sensitive branch structure on a fixed-support substrate in Six Birds Theory. Building on prior work on event packaging and predictive holonomy, we introduce branch assemblages and two quotient levels at an interface: a branchwise predictive quotient ( K_i ), which captures independent predictive treatment of the branches, and a recombination quotient ( R_i ), which captures admissible recombination observables on branch families. On this architecture we exhibit a benchmark suite separating classical mixture, hidden predictive memory without recombination sensitivity, route-marked suppression, erasure-conditioned recovery, cyclic-family generalization, dissipative washout, and artifact controls based on protocol internalization and flattening/completion. A supporting theorem layer proves the abstract factorized no-interference regime and its obstruction by strict refinement, and one promoted positive family is connected to a theorem-backed concrete witness in an aligned Lean model. We do not claim a general reconstruction of non-Hilbert interference or a formalization of the full benchmark runtime. The claim is narrower: these recombination phenomena arise on fixed support, can be audited exactly, and admit a partial formal backbone on the Six Birds substrate.

conclusion: The previous sections are empirical. This section records the supporting theorem layer established in the Lean development. Its role is interpretive: it identifies the abstract no-interference regime, proves that strict refinement obstructs that regime, and supplies one theorem-backed concrete positive instance for an aligned Lean model of the strongest promoted family. It is not a formalization of the full benchmark runtime. The supporting formal development is implemented in Lean . At the level of mathematical form, quotient descent, factorization through quotients, and state separation by observables are standard patterns; see, for example, . The contribution here is their use in the present fixed-support substrate and benchmark program. Two explicit assumption packages organize the abstract theorem layer. The first is a detectability assumption: branchwise summaries are visible through a distinguished observable layer that separates them. The second is a global factorization assumption: every admissible recombination observable factors through the branchwise summary. Under these assumptions, the Lean development proves the following backbone results.

It does not provide a reconstruction of quantum theory, and it does not claim to be the first general treatment of interference beyond Hilbert-space formalisms; generalized-measure and operational/GPT frameworks already provide broader settings for such questions \cite{Sorkin1994QuantumMeasure,Barrett2007GPT,BarnumMuellerUdudec2014HigherOrder,LeeSelby2017HigherOrder,DakicPaterekBrukner2014DensityCubes,GarnerEtAl2013PhaseInterference,Plavala2023GPTIntro,ChiribellaDarianoPerinotti2011InformationalDerivation}. It does not prove the paired erasure benchmark in full runtime detail, the full cyclic-family generalization, or the dissipative control. Those results remain empirical exact-finite evidence. Likewise, route readability and visibility recovery remain concrete diagnostics in the computational layer rather than formal objects on the Lean side.

conclusion: This paper isolates a control-stable intrinsic family inside the fixed-support recombination layer of Six Birds theory. The first three papers of the series established admissible event packages on fixed support, predictive quotients on single histories, and the branchwise and recombination quotients on branch assemblages. Here we identify a two-anchor relative-cycle family in which branchwise predictive agreement does not determine later recombination observables. We instantiate the standard factorized no-interference collapse on the flagship surface, exhibit exact-finite separation for two flagship anchors, and formalize a concrete Lean witness kernel for the reference-positive anchor, including a no-factorization corollary. We separate the flagship positives from classical mixture, hidden predictive memory, protocol artifact, and boundary-collapse or completion-sensitive negatives using an explicit matched control bundle. We also show that nearby exact positives exist within the same relative-cycle family, while the erasure side remains empirical support rather than formal core.

conclusion: This appendix collects the formal definitions and theorem statements used in the main text. At the level of general mathematical form, the quotient and factorization language used here sits near behavioral equivalence, bisimulation, exact aggregation, and standard quotient-factorization arguments . It does not reproduce proofs. The comparison base is inherited from the first three papers of the series: fixed support and admissibility, the current and predictive quotients on single histories, and the branchwise and recombination quotients on branch assemblages. The present paper uses those inherited structures only to define and compare the flagship recombination family on a common exact-finite support. At the single-history level, the current quotient Q_i identifies reachable histories that are indistinguishable by the current event package, while the predictive quotient M_i identifies histories that remain indistinguishable under all admissible future generator/observable words on the reachable image. At the branch-assemblage level, the branchwise quotient K_i identifies assemblages with the same weighted multiset of predictive classes, while the recombination quotient R_i identifies assemblages that are indistinguishable by admissible later recombination observables. When recombination equivalence refines branchwise equivalence there is a canonical forgetful map _i : R_i → K_i .

conclusion: We instantiate a certificate-based closure calculus (Six Birds Theory) on an exact-finite class of kinetically constrained glass models, where kernels, stationary measures, witnesses, and zero controls are exact ratios of integers and the remaining certificate evidence is deterministic float64, labeled as such in each artifact. On the declared scope: the thermodynamic lens has a positive closure deficit exceeding its own constrained-equilibrium baseline by a certified margin of 3/2 (achieved 1.64 ) — and that baseline is provably nonzero, since closure is a lumpability property, not an equilibrium property (GT1). The Kovacs protocol yields an exact split-pair witness: two preparation histories current-equal and future-different (GT2). All 512 predicates definable from the declared energy lens agree on a witness pair that a memory readout separates, constructively foreclosing the static-order-parameter search on that declared class (GT3). A kill-test panel correctly executes five constructed artifact regimes (GT4). Resolving the witness pair costs exactly one declared memory scalar — fictive temperature is a lawful memory coordinate, and the buyback ledger demonstrates the mechanism without proving general single-scalar insufficiency (GT5). The predictive-structure layer receives a shell-local strict-promotion certificate via non-factorization, with the fuller completion-dynamics route explicitly not invoked (GT6). Aging readouts frozen on the East model and transferred out-of-sample under a pre-registered no-fitting protocol scored 8 passes and 14 one-sided failures, with the trap family structurally unobservable for a reason we prove: the declared trap weight family's stationary distribution is exactly temperature-invariant (GT7). A vendored Lean core machine-checks the abstract witness/refinement theorems; attempting to encode the numeric witness produced a machine-checked impossibility theorem locating that core's expressiveness boundary. Every claim is hash-pinned to its artifacts, and the full nonclaims ledger is printed unabridged.

\claimref{GB1}{4173705a52c358bc74b51815929cb2a28c8f680b3421dafdb7633e97b051fa8e}
The published protocol-trap theorem (F-I T-AOT-02) requires all phase kernels reversible w.r.t.\ a
\emph{common} stationary measure; Kovacs kernels $K_\epsilon$ are reversible w.r.t.\ different
Gibbs measures per $\epsilon$, so the theorem does not apply as published. GB1 --- the
temperature-protocol version, in the style of the protocol-trap microarticle
\sbtcite{sbt-protocol-trap} --- ships as a recognition-grade math demo: a pseudo-EPR identity
plus a finite exact numerical check, with the closed general theorem filed as an explicitly open
obligation in the artifact payload. GT4's triage therefore carries the GB1 caveat as a standing
theorem-wrapper limitation: the triage computation itself is deterministic and exact, but the
protocol-trap \emph{discipline} it applies rests partly on a demo, not a closed theorem. This is
F-II conditional reporting working as designed.

conclusion: We introduce a fixed-support route-transport framework in which histories can be equivalent at a current event interface yet differ as predictors of later admissible observations. For each interface, we define a current quotient by present-event indistinguishability and a predictive quotient by equality of all later admissible event statistics under continuation. Standard quotient-algebraic results then apply in this setting: future-predictive equivalence refines current-event equivalence, admissible continuations induce well-defined transport on , and the current class after transport is determined by the source predictive class through a canonical mixed map _i _j . Generic transport on along all outgoing continuations exists precisely at flat interfaces, where current equivalence already determines all future observations. The predictive quotient is future-sufficient, and every future-sufficient state abstraction factors uniquely through on the reachable image. Strict refinement of is equivalent to existence of a pair of histories that are current-equivalent but future-distinct. For endo-continuations, representative push can preserve the current class of every history while moving a predictive class. The contribution of the paper is the framework itself and the demonstration that it is non-vacuous: an axiom-audited finite memory-wheel instance in Lean and exact finite fixed-support benchmarks instantiate strict refinement and the loop asymmetry, while the computational suite separates artifact, flattenable, explicit-latent, dissipative, and coherent-candidate regimes with bounded robustness under perturbation. Small discovery searches recover additional coherent candidates beyond the hand-built examples while a control search space remains all-flat.

h \CurrentEquiv_i h'

\label{thm:predictive-transport}
For every admissible continuation $\gamma\in\mathcal{C}_{i\to j}$, pushing representatives along $\gamma$ descends to a well-defined predictive transport
\[
T^{M}_{\gamma} : \PredictiveQ_i \to \PredictiveQ_j.
\]
It also descends to a mixed map
\[
\widehat T^{M\toQ}_{\gamma} :
\PredictiveQ_i \to \CurrentQ_j,
\qquad
[h]_{\FutureEquiv_i}\longmapsto
[\operatorname{push}_{\gamma}h]_{\CurrentEquiv_j},
\]
and these maps form the commutation triangle
\[
\pi_j \circ T^{M}_{\gamma}
=
\widehat T^{M\toQ}_{\gamma}.
\]
For a fixed source interface $i$, current-event equivalence is stable under every outgoing push if and only if $i$ is flat:
\[
\bigl(h\CurrentEquiv_i h'\Longrightarrow h\FutureEquiv_i h'\bigr)
\quad\text{for all }h,h'\in\Histories_i.
\]
Thus current-quotient transport induced by representative push along every outgoing continuation is available exactly in the flat case, not as part of an arbitrary route transport package.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:reachable-factorization}
Let $s : \Histories_i \to S$ be any future-sufficient state abstraction at interface $i$. Then on the reachable image
\[
\operatorname{Reach}(s) := \{\,s(h) : h\in\Histories_i\,\},
\]
there exists a factor map
\[
f : \operatorname{Reach}(s) \to \PredictiveQ_i
\]
such that
\[
f(s(h)) = [h]_{\FutureEquiv_i}
\qquad
\text{for all } h\in\Histories_i.
\]
Moreover, this factorization is unique on the reachable image: if two maps from $\operatorname{Reach}(s)$ to $\PredictiveQ_i$ agree with the predictive quotient on all histories, then they agree everywhere on $\operatorname{Reach}(s)$.

\label{thm:loop-asymmetry}
Let $\ell\in\mathcal{C}_{i\to i}$ be a loop at interface $i$. Then $\ell$ induces the predictive endomorphism
\[
L^{M}_{\ell} : \PredictiveQ_i \to \PredictiveQ_i.
\]
Suppose current triviality holds at representative level,
\[
\operatorname{push}_{\ell}h \CurrentEquiv_i h
\qquad\text{for every }h\in\Histories_i,
\]
while $L^{M}_{\ell}$ is nontrivial. Then there exists a predictive class $q\in\PredictiveQ_i$ such that
\[
L^{M}_{\ell}(q)\neq q
\qquad\text{but}\qquad
\pi_i\bigl(L^{M}_{\ell}(q)\bigr)=\pi_i(q).
\]

conclusion: Beyond the scope boundaries stated in Section , two further limitations deserve mention. The Lean formalization is intentionally partial: it covers the quotient comparison, predictive and mixed transport, the flatness characterization, sufficiency on the reachable image, witness/strict-refinement equivalence, representative-level loop asymmetry, and a finite non-vacuity instance, but does not yet formalize moved-class sets, cardinality-based nontriviality criteria, or richer action-level invariants. Those omissions do not undermine the present results, but they mark the current boundary of the formal development. The benchmark and discovery labels should also be read operationally rather than ontologically. In particular, coherent_candidate denotes a benchmark or discovered candidate that exhibits the loop asymmetry and witness structure targeted by the paper. It is not a claim that a stronger external state representation has been forced.

expanded_source_wording_tex: At the level of adjacent literatures, the predictive quotient is closest to future-oriented state constructions such as causal states, observable operator models, and predictive state representations \citep{ShaliziCrutchfield2001ComputationalMechanics,Jaeger2000ObservableOperatorModels,LittmanSuttonSingh2002PredictiveRepresentationsState}. The current/future comparison layer added here is closer in spirit to a comparison between observational and behavioral equivalence, and thus also sits near bisimulation traditions in concurrency and probabilistic processes \citep{Park1981ConcurrencyAutomata,Milner1989CommunicationConcurrency,LarsenSkou1991BisimulationThroughProbabilisticTesting}. The paper does not claim to subsume those frameworks. Its claim is narrower: on fixed support, one can compare what is visible now with what matters later, and one can separate flat, artifactual, removable, currentizable, dissipative, and loop-asymmetric cases within one operational language.

In particular, the benchmark and discovery sections do not change the theorem layer; they instantiate it.

\subsection{Current formal scope}\label{appsubsec:lean-scope}
The Lean development currently covers the quotient comparison story needed for the paper: equivalence refinement, predictive transport, the mixed predictive-to-current triangle, the flatness characterization for current push stability, reachable-image sufficiency and factorization, witness strictness, representative-level loop asymmetry, and finite non-vacuity. It does not assert generic current-quotient transport or a generic current-quotient loop action. It does not yet formalize moved-class sets, cardinality-based nontriviality criteria, or richer action-level invariants. Those omissions are real, but they do not undercut any theorem claim made in the main body.

\subsection{Current formal scope}\label{appsubsec:lean-scope}
The Lean development currently covers the quotient comparison story needed for the paper: equivalence refinement, predictive transport, the mixed predictive-to-current triangle, the flatness characterization for current push stability, reachable-image sufficiency and factorization, witness strictness, representative-level loop asymmetry, and finite non-vacuity. It does not assert generic current-quotient transport or a generic current-quotient loop action. It does not yet formalize moved-class sets, cardinality-based nontriviality criteria, or richer action-level invariants. Those omissions are real, but they do not undercut any theorem claim made in the main body.

conclusion: Protocol-driven dynamics often conflate route dependence (noncommutativity/holonomy of update steps) with an arrow of time, making time-asymmetry audits vulnerable to scheduling artifacts. We introduce an autonomous lifted-protocol formulation and a path-reversal audit decomposition, operationalize it via a fully explicit finite-state benchmark, and demonstrate a clean null-versus-driven separation between holonomy and directionality. Concretely, we define two reversible Markov kernels K_0,K_1 on three states and compare (i) an externally scheduled stroboscopic composition on X with (ii) an autonomous time-homogeneous lift on Z=X driven by a clock. Under external scheduling, each step is reversible but the stroboscopic update has strictly positive entropy production EPR , with a noncommutativity witness \|K_0K_1-K_1K_0\|_ = . Under the autonomous lift with a reversible (unbiased) clock (null control), the lifted chain is reversible and the arrow audit collapses to EPR (equivalently, path-reversal asymmetry vanishes). Turning on clock bias (drive) yields a positive arrow and the measured EPR_ lifted matches EPR_ clock across a bias sweep (Figure ). This separation reduces false positives when interpreting protocol effects as directionality and provides a reproducible audit template for switching Markov models and algorithmic protocols. We do not claim a general characterization of all nonequilibrium protocols; the conclusions are for finite-state discrete-time kernels and the random-scan autonomous lift studied here.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Assume:
(i) \(S\) is reversible with respect to a stationary distribution \(s\) on \(\Phi\); and
(ii) each \(K_\phi\) is reversible with respect to a \emph{common} stationary distribution \(\pi\) on \(X\).
Then the product measure \(\mu(x,\phi):=\pi(x)s(\phi)\) is stationary for \(P\), and \(P\) is reversible with respect to \(\mu\).
Indeed, write \(P=\alpha P_{\mathrm{phase}}+(1-\alpha)P_{\mathrm{state}}\), where
\(P_{\mathrm{phase}}((x,\phi),(x',\phi'))=\mathbf{1}_{x'=x}S(\phi,\phi')\) and
\(P_{\mathrm{state}}((x,\phi),(x',\phi'))=\mathbf{1}_{\phi'=\phi}K_\phi(x,x')\).
For \(\mu(x,\phi)=\pi(x)s(\phi)\), detailed balance for \(P_{\mathrm{phase}}\) reduces (on the support \(x=x'\)) to \(s(\phi)S(\phi,\phi')=s(\phi')S(\phi',\phi)\), and detailed balance for \(P_{\mathrm{state}}\) reduces (on the support \(\phi=\phi'\)) to \(\pi(x)K_\phi(x,x')=\pi(x')K_\phi(x',x)\). Since both components satisfy detailed balance with respect to \(\mu\), their convex combination \(P\) does as well.
The assumption of a common stationary \(\pi\) is essential: if the conditional kernels had different equilibria, state updates could contribute nonzero entropy production even with a reversible clock.
Consequently,
\[
\mathrm{EPR}(P,\mu)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\Sigma_T(\mu)=0\ \ \text{for all }T\ge 1.
\]

Let \(P\) be the lifted kernel~\eqref{eq:lifted_kernel} on \(Z=X\times\Phi\), and suppose each \(K_\phi\) is reversible with respect to a common stationary \(\pi\) on \(X\) while \(S\) has stationary distribution \(s\) on \(\Phi\).
Then the entropy production of the lifted chain decomposes as
\[
\mathrm{EPR}(P,\pi\times s)
=
\alpha\,\mathrm{EPR}(S,s)
+
(1-\alpha)\sum_{\phi\in\Phi} s(\phi)\,\mathrm{EPR}(K_\phi,\pi).
\]
This follows by splitting the edge-sum in \eqref{eq:epr} into disjoint transitions that change only \(\phi\) (phase updates) versus only \(x\) (state updates), which do not overlap in~\eqref{eq:lifted_kernel}.
In our construction \(\mathrm{EPR}(K_\phi,\pi)=0\) for all \(\phi\), so the arrow audit is entirely attributable to clock drive:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:epr_clock_only}
\mathrm{EPR}_{\mathrm{lifted}}=\alpha\,\mathrm{EPR}_{\mathrm{clock}}.
\end{equation}
This gives a precise sense in which protocol holonomy alone is not an arrow-of-time certificate: without clock drive (or external scheduling), the audit vanishes.

conclusion: Confluence is usually read as order-independence of reduction, while flatness is usually read as path-independence of transport. This paper argues that their local cores coincide once rewriting is equipped with its missing two-dimensional cells. The relevant object is not the bare reduction graph but a reduction 2-complex whose 0 -cells are states, whose 1 -cells are one-step rewrites, and whose generating 2 -cells are local peaks or, in structured rewriting settings, reachable critical pairs. In that setting, elementary flatness is exactly local confluence. We prove this core equivalence and record the supporting fact that confluence plus normalization yields a unique normal form from a chosen start state. We then show computationally that the corrected local/global picture survives exhaustive finite-ARS stress tests in the terminating regime, curated string-rewriting examples, and a curated left-linear term-rewriting bridge with genuine nonroot overlap. These experiments also show that bare graph-flatness surrogates fail, while reachable critical-pair defects align with the observed local obstruction layer. Finally, explicit before/after examples show that completion can be read as holonomy elimination: the local generator persists while its defect disappears. The full finite terminating left-linear TRS theorem package remains to be written in full generality, but the correct object, local generators, and evidence boundary are now fixed.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\noindent
Confluence is usually read as order-independence of reduction, while flatness is usually read as path-independence of transport.
This paper argues that their local cores coincide once rewriting is equipped with its missing two-dimensional cells.
The relevant object is not the bare reduction graph but a reduction 2-complex whose $0$-cells are states, whose $1$-cells are one-step rewrites, and whose generating $2$-cells are local peaks or, in structured rewriting settings, reachable critical pairs.
In that setting, elementary flatness is exactly local confluence.
We prove this core equivalence and record the supporting fact that confluence plus normalization yields a unique normal form from a chosen start state.
We then show computationally that the corrected local/global picture survives exhaustive finite-ARS stress tests in the terminating regime, curated string-rewriting examples, and a curated left-linear term-rewriting bridge with genuine nonroot overlap.
These experiments also show that bare graph-flatness surrogates fail, while reachable critical-pair defects align with the observed local obstruction layer.
Finally, explicit before/after examples show that completion can be read as holonomy elimination: the local generator persists while its defect disappears.
The full finite terminating left-linear TRS theorem package remains to be written in full generality, but the correct object, local generators, and evidence boundary are now fixed.

We prove this core equivalence and record the supporting fact that confluence plus normalization yields a unique normal form from a chosen start state. We then show computationally that the corrected local/global picture survives exhaustive finite-ARS stress tests in the terminating regime, curated string-rewriting examples, and a curated left-linear term-rewriting bridge with genuine nonroot overlap. These experiments also show that bare graph-flatness surrogates fail, while reachable critical-pair defects align with the observed local obstruction layer. Finally, explicit before/after examples show that completion can be read as holonomy elimination: the local generator persists while its defect disappears. The full finite terminating left-linear TRS theorem package remains to be written in full generality, but the correct object, local generators, and evidence boundary are now fixed.

\noindent
Confluence is usually read as order-independence of reduction, while flatness is usually read as path-independence of transport.
This paper argues that their local cores coincide once rewriting is equipped with its missing two-dimensional cells.
The relevant object is not the bare reduction graph but a reduction 2-complex whose $0$-cells are states, whose $1$-cells are one-step rewrites, and whose generating $2$-cells are local peaks or, in structured rewriting settings, reachable critical pairs.
In that setting, elementary flatness is exactly local confluence.
We prove this core equivalence and record the supporting fact that confluence plus normalization yields a unique normal form from a chosen start state.
We then show computationally that the corrected local/global picture survives exhaustive finite-ARS stress tests in the terminating regime, curated string-rewriting examples, and a curated left-linear term-rewriting bridge with genuine nonroot overlap.
These experiments also show that bare graph-flatness surrogates fail, while reachable critical-pair defects align with the observed local obstruction layer.
Finally, explicit before/after examples show that completion can be read as holonomy elimination: the local generator persists while its defect disappears.
The full finite terminating left-linear TRS theorem package remains to be written in full generality, but the correct object, local generators, and evidence boundary are now fixed.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:boundary-filler-data}
Let $\sigma$ be a generating $2$-cell with source $x$ and one-step branches to $y_\ell$ and $y_r$. Its boundary data consist of

x \to y_\ell

\[
y_\ell \to^* w
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
y_r \to^* w.
\]
When such a filler exists, we call $w$ a \emph{join witness} for $\sigma$.

These include: finite abstract rewriting systems, reflexive-transitive reachability, joinability, normal forms, local confluence, elementary peaks, elementary flatness. The file \code{ConfluenceFlat/Core.lean} formalizes the abstract rewriting notions used in \Cref{sec:core-theorem}. These include:
\begin{itemize}
    \item finite abstract rewriting systems,
    \item reflexive-transitive reachability,
    \item joinability,
    \item normal forms,
    \item local confluence,
    \item elementary peaks,
    \item elementary flatness.
\end{itemize}

The file \code{ConfluenceFlat/UniqueNormalForm.lean} adds the supporting global notions used later in \Cref{sec:core-theorem}, including:
\begin{itemize}
    \item confluence,
    \item normalization,
    \item uniqueness of normal form from a chosen start state,
    \item existence and uniqueness of normal form under confluence and normalization.
\end{itemize}

conclusion: Previous demonstrations of contextuality-type obstruction start from quantum mechanics or from externally specified measurement scenarios. We show that the same locally-Boolean-but-globally-obstructed structure can arise from an autonomous emergence framework—Six Birds Theory—without importing Hilbert space, amplitudes, or the Born rule. The formal vehicle is a finite event package: a family of stable-record contexts, each carrying a finite Boolean event algebra, together with a layer-relative shared-event identification and an audit layer. Obstruction is the failure of admissible global realization for that package. The computational framework combines exact and quotient-backed feasibility, structural and statistical deficits, provenance auditing, and false-positive controls. The evidence base includes a classical control, a boundary-case epistemic calibration, an explicit finite parity/context witness, and autonomous discovery organized by mechanism, lens, and packaging axes. The results are stratified: mechanism variation yields package-sensitive structure with a quotient-backed witness under a weaker claim ceiling; lens variation closes with a cross-resolution strict extension obstruction on fixed support; and packaging variation produces the strongest current obstruction, subject to a package conflict caveat. Where applicable, the principal cases persist under bounded robustness checks. The paper therefore provides the first computationally explicit evidence that contextuality-type obstruction can emerge from a system's own packaging structure rather than from quantum theory or an externally imposed scenario.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
An \emph{admissible global realization} of an event package
\[
\mathfrak{E}=(\mathcal C,\{B_c\}_{c\in\mathcal C},\sim,\mathcal A)
\]
consists of a finite set \(\Omega\) and maps \(\pi_c:\Omega\to A_c\) for all \(c\in\mathcal C\) such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Context coverage.} For every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and every atom \(a\in A_c\), there exists \(\omega\in\Omega\) with \(\pi_c(\omega)=a\).
    \item \textbf{Event realization.} Each context event \(E\in B_c\) is realized by \(\mathopen{[\mkern-3mu[} E \rrbracket_\Omega^c\subseteq \Omega\).
    \item \textbf{Shared-event consistency.} Whenever \(E\in B_c\), \(F\in B_d\), and \(E\sim F\), one has
    \[
    \mathopen{[\mkern-3mu[} E \rrbracket_\Omega^c = \mathopen{[\mkern-3mu[} F \rrbracket_\Omega^d.
    \]
    \item \textbf{Audit admissibility.} The realization respects the package discipline encoded in \(\mathcal A\): no unlicensed hidden distinctions are introduced, and the realization remains within the layer's admissible record and interface class.
\end{enumerate}

\[
\EventPackage=(\mathcal C,\{B_c\}_{c\in\mathcal C},\sim,\mathcal A)

consists of a finite set \(\Omega\) and maps \(\pi_c:\Omega\to A_c\) for all \(c\in\mathcal C\) such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Context coverage.} For every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and every atom \(a\in A_c\), there exists \(\omega\in\Omega\) with \(\pi_c(\omega)=a\).
    \item \textbf{Event realization.} Each context event \(E\in B_c\) is realized by \(\llbracket E \rrbracket_\Omega^c\subseteq \Omega\).

    \llbracket E \rrbracket_\Omega^c = \llbracket F \rrbracket_\Omega^d.
    \]
    \item \textbf{Audit admissibility.} The realization respects the package discipline encoded in \(\mathcal A\): no unlicensed hidden distinctions are introduced, and the realization remains within the layer's admissible record and interface class.
\end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:fixed-context-booleanity}
For every context \(c\in\mathcal{C}\), the event algebra
\[
\BoolAlg{c}=\mathcal P(A_c)
\]
is a finite Boolean algebra whose atoms are exactly the singleton atomic outcomes of \(A_c\). In particular, every event \(E\in \BoolAlg{c}\) is uniquely determined by its atomic support
\[
\operatorname{supp}_c(E):=\{a\in A_c : a\in E\},
\]
and every context is locally classical in the finite Boolean sense.

\label{thm:fixed-context-booleanity}
For every context \(c\in\CtxFamily\), the event algebra
\[
\BoolAlg{c}=\mathcal P(A_c)
\]
is a finite Boolean algebra whose atoms are exactly the singleton atomic outcomes of \(A_c\). In particular, every event \(E\in \BoolAlg{c}\) is uniquely determined by its atomic support
\[
\operatorname{supp}_c(E):=\{a\in A_c : a\in E\},
\]
and every context is locally classical in the finite Boolean sense.

\paragraph{Proof sketch of \Cref{thm:shared-event-quotient}.}
The theorem is conditional on the admissibility and Boolean-stability of the shared-event relation on the relevant fixed comparison object. Under that assumption, if \(E_1\sim F_1\) and \(E_2\sim F_2\), then admissible probes and downstream identifications cannot distinguish the left and right unions either, so \(E_1\cup E_2\sim F_1\cup F_2\). Likewise, if \(E\sim F\), then admissible Boolean complementation on the local event algebras preserves the identification. The quotient is therefore stable under the local Boolean operations that the theorem uses. \qed

conclusion: When must an operator-valued obstruction associated with an involutive system vanish? This paper answers that question inside the Six Birds framework by naming Self-Dual Trace Confinement (SDTC) as the recognition source for formed closures with genuine involutive self-duality. The mechanism is the duality-confinement membrane theorem: for an involutive object ledger with separating anti-invariant readout, a sequence of positive domination records B_n with B_n 0 forces the anti-invariant ledger to vanish and confines visible mass to the fixed locus of the duality. The supporting apparatus develops the involutive object ledger, the anti-invariant ledger and trace identity, direct qualitative and quantitative confinement, completed-domination bridges, Douglas factorization in typed-cone form, exhaustive moving ledgers, and optimized scalar trace budgets. Operator-theoretic realization over trace-class operators is an open extension, as is a derivation of the AM–GM step inside a typed real-arithmetic structure. The development is formalized in Lean as a mathlib-free mechanization at the typed positive-cone level (Appendix ). Cross-substrate generalizations such as CPT symmetry, gauge invariance, quantum self-adjointness, and function-field RH are presented as structural predictions, not theorems; the paper develops the abstract apparatus layer and names the hypotheses any substrate-specific application must supply.

\label{def:duality_confinement:anti-invariant-ledger}
The \emph{anti-invariant object ledger} of \(\hat{\mathfrak{X}}\) is the positive
cone element
\[
  A_{X}
  :=
  \int_X \psi_{-}(x)\psi_{-}(x)^*\,d\mu(x),
  \qquad
  \psi_{-}(x)=P_{-}\psi(x).
\]
Equivalently, \(A_{X}\) is the Gram-type positive element generated
by integrating the anti-invariant readout against the object-ledger
measure \(\mu\).

\label{def:duality_confinement:separating-readout}
The anti-invariant readout \(\psi_{-}\) is
\emph{qualitatively separating} when, on the visible support of
\(\mu\),
\[
  \psi_{-}(x)=0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  x\in\Fix(J).
\]
In the finite weighted case this means the equivalence holds for
every \(x\in X\) with positive weight.  In the measure-theoretic
case it means the equivalence holds outside a \(\mu\)-null set.

It is \emph{quantitatively separating} with modulus \(m\) when
\[
  m:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)
\]
and, for every \(\varepsilon>0\) and every \(x\in X\),
\[
  \dist(x,\Fix(J))\geq\varepsilon
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \|\psi_{-}(x)\|\geq m(\varepsilon).
\]

\[

\]

This section states the main result: the duality-confinement
membrane theorem, also called the master theorem.  It takes the
apparatus built in the preceding sections and turns a sequence of
domination records into fixed-locus confinement.  The input is
algebraic and trace-theoretic---\(A_{X}\) is dominated by positive
bounds \(B_n\) whose traces tend to zero---and the output is
geometric: visible mass is confined to \(\Fix(J)\).  In framework
terms, this is the apparatus theorem for the SDTC structural law
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC}}\): it does not derive the recognition source, only the
mathematical consequence once the source has supplied the required
sequence.

\begin{theorem}[Duality-confinement membrane theorem\protect\footnote{Verified in the Lean formalization at the typed positive-cone level; see App~\ref{app:formalization}.}]
\label{thm:duality_confinement:master-theorem}
Let \(\hat{\mathfrak{X}}\) be an involutive object ledger with carrier \(X\),
involution \(J\), measure \(\mu\), anti-invariant readout
\(\psi_{-}\), and anti-invariant ledger \(A_{X}\).  Assume that
\(\psi_{-}\) is qualitatively separating.  Suppose there is a sequence
of positive cone elements \(B_n\) such that
\[
  A_{X}\preceq B_n
  \qquad (n=1,2,\ldots)
\]
and
\[
  \trace B_n\to0
  \qquad (n\to\infty).
\]
Then \(A_{X}=0\) in the typed positive cone.  Consequently,
\[
  \mu\bigl(X\setminus\Fix(J)\bigr)=0.
\]
\end{theorem}

\label{def:duality_confinement:exhaustive-moving-ledger}
An \emph{exhaustive moving ledger} over an involutive object ledger
\(\hat{\mathfrak{X}}\) consists of a sequence of positive cone elements
\(A_{X,n}\), inclusion transports \(\iota_n\), and positive tails
\(T_n\) with \(0\preceq T_n\), such that, for every \(n\),
\[
  A_{X}\preceq \iota_n A_{X,n}\iota_n^*+T_n.
\]
It is \emph{vanishing-exhaustive} when there are positive bounds
\(B_n\) satisfying
\[
  A_{X,n}\preceq B_n
\]
and
\[
  \trace(\iota_n B_n\iota_n^*)+\trace T_n\to0
  \qquad (n\to\infty).
\]

\label{def:duality_confinement:defected-budget}
A \emph{defected obstruction budget} at level \(n\) is a domination
record of the form
\[
  \AX
  \preceq
  (1+t)\bigl(\Kminus_{n}+E_{\mathrm{src},n}\bigr)
  +(1+t^{-1})E_{\mathrm{br},n},
\]
where \(t>0\), where \(E_{\mathrm{src},n}\) is a source defect, and
where \(E_{\mathrm{br},n}\) is a bridge defect.  Both defects are
positive cone elements.  The unparameterized budget is obtained by
setting \(t=1\), which adds the two defect contributions without
optimization.

\label{prop:duality_confinement:optimized-trace-budget}
For a defected obstruction budget at level \(n\), set
\[
  a_n=\trace(\Kminus_{n}+E_{\mathrm{src},n}),
  \qquad
  b_n=\trace E_{\mathrm{br},n},
\]
with \(a_n,b_n\geq0\).  Then
\[
  \inf_{t>0}
  \bigl[(1+t)a_n+(1+t^{-1})b_n\bigr]
  =
  \bigl(\sqrt{a_n}+\sqrt{b_n}\bigr)^2.
\]
In particular, if \(a_n\to0\) and \(b_n\to0\), then the optimized
trace budget tends to zero.

conclusion: We ask not merely whether layer birth occurs, but how many primitive kinds of birth are experimentally accessible. Within the Six-Birds framework, birth events can be organized by activation of packaging ( P5 ), directed circulation ( P6_ drive ), and staging anomaly ( P4 ). We show that these primitives support a small canonical taxonomy of four layer-birth classes and that the corresponding classes can be operationally instantiated and separated in a common measured observable space. Class-I activates packaging without drive; Class-II activates packaging together with directed circulation; Class-III activates packaging together with a staging anomaly but without drive; and Class-IV activates all three. The strongest empirical separation is between Class-I and Class-II, where affinity at structural birth robustly discriminates drive-free from driven births and explicit no-fake-arrow controls rule out coarse-graining artifacts. We then place all four classes on a shared observable map using structural boundary location, affinity at boundary, and a strict-rule-aligned staging proxy. Capacity/depth behaves as a post-birth field rather than a primary classifier, and at least one upstream/PICA-style system can be embedded in the same coordinate system. We do not claim stabilized universality exponents. Instead, we provide a primitive taxonomy and observable separation of layer-birth classes that future universality work must respect.

expanded_source_wording_tex: This is also the place where the paper must be explicit about robustness limits. Under non-manual lens swaps, neither Class-III nor Class-IV reproduces its full canonical label cleanly. For Class-III, both the spectral and diffusion lenses collapse the representative back toward the Class-I side while still preserving the basic structural/no-drive signature. For Class-IV, the same lens swaps degrade the result further, yielding unclassified or Class-II-like outcomes as the P4 channel and, in some cases, the drive-confidence channel weaken. Table~\ref{tab:class-iii-iv-lens-caveat} summarizes this caveat. expanded_source_wording_tex:
The main result of this paper is not a final exponent-level universality classification. It is a primitive taxonomy and observable separation of layer-birth classes. Within the Six-Birds framework, the experimentally accessible low-complexity births are organized by activation of $P5$, $P6_{\mathrm{drive}}$, and $P4$, and the four corresponding canonical classes can be instantiated and separated in a common measured observable space. That is the level at which the evidence is now strongest, and it is the level at which the paper should be read.

The most mature part of that result is the Class-I / Class-II contrast. Both classes exhibit structural birth, but only Class-II carries a robust directed-circulation signal at structural birth. The empirical separation is therefore not merely taxonomic by declaration. It is enforced by a validated observable channel: affinity. The no-fake-arrow controls make that point especially important. Reversible controls do not get spuriously promoted into the driven class, while hidden-schedule protocol-trap constructions do produce the expected driven-positive signal under naive handling. This is precisely the kind of evidential discipline that a primitive taxonomy needs if it is to be more than nomenclature.

source_wording_digest: What remains open is therefore clear. First, the lens robustness of the P4-active classes should be improved beyond the canonical manual channel. Second, the asymptotic status of the classes—whether they correspond to distinct stabilized universality classes, or to a smaller number of exponent-level classes decorated by secondary fields—remains unresolved. Third, broader upstream coverage is needed if the taxonomy is to be claimed as more than a controlled synthetic-and-bridged program. The paper leaves the field with a controlled rubric, a confirmed set of low-complexity classes, and an observable map that future work will have to respect. Conclusion

conclusion: treats holonomy as a constrained non-axis rather than a missing success
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Several of the project's most useful outcomes are negative in form. They do not undermine the paper's main claims; they define their scope. This appendix records the most important of those constraints so that the main text does not have to carry them in full detail.

The first is the holonomy result. The project tested whether route mismatch could function as a clean crossover field and found that it could not. The initial construction produced affinity contamination, and the refined construction eliminated the contamination without producing a meaningful boundary-shift effect. This should not be read as an unsuccessful side experiment. It is an empirical confirmation of a structural point already built into the primitive framework: $P3$ is diagnostically important, but it is not a directionality certificate on its own. Whenever the route-mismatch channel appeared to generate a class-relevant effect, it did so by coupling into the drive channel rather than by standing independently. The paper therefore treats holonomy as a constrained non-axis rather than a missing success.

conclusion: We study a class of continuous Cantor substrates generated by six interacting mechanisms—operator rewrite, admissibility gating, protocol/timescale adaptation, lens selection, packaging/completion, and budget dynamics—and isolate an audited shell on which the resulting full-loop dynamics are lawful. On this shell we define a base cocycle-pressure theory T_0 and a completion-based extension T_1 built from an evolve–forget–reinstantiate packaging endomap. We prove four theoremlets on this shell-stable class: (i) a continuous full-loop lawfulness theoremlet, (ii) closure of a selector-weighted cocycle pressure object, (iii) a strict theory-extension theoremlet showing that T_1 is not definable from T_0 , via saturation, material P4 P5 forcing, and macro-admissibility obstruction, and (iv) a thermodynamic consequence theoremlet in the form of a nontrivial conditional pressure disintegration over packaging fibers. The contribution is therefore a theorem of theory depth rather than broader family coverage: the packaged object carries object structure not present in the cocycle object even on a fixed shell-stable class. We make no broader-class, shell-general, or non-SFT breadth claim beyond this audited shell, but the resulting hybrid Cantor object yields a closed and thermodynamically meaningful audited-shell theorem package.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:cocycle-pressure}
Let \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\) be the audited shell-stable class from Section~\ref{sec:lawfulness}, and let \(a_n(s;x)\) be the selector-weighted operator growth observable associated with the base cocycle theory \(T_0\). Define
\[
\Phi_n(s):=\sup_{x\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}} a_n(s;x).
\]
Assume the shell-stable hypotheses of the lawfulness theoremlet, together with the shell-uniform cocycle bounds and bounded-error comparison estimates required by the Fekete-sup route. Then the following hold on the audited shell.

\begin{enumerate}
    \item The pressure object
    \[
    P_{T_0}(s)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log \Phi_n(s)
    \]
    exists on the relevant parameter window.
    \item \(P_{T_0}(s)\) is finite and nondegenerate on that window.
    \item \(P_{T_0}(s)\) is monotone in \(s\).
    \item \(P_{T_0}(s)\) has enough regularity to support a later root-based thermodynamic theorem.
\end{enumerate}

Therefore the cocycle-pressure object of the base theory \(T_0\) is closed on the audited shell.
