expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:strict-extension}
Let \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\) be the audited shell-stable class, let
\[
\pi_0:\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\to \mathcal{O}_0
\]
be the cocycle-level object map of the base theory \(T_0\), and let
\[
\pi_1:\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\to \mathcal{O}_1
\]
be the packaged-object map defined by the completion theory \(T_1\). Assume:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item the cocycle-pressure theory \(T_0\) is closed on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\),
    \item the completion endomap is well-defined on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\),
    \item saturation of the completion dynamics occurs on the audited shell,
    \item material \(P4\leftarrow P5\) forcing produces new packaged strata after saturation,
    \item and the cocycle-level theory exhibits macro-admissibility obstruction on the packaged future.
\end{enumerate}
Then \(T_1\) is a strict theory extension of \(T_0\) on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\). Equivalently, there is no factorization
\[
\pi_1=\phi\circ \pi_0
\qquad \text{on } \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}
\]
for any map \(\phi:\mathcal{O}_0\to\mathcal{O}_1\).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:conditional-disintegration}
Let \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\) be the audited shell-stable class, let \(P_{T_0}(s)\) be the closed cocycle pressure object of the base theory \(T_0\), and let \(\mathcal{F}(x)\) be the persistent packaged strata of the extended theory \(T_1\) with weights \(w_{\Sigma}(x)\). Define
\[
\Delta_{T_0\to T_1}(s)
:=
P_{T_0}(s)
-
\sum_{\Sigma\in\mathcal{F}(x)} w_{\Sigma}(x)\,P_{\Sigma}(s).
\]
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item the cocycle pressure object of \(T_0\) is closed on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\),
    \item the packaged-object theory \(T_1\) is well-defined on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\),
    \item the strict theory-extension theoremlet holds on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\),
    \item and the package-conditioned pressure profiles are well-defined on the audited shell.
\end{enumerate}
Then the weighted package-conditioned pressure gap is nontrivial on the audited shell. Equivalently, the cocycle-level pressure is not sufficient for the packaged future, and the thermodynamic consequence of the extension is a nontrivial conditional pressure disintegration.

\paragraph{Alternative thermodynamic consequence routes.}
The direct stratumwise route was investigated and rejected as the wrong thermodynamic object for the present paper. The accepted route is conditional pressure disintegration. Whether stronger package-conditioned or measure-theoretic consequences can be obtained remains open.

conclusion: Many sciences rely on maps of macroscopic behavior—phase diagrams, stability charts, bifurcation sets, and feasibility regions—but emergence itself is rarely treated as a mapping problem. We introduce emergence atlases: subsets and scalar fields on control space indicating where a macro-description is feasible. In the finite-state setting used here, feasibility means that a packaged description is simultaneously closed, nontrivial, audit-safe, and budget-feasible. We compute such atlases in three settings: analytic law families, full packaging spaces of small systems, and the PICA mechanism algebra. The resulting maps recover exact closure loci and reversible lines, expose multi-objective tradeoffs among closure, directionality, effective information, novelty slack, and budget, and identify mechanism-space regimes together with their sensitive ablations and conservative compact supports. These computations support a simple reframing: emergence is usefully treated as a phase-diagram problem for effective theories in control space. In that view, effective information, irreversibility, coarse-graining quality, and mechanism-space analyses appear not as rival definitions of emergence, but as slices of a larger atlas.

conclusion: A control space U is any set of variables over which macro-law feasibility is to be charted. A control point u ∈ U may include a microscopic law parameter, a packaging or lens, a staging depth tau , a protocol or mechanism variable, and a budget coordinate. Different atlases in this paper use different choices of U : law-space atlases vary microscopic law parameters while holding packaging fixed, packaging-space atlases vary the packaging while holding the microscopic law fixed, and mechanism-space atlases vary protocol/mechanism choices over a fixed finite-state substrate. For a given control point u , let x_t ∈ X denote the microscopic state and let x_ t+1 K_u( x_t) denote the corresponding microscopic update law. Let tau(u) ∈ N be the staging depth at which the macro-description is assessed. An admissible macro-description at u is a pair (Pi,L) ∈ C(u) , where Pi : X → Y is a packaging map and L is a candidate macro update rule on Y . The family C(u) collects whichever package/law pairs are allowed at that control point.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:control_space}
A \emph{control space} $\mathcal{U}$ is any set of variables over which macro-law feasibility is to be charted. A control point $u \in \mathcal{U}$ may include a microscopic law parameter, a packaging or lens, a staging depth $\tau$, a protocol or mechanism variable, and a budget coordinate. Different atlases in this paper use different choices of $\mathcal{U}$: law-space atlases vary microscopic law parameters while holding packaging fixed, packaging-space atlases vary the packaging while holding the microscopic law fixed, and mechanism-space atlases vary protocol/mechanism choices over a fixed finite-state substrate.

For a given control point $u$, let $x_t \in X$ denote the microscopic state and let
\[
x_{t+1} \sim K_u(\,\cdot \mid x_t)
\]
denote the corresponding microscopic update law. Let $\tau(u) \in \mathbb{N}$ be the staging depth at which the macro-description is assessed. An \emph{admissible macro-description} at $u$ is a pair $(\Pi,L) \in \mathfrak{C}(u)$, where $\Pi : X \to Y$ is a packaging map and $L$ is a candidate macro update rule on $Y$. The family $\mathfrak{C}(u)$ collects whichever package/law pairs are allowed at that control point.

conclusion: shows exactly where it aligns with those quantities and where it does not. The result is a more informative scientific object than either a closure-only ranking or an EI-only ranking
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The most direct packaging-space support for the paper's comparison thesis is the EI slice itself. Figure~\ref{fig:packaging_ei_slice} plots EI against closure while encoding objecthood and budget. What it shows is exactly the relationship the atlas view predicts: EI is informative but not dispositive. Some of the highest-EI packagings are trivial as macro-objects; some of the most scientifically useful packagings have only moderate EI but much better closure or objecthood properties. The right interpretation is not that EI is wrong. It is that EI is one coordinate projection of packaging quality.

That point matters because it lets the paper treat causal-emergence-style quantities constructively rather than polemically \cite{hoel2013causal,hoel2017map,rosas2020reconciling}. The atlas does not dismiss effective information. It computes it, places it on the same packaging-space rows as closure, objecthood, novelty, directionality retention, and budget, and then shows exactly where it aligns with those quantities and where it does not. The result is a more informative scientific object than either a closure-only ranking or an EI-only ranking.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Budget is instantiated through explicit within-domain proxies. For analytic and packaging rows, the default structural budget is
\[
\operatorname{Bud}_{\mathrm{pack}}
=
K + c_{\mathrm{lift}} + \tau,
\]
with $c_{\mathrm{lift}}=1$ for uniform lift and $c_{\mathrm{lift}}=K$ for prototype lift. In PICA, the main budget coordinates are enabled-cell count, gated-edge count, and the saved mechanism-budget proxy when available. These budget quantities are comparative within domain; the paper does not claim a universal cross-domain cost unit.

Under calibrated controls, stroboscopic protocols can exhibit _T>0 while their autonomous lifts yield _T 0 (protocol trap), whereas turning on internal phase drive produces a clean null-vs-driven separation with _T(Z)>0 and a detectable projected macro arrow; moreover deterministic coarse-graining never increases _T and can erase it entirely, and packaging along refinement routes exhibits a prototype-driven holonomy defect that is large at moderate timescales while a uniform baseline is near zero and satisfies a gain-plus-mismatch bound. \label{def:substrate}
A substrate $\mathcal S$ consists of:
(i) a state carrier $Z$ (finite in our canonical machine model),
(ii) a composable dynamics primitive (autonomous in the canonical model),
and (iii) an admissible family of deterministic observational maps (lenses) from $Z$ to coarser description spaces.
Additional internal structure may be present (e.g.\ registers, ledgers, prototype selectors), but must be represented as part of state or as derived operators.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:packaging-endomap}
A packaging endomap is a function $e:\alpha\to\alpha$ (for an appropriate carrier $\alpha$) that is exactly or approximately idempotent.
Exact idempotence is the equation $e\circ e = e$.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Realizability alone does not turn a language into a machine: we also want a notion of normal form and mutual simulation.
The appropriate equivalence notion is \emph{packaging equivalence} induced by idempotent(-like) endomaps (\Cref{def:packeq}).
The Lean appendix mechanizes the corresponding algebra: idempotent splitting (fixed points, inclusion/retraction), packaging equivalence as an equivalence relation, and lens saturation as a closure operator (\Cref{app:lean}).

\begin{theorem}[Compilation to $\mathcal S_{\min}$ up to packaging equivalence]
\label{thm:normal-form}
Let $\mathcal S$ be a substrate that realizes P1--P6 without smuggling in the sense of \Cref{def:no-smuggling}.
Assume further that the realized operators are finitary (state and registers can be encoded in a finite carrier) and autonomous once all protocol state is represented.
Then there exists a substrate $\mathcal M\in\mathcal S_{\min}$ and an encoding of $\mathcal S$ into $\mathcal M$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em]
  \item the lens/refinement structure of $\mathcal S$ is simulated by deterministic lenses on $\mathcal M$,
  \item packaging in $\mathcal S$ is simulated by internal packaging endomaps on $\mathcal M$ up to packaging equivalence, and
  \item admissible audits in $\mathcal S$ are represented by intrinsic audits on $\mathcal M$ (in particular, directionality audits respect monotonicity under coarse-graining).
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if two compilations choose the same canonical prototype-selection scheme for each lens (e.g.\ uniform-on-fiber) and the same auditing conventions, then they are mutually simulable up to packaging equivalence via packaging-respecting maps in the sense of \Cref{def:pack-morphism}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Compilation to $\mathcal S_{\min}$ up to packaging equivalence]
\label{thm:normal-form}
Let $\mathcal S$ be a substrate that realizes P1--P6 without smuggling in the sense of \Cref{def:no-smuggling}.
Assume further that the realized operators are finitary (state and registers can be encoded in a finite carrier) and autonomous once all protocol state is represented.
Then there exists a substrate $\mathcal M\in\mathcal S_{\min}$ and an encoding of $\mathcal S$ into $\mathcal M$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em]
  \item the lens/refinement structure of $\mathcal S$ is simulated by deterministic lenses on $\mathcal M$,
  \item packaging in $\mathcal S$ is simulated by internal packaging endomaps on $\mathcal M$ up to packaging equivalence, and
  \item admissible audits in $\mathcal S$ are represented by intrinsic audits on $\mathcal M$ (in particular, directionality audits respect monotonicity under coarse-graining).
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if two compilations choose the same canonical prototype-selection scheme for each lens (e.g.\ uniform-on-fiber) and the same auditing conventions, then they are mutually simulable up to packaging equivalence via packaging-respecting maps in the sense of \Cref{def:pack-morphism}.
\end{theorem}

hypotheses.text: The following substrate features are necessary (up to equivalent internal encodings) to realize the corresponding primitives without smuggling: [leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.35em] Autonomy requires phase-in-state (P3). If a substrate permits staged protocols but does not represent protocol state internally, then stroboscopic composition can produce apparent arrows of time that vanish once the dynamics is made autonomous by lifting state. Therefore, any autonomous semantics for protocols must encode phase-in-state (or an equivalent internal mechanism). Genuine arrows require internal drive (P6 drive ). Autonomy plus staging does not imply directionality. In an autonomous lifted model with reversible internal phase dynamics, protocol-induced arrows can disappear ( Sigma_T 0 ). To obtain a genuine arrow in an autonomous substrate, one needs internal drive detectable by a nonzero affinity class (ACC cycle integrals). Audits must be monotone under coarse-graining (P6). There exist processes with real micro irreversibility but macro observations whose path law is reversal-invariant ( Sigma_T^ macro =0 ). Any audit that reports increased directionality after coarse-graining violates limited-access semantics and is therefore smuggled. Packaging must be an internal (approximate) idempotent endomap (P5). Without an internal endomap e (or closure operator) that induces packaging equivalence x _e y iff e(x)=e(y) , there is no internal notion of ``same packaged object'' and no internal fixed-point criterion for stability. Declaring macrostates by fiat is smuggling. Route mismatch is distinct from directionality (P3 vs.\ P6). Packaging along different refinement routes can yield a measurable holonomy defect (route mismatch), even when directionality audits obey data processing

They are stated at a level that cleanly separates: (i) algebraic infrastructure (idempotents/closure), (ii) audit infrastructure (monotone directionality/drive certificates), and (iii) autonomy discipline (phase-in-state for protocols). The witness suite provides concrete finite constructions and quantitative diagnostics that support the separation claims, while the Lean appendix checks the reusable algebraic lemmas.

conclusion: Time is often treated as a primitive background parameter, and empirical discussions frequently conflate three distinct notions—event ordering, clock measurement, and irreversible directionality—making it difficult to determine when a layer has time versus when time is an artifact of description. Building on Six Birds Theory (SBT) , we propose a layer-relative account in which time is a closure artifact assembled from stable succession (order), staged repeatable carriers (ticks), and irreversible bookkeeping (arrow). We distinguish causation-time within a fixed closure from enablement-time, where the closure itself is rewritten. We instantiate this account in a finite-state Markov laboratory ( Z=X R ) and operationalize it through an audit-and-control workflow: calibrated null regimes, matched controls, and auto-generated evidence tables from reproducible artifacts. We obtain four controlled separations: (i) in a nearly reversible null regime, arrow proxies are 0 , whereas in a record-coupled driven regime they become decisively nonzero (with absolute irreversibility signaled by EP= ); (ii) under consistent estimation, coarse-graining reduces path-space asymmetry (micro macro), preventing ``fake arrows''; (iii) increasing maintenance budget reduces clock drift and failure, while progress metrics detect stall regimes that would otherwise appear stable; and (iv) closure-defect thresholds trigger theory extension only in an enablement regime (not in a no-birth control), and protocol loops exhibit nonzero holonomy in a noncommuting regime but 0 under a commuting control, obstructing a global time potential. These results provide a reproducible method for separating arrows, clocks, constraints, and protocol effects, and for clarifying when ``instant updates'' reflect constraints and records rather than causal channels. We do not derive physical spacetime here; our conclusions rely on audited proxies in a minimal laboratory together with lightweight mechanized structural lemmas.

These results provide a reproducible method for separating arrows, clocks, constraints, and protocol effects, and for clarifying when ``instant updates'' reflect constraints and records rather than causal channels. We do not derive physical spacetime here; our conclusions rely on audited proxies in a minimal laboratory together with lightweight mechanized structural lemmas.

conclusion: First, we do not claim that the laboratory's Phi is ``physical time'' Second, we do not claim that entropy production is the unique arrow
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Limits and scope.}
Several limitations are intentional. First, we do not claim that the laboratory's $\Phi$ is ``physical time''; it is a staged carrier used to audit when a clock can exist in a closure. Second, we do not claim that entropy production is the unique arrow; it is one audit proxy among many, selected for exactness in finite Markov worlds. Third, our enablement mechanism is deliberately simple (a thresholded closure defect). In richer systems, enablement is likely multi-scale and multi-object, with competing closures and budgets. Finally, we do not resolve foundational questions in quantum theory or relativity; we provide an SBT parsing that distinguishes feasibility constraints from causal channels and highlights the role of records and protocol dependence.

conclusion: Randomness is often treated as either ontic indeterminacy or epistemic ignorance. We develop a third, operational account within Six Birds: layer-relative randomness is the predictive residue of non-closure under a chosen packaging and budget. For a micro process X_t and a packaging : X Y , we define the micro-closure deficit at scale by CD_ ( )=I(X_t; Y_ t+ Y_t) , the information about the next packaged state that remains hidden inside the current macro-object. This yields the exact decomposition H(Y_ t+ Y_t)=H(Y_ t+ X_t)+CD_ ( ) , separating intrinsic substrate uncertainty from randomness introduced by discarded distinctions. We connect this exact quantity to computable diagnostics native to earlier Six Birds work, including route mismatch for coarse-grained Markov dynamics and predictive log-loss gaps under limited-memory models. In controlled Markov benchmarks, closure deficit vanishes on exactly lumpable partitions and rises with within-fiber heterogeneity, while route mismatch tracks it closely. In budgeted prediction, increasing memory order buys back hidden distinctions and lowers held-out log loss. In toy hashing, one-wayness and random-lookingness emerge as the same packaging-and-budget phenomenon: high-entropy inputs obey q/2^n inversion scaling, while low-entropy inputs collapse the effect. The result is a measurable account of randomness that unifies coarse-graining, limited prediction, and feasible one-wayness without treating randomness as primitive.

expanded_source_wording_tex: Our claims are deliberately narrower than the familiar metaphysical debate between ontic and epistemic randomness. We do not claim that all randomness is reducible to hidden microstructure, nor do we identify route mismatch with genuine irreversibility. conclusion: The controlled Markov benchmark established what unresolved closure is. The complementary question is what it costs to buy the missing distinctions back once the current package has already failed to stabilize them. To expose that accounting side directly, we fix the strongest hidden-type benchmark and measure the budgeted randomness curve Rand_B empirically using packaged predictors of increasing memory order. The empirical curve is reported in the feasible-class sense of : at budget B=L , we plot the best held-out log loss available among predictors of order at most L . This matters because sparse higher-order contexts can make the raw loss of a particular order- L fit fluctuate upward in finite data, whereas the feasible-class quantity itself should never worsen when the admissible predictor class strictly expands.

Hashing provides an engineered version of the same logic in a deterministic many-to-one map. A truncated digest $H_n : \{0,1\}^m \to \{0,1\}^n$ does not create new entropy; it packages a large input space into a short stable record and leaves preimage identification to whatever budget the observer can afford \citep{rogaway2004cryptographichashfunctionbasics}. We therefore examine three input regimes on small safe truncations: a uniform high-entropy source, a low-entropy synthetic dictionary of size $256$, and a fifty-fifty medium mixture of dictionary and out-of-dictionary inputs.

In the uniform regime, the familiar one-wayness heuristic appears exactly where it should: in the small-success region $q/2^n \le 0.25$, empirical inversion success tracks the line $q/2^n$ with mean absolute deviation $3.70\times 10^{-3}$. \Cref{fig:hashing-inversion} plots empirical success against $q/2^n$ directly. For example, at $n=16$ and budget $q=256$, the empirical success rate is $6.67\times 10^{-3}$ against the simple baseline $256/2^{16}=3.91\times 10^{-3}$. In this regime, the digest is effectively random-looking relative to the bounded inversion budget, even though the map is fully deterministic.

This appendix records the representation-learning result that we treat as auxiliary rather than core evidence \citep{tishby1999bottleneck,geiger2015optimalkullbackleibleraggregation}. The experiment asks whether increasing representational budget, measured by the number of learned clusters $k$, automatically reduces predictive non-closure when packaging is learned from observations rather than supplied by construction. It does not.

We generate observation sequences from the hidden-type process used earlier and learn $k$-means partitions on those observations for $k \in \{2,4,8\}$ \citep{macqueen1967somemethods}. For each learned packaging we then evaluate the resulting packaged sequence by held-out first- and second-order predictive log loss and by the empirical conditional mutual information
\[
\widehat I(X_t;Y_{t+1}\mid Y_t),
\]
computed from the joint sequence of hidden microstates and learned packaged labels. In this appendix we report the \emph{raw} empirical conditional mutual information, not the normalized version used only for diagnostics during development.

conclusion: Formal theories of consciousness often mix mathematical structure, empirical access, and ontological interpretation inside single claims. We present an architecture that separates them by construction: an eight-clause closure package (objecthood, strict promotion, a reflexive self-coordinate, non-exposure, action credit, temporal closure, binding, and viability) specified as a full design and audit contract, with every result graded as a structural theorem, a recognition bridge, a conditional ontological implication, or an open target. The evidence base consists of exact finite studies, meaning exhaustively enumerated rational computations on declared carriers, together with selected machine-checked Lean kernels. The central exact result: on a declared twelve-state deadline carrier, every public-lens policy has an empty viability kernel, the canonical predictive quotient restores a ten-state kernel, and the unique minimal closure-restoring refinement splits exactly one public fiber; extension beyond the carrier is a conditional schema, not a generic theorem. A structural catalog then recasts privacy, the explanatory gap, zombies, free will, binding, temporal experience, valence, quality geometry, inverted spectra, personal identity, combination, and the meta-problem as interface-relative factorization, quotient, viability, gauge, and audit results. Realization is split into seven graded claims: a mechanized conditional bridge purchases it only from assumed certificate soundness plus an ontic-closure postulate, and there is no integrated certified instance and no empirical validation. An auditable code baseline with executable finite controls and predeclared prospective empirical obligations accompanies the paper.

conclusion: Formal theories of consciousness are difficult to compare, and difficult to trust, partly because three different kinds of claim routinely travel in one sentence: mathematical claims about a formal structure, empirical claims about how that structure meets observation, and ontological claims about what the structure's satisfaction would be. The field has begun to treat this as a foundational problem rather than a stylistic one. General frameworks for mathematical models of consciousness ask what a model must declare before it says anything ; formal work on testability shows that inference procedures and prediction data can interact so badly that a theory becomes unfalsifiable or trivially falsified ; and large adversarial collaborations have demonstrated how much machinery is needed to test even two well-resourced theories against each other, without producing a definitive verdict . Landscape reviews count theory families by the dozen . In such a field, a paper's first obligation is to say exactly what kind of claim each of its sentences makes. This paper takes that obligation as its organizing principle. It presents an architecture for consciousness built from standard finite mathematics: finite carriers, lenses, quotients, refinements, closure operators, viability kernels, and audited promotion between description layers. Around that architecture it assembles a catalog of exact finite results, a small set of machine-checked kernels, and one explicitly priced ontological bridge. Every scientific sentence in the paper is assigned to one of four claim lanes, defined in Section : structural results [S] (theorems and exact finite constructions), recognition bridges [R] (proposed interpretive mappings, never derivations), ontological implications [O] (conditional on named postulates), and open targets [OPEN] . The lane discipline is not decoration; it is enforced by a sentence-level claim ledger in the artifact, and the paper's central negative rule is that no amount of [S] material ever implies an [O] conclusion without the named purchases.

\begin{description}
\item[Tier S (structural).] Mathematical content about declared finite
objects. Tier~S subdivides by \emph{claim form}: a \emph{theorem-grade exact
result} is proved or exhaustively computed on its declared carrier; a
\emph{schema} is a definition or conditional statement whose hypotheses are
displayed and not discharged; a \emph{pointer} re-scopes an existing result to
a new reading without new mathematics; a \emph{composition} combines landed
results under a declared convention. Tier~S claims are established relative to
their carriers and interfaces, and to nothing else.
\item[Tier R (recognition).] A proposed mapping between a structural object
and a familiar mental or phenomenal category, for example reading a
constraint's dual price as felt valence. Recognition bridges are hypotheses.
They are \emph{proposed}, \emph{named}, and \emph{retractable}; they are never
derivations, and a counterexample to a bridge retracts the bridge, not the
mathematics under it.
\item[Tier O (ontological).] A claim about what satisfaction of the structure
would be. All Tier~O content in this paper is conditional on named postulates
(Section~\ref{sec:t17}); the paper contains no unconditional Tier~O sentence.
\item[OPEN.] A target that is stated, motivated, and not achieved. Open
targets are recorded in the artifact with explicit markers rather than
implied by silence.
\end{description}

conclusion: A carrier is a finite set X of states. conclusion: Fix a carrier with declared dynamics and a lens q . Two states (or histories) are observationally equivalent when all admissible current observables agree on them; the induced quotient is the current public quotient Q . They are predictively equivalent when they agree on the full family of admissible future behavior (continuation laws, or distributions over future observable trajectories under all admissible continuations); the induced quotient is the predictive quotient M . Predictive equivalence refines observational equivalence, giving a canonical comparison map pi : M → Q . The gap between them, same Q -class with different M -class, is a factorization defect and is the recurring engine of this paper.

conclusion: The full C-package C is the eight-clause full-design and audit contract C1 – C8 , together with cross-clause coherence data and a full promotion-gate panel. A candidate consists of a carrier X , declared transition/action families, a public lens and exposure channels, a predictive self-lens, branch structure, a maintenance ledger, and protocol generators; the clauses constrain that data as follows. A declared multiscale exposure-closure family with robust fixed-point structure: closure operators E_tau at declared stagings tau , exact fixed-point and defect bookkeeping, and perturbation audits with declared retention thresholds. A strict promoted distinction across declared layers: Delta_ fact (pi_0,pi_1)≠∅ for the declared lower and promoted readouts, certified by a split pair. A recursively stable self-coordinate: refinement of the public self-lens by dynamical profiles terminates at a predictive quotient that carries the package's own continuation coordinate. The determining predictive state is not exposed relative to the declared public channel family: no admissible current observable factors through it non-constantly on the realized support. Hiddenness is channel-relative by construction. A declared audit of action credit: generator provenance routes computed directionality into self, other, or none, with scheduled and internalized controls that must not be credited as self. A maintained, funded order/tick/arrow structure: a staged phase carrier that persists and progresses under budget, with the arrow carried by the package's own audit channel rather than by external scheduling. Strict recombination refinement over the branchwise quotient: joint content over declared branches, witnessed by R_ rec K_ bw (Section ). Nonempty maintained viability: K_ viab ≠∅ under the declared maintenance ledger, with underfunding collapsing the kernel.

\label{def:cpackage}
The \emph{full C-package} $\mathfrak{C}$ is the eight-clause full-design and audit
contract $\mathrm{C1}$--$\mathrm{C8}$, together with cross-clause coherence
data and a full promotion-gate panel. A candidate consists of a carrier $X$,
declared transition/action families, a public lens and exposure channels, a
predictive self-lens, branch structure, a maintenance ledger, and protocol
generators; the clauses constrain that data as follows.
\begin{description}
\item[C1 (objecthood).] A declared multiscale exposure-closure family with
robust fixed-point structure: closure operators $E_\tau$ at declared stagings
$\tau$, exact fixed-point and defect bookkeeping, and perturbation audits with
declared retention thresholds.
\item[C2 (strict promotion).] A strict promoted distinction across declared
layers: $\Delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\emptyset$ for the declared lower and promoted
readouts, certified by a split pair.
\item[C3 (reflexive self-coordinate).] A recursively stable self-coordinate:

\label{def:cpackage}
The \emph{full C-package} $\Cpkg$ is the eight-clause full-design and audit
contract $\mathrm{C1}$--$\mathrm{C8}$, together with cross-clause coherence
data and a full promotion-gate panel. A candidate consists of a carrier $X$,
declared transition/action families, a public lens and exposure channels, a
predictive self-lens, branch structure, a maintenance ledger, and protocol
generators; the clauses constrain that data as follows.
\begin{description}
\item[C1 (objecthood).] A declared multiscale exposure-closure family with
robust fixed-point structure: closure operators $E_\tau$ at declared stagings
$\tau$, exact fixed-point and defect bookkeeping, and perturbation audits with
declared retention thresholds.
\item[C2 (strict promotion).] A strict promoted distinction across declared
layers: $\Dfact(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\emptyset$ for the declared lower and promoted
readouts, certified by a split pair.
\item[C3 (reflexive self-coordinate).] A recursively stable self-coordinate:
refinement of the public self-lens by dynamical profiles terminates at a
predictive quotient that carries the package's own continuation coordinate.
\item[C4 (non-exposure).] The determining predictive state is not exposed
relative to the declared public channel family: no admissible current
observable factors through it non-constantly on the realized support.
Hiddenness is channel-relative by construction.
\item[C5 (drive/credit).] A declared audit of action credit: generator
provenance routes computed directionality into \emph{self}, \emph{other}, or
\emph{none}, with scheduled and internalized controls that must not be
credited as self.
\item[C6 (temporal closure).] A maintained, funded order/tick/arrow structure:
a staged phase carrier that persists and progresses under budget, with the
arrow carried by the package's own audit channel rather than by external
scheduling.
\item[C7 (binding).] Strict recombination refinement over the branchwise
quotient: joint content over declared branches, witnessed by
$\Rrec \succ \Kbw$ (Section~\ref{sec:structure}).
\item[C8 (viability).] Nonempty maintained viability: $\Kviab\neq\emptyset$
under the declared maintenance ledger, with underfunding collapsing the
kernel.
\end{description}

Scope: the declared twelve-state deadline carrier, its action family, and its lens. On this carrier: Public exhaustion. The five-class continuation-law abstraction L restores a ten-state kernel, and the canonical predictive quotient M = q × L restores exactly the same ten states: K_ viab (L) = K_ viab (M) , |K_ viab (M)| = 10 , certified by a separate nine-class search and a refinement audit. expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Exact forcing and minimal restoration; T1]
\label{thm:t1}
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} theorem-grade on the exact T1-L1 carrier; conditional
family schema beyond it. \emph{Scope:} the declared twelve-state deadline
carrier, its action family, and its lens. On this carrier:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Public exhaustion.} Every $q$-measurable feedback policy has an
empty deadline viability kernel: $K_{\mathrm{viab}}(q) = \emptyset$, by exhaustive
enumeration of all public-lens policies.
\item \textbf{Predictive restoration.} The five-class continuation-law
abstraction $L$ restores a ten-state kernel, and the canonical predictive
quotient $M = q \times L$ restores exactly the same ten states:
$K_{\mathrm{viab}}(L) = K_{\mathrm{viab}}(M)$, $|K_{\mathrm{viab}}(M)| = 10$, certified by a separate
nine-class search and a refinement audit.
\item \textbf{Unique minimal repair.} Among all $64$ refinements of the
public lens, the unique minimal closure-restoring refinement is the
seven-class quotient $\Pi_*$ that splits exactly the public fiber $p=1$;
every closure-restoring refinement splits that fiber, and the maximal
refinement that leaves $p=1$ unsplit has empty kernel.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Assumptions:} deadline active; live, resettable, non-publicly-definable
phase. \emph{Nonclaim:} this does not show that all bounded self-predicting
systems must form selves, and it is not an empirical result about any actual
system.
\end{theorem}

Here $p=1$ is a public \emph{position coordinate} value naming the fiber the
minimal refinement splits; it is not a probability, and not a refinement
parameter.

\begin{theorem}[Exact forcing and minimal restoration; T1]
\label{thm:t1}
\gradeS{} \emph{Grade:} theorem-grade on the exact T1-L1 carrier; conditional
family schema beyond it. \emph{Scope:} the declared twelve-state deadline
carrier, its action family, and its lens. On this carrier:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Public exhaustion.} Every $q$-measurable feedback policy has an
empty deadline viability kernel: $\Kviab(q) = \emptyset$, by exhaustive
enumeration of all public-lens policies.

abstraction $L$ restores a ten-state kernel, and the canonical predictive
quotient $M = q \times L$ restores exactly the same ten states:
$\Kviab(L) = \Kviab(M)$, $|\Kviab(M)| = 10$, certified by a separate
nine-class search and a refinement audit.

public lens, the unique minimal closure-restoring refinement is the
seven-class quotient $\Pi_*$ that splits exactly the public fiber $p=1$;
every closure-restoring refinement splits that fiber, and the maximal
refinement that leaves $p=1$ unsplit has empty kernel.
\end{enumerate}

phase. \emph{Nonclaim:} this does not show that all bounded self-predicting
systems must form selves, and it is not an empirical result about any actual
system.
\end{theorem}

Here $p=1$ is a public \emph{position coordinate} value naming the fiber the
minimal refinement splits; it is not a probability, and not a refinement
parameter.

conclusion: What generalizes, and at what price, is stated once and inherited everywhere. For substrates satisfying the published deadline-family conditions (a live, resettable, non-publicly-definable phase, and a deadline that makes the hidden continuation law viability-relevant), self-prediction through a bounded public self-lens generically carries a predictive non-factorization obstruction, and under the deadline that obstruction is viability-relevant. That family statement is a conditional schema [S] : all hypotheses displayed, none discharged beyond the exact carrier. The conditions are strong, and systems lacking them fall into the controls, not into the forced case. No claim is made that the conditions are universal or empirically common, and no generic ``selfhood theorem'' is asserted. Mechanization boundary. The Lean kernel for this law formalizes the full twelve-state carrier and the finite public, continuation-law, and canonical quotient tables; the exhaustive policy and refinement searches are certified by the Python study and its tests, not by a general Lean fixed-point theorem. Lean's C1 facts cover the tau=1 operator (fixed-point verification by evaluation and the defect witness), not uniqueness, the tau=2..4 rows, or the perturbation audit; Lean's C3 facts prove terminal-partition stability and public instability with the 6/7/7 sizes as declared constants, while the refinement execution is Python-certified.

conclusion: [S] Grade: theorem-grade direct finite instantiation; the C4 condition is generic and declared, not universal. Scope: the declared channel family Lambda on the finite privacy-wheel carrier. \label{thm:t5}
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} clauses graded individually below. \emph{Scope:} one
declared deterministic support, bounded observer budgets, declared generator
provenance. \emph{Nonclaim:} no ontic indeterminacy, no metaphysical
freedom, no disproof of every libertarian view.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Lawfulness} (framing). Choices are readouts of the run; no
spontaneity primitive is added.
\item \emph{External underivability} (theorem-grade toy instantiation). A
bounded public observer at budget $B$ can face positive priced residue:
same-summary states with different deterministic choices. The exact scores at
budgets $0,1,2$ are $1, 1, 1/2$, non-increasing, with a split witness at every
budget.
\item \emph{Self-underivability} (direct imported-theorem instantiation). The
self-model is a bounded packaging; a complete same-level self-audit
classifies \texttt{undefined\_circular} (an out-of-scope variant:
\texttt{outside\_scope}), and the self-model summary has its own
same-summary/different-choice split pair.
\item \emph{Authorship} (direct instantiation of no-fake-arrow audits).
Directionality is credited to the agent only when it survives the
protocol-trap and data-processing nulls and one common credit rule returns
\emph{self}: genuine autonomous drive has unequal exact self-channel cycle
products $8/27$ versus $1/27$; the externally scheduled apparent arrow has
unequal \emph{other}-channel products ($0$ versus $16/81$), a real arrow
credited to other rather than to self; and after schedule internalization the lifted kernel decomposes
exactly into clock and content channels, both balanced ($0$ versus $0$ on
credited products; canonical lifted cycle $1/324$ each way), so the same rule
returns \emph{none}. Deterministic coarsening of the blocked case leaves
equal path fluxes ($1/27$ each way): observation does not create affinity.
\item \emph{Libertarianism foreclosed} (foreclosure argument). The positive
residue of clauses 2--3 is bounded-observer ignorance under declared
packaging and budget, not substrate spontaneity.
\item \emph{Deflation foreclosed} \textsf{[O]}-flavored. ``Only a lower-layer
event'' commits the factorization error: once the layer is strict, the layer
claim cannot be replaced by a base-layer paraphrase without losing the
certificate, as T3 establishes. This is a foreclosure argument with an
ontological flavor, not a Tier~S theorem.
\end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{T6: introspection limits without introspection nihilism.}
\begin{theorem}[Same-level audit failure, rotating towers, confabulation; T6]
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} direct instantiation of imported self-audit theorems
plus finite toy extension. \emph{Scope:} instrument-indexed claims; complete
same-level self-certification, not ordinary introspection. No instrument
certifies its own complete soundness at its own level: the claim classifies
\texttt{undefined\_circular} or \texttt{outside\_scope}; a level-shift bridge
reclassifies it as \texttt{provisional}, never as same-level final. Every
finite rotating-audit tower has an uncertified top: the three-level toy tower
computes own-level statuses (\texttt{undefined\_circular} at each level),
bridge statuses (\texttt{provisional}, \texttt{provisional}), and
top-requires-next-level $=$ true. \emph{Confabulation corollary} (toy
extension; schema beyond it): with an audit update missing, the unique
closure-preserving completion from visible records is \emph{left} while the
hidden true state is \emph{right}: coherent and wrong. With the update
present, the unique completion is correct and the verdict disappears.
\emph{Nonclaim:} introspection is neither impossible nor worthless; partial,
level-shifted, bounded audit remains admissible, and self-image stability
over time is named as dependent on an open conjecture, not claimed.
\end{theorem}

conclusion: [S] Grade: theorem-grade finite instantiation of imported strict-refinement machinery. Scope: the declared branch family and interfaces. Binding is certified by strict refinement R_ rec K_ bw : two assemblages in one branchwise class and distinct recombination classes. On the exact carrier: the coupled regime has K_ bw blocks (2) and R_ rec blocks (1,1) with witness (bound-diagonal, bound-crossed); marking a branch-identifying observable collapses the partitions to exact equality ( R_ rec = K_ bw , both (1,1) ); erasure of the mark restores the original witness; and the aggregation control, in which no joint observable is ever declared, has R_ rec = K_ bw from the start (a never-coupled product, not a marked collapse). conclusion: [S] Grade: theorem-grade finite instantiation of imported clock and protocol criteria. Scope: the declared three-phase clock carrier and protocol family. The experienced-present proxy is the package's stabilized (order, tick, arrow) triple, with width the closure timescale tau . The single mechanism advance = b/(b+1) at budget b=2 gives exact progress 2/3 and tick rate 2/9 ; the funded nine-step trace has six advances, two completed wraps, and a monotone ledger with Delta A = 2 > 0 ; the unfunded control ( b=0 ) stalls exactly ( 0 progress, 0 ticks, constant trace, no arrow). No single global ``now'' is guaranteed across sub-closures: the noncommuting protocol pair (rotation, swap) has holonomy defect 1 and the commuting control ( R , R^2 ) defect 0 , so path-dependent local time translations admit no global potential. Finally, felt-flow candidates route through the audit channel, never through holonomy alone: the holonomy-without-drive control derives an unbiased audit support with equal products ( 3/1000 each way) and is classified blocked. Nonclaim: no universal specious-present width, no physical time or spacetime, and holonomy is never a directionality certificate.

conclusion: [S] Grade: theorem-grade finite duality core. Scope: one exact rational linear program over a three-action policy simplex with two maintenance budgets. At binding budgets b=(2,2) : optimum value 76/11 , both constraints tight, exact local duals lambda = (24/11, 14/11) . Slack regime at b=(5,1) : lambda_1 = 0 exactly. Tightening the first budget across (4,3,2,3/2) recomputes lambda_1 = (0, 4/3, 24/11, 24/11) , non-decreasing. Proxy discipline: a declared row-permuted proxy cost yields unstable recovered proxy prices across two environment phases ( 4 and 0 ), while the true LP is phase-independent by construction; a planted dual certificate with positive price on a slack constraint violates complementary slackness and is rejected. Viability tie: the kernel is nonempty when both budgets meet their thresholds and empty when either is underfunded by 1/11 . Nonclaim: shadow-price duality is standard mathematics, and none of these values generalizes to actual subjects.

\paragraph{T13: the inverted spectrum as a gauge computation.}
\begin{theorem}[Descent-fixing gauge and rigidification; T13]
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} theorem-grade exact finite construction; the broader
quality-space rigidification principle is schema-grade. \emph{Scope:} an
eight-state fiber bundle, $|Q| = 4$ public classes with two fiber points
each, declared descents. Define the descent-fixing gauge group
$G = \{\sigma \in \mathrm{Aut}(M) : \pi\sigma = \pi \text{ and } d\sigma = d
\text{ for every admissible descent } d\}$. Spectrum inversion is a lawful
distinct possibility exactly to the extent that $G$ is nontrivial. Exact
enumeration: $|\mathrm{Aut}|=40320$ automorphisms of the support, $16$
projection-fixing, and $G = \{\mathrm{id}, \text{global swap}\} \cong
\mathbb{Z}_2$ in the symmetric case; adding \emph{one} declared,
descent-visible discrimination-density orientation (calibrated by T12's
landed local signature at one public class) recomputes $G = \{\mathrm{id}\}$.
Route transport between two isomorphic fibers shows the same contrast: two
admissible transports symmetric, exactly one rigidified. \emph{Nonclaim:} no
claim that any particular quality space has nontrivial $G$; the rigidifier is
a modeled assumption, not a measurement; and if richer quality spaces always
rigidify, the inverted spectrum dissolves, which is an allowed outcome.
\end{theorem}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{T18a (layer-minted proper time).} \textsf{[S]} theorem-grade finite
extension. The package's temporal coordinate does not factor through
substrate time: the exact strictness witness is a state pair with equal
substrate time and different package tick parity, so
$\Delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\text{substrate time}, \text{package time}) \neq \emptyset$; T8's
funded triple is reused unchanged. Nonclaim: no relativistic proper time, no
claim that every subject has this clock.
\item \textbf{T18b (enablement as a lens rewrite).} \textsf{[S]} theorem-grade
exact finite instantiation. Promotion of a layer is an \emph{enablement-time}
event: a closure rewrite that creates the variable set in which the layer's
causation-time then runs. Exactly: the phase-omitting coarse lens has closure
defects $(1,1,1)$ across horizons; the enriched lens has $(0,0,0)$; the
partial-enrichment variant drops $(4/7,4/7,4/7)$ to $(0,0,0)$ using only the
relevant parity coordinate, strictly coarser than full reveal; the no-birth
control has zero defects before and after, so no beneficial rewrite exists.
Nonclaim (the repository name is ``subject birth''): no subject is created or
detected; the theorem is a finite lens-rewrite computation.
\item \textbf{T18c (demoted).} The intended theorem, temporal closure as a
precondition for stating the other clauses, is \emph{not} landed. The
static source audit finds explicit horizon/deadline tokens only in T1 among
T1/T2/T5/T7. T18c is therefore a schema-grade dependency observation,
recorded as demoted, and nothing in this paper cites it as a theorem.
\item \textbf{T18d (state taxonomy by funding and gating).} \textsf{[S]}
taxonomy-grade finite construction. Funding and entrainment gates classify

\paragraph{T10: a graded, hysteretic, clause-decomposable boundary.}
\begin{theorem}[Existence boundary schema; T10]
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} schema plus exact correspondences. \emph{Scope:} a
three-state maintenance carrier with a threaded record accumulator (credit
accrues $1/8$ after a nonempty kernel to a cap of $1/4$, decays $1/8$ after
an empty one) over the budget grid $\{0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1\}$.
Existence-boundary labels are modeled as viability collapses, that is, as
crossings of $K_{\mathrm{viab}}=\emptyset$ under the declared ledger, and the finite
prediction is threefold. \emph{Graded:} kernel sizes pass through intermediate
islands, up-sweep $[0,0,1,2,3]$, down-sweep $[3,3,2,1,0]$. \emph{Hysteretic:}
the up-sweep first-nonempty threshold is $1/2$ while the primed down-sweep
last-nonempty threshold is $1/4$; recovery and collapse thresholds differ
because the mechanism carries record state, not because thresholds were
tabled separately. \emph{Clause-decomposable:} C1-style persistence can
coexist with collapsed C7 binding (covert-awareness pattern) or collapsed C6
temporal closure (timeless pattern), by importing the respective controls;
full collapse zeroes all three. Robustness is conditional, not universal: a
weaker accumulator rule loses strict hysteresis and a stronger one never
re-crosses on the tested grid. \emph{Nonclaim:} no claim that actual loss or
recovery of consciousness is hysteretic, and any external measure of closure
depth would need its own descent audit, and none is given.
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{T14: identity as predictive lineage.}
\begin{theorem}[Lineage, trauma, fission/fusion, empty target; T14]
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} theorem-grade transfer of imported route-transport
machinery plus finite extensions. \emph{Scope:} a declared memory-wheel route
package with three histories, one current class, two predictive classes.
Identity over time is represented by the lineage of the predictive quotient
$M$: by the imported reachable-image factorization theorem, any
future-sufficient self-summary factors to $M$ (the toy computes the factor
from a strictly finer candidate and rejects the reverse). \emph{Trauma
shape:} a loop that is current-trivial and predictively nontrivial moves
$0/1$ of current classes and $1/1$ of predictive classes: same by all
present tests, changed in continuation. The identity-loop control moves
neither. \emph{Fission/fusion:} continuation maps on $M$-fibers classify
exactly as fiber-splitting (duplicated support) and fiber-merging (merged
support). \emph{Empty target:} the funded support has kernel size $3$; the
underfunded support has $K_{\mathrm{viab}}=\emptyset$ and empty post-exit fiber image,
so no continuation preserves the pre-exit $M$-fiber. \emph{Nonclaim:} no
complete metaphysics of personal identity. Token-independence and
death-as-dissolution readings are one-sentence Tier~O pointers deferred to
Section~\ref{sec:t17}; the Tier~S death fact is only $K_{\mathrm{viab}}=\emptyset$ plus
no fiber-preserving continuation, and the empty-target computation is
Python-certified (it is outside the law's Lean kernel).
\end{theorem}

\begin{description}
\item[T17-S (simplified certificate schema).] \textsf{[S]} structural schema.
Lean defines a carrier-indexed \emph{simplified} certificate
$\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}(X)$: mechanics-based clause predicates C1--C8 over one declared
transition/action family and lens family (the C1/C5/C6/C8 audit objects are
equation-coupled to the declared mechanics; C4/C7 are structurally
constrained on the same support but not transition-coupled, a schema-grade
distinction recorded explicitly), cross-clause coherence requiring one
nonempty communicating viable hub containing the clause witnesses, and a
simplified promotion ledger. The schemas are not ordered by any landed
theorem: $\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}$ uses a weaker imported gate ledger while adding one-step
restrictions absent from the full design definition; no implication or
equivalence between $\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}$ and $\mathfrak{C}$ has been proved or is claimed,
and no integrated instance is exhibited. T17-S does not claim its schema
suffices for lawful closure or consciousness; that is exactly the
additional purchase in T17-O.
\item[T17-P (witness catalog and hygiene protocol).] \textsf{[S]}
protocol/catalog. The Python protocol imports and re-verifies eight per-law
witness fields (one row per clause, sourced from the landed laws of
Sections~\ref{sec:t1}--\ref{sec:clusters}) and recursively scans stored
condition-bearing values for smuggled vocabulary. Every current row carries
the verdict \texttt{witness\_verified}; no row label is a realization
verdict, and the protocol constructs no candidate, no integrated carrier, no
gate-panel object, and no realization result.
\item[T17-M (simplified certificate contrast).] \textsf{[S]} schema. Lean
defines $\mathrm{SimplifiedCertificateContrast}(a,b) :=
\mathrm{PublicMatch}(a,b) \wedge \mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}(a) \wedge \neg\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}(b)$:
dynamic public-statistics matching over the complete public observation, a
simplified certificate for $a$, and its absence for $b$. This is an
explicitly simplified approximation of T4b's demarcation target, not the
full-certificate relation, which remains open until a full certificate
exists.
\item[T17-O (conditional realization bridge).] \textsf{[O]} axiom-relative
conditional schema; the exact logical form is displayed below.
\item[T17-I (integrated instance).] \textsf{[OPEN]}. The required deliverable is
absent: an exhibited carrier and package satisfying a \emph{full} design-level
certificate, together with a \emph{proved} (not assumed) certificate-soundness
theorem. Both artifacts record this explicitly: Lean pins
$\texttt{singleCarrierInstanceExhibited}=\texttt{false}$ and Python pins the
same flag with realization grade \texttt{schema}.
\item[T17a (report-interface pointer).] \textsf{[S]} interface-relative pointer.
On the finite T3/T9 carrier, hidden no-report content does not factor through
the declared report channel. This says nothing about whether a designer could
specify or predict content from the complete state, initial conditions, or
dynamics.
\item[T17b (declared-interface opacity pointer).] \textsf{[S]}
interface-relative pointer. Relative to the declared current channels, T2's
hidden structure does not descend and T9 blocks overreading the report
boundary. Opacity may disappear under an expanded interface (T2's own
dissolution control demonstrates this); this is not opacity to every creator
or instrument, and it carries no moral-status conclusion.
\end{description}

\label{thm:t17o}
\textsf{[O]} \emph{Grade:} axiom-relative conditional schema, mechanized.
\emph{Scope:} arbitrary carrier type $X$ and package $\mathrm{pkg}$;
$\mathrm{ClosureComplete}$ and $\mathrm{Realized}$ are caller-supplied
predicate parameters. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(H1)] \emph{certificate soundness}: every simplified certificate is
sound for lawful audited closure,
$\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}(X, \mathrm{pkg}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{ClosureComplete}(X,
\mathrm{pkg})$, an unproved schema premise that is neither A1 nor A2; and
\item[(H2)] \emph{A1}: lawful audited closure is realization,
$\mathrm{ClosureComplete}(X, \mathrm{pkg}) \Rightarrow
\mathrm{Realized}(X, \mathrm{pkg})$.
\end{itemize}
Then every simplified-certified package is realized:
$\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}(X, \mathrm{pkg}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Realized}(X, \mathrm{pkg})$,
uniformly in the carrier type. \emph{Nonclaim:} neither premise is proved;
no A2 transport or invariance theorem exists (the universal carrier parameter
is A2's only footprint, not a proof step); no package is realized
unconditionally; and no candidate is certified.

\label{thm:t17o}
\gradeO{} \emph{Grade:} axiom-relative conditional schema, mechanized.
\emph{Scope:} arbitrary carrier type $X$ and package $\mathrm{pkg}$;
$\mathrm{ClosureComplete}$ and $\mathrm{Realized}$ are caller-supplied
predicate parameters. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(H1)] \emph{certificate soundness}: every simplified certificate is
sound for lawful audited closure,
$\Certsimp(X, \mathrm{pkg}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{ClosureComplete}(X,
\mathrm{pkg})$, an unproved schema premise that is neither A1 nor A2; and
\item[(H2)] \emph{A1}: lawful audited closure is realization,
$\mathrm{ClosureComplete}(X, \mathrm{pkg}) \Rightarrow
\mathrm{Realized}(X, \mathrm{pkg})$.
\end{itemize}
Then every simplified-certified package is realized:
$\Certsimp(X, \mathrm{pkg}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Realized}(X, \mathrm{pkg})$,
uniformly in the carrier type. \emph{Nonclaim:} neither premise is proved;
no A2 transport or invariance theorem exists (the universal carrier parameter
is A2's only footprint, not a proof step); no package is realized
unconditionally; and no candidate is certified.

Twelve limitations, before any conclusion.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Exact finite models only.} Every positive result lives on a
declared toy carrier. Nothing licenses transfer to large, noisy, or
continuous systems beyond the displayed conditional schemas.
\item \textbf{No empirical content.} No dataset, no parameter fit, no
validation, no phenomenon rows (Section~\ref{sec:empirical}).
\item \textbf{Provenance of predictions.} The artifact contains documents
labelled as predictions, but their initial Git history does not establish
temporal precedence over implementations, and later corrections are
versioned. Nothing in this paper calls them preregistered.
\item \textbf{Selected mechanization.} Lean coverage is selected, not
catalog-wide: kernels prove core facts and pin many enumerated values as
certified constants matching the Python computations (per-law boundaries in
Table~\ref{tbl:catalog} and Appendix~\ref{app:repro}); the current
manifest-level validator accepts a zero-row schema and is a known release
blocker, so no manifest-audited coverage claim is made.
\item \textbf{Inherited trust base.} The Lean development trusts vendored
foundations modules and declared axioms from the companion corpus, cataloged
in Appendix~\ref{app:repro}; their opacity guards are inherited, not
re-proved.
\item \textbf{T1's family boundary.} The forcing theorem is exact on one
carrier; the family schema's hypotheses (live non-definable phase, deadline
relevance) are strong and not claimed common (Section~\ref{sec:t1family}).
\item \textbf{T12's open target.} Geometry birth (fitted distortion,
dimension, curvature transport) is not landed; the landed object is an
audited induced geometry.
\item \textbf{T16's conventions.} The meta-problem composition is relative
to a declared completion convention, and its carrier collapses several
premises extensionally.
\item \textbf{T17's open core.} The simplified/full schema relation is
unproved in both directions, certificate soundness is assumed where used,
A2 has no formal theorem, and T17-I, the integrated instance, is open
(Section~\ref{sec:t17}).
\item \textbf{T18c demoted.} The temporal-precondition claim is a dependency
observation, not a theorem.
\item \textbf{Recognition bridges are unproved.} Valence, phenomenological
clause mappings, attention readings, and all state-taxonomy readings are
named hypotheses (\textsf{[R]}), each retractable without structural loss.
\item \textbf{Review status.} The artifact's ``external review request''
documents record an internal author-driven review loop; they are not
independent peer review, and this preprint has not been peer reviewed.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: We present a reproducible computational framework for defining and measuring agency in finite controlled Markov kernels without assuming goals, utilities, or homunculi. The framework operationalizes three complementary metrics: (i) viability kernels (greatest controlled-invariant safe sets under ledger-gated feasibility and successor-support semantics), (ii) feasible empowerment (channel capacity of the induced action-to-output channel restricted by budgets), and (iii) an empirical packaging endomap whose idempotence defect quantifies objecthood for coarse lenses. Building on Six Birds Theory (SBT, ), we propose that an agent is a theory object—a maintained package inside an induced layer with a ledger-gated interface—and we separate agenthood (enablement: the layer exists and persists) from agency (causation: interface interventions change outside futures). Throughout, ``theory'' is used in the SBT technical sense—a closure (lens + completion + audit)—not as a speculative hypothesis or manuscript-type category. Across matched-control ablations in a minimal ring-world substrate, we obtain four auditable separations: (1) calibrated null regimes prevent false positives (single-action: 0-bit empowerment; schedule trap: 1 bit under the wrong model, 0 under the correct one); (2) enabling repair collapses idempotence defect at =2 from 1 to 0; (3) enabling protocol holonomy leaves H=1 unchanged but increases empowerment for H 2 ; and (4) operator rewriting (skill ) monotonically increases median empowerment ( 0.73 1.34 bits). All experiments are driven by deterministic, hash-traceable scripts with a strict audit mode, and a Lean 4 anchor formalizes the viability-kernel fixed-point property. We are explicit that stronger claims about goals, consciousness, or real organisms are not established here; our conclusions rely on finite witnesses and operational proxies under explicit controls.

conclusion: Definition (Theory object). A theory object is an object inside a theory: a packaged macro label (or invariant package) that is stable under the closures induced by T at the relevant horizon. Operationally, low idempotence defect means the macro labels behave like objects under composition; nonempty viability kernel means such objects can persist under robust support semantics. An agent is a theory object equipped with an interface alphabet whose feasible interventions induce a nontrivial action channel to outside outputs (positive feasible empowerment).

conclusion: A controlled stochastic kernel is a row-stochastic tensor P[a,s,s'] Pr(s_ t+1 =s' s_t=s, a_t=a), with P[a,s,s'] 0 and _ s' P[a,s,s']=1 for all (a,s) . For a state distribution d (row vector), one step under action a is d' = d P[a, , ] .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Let $S=\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ be a finite state space and $A=\{0,1,\dots,m-1\}$ a finite action set. A controlled stochastic kernel is a row-stochastic tensor
\[
P[a,s,s'] \equiv \Pr(s_{t+1}=s' \mid s_t=s, a_t=a),
\]
with $P[a,s,s']\ge 0$ and $\sum_{s'}P[a,s,s']=1$ for all $(a,s)$. For a state distribution $d$ (row vector), one step under action $a$ is $d' = d\,P[a,\cdot,\cdot]$.

\[

A ledger is a nonnegative scalar extracted from state, $r:S\to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$. Each action has a nonnegative cost $c:A\to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$. The feasible actions at state $s$ are
\[
A_{\mathrm{feas}}(s) \;:=\; \{\, a\in A \;:\; c(a)\le r(s)\,\}.
\]
This is the operational form of P$_2$ (constraints) and P$_6$ (accounting): infeasible interface commands are not ``actions'' in the induced layer.

\paragraph{Definition (Viability operator / controlled-invariance map).}
Given a candidate set $K\subseteq S$, define the contracting controlled-invariance operator
\[
\mathcal{V}(K) \;:=\; \Bigl\{\, s\in K \;:\; \mathrm{Safe}(s)\ \wedge\ \exists a\in A_{\mathrm{feas}}(s)\ \text{s.t.}\ \mathrm{Post}(s,a)\subseteq K \Bigr\}.
\]
Intuitively: $s$ remains in $K$ if it is safe and there exists a feasible action whose entire successor support stays inside $K$. The explicit condition $s\in K$ makes $\mathcal{V}$ pointwise contracting ($\mathcal{V}(K)\subseteq K$), matching the standard ``greatest controlled-invariant subset'' construction and the assumptions of our Lean fixed-point anchor.

\paragraph{Definition (Viability kernel).}
The viability kernel $\mathcal{K}\subseteq S$ is the greatest fixed point of $\mathcal{V}$ \citep{aubin1991,tarski1955},

\mathcal{K} \;=\; \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{K}),

\paragraph{Definition (Action-sequence channel).}
Fix an initial state $s_0$ and a horizon $H\ge 1$. For an action sequence $\alpha=(a_0,\dots,a_{H-1})$, let $S_H$ be the random state after rolling out the kernel under $\alpha$, and define $Y=f(S_H)$. The induced channel from sequences to outputs is
\[
W[\alpha, y] \;:=\; \Pr(Y=y \mid s_0,\alpha).
\]
Equivalently, each row of $W$ is the output distribution obtained by propagating $\delta_{s_0}$ through the sequence and aggregating probability mass by $f$.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Definition (Feasible empowerment).}
To respect P$_2$/P$_6$, we restrict the sequence set by ledger feasibility. Given costs $c(a)$ and budget $r(s_0)$, a sequence $\alpha$ is feasible if $\sum_{t=0}^{H-1} c(a_t) \le r(s_0)$. Feasible empowerment is the capacity of the restricted channel:
\[
\Emp_{\mathrm{feas}}(s_0;H,f) \;:=\; \mathrm{Cap}\bigl(W\ \text{restricted to feasible }\alpha\bigr).
\]
\paragraph{Remark (what ``feasible'' means in this paper).}
In principle, feasibility can be state- and branch-dependent because the ledger is part of the state and may evolve over the horizon. In this paper we use a deliberately simple, explicit notion: we treat the channel input alphabet as \emph{open-loop} action sequences and restrict it by an \emph{initial-budget} gate, i.e.\ $\sum_{t=0}^{H-1} c(a_t)\le r(s_0)$. This yields an ``open-loop budgeted empowerment'' that is easy to audit and compare under matched controls. It can over- or under-approximate stricter stepwise feasibility in settings with replenishment or branch-dependent constraints; we therefore treat it as an operational proxy and include calibrated nulls (Section~\ref{sec:ex_nulls}) to guard against mis-typed control channels.

This yields an ``open-loop budgeted empowerment'' that is easy to audit and compare under matched controls. It can over- or under-approximate stricter stepwise feasibility in settings with replenishment or branch-dependent constraints; we therefore treat it as an operational proxy and include calibrated nulls (Section~\ref{sec:ex_nulls}) to guard against mis-typed control channels.

conclusion: Definition (Empirical packaging endomap). Fix a horizon tau 0 and a stationary policy mu(a s) (deterministic or stochastic). For each macro label x , initialize a reference micro-distribution d_0 that is uniform over S_x . Let T_mu be the induced one-step transition under mu : T_mu := _ a∈ A mu(a s) P[a,s,s']. Evolve d_tau := d_0 T_mu^tau , aggregate to a macro distribution over X via pi , and define E(x) as the mode macro label at time tau (ties broken deterministically by smallest label). The resulting map E: X→ X is an empirical packaging endomap: it says ``starting from macro label x (with hidden microstate randomized), what macro label do we typically return to after tau steps under the policy?''
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Definition (Empirical packaging endomap).}
Fix a horizon $\tau\ge 0$ and a stationary policy $\mu(a\mid s)$ (deterministic or stochastic). For each macro label $x$, initialize a reference micro-distribution $d_0$ that is uniform over $S_x$. Let $T_\mu$ be the induced one-step transition under $\mu$:
\[
T_\mu[s,s'] := \sum_{a\in A} \mu(a\mid s)\,P[a,s,s'].
\]
Evolve $d_\tau := d_0\,T_\mu^\tau$, aggregate to a macro distribution over $X$ via $\pi$, and define $E(x)$ as the mode macro label at time $\tau$ (ties broken deterministically by smallest label). The resulting map
\[
E: X\to X
\]
is an empirical \emph{packaging endomap}: it says ``starting from macro label $x$ (with hidden microstate randomized), what macro label do we typically return to after $\tau$ steps under the policy?''

If Def(E) 0 , the macro labels behave like stable objects under the lens pi and the policy mu ; if Def(E) is large, the lens fails to induce objecthood (labels do not compose stably).
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Definition (Idempotence defect).}
The idempotence defect of $E$ is
\[
\mathrm{Def}(E) \;:=\; \frac{|\{x\in X: E(E(x))\neq E(x)\}|}{|X|}.
\]
If $\mathrm{Def}(E)\approx 0$, the macro labels behave like stable objects under the lens $\pi$ and the policy $\mu$; if $\mathrm{Def}(E)$ is large, the lens fails to induce objecthood (labels do not compose stably).

conclusion: Definition (Agent as a theory object, operational). Fix a theory layer T (kernel + feasibility + ledger), lenses (f,pi) , horizons (H,tau) , and a maintenance policy mu for E . We call the induced package an agent theory object at this scale if (i) the viability kernel K is nonempty for the chosen safety predicate (maintained existence), (ii) the macro labels behave object-like under pi and mu at horizon tau (low idempotence defect), and (iii) the within-layer action channel to f at horizon H is nontrivial (positive feasible empowerment on K ). The exhibits report these as |K| , median empowerment on K , and Def(E) .

\subsection{Result: defect collapses at $\tau=2$}
Figure~\ref{fig:packaging_ring} plots $\mathrm{Def}(E)$ versus horizon $\tau$ for the two regimes. At $\tau=2$ we obtain:
\[
\mathrm{Def}(E)_{\text{repair OFF}} = 1.0,
\qquad
\mathrm{Def}(E)_{\text{repair ON}} = 0.0.
\]
That is: without maintenance, the macro labels $(y,r,\phi)$ behave maximally non-object-like under composition; with maintenance, the same coarse lens becomes perfectly idempotent at the staging-aligned horizon.

\subsection{Result: a collapse boundary in $(p_{\mathrm{flip}}, \mathrm{cost})$ space}
Figure~\ref{fig:sweep_heatmaps} shows the two heatmaps. The qualitative picture is straightforward:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em]
  \item Increasing noise $p_{\mathrm{flip}}$ makes it harder to keep $u=0$ in the robust-support sense: all nonzero-probability successors must remain safe.
  \item Increasing repair cost shrinks the feasible action set $A_{\mathrm{feas}}(s)$ (Section~\ref{sec:engine}), eventually making it impossible to guarantee repair when damage occurs.
\end{itemize}
Because we use successor-support (almost-sure under the modeled kernel) semantics, $\mathcal{K}$ can be nonempty under noise only when there exists at least one feasible action whose transition support avoids unsafe states (e.g., repair actions that restore $u=0$ with probability 1 in the model); if all actions admit any unsafe successor with nonzero probability, the robust kernel collapses by design.
The combined effect produces a region where $|\mathcal{K}|$ collapses to $0$ (no policy can keep the system safe-and-coherent for all support outcomes), and a complementary region where $|\mathcal{K}|$ remains substantial. Empowerment collapses along the same boundary because a nontrivial action channel requires an induced layer that persists: without viability, there is no stable domain on which actions are meaningful.

JSON artifacts are required to include (possibly with type-specific naming for multi-config comparisons): [leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em] Configuration identity: a config dictionary and its config_hash, where the hash is a stable JSON hash of the config. Metrics payload: a metrics dictionary (or a type-specific payload for traces/sweeps) containing the quantitative outputs used in the paper. All experiment outputs live under \texttt{results/} and are machine-checkable. JSON artifacts are required to include (possibly with type-specific naming for multi-config comparisons):
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em]
  \item \textbf{Configuration identity:} a \texttt{config} dictionary and its \texttt{config\_hash}, where the hash is a stable JSON hash of the config.
  \item \textbf{Metrics payload:} a \texttt{metrics} dictionary (or a type-specific payload for traces/sweeps) containing the quantitative outputs used in the paper.
  \item \textbf{Provenance:} a timestamp field (e.g., \texttt{created\_at\_utc}) and a \texttt{versions} dictionary (Python, NumPy, Matplotlib as applicable).
\end{itemize}
Filenames also encode hashes when appropriate, so that a plot or table can be traced to a configuration without opening the file.

For paper-facing stability, we export stable-named assets (figures and generated tables) into \texttt{paper/figures/} and \texttt{paper/generated/}. The file \texttt{paper/generated/numbers.json} collects the key scalars cited in the exhibits (e.g., idempotence defect at $\tau=2$, empowerment arrays, and learning medians) together with the hashes of the runs they were extracted from.

conclusion: Outlook Three directions follow naturally.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\subsection{Outlook}
Three directions follow naturally. First, extend the substrate to multi-agent settings where P$_2$ constraints and P$_4$ tokens can encode commitments, ownership, and norms. Second, move from exact kernels to approximate learned models while preserving the audit posture (hashing, manifests, and invariants). Third, explore alternative causal proxies (risk-sensitive empowerment, reachability volumes, intervention-based causal effect sizes) and characterize when they agree or disagree.

conclusion: Next-token prediction is not, by itself, a theory of compositional content: finite predictive statistics can agree while the induced quotients compose differently under larger contexts. We study an alternative, non-gradient formulation in which a language model is an audited ledger of finite theory extensions rather than a parameter vector. Six Birds Theory (SBT) supplies the admissibility calculus: typed closure-package layers, explicit quotient maps, audit records, nonclaim records, and promotion gates based on descent, stability, control, no-smuggling, legibility, and strict factorization failure. We introduce Language Theory Models (LTMs), a prototype architecture for structural recovery on fixed sequence corpora. An LTM accumulates typed transition evidence, monitors each active layer with a conditional-information closure-deficit statistic and an idempotence/self-consistency defect, and proposes new layers only when the current quotient leaves recoverable structure unresolved. Candidate layers are committed only after an explicit gate panel emits a strict-extension certificate; otherwise the runtime records a typed defect or remains silent rather than laundering fallback evidence into a stronger claim. We report a code-backed feasibility study on Shakespeare: the runtime builds closure-package layers, records promotion attempts and failures, emits halt verdicts, caps unaudited fallback readout, and demonstrates strict R-layer growth in bounded runs. Independent of the LTM runtime, we provide a structural probe suite that tests SBT framework-level commitments under blue-team and red-team cases, including growth, forgetting, uncertainty, auditability, and concept-separation scenarios. The contribution is a concrete audited substrate for testing whether compositional structure in a fixed corpus can be recovered as a finite ladder of certified theory refinements.

conclusion: Six Birds Theory (SBT) supplies the admissibility calculus for that ledger: typed audited layers of the language model (called closure-package layers when formalized in ), explicit quotient maps, audit and nonclaim records, and promotion gates for deciding when a proposed layer is a strict extension rather than an unaudited readout .
expanded_source_wording_tex: We study an alternative formulation: a non-gradient setting in which the language model is an audited ledger of finite theory extensions rather than a parameter vector. Six Birds Theory (SBT) supplies the admissibility calculus for that ledger: typed audited layers of the language model (called closure-package layers when formalized in \Cref{sec:problem-setup}), explicit quotient maps, audit and nonclaim records, and promotion gates for deciding when a proposed layer is a strict extension rather than an unaudited readout \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}. These objects are not presented as a replacement for large-scale parametric training, but as a controlled substrate for asking when a fixed corpus supports a structural refinement claim. We instantiate the substrate as Language Theory Models (LTMs), a prototype architecture whose runtime accumulates transition evidence, proposes audited layers, and records failed or non-certifying attempts rather than converting fallback evidence into stronger claims. \Cref{sec:methods} describes the gate panel and runtime mechanics; here the point is the modelling shift from learned weights alone to an explicit audit trail of finite extensions.

expanded_source_wording_tex: Six Birds Theory (SBT) enters this paper as an admissibility calculus for structural claims, not as a replacement training objective. Its primitive objects are typed audited layers, explicit quotient maps, audit and nonclaim records, and promotion gates that determine whether a proposed extension can be claimed \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI,Tsiokos2026FoundationsII,Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}. In ML terms, the calculus specifies what counts as evidence, what must be logged, what must remain a nonclaim, and when a gate panel may certify that a candidate layer strictly refines the current quotient; this is distinct from learning, since it constrains when a recovered structure is admissible rather than choosing what the next model should optimize. The load-bearing sources are used narrowly: Foundations I supplies the typed layer atom and its idempotence condition \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}, Foundations II the admissibility meta-theory \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII}, Foundations III the dependency-relation calculus and gate scaffolding \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}, with Promotion Criteria for gate templates \cite{Tsiokos2026PromotionCriteria}, the strict-extension paper for the relabeling-rejection hypothesis cluster \cite{Tsiokos2026CantorShell}, the accepted-new-layer tests for readout-sufficiency contracts \cite{Tsiokos2026AcceptedNewLayer}, To Notch a Stone for the causation/enablement-time distinction \cite{Tsiokos2026NotchAStone}, Recombination Witnesses for the recombination-aware quotient \cite{Tsiokos2026RecombinationWitnesses}, and the no-go results for the conditional-information obstruction \cite{Tsiokos2026NoGo}.
