expanded_source_wording_tex:
Relative to next-token and autoregressive language modeling \cite{Bengio2003NPLM,Vaswani2017Attention}, the LTM is not a replacement objective: it adds a non-gradient ledger that audits where a fixed corpus does or does not support compositional refinement claims. Relative to compositional generalization benchmarks such as SCAN, COGS, and CFQ, which usually evaluate trained models post hoc \cite{Hupkes2020Compositionality}, the LTM instruments the recovery process itself and records non-certifying attempts before a finished artifact is declared; relative to mechanistic interpretability and circuits work \cite{Olah2020ZoomIn,Elhage2021Framework,Olsson2022InductionHeads,Conmy2023ACDC}, it shares the auditability motivation but tracks typed recovery layers and gate-panel decisions rather than activation patches or circuit attributions; and relative to symbolic, neurosymbolic, and program-induction approaches \cite{Ellis2023DreamCoder,GarcezLamb2020Neurosymbolic}, it is adjacent in seeking typed structural objects but treats them as recoveries from a fixed corpus with explicit nonclaim records rather than as programs from a search engine.

expanded_source_wording_tex: The LTM setting in this paper is fixed-corpus inverse recovery: the input is a finite sequence corpus, and the task is to recover audited refinements already supported by that corpus rather than to explain how the corpus was produced. The locked empirical instantiation uses a Shakespeare corpus derived from a Gutenberg source, tokenized by a word-punctuation regular-expression tokenizer with a frozen vocabulary; \Cref{sec:primary-results} reports the resulting run. At startup, the runtime declares its scope in a regime record naming the corpus, tokenization surface, lens family, candidate-search family, budget profile, and audit instrument stack. This declaration is the operational boundary for every later evidence record: candidate layers, quotient tests, and gate outcomes are interpreted only relative to the declared corpus and tokenizer. In SBT terms this is an inverse-emergence regime, but the ML claim is narrower: fixed-corpus structural recovery under explicit nonclaim discipline, with runtime mechanics described in \Cref{sec:methods} \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII}. The runtime, locked-run artifact set, and probe suite are available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/how-to-chat-a-stone-nips} (anonymous code repository for double-blind review).

expanded_source_wording_tex: The runtime begins with a non-native bootstrap layer, $\Tlayer{0}$, rather than with a layer certified by the same gate panel as later growth. Its seed quotient is derived from the declared corpus surface, such as raw token-level statistics, and gives the system an initial partition from which audited refinements can be proposed. Native growth begins at $\Tlayer{1}$: from that point onward, every committed layer passes through the same admissibility machinery. The bootstrap layer carries an explicit nonclaim that its strict-extension status was not audited, so downstream reports can separate the scoped starting surface from committed native layers; \Cref{sec:primary-results} reports the locked-run instantiation, and \Cref{app:artifact-map} maps the literal bootstrap-policy field.

conclusion: Candidate layers enter the LTM ledger through a six-gate promotion panel, not through an unconstrained score threshold. The conjunctive panel is in the spirit of verifier-based and process-supervised pipelines that license outputs only after explicit per-step checks pass . The gates are descent, stability, control, no-smuggling, legibility, and strict factorization failure: respectively, residual reduction, quotient robustness, falsification evidence, audit-scope compliance, audit-log reconstructability, and a parent-identified/candidate-distinguished witness pair . The panel is conjunctive: all six gates must pass before the runtime commits the candidate and emits a strict-extension certificate; otherwise the runtime records a typed defect or remains silent, with evaluator details in , notation in , and empirical outcomes in .

\paragraph{Dependency relations and active relation kinds.}\label{subsec:dep-relations}
The audit ledger also records a typed dependency relation for each committed child layer. We use the dependency-relation vocabulary from the SBT admissibility calculus, whose full form declares eight relation kinds \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}. In this paper, only upward layer-birth dependence is active: the parent's audit surface enables the child's strict extension. This restricted relation is sufficient for the static-parent setting because every committed native layer is justified as a child extension of the previous audited surface, not as a claim about parent revision or bidirectional flow. Other relation kinds are deferred to future work and appear as paper-level limitations in \Cref{sec:discussion}; \Cref{app:formalization} lists the full vocabulary.

conclusion: The readout path is capped by the same nonclaim discipline as layer promotion . When the audited path does not produce a committed answer, for example because no current layer's quotient covers the requested microstate at sufficient confidence, the runtime does not promote fallback statistics into a stronger claim. Instead, it either emits a provisional or silent claim with a typed defect record, or refuses to emit a token claim. The structural posture is the abstention / reject-option discipline familiar from selective classification , paired with the reliability concern that motivates calibration in modern neural networks . At pass end, a halt-verdict classifier reports the final status as accepted, provisional, blocked, outside-scope, failed-audit, absent-with-record, or below-threshold . Each verdict is paired with required nonclaim references that state what is and is not in scope; reports the locked-run outcome, analyzes the verdict semantics, and gives the verdict-class table.

conclusion: A typed audited layer is a pair Tlayer i =(Xspace i , i ), where Xspace i is a finite microstate space and i :Xspace i →Xspace i is an idempotent self-map, i i = i . The induced equivalence relation on Xspace i identifies two microstates when they lie in the same pre-image of a fixed point in the image of i . Equivalently, the quotient partition is the partition of Xspace i into fibers of the map onto its fixed-point image .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
A typed audited layer is a pair
\[
\Tlayer{i}=(\Xspace{i},\opmap{i}),
\]
where \(\Xspace{i}\) is a finite microstate space and \(\opmap{i}:\Xspace{i}\to\Xspace{i}\) is an idempotent self-map,
\[
\opmap{i}\circ\opmap{i}=\opmap{i}.
\]
The induced equivalence relation on \(\Xspace{i}\) identifies two microstates when they lie in the same pre-image of a fixed point in the image of \(\opmap{i}\). Equivalently, the quotient partition is the partition of \(\Xspace{i}\) into fibers of the map onto its fixed-point image \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}.

conclusion: Given a layer Tlayer i and a declared lookahead tau , the closure-deficit statistic CD_ tau is the conditional-information residual measuring how much next- tau -token structure on Xspace i remains unresolved by the quotient map i . Schematically, for an observed current microstate X_0 and a future window X_ >0, tau , CD_ tau H (X_ >0, tau i (X_0) ) - H (X_ >0, tau X_0 ). Given a layer \(\Tlayer{i}\) and a declared lookahead \(\tau\), the closure-deficit statistic \(\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}\) is the conditional-information residual measuring how much next-\(\tau\)-token structure on \(\Xspace{i}\) remains unresolved by the quotient map \(\opmap{i}\). Schematically, for an observed current microstate \(X_0\) and a future window \(X_{>0,\le \tau}\),
\[
\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}
\;\approx\;
H\!\left(X_{>0,\le \tau}\mid \opmap{i}(X_0)\right)
-
H\!\left(X_{>0,\le \tau}\mid X_0\right).
\]
Thus \(\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}\) is the conditional-entropy gap between prediction from the layer quotient and prediction from the raw microstate, restricted to the declared lookahead window. The runtime estimates this quantity from finite samples and reports estimator-quality flags alongside the value \cite{Tsiokos2026NoGo}.

Given a layer \(\Tlayer{i}\), lookahead \(\tau\), and readout \(f\), the idempotence/self-consistency defect \(\delta_{\tau,f}\) is the empirical fixed-point gap measuring deviation from \(\opmap{i}\circ\opmap{i}=\opmap{i}\) on observed data through \(f\). A typical estimator is a total-variation or analogous distributional distance between the empirical readout distribution after one application of \(\opmap{i}\) and after two applications:
\[
\delta_{\tau,f}
\;\approx\;
d\!\left(f(\opmap{i}(X_0)),\, f(\opmap{i}(\opmap{i}(X_0)))\right),
\]
with the future window and readout determining which empirical events are compared. As with \(\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}\), the runtime reports finite-sample support and propagates estimator-quality flags rather than treating small empirical deviations as exact equalities \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}.

Let \(q_i(s)=\opmap{i}(s)\) denote the parent quotient representative for a parent layer \(\Tlayer{i}\), and let \(q_{i+1}\) denote the candidate quotient evaluated on the same observed support through the declared candidate lift into \(\Xspace{i+1}\). A candidate layer \(\Tlayer{i+1}\) is a strict extension of \(\Tlayer{i}\) when there exist observed microstates \(s,s'\in \Xspace{i}\) such that
\[
q_i(s)=q_i(s')
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
q_{i+1}(s)\ne q_{i+1}(s').
\]
Equivalently, the candidate quotient does not factor through the parent quotient: it separates at least one pair that the parent identifies. The strict-extension certificate \(\mathsf{StrictExtCert}\) records such a witness pair together with the audit evidence that licenses committing the candidate as a new layer \cite{Tsiokos2026CantorShell}.

conclusion: Repeated interaction routinely produces structure absent from the one-shot game: reputations, norms, conventions, and other institutions. The problem is to say what this structure is, when the bare game predicts play, and where the extra structure comes from. This paper argues that the institutional content of repeated play is a strict extension of the stage game: a refinement with genuinely new predictive distinctions not definable as a function of the game's own vocabulary. The argument uses a finite, fully explicit repeated-game laboratory, with mathematical claims verified by exact finite recomputation and reproducible validators, and a pre-registered re-analysis of a published human repeated Prisoner's Dilemma dataset. The institutional state studied here has a canonical form: the coarsest predictive summary of history, equivalent to a predictive-sufficiency or causal-state construction. On the finite carrier this object is non-definable from the game itself, and the predictive failure of stage-vocabulary models is priced exactly by a conditional mutual information. The quantitative constants governing institutional collapse are reproducible within declared protocols but resist shortcut: across a declared formula class and three frozen out-of-sample transfer attempts, no tested low-complexity shortcut transfers across families. In the human data, the corresponding predictive-residue hypothesis is confirmed out of sample under a protocol registered before any data access, while a more specific pre-registered timing hypothesis fails in the reverse direction: history-dependence grows with experience. Claims are scoped to the declared finite carrier, declared run families and protocols, and analyzed dataset; broader framework theorems are imported and cited, not re-proved here.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
This calls for an explicit anti-relabeling stance.  This paper does not claim
the folk theorems, global games, reputation models, stochastic stability,
correlated equilibrium, Bayesian types, Markov states, or causal-state
quotients as its own results.  Those literatures are reference points: each
shows a way in which additional structure can matter.  The contribution here is the
certified inter-layer account that connects them without collapsing them into
one another: a canonical predictive institution, exact information-theoretic
price, finite non-definability certificates, material-feedback tests, and a
registered run/data program.  The strict-extension, predictive-quotient, and
closure-deficit theorem layers are imported from the cited source papers and
instantiated here on the declared carrier
\citep{Tsiokos2026CantorShell,
Tsiokos2026CastStone,Tsiokos2026NoGo}.  The precise novelty conjunction is
deferred to \Cref{sec:final-gate}, after the carrier, run-layer, and data results are
on the table.

certificate and not a claim about the world.  The broader theorems used by the
paper---predictive quotients and factorization, closure deficit, strict
extension obligations, and promotion-gate logic---are imported from their
source papers and cited for their own status; they are not re-proved here
\citep{Tsiokos2026CastStone,
Tsiokos2026CantorShell,Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}.  Two carrier grades recur.
A theorem-grade-on-the-carrier claim is an exact, enumeration-complete
statement with a proof, a complete finite check, or both, on the declared
carrier.  A finite-carrier diagnostic is an exact computation that characterizes
the carrier but is not promoted to a theorem-grade claim.  In both cases the
scope is the declared carrier and its declared lenses, priors, horizons, and
extensions; the artifact and reproducibility map is deferred to
\Cref{app:methods}.  Unless a different grade is stated, the propositions in
\Cref{sec:primary-results,sec:secondary-results} are theorem-grade-on-the-carrier;
the remaining grades used below (finite-run measured, registration-grade,
recovery-grade, and interpretation-grade) are defined where they first occur and
summarized in \Cref{app:formalization}.

conclusion: Let K^ be the closed base law, the best autonomous stage-vocabulary kernel P(Y^+_ t,tau Y_t^Pi) , and let the canonical institution M refine the stage package. On the declared carrier, CD Pi tau =Gap Pi tau +ResidualEnt Pi tau , where Gap Pi tau = E is the expected Kullback–Leibler gain obtained by conditioning on the institution, and ResidualEnt Pi tau =H(Y^+_ t,tau M) is the residual future uncertainty left after conditioning on the institution.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:gap-residual-decomposition}
Let \(\ensuremath{K^\star}\) be the closed base law, the best autonomous
stage-vocabulary kernel \(P(Y^+_{t,\tau}\mid Y_t^\Pi)\), and let the canonical
institution \(\ensuremath{M}\) refine the stage package.  On the declared carrier,
\[
\CD{\Pi}{\tau}=\Gap{\Pi}{\tau}+\ResidualEnt{\Pi}{\tau},
\]
where
\[
\Gap{\Pi}{\tau}
 =
\mathbb E\!\left[
\ensuremath{D_{\mathrm{KL}}}\!\left(
P(Y^+_{t,\tau}\mid \ensuremath{M})
\middle\| \ensuremath{K^\star}(\cdot\mid Y_t^\Pi)
\right)\right]
\]
is the expected Kullback--Leibler gain obtained by conditioning on the
institution, and
\[
\ResidualEnt{\Pi}{\tau}=H(Y^+_{t,\tau}\mid \ensuremath{M})
\]
is the residual future uncertainty left after conditioning on the institution.

conclusion: It does not assert universal forcing.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
An example of the successful label is a recent-deviation bit: it can be on
because a defection occurred in the last two completed profiles, and then turn
off after two clean rounds.  This is public and history-computable, but it is
not merely the current stage profile or the empirical count summary.  Because
the trigger can be live at the comparison round, two histories that look
the same through the base game can lead extended strategies to different
future laws.  The landed exhibit holds relative to
the declared extension.  Its institutional reading is narrow:
publishing institutional state can change behavior broadly, but it enriches
the institution itself only under specific conditions--live,
non-stage-definable, reactive feedback--and, on this carrier, only where the
structure is still forming.  It does not assert universal forcing.

conclusion: A certificate, in the sense used here, is a finite package of obligations and evidence. It is meant to prevent a higher-level object from being accepted merely because it has been renamed. The imported strict-extension framework specifies the obligations for certifying that a higher vocabulary is a genuine strict extension of a lower one . For the repeated-game setting, the relevant obligations are: a closed base law for the lower layer, meaning the best autonomous predictor available in the stage vocabulary; saturation of the higher vocabulary, meaning a predictive refinement fixed point; non-factorization, witnessed by split pairs whose distinctions are not definable from below; an exact quantitative price for omitting the higher layer, given by positive closure deficit and the gap–residual decomposition; material forcing, when a declared extension lets the higher layer feed back into play; and admissibility of the promoted object, checked by the gate battery described in . evidence.  It is meant to prevent a higher-level object from being accepted
merely because it has been renamed.  The imported strict-extension framework
specifies the obligations for certifying that a higher vocabulary is a genuine
strict extension of a lower one \citep{Tsiokos2026CantorShell,Tsiokos2026FoundationsI,Tsiokos2026FoundationsII,Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII,Tsiokos2026OneMetaTheory}.
For the repeated-game setting, the relevant obligations are: a closed base law
for the lower layer, meaning the best autonomous predictor available in the
stage vocabulary; saturation of the higher vocabulary, meaning a predictive
refinement fixed point; non-factorization, witnessed by split pairs whose
distinctions are not definable from below; an exact quantitative price for
omitting the higher layer, given by positive closure deficit and the
gap--residual decomposition; material forcing, when a declared extension lets
the higher layer feed back into play; and admissibility of the promoted object,
checked by the gate battery described in \Cref{subsec:promotion-certificate}.

\begin{proposition}[Strict-extension certificate on the declared carrier]
\label{prop:strict-extension-certificate}
On the declared finite carrier, the canonical institutional state
\(\ensuremath{M}=\ensuremath{P_\star}\) is a certified strict extension of the stage game.  The
closed base law and exact price are supplied by
\Cref{prop:stage-lens-obstruction,prop:deterministic-substrate-identity,prop:gap-residual-decomposition};
non-factorization is supplied by \Cref{prop:carrier-nondefinability};
saturation is supplied by \Cref{prop:saturation-fixed-point}; material forcing
is supplied, relative to its declared label-feedback extension, by
\Cref{prop:material-forcing}; and admissibility is supplied by the promotion
certificate \Cref{prop:promotion-certificate}.
\end{proposition}

conclusion: The anti-relabeling ledger is part of the result. This paper does not claim the predictive-state or causal-state quotient construction as new; that is a standard way to summarize a process by its predictive consequences . It does not claim the closure-deficit identity, or the optimality of the best autonomous macro-predictor, as new; those are imported from the closure-deficit and no-go accounts . It does not claim the strict-extension, saturation, or promotion-obligation framework as new; those are imported standards for recognizing when a higher vocabulary is a genuine layer rather than a relabeling . Nor does it claim as new the game-theoretic fact that added structure matters. Folk theorems show that repeated interaction can support many outcomes; global games show how noisy private information can select; reputation models show how type structure changes play; evolutionary and stochastic-stability models show that convention selection can be a property of a run; correlated equilibrium and type spaces show how signals and hidden state enlarge the game . These are reference points the paper uses, not results it rebrands. The contribution is the conjunction, on one explicit repeated-game object, under one evidentiary discipline. First, the paper installs the predictive state as the canonical institution of repeated play and verifies, on the finite carrier, that it is not definable from the game's own stage vocabulary: the institutional partition strictly refines the stage partition and does not factor through it. Second, the paper prices the omission exactly by closure deficit, with a gap–residual decomposition that separates what conditioning on the institution recovers from what remains unpredictable even after that conditioning. Third, it assembles these facts into a certified strict-extension object: the institutional vocabulary saturates, admits an active label-feedback exhibit under a declared extension, and passes the admissibility gates for a promoted layer on the carrier. Fourth, the picture is subjected to tests that could have failed silently but were reported in full: the run-layer constants are reproducible within protocol yet fail three frozen out-of-sample transfer attempts, and the human-data analysis confirms the predictive-residue hypothesis while reversing the proposed timing bridge. The registered negatives are not qualifications to the result; they are part of the evidence for the strict-extension reading.

The anti-relabeling ledger is part of the result.  This paper does not claim
the predictive-state or causal-state quotient construction as new; that is a
standard way to summarize a process by its predictive consequences
\citep{ShaliziCrutchfield2001ComputationalMechanics,
LittmanSuttonSingh2001PredictiveRepresentations}.  It does not claim the
closure-deficit identity, or the optimality of the best autonomous
macro-predictor, as new; those are imported from the closure-deficit and no-go
accounts \citep{Tsiokos2026CastStone,Tsiokos2026NoGo}.  It does not claim the
strict-extension, saturation, or promotion-obligation framework as new; those
are imported standards for recognizing when a higher vocabulary is a genuine
layer rather than a relabeling
\citep{Tsiokos2026CantorShell,Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}.  Nor does it claim
as new the game-theoretic fact that added structure matters.  Folk theorems
show that repeated interaction can support many outcomes; global games show
how noisy private information can select; reputation models show how type
structure changes play; evolutionary and stochastic-stability models show
that convention selection can be a property of a run; correlated equilibrium
and type spaces show how signals and hidden state enlarge the game
\citep{FudenbergMaskin1986FolkTheorem,CarlssonVanDamme1993GlobalGames,
KrepsMilgromRobertsWilson1982RationalCooperation,
KandoriMailathRob1993LearningMutation,Young1993EvolutionConventions,
Aumann1974SubjectivityCorrelation}.  These are reference points the paper uses, not
results it rebrands.

conclusion: Discussion, scope, and outlook
expanded_source_wording_tex:
This conjunction also answers the three questions posed at the start, within
the declared scope.  What is an institution?  In this paper it is the canonical
predictive state of repeated play: the coarsest history summary sufficient for
the declared future.  When does the bare game predict behavior?  Exactly when
the stage vocabulary is closed, equivalently when its closure deficit is zero;
when the deficit is positive, the missing predictive information has an exact
price.  Where does the structure come from?  On the finite carrier, it appears
where the stage layer discards predictive information, can be made active only
under live non-stage-definable feedback, and produces run constants that are
reachable by running the process rather than by the tested low-complexity
shortcuts.  In the analyzed data, the corresponding residue is present, while
its timing points away from the fixed-population formation picture and toward
acquisition with experience.  These statements are scoped to the declared
carrier, declared run families and protocols, and the analyzed dataset; the
broader framework theorems are imported and cited, not re-proved here.
 \section{Discussion, scope, and outlook}\label{sec:discussion}

conclusion: The exact results in this paper live on a specific finite carrier: a memory-one reactive-rule catalog, two main payoff families, a uniform prior, and declared lenses, rounds, horizons, and extensions. Their highest grade is theorem-grade-on-the-carrier, not a general repeated-game theorem. The run constants are scoped to the declared payoff families, evolutionary dynamics, population sizes, noise grids, estimators, and protocols. The no-shortcut conclusion is correspondingly scoped to the tested formula classes and the three frozen transfer tests; it is not a proof that no transferable shortcut exists. The human-data analysis is one published dataset analyzed under one frozen protocol, with mapping amendments recorded before analysis; it does not confirm or refute any carrier theorem. The broader framework results used here, including predictive quotients, closure deficit, strict-extension obligations, and promotion gates, are imported and cited , not re-proved. Finally, the material-forcing result is relative to its declared label-feedback extension; it is not a claim that institutional labels generally enrich play.

conclusion: Outlook.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Outlook.}
The most direct next construction is a within-agent learning or acquisition
carrier, in which the individual agent is treated as a carrier object in the
sense of the Six Birds treatment of agency \citep{Tsiokos2026ThrowStone}.  The
failed crystallization bridge in
\Cref{subsec:crystallization-bridge} shows that experience-as-composition
selection makes the finite carrier more homogeneous and more stage-predictable,
whereas the data show history-dependence growing with experience.  A carrier
in which individual agents acquire conditional rules over their own histories
would test the mechanism that this contrast leaves open.  A second direction
is a broader family of noisy and dissipative carriers, to map route memory
beyond the tested noise grid and to learn when currentizable traces become
genuinely coherent.  A third is to enlarge the strategic and payoff substrate:
richer automata, larger action spaces, asymmetric games, and longer public
signals would test which carrier facts persist and which are artifacts of the
minimal catalog.

conclusion: The most direct next construction is a within-agent learning or acquisition carrier, in which the individual agent is treated as a carrier object in the sense of the Six Birds treatment of agency . The failed crystallization bridge in shows that experience-as-composition selection makes the finite carrier more homogeneous and more stage-predictable, whereas the data show history-dependence growing with experience. A carrier in which individual agents acquire conditional rules over their own histories would test the mechanism that this contrast leaves open. A second direction is a broader family of noisy and dissipative carriers, to map route memory beyond the tested noise grid and to learn when currentizable traces become genuinely coherent. A third is to enlarge the strategic and payoff substrate: richer automata, larger action spaces, asymmetric games, and longer public signals would test which carrier facts persist and which are artifacts of the minimal catalog. The run layer also invites a bounded-rationality connection. The imitation dynamics used here contain a logit-style temperature parameter; in a maximum-entropy or shadow-price reading, such a parameter can be interpreted as the dual of a binding cognitive or informational budget rather than a free behavioral knob . That connection is only an opening in this paper, but it suggests how run-only constants might be tied to explicit resource constraints. On the empirical side, the immediate extension is broader pre-registered testing of the residue hypothesis and the timing reversal on other repeated-game datasets, with the same discipline: hypotheses, predictors, bands, folds, and amendments fixed before outcome analysis.

\begin{description}
\item[Stage games.]
A stage game \(g\) is a declared two-player \(2\times2\) game with action sets
\(\Act_i=\{C,D\}\), joint-profile set
\(\ensuremath{\Omega}=\Act_1\times\Act_2=\{CC,CD,DC,DD\}\), and exact rational payoff
map \(u_g:\ensuremath{\Omega}\to\mathbb Q^2\).

\item[Memory-one rules.]
A deterministic memory-one reactive rule is
\[
  r=(\alpha,r_{CC},r_{CD},r_{DC},r_{DD})\in\{C,D\}^5,
\]
where \(\alpha\) is the initial action and \(r_\omega\) is the action after
the previous joint profile \(\omega\in\ensuremath{\Omega}\).  The catalog \(\ensuremath{\mathcal R_{32}}\)
contains all \(2^5=32\) such rules; named rules such as always-cooperate,
always-defect, tit-for-tat, grim, and win-stay-lose-shift are catalog entries.

conclusion: [label= .,leftmargin=*] The exact carrier results are scoped to the declared finite carrier: the memory-one reactive catalog, the two payoff families, the uniform prior, and the declared lenses, rounds, horizons, and extensions. They are not general theorems about all repeated games. The no-shortcut conclusion concerns the tested low-complexity formula classes and the three frozen transfer tests. It is not a proof that no transferable shortcut exists. The run constants are scoped to the declared payoff families, stochastic dynamics, population sizes, noise grids, estimators, and execution protocols. Changing any of these can change the measured constant. The human-data analysis concerns one published dataset under one frozen protocol. It neither validates nor invalidates any carrier theorem, and the memory-one strategy-space alignment is a shared language rather than a bridge theorem. The material-forcing result holds relative to its declared label-feedback extension. It is not a claim that public institutional labels generally enrich play. The paper makes no welfare, mechanism-design, real-world-institution, or universal-equilibrium-selection claim. The bridge from the canonical predictive state to substantive institutions remains interpretive. Mixed-strategy and belief objects are not given a literal psychological reading. The institution in this manuscript is a predictive-state object, not a claim about agents' internal representations. The crystallization mechanism suggested by the human timing reversal is open. A within-agent learning or acquisition layer is named as the next construction, not resolved here. The paper's own finite-carrier results are verified by exact finite recomputation rather than by a proof assistant. Imported framework theorems carry their own status in the cited source papers.

conclusion: Six Birds Theory has produced three landed Clay-class conditional closures: Navier–Stokes regularity, the Riemann Hypothesis, and P vs NP, each under the SB closure assumption of Foundations I. This paper does not re-prove those substrate results. It extracts their common meta-theoretic form for a reader who treats Six Birds as a typed framework for organizing attempted closures of open conjectures. The account has two complementary halves. The negative half, Foreclosure, studies a typed primary carrier, meaning an attempted proof construction whose type signature targets a designated conjecture, and proves that admissible carriers fall into a finite state space: non-target-equivalent, target-equivalent tautological, bridge-failed, or matrix-element-terminal. The positive half, Recognition-Mode Landing, gives a seven-stage route for trace-state-only substrates: instead of deriving the load-bearing source from framework primitives, it imports that source as named recognition under closure formation. The v5 refinement states the joint thesis: derivation routes remain subject to foreclosure, while recognition-mode landings are structurally distinct peer routes under the same closure assumption. A third part, the Calibration Family, provides the typed bookkeeping that makes this comparison uniform across substrates: calibrations, bridges-as-theorems, directed bridge types, coverage geometry, framework-type mismatch, and named functorial gates. Layer-instantiation examples appear throughout: the three substrate validation rows (NS, RH, and PvNP), a thirteen-entry calibration seed catalog of typed detectors, two named coverage holes, and three named functorial gates from the PvNP track. The formal catalog contains seventeen rows: three partial structural derivations, eight primary theorem-grade rows, and six primary obligation rows. The body gives the mathematical proofs or obligation analyses, while Lean serves as the mechanization companion and audit trail. The nine honest obligation axioms are recorded with opacity guards, so their assumptions are explicit rather than silently instantiated; the full validator chain cross-checks the inventory, manifest, and trust base. The scope is deliberately limited: BSD and Hodge are out of scope except as future work or prediction, and no substrate closure is strengthened here to a standard-ZFC unconditional claim.

conclusion: It is modest because it does not claim new unconditional results about the Clay problems.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The present paper is not a survey of the analytic, arithmetic, or
complexity-theoretic details of the three substrate papers.  It
extracts from them the common structural question: when the framework
has produced a formed setting, which parts of the work are genuinely
internal, which parts are named external mathematics, and how does the
audit prevent the two from being conflated?  The resulting answer is
modest in one respect and ambitious in another.  It is modest because
it does not claim new unconditional results about the Clay problems.
It is ambitious because it claims that the framework's closure
behavior has a reusable meta-theoretic form.

conclusion: The paper does not claim that the space of mathematical ideas is finite.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
This also explains the precise sense in which the paper speaks of
foreclosure.  The paper does not claim that the space of mathematical
ideas is finite.  It claims that, after the framework fixes the type
of the target and the admissible role of a carrier, the audit sees a
finite set of state-types through which a derivation-mode attempt can
pass.
The word ``foreclosure'' is therefore not a statement about human
ingenuity.  It is a statement about typed bookkeeping: certain moves
cannot be counted as free progress because they reintroduce the target
content, miss the target, or terminate at content not supplied by the
carrier.  This is the level at which a meta-theorem can speak across
Navier--Stokes, RH, and P versus NP without pretending that the three
problems have the same mathematics.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
A closure formation is the background act of organizing an open
problem, its admissible source material, and the claimed closure event
inside one formal setting.  In this paper the framework-native name is
\textsc{Foundations~I}\ closure formation, and we use it only as a black-box import from
\textsc{Foundations~I}\ \cite{Tsiokos2026EmergenceCalculus}.  A formed Six Birds
closure is therefore a formal closure of an open problem in which the
closure event is itself treated as a structural fact about the
problem's mathematical setting, rather than as an informal label
attached after the fact to a proof.  The SB closure assumption is the
\textsc{Foundations~I}\ closure-formation working axiom under which all substrate
landings cited in this paper are stated.  It is not a
standard-ZFC-unconditional claim, and it is not re-proved here.

\label{def:four-typed-states}
For a typed primary carrier \(C\) aimed at \(X\), the four Part I
states are the following.  The non-$X$-equivalent\ state says that the
residual closure of \(C\) is logically equivalent to some conjectural
content \(X'\) distinct from \(X\).  The three carrier-residual
equivalent states are \textsc{CRE-TE}, the target-equivalent fallback;
\textsc{CRE-BF}, the bridge-failed dead end; and \textsc{CRE-CTMT}, the
cascade-terminal matrix-element case.  The last three are the
three typed foreclosure modes available once the residual closure is
$X$-equivalent.
Equivalently, writing \(\mathcal B\) for the accepted-imports base,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      \exists X'.\, (R_C=0\leftrightarrow X')\wedge X'\neq X,\\
  \operatorname{OpenPending}_{\mathcal B}(X')
    &\Longleftrightarrow \neg \mathcal B(X'),\\
  \operatorname{NativeOutcome}_{\mathcal B}(C,X')
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      (\mathcal B(X')\wedge R_C=0)\vee
      \operatorname{OpenPending}_{\mathcal B}(X'),\\
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      (R_C=0\leftrightarrow X)\wedge
      \operatorname{SelfAuditFail}(C),\\
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      \operatorname{NoBridge}(C,X)\vee
      \operatorname{BridgeMismatch}(C,X),\\
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow
      \operatorname{MRed}(C)\wedge
      \neg\operatorname{IRDec}(C)\wedge
      \neg\operatorname{MDEqTarget}(C,X).
\end{aligned}
\]

\label{thm:carrier-dichotomy}
Let \(\mathcal B:\mathrm{Prop}\to\mathrm{Prop}\) be an
accepted-imports base, and assume import soundness
\[
  \forall Y.\ \mathcal B(Y)\Longrightarrow Y .
\]
Let \(X\) be an open target conjecture and let \(C\) be a typed primary
carrier satisfying
\[
  C\leadsto X,\qquad C\models\text{typed-context discipline},\qquad
  \operatorname{CoverageCtx}(X,C).
\]
Then the carrier audit has the following two-branch form:
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C)
  &\Longrightarrow
    \exists X'.\,
      (R_C=0\leftrightarrow X')\wedge X'\neq X\wedge
      \operatorname{NativeOutcome}_{\mathcal B}(C,X'),\\
  \mbox{$X$-equivalent}_X(C)
  &\Longrightarrow
    \operatorname{ExactlyOne}\bigl(
      \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C),\mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C),\mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C)
    \bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{ExactlyOne}(A,B,D)
  \Longleftrightarrow{}&
  (A\wedge\neg B\wedge\neg D)\vee
  (B\wedge\neg A\wedge\neg D)\\
  &{}\vee(D\wedge\neg A\wedge\neg B).
\end{aligned}
\]

\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(C\) is non-$X$-equivalent, so that the residual closure of \(C\) is
  logically equivalent to some \(X'\neq X\), then the
  native-closure outcome\ of \(C\) is one of two kinds: either \(X'\) is
  already in the accepted-imports base and the carrier closes natively,
  or \(X'\) remains open-pending relative to that base.
\item If \(C\) is $X$-equivalent, so that the residual closure of \(C\) is
  logically equivalent to \(X\), then exactly one of the three
  carrier-residual-equivalent foreclosure modes applies:
  \[
    \textup{\textsc{CRE-TE}},\qquad \textup{\textsc{CRE-BF}},\qquad \textup{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}.
  \]
\end{enumerate}

Consequently, under the Coverage Theorem, every admissible typed
primary carrier aimed at \(X\) is exhausted by the four-state audit:
\[
  \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C),
\]
with the three
$X$-equivalent\ modes disjoint in the audit classification.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
This corollary is deliberately local to the carrier audit.  It is not a
general no-go theorem for external proof methods, and it does not claim
that every mathematical bridge into \(X\) is impossible.  It says only
that, inside the typed carrier setup of Part I, a bridge that turns a
non-\(X\)-equivalent carrier into an \(X\)-equivalent composite must
carry the target-strength content it appears to transport.  The next
subsections broaden the audit: the Coverage Theorem supplies
exhaustiveness, and Attack Foreclosure v4 applies the resulting

\label{thm:coverage}
Let \(X\) be an open target conjecture, and let \(C\) be a typed
primary carrier aimed at \(X\) under the typed-context discipline.  Assume \(C\) lies in an
admissible coverage context for \(X\).  Then the four typed states are
exhaustive: \(C\) is non-$X$-equivalent, or \(C\) is in \textup{\textsc{CRE-TE}},
or \(C\) is in \textup{\textsc{CRE-BF}}, or \(C\) is in \textup{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}.
Equivalently, under
\[
  C\leadsto X,\qquad C\models\text{typed-context discipline},\qquad
  \operatorname{CoverageCtx}(X,C),
\]
every admissible typed primary carrier aimed at \(X\) satisfies the
four-way disjunction
\[
  \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C).
\]
The assertion is exhaustiveness only; disjointness of the three
$X$-equivalent\ modes is the separate exactly-one conclusion used in
Theorem~\ref{thm:carrier-dichotomy} (Carrier Dichotomy).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:type-finite-foreclosure}
Let \(X\) be an open target conjecture, and let \(C\) range over typed
primary carriers aimed at \(X\) under the typed-context discipline\ and an admissible
coverage context.  Then the carrier-state door-space is type-finite:
every such \(C\) is classified by one of the four states
non-$X$-equivalent, \textup{\textsc{CRE-TE}}, \textup{\textsc{CRE-BF}}, or \textup{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}.
Thus the codomain of audit classifications has exactly four entries,
and the image of any family of typed carriers aimed at \(X\) has
cardinality at most four, even when the carrier family itself is
infinite.
Formally, for
\[
  \mathsf{State}
  =\{\mathsf{nonX},\mathsf{TE},\mathsf{BF},\mathsf{CTMT}\},
\]
define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \operatorname{ClassifiesAs}(\mathsf{nonX},X,C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C),\\
  \operatorname{ClassifiesAs}(\mathsf{TE},X,C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C),\\
  \operatorname{ClassifiesAs}(\mathsf{BF},X,C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow \mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C),\\
  \operatorname{ClassifiesAs}(\mathsf{CTMT},X,C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C).
\end{aligned}
\]
Then
\[
  C\leadsto X\wedge C\models\text{typed-context discipline}\wedge
  \operatorname{CoverageCtx}(X,C)
  \Longrightarrow
  \exists s\in\mathsf{State}.\,
    \operatorname{ClassifiesAs}(s,X,C).
\]

\label{thm:attack-foreclosure-v4}
Let \(X\) be a target conjecture in framework scope.  Let \(m\) be a
framework-internal move, where
\[
  m\in\{\mbox{carrier pivot},\mbox{bridge import},
  \mbox{cascade-internal computation}\}.
\]
Then \(m\) does not advance \(X\) without importing external
mathematical content:
\[
  \operatorname{InScope}(X)
  \Longrightarrow
  \neg\,\operatorname{AdvancesWithoutExternal}(m,X).
\]
Equivalently, a framework-internal move has one of two typed outcomes:
either it remains inside the four-state carrier classification from
Theorem~\ref{thm:carrier-dichotomy} (Carrier Dichotomy)\ and Conditional schema~\ref{thm:coverage} (Coverage), without closing \(X\) by
internal means, or it exposes framework-external\ content that must be
accepted through the closure-formation discipline rather than generated
by the framework-internal move itself.  The same statement applies
pointwise to chains by auditing each move in the chain.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:ctmt-recursion}
For any target \(X\) and typed primary carrier \(C\), the
\textsc{CRE-CTMT}\ state admits a depth-indexed recursion tower.  The base case
is the depth-\(1\) tower: \(C\) is in \textsc{CRE-CTMT}\ exactly when \(C\) has
a one-level matrix-element terminus.  If \(C\)'s cascade reduces to a
deeper carrier-native matrix-element family whose own decision carries
a CTMT tower of positive depth, then \(C\) carries the next tower
level.  Formally, for any cascade semantics \(\sigma\),
\[
  \mathsf{Tower}_{\sigma}(X,C,1)
  \Longleftrightarrow
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C),
\]
and for every \(n\geq 0\),
\[
  \mathsf{Tower}_{\sigma}(X,C',n+1)\wedge
  \operatorname{Reduces}_{\sigma}(X,C,C')
  \Longrightarrow
  \mathsf{Tower}_{\sigma}(X,C,n+2).
\]
Thus matrix-element terminality can fire at depth \(1\), depth \(2\),
and iteratively at any finite positive depth admitted by the
inherited-records base.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:attack-foreclosure-v5}
Let \(X\) be a target in framework scope, and let \(c\) be a formed
closure whose substrate lies in the V-Differential trace-state-only column\ under the SB closure
assumption.  Then the v5 refinement has the following three-conjunct
form:
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\forall m.\,
    \operatorname{DerivationRoute}(m)
    \Longrightarrow
    \neg\operatorname{AdvancesWithoutExternal}(m,X),\\
  &\forall l:\operatorname{RMLanding}(c,X).\,
    \operatorname{ImportsAsNamedRecognition}(l,s_{c,X}),\\
  &\forall l:\operatorname{RMLanding}(c,X).\,
    \operatorname{LandsAtTheoremGrade}(c,X).
\end{aligned}
\]
The first conjunct is the v4 foreclosure conclusion restricted to
derivation routes.  The second says that recognition-mode landings
import the load-bearing source as named recognition.  The third says
that such landings reach theorem-grade under the SB closure assumption.
Thus v5 refines, does not replace, v4: derivation routes remain
foreclosed, while recognition-mode landings are structurally distinct
and peer with derivation-mode landings under the SB closure assumption.

conclusion: The four-axis calibration profile of a calibration consists of its algebraic identities, detector class, descent invariants, and carrier orientation. A candidate calibration is a rebadge of an existing calibration when the two profiles match on all four axes. It is genuinely new relative to a family when it is not a rebadge of any existing family member. Thus a profile is the product Profile = AlgId× DetectorClass× DescentInv× CarrierOrient. For profiles p and q , Rebadge(p,q) iff p_ alg =q_ alg p_ det =q_ det p_ desc =q_ desc p_ orient =q_ orient , and GenuineNew(p, F) iff q∈ F,\ (p,q).
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:four-axis-profile}
The four-axis calibration profile of a calibration consists of its algebraic identities,
detector class, descent invariants, and carrier orientation.  A candidate
calibration is a rebadge of an existing calibration when the two profiles
match on all four axes.  It is genuinely new relative to a family when it
is not a rebadge of any existing family member.
Thus a profile is the product
\[
  \mathsf{Profile}
  =
  \mathsf{AlgId}\times
  \mathsf{DetectorClass}\times
  \mathsf{DescentInv}\times
  \mathsf{CarrierOrient}.
\]
For profiles \(p\) and \(q\),
\[
  \mathsf{Rebadge}(p,q)
  \iff
  p_{\mathsf{alg}}=q_{\mathsf{alg}}\wedge
  p_{\mathsf{det}}=q_{\mathsf{det}}\wedge
  p_{\mathsf{desc}}=q_{\mathsf{desc}}\wedge
  p_{\mathsf{orient}}=q_{\mathsf{orient}},
\]
and
\[
  \mathsf{GenuineNew}(p,\mathcal F)
  \iff
  \forall q\in\mathcal F,\ \neg\mathsf{Rebadge}(p,q).
\]

conclusion: Within a calibration family, a candidate calibration is genuinely new if and only if, for every existing family member, it differs on at least one axis of the four-axis calibration profile. Equivalently, a candidate matching an existing member on algebraic identities, detector class, descent invariants, and carrier orientation is a rebadge; on attempted earning-its-place, it collapses to the existing member's content. Equivalently, for a candidate profile p and family F , GenuineNew(p, F) iff q∈ F, p_ alg q_ alg p_ det q_ det p_ desc q_ desc p_ orient q_ orient .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:rebadge-discipline}
Within a calibration family, a candidate calibration is genuinely new if
and only if, for every existing family member, it differs on at least one
axis of the four-axis calibration profile.  Equivalently, a candidate matching an existing
member on algebraic identities, detector class, descent invariants, and
carrier orientation is a rebadge; on attempted earning-its-place, it
collapses to the existing member's content.
Equivalently, for a candidate profile \(p\) and family \(\mathcal F\),
\[
  \mathsf{GenuineNew}(p,\mathcal F)
  \iff
  \forall q\in\mathcal F,\,
  p_{\mathsf{alg}}\ne q_{\mathsf{alg}}\vee
  p_{\mathsf{det}}\ne q_{\mathsf{det}}\vee
  p_{\mathsf{desc}}\ne q_{\mathsf{desc}}\vee
  p_{\mathsf{orient}}\ne q_{\mathsf{orient}}.
\]

conclusion: Calibration-side typed bridges carry a directed source-to-target type signature. For a bridge B with source S and target T , the bridge is symmetric with its reversal if and only if S=T . In particular, when S T , the existence of a typed bridge S→ T does not by itself supply a usable typed bridge T→ S . Formally, B=B^ op iff source(B)=target(B).
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:bridge-type-direction}
Calibration-side typed bridges carry a directed source-to-target type
signature.  For a bridge \(B\) with source \(S\) and target \(T\), the
bridge is symmetric with its reversal if and only if \(S=T\).  In
particular, when \(S\ne T\), the existence of a typed bridge \(S\to T\)
does not by itself supply a usable typed bridge \(T\to S\).
Formally,
\[
  B=B^{\mathrm{op}}
  \iff
  \mathsf{source}(B)=\mathsf{target}(B).
\]

source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:bridge-type-direction}
Calibration-side typed bridges carry a directed source-to-target type
signature.  For a bridge \(B\) with source \(S\) and target \(T\), the
bridge is symmetric with its reversal if and only if \(S=T\).  In
particular, when \(S\ne T\), the existence of a typed bridge \(S\to T\)
does not by itself supply a usable typed bridge \(T\to S\).
Formally,
\[
  B=B^{\mathrm{op}}
  \iff
  \mathsf{source}(B)=\mathsf{target}(B).
\]

conclusion: A framework-type is a four-axis record consisting of uniformity, worst-caseness, scoping, and packaging. On the P versus NP track, the cascade framework-type is nonuniform, average-case, scoped, and package-based. The standard Clay target framework-type is uniform, worst-case, unconditional, and language-based. The uniform / nonuniform and worst-case / average-case axes are the framework-type analogues of the distinctions surveyed in . Thus framework-type = Uniformity× WorstCaseness× Scoping× Packaging. For the P versus NP row, F_ PvNP = (nonuniform,averageCase, scoped,packageBased), T_ Clay = (uniform,worstCase, unconditional,languageBased). expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:framework-type}
A framework-type is a four-axis record consisting of uniformity,
worst-caseness, scoping, and packaging.  On the \(P\) versus \(NP\)
track, the cascade framework-type is nonuniform, average-case, scoped,
and package-based.  The standard Clay target framework-type is uniform,
worst-case, unconditional, and language-based.  The uniform /
nonuniform and worst-case / average-case axes are the framework-type
analogues of the distinctions surveyed in \cite{Impagliazzo1995FiveWorlds}.
Thus
\[
  framework-type
  =
  \mathsf{Uniformity}\times
  \mathsf{WorstCaseness}\times
  \mathsf{Scoping}\times
  \mathsf{Packaging}.
\]
For the \(P\) versus \(NP\) row,
\[
\begin{aligned}
  F_{\mathrm{PvNP}}
  &=
  (\mathsf{nonuniform},\mathsf{averageCase},
    \mathsf{scoped},\mathsf{packageBased}),\\
  T_{\mathrm{Clay}}
  &=
  (\mathsf{uniform},\mathsf{worstCase},
    \mathsf{unconditional},\mathsf{languageBased}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The matching predicate is componentwise equality on these four axes.

conclusion: A named functorial gate consists of a name, a typed source, a typed target, a direction, and a stated theorem obligation. It is a typed bridge-as-content: the gate does not assert that the transport has been supplied, but records exactly what a supplied transport would have to prove. The record shape is FunctorialGate = \ name,source,target, direction,theoremObligation\ . Here source and target are typed-source descriptions: calibration, regime, or framework/target type labels, depending on the gate.

\begin{proof}
Define \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{named}}\) to be the three records in
\Cref{tab:functorial-gates}.  Each record has the five fields in
\Cref{def:functorial-gate}: name, source, target, direction, and theorem
obligation.  Inspection of the displayed catalog gives exactly three
entries, so
\[
  |\mathcal G_{\mathrm{named}}|=3.

obligation field.  Therefore every \(g\in\mathcal G_{\mathrm{named}}\)
satisfies the species-level well-formedness condition.  This proves the
catalog theorem.  No individual gate obligation is solved by this
argument; those obligations are exactly the source-to-target transports
named in the fifth field of each gate record.
\end{proof}\footnote{\raggedright This theorem is verified in Lean as
\texttt{SixBirdsMetaMath.MetaMath.\allowbreak

conclusion: This section records predictions and open problems only. None of the paragraphs below is used as evidence for the formal statements of Parts I–III, and none is a claim that a missing substrate landing has already been supplied. The common theme is that the present paper has identified a small number of testable structural continuations: a third trace-state-only substrate for the recognition-mode template, a track-independent bound for CTMT recursion, and functorial gates beyond the three named in the current typed-deposit catalog.

conclusion: Lifting the four Part II schemas to theorem-grade across the framework requires two future inputs: (a) a third-instance substrate landing on a V-Differential trace-state-only substrate beyond PvNP and RH, with Hodge as the leading candidate; and (b) a structural argument from the V-Differential column-membership predicate to the (ii)/(iii)/(ii) verdict pattern. Until both inputs exist, each of the four Part II universal claims remains a candidate meta-theorem. The first input is empirical in the corpus sense: it asks for a third landed trace-state-only example, audited by the same seven-stage template and by the same two-instance signature comparison already used for PvNP and RH. The second input is structural: it asks for a reason why trace-state-only column membership should force the framework-primitive, SAU non-descent, and V-Differential elevation sweep to display the (ii)/(iii)/(ii) pattern. Without the structural argument, a third example would still be suggestive rather than theorem-grade.

conclusion: The open problem is to identify a substrate-independent invariant that would bound CTMT depth across cascades.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The open problem is to identify a substrate-independent invariant
that would bound CTMT depth across cascades.  Candidate invariants
could measure inherited-record complexity, descent height, native
matrix-family rank, or some future refinement of the carrier's
adequacy residual.  Any such proposal would need to be compatible with
the recursive constructor of \Cref{thm:ctmt-recursion}: a depth bound
cannot merely rule out further reductions by definition; it must
explain why the next deeper matrix-element family cannot arise under
the typed-context discipline.

conclusion: This paper proves a conditional separation between P and NP inside Six Birds Theory, a typed framework for closure formation in mathematical structures. For SAT, the framework supplies a saturated SAT layer — a typed carrier of polynomial-time SAT computations together with their audit data — observed through a lawful polynomial-time instrument that declares which observations on the layer count as current. Two translation theorems connect this setup to standard SAT semantics. Translation A identifies SAT P with decision currentization: the SAT decision bit is itself a current observation on . Translation B identifies decision currentization with currentization of the canonical witness producer of the autonomous lift , using SAT self-reducibility and closure of current observables under post-processing, finite products, and composition. The structural hypothesis of says that this canonical witness producer is not a lawful current observable on . Under that hypothesis, the four-step contradiction chain gives SAT P ; combined with SAT NP from the standard verifier package, the framework accepts at recognition grade. Outside the framework, the result is the conditional theorem: formed-SAT closure carrying under implies P NP . The same closure records also tag , in the audit-closure register of , as a carrier-attached cascade-stable AOR package under . This is packaging of the same conditional theorem. The hypothesis further localizes to one residual: the canonical lexicographic SAT-branching readout is not a lawful current observable on the standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier. A scoped Class-B Irremovability theorem rules out one removal route: no basis-generated Class-B carrier-feature method can remove that residual, except by leaving the basis or importing a target-equivalent lower bound. The paper does not claim an unconditional standard-ZFC separation of P and NP , derivability of from framework primitives, circumvention of the classical barriers in their native senses, absolute irremovability of , or any AOR claim outside the stated formed-SAT, standard-basis scope.

This paper proves a conditional separation between \(P\) and \(NP\)
inside Six Birds Theory, a typed framework for closure formation in
mathematical structures.  For SAT, the framework supplies a saturated
SAT layer \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\) --- a typed carrier of polynomial-time SAT
computations together with their audit data --- observed through a
lawful polynomial-time instrument \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\) that declares which
observations on the layer count as \emph{current}.  Two translation
theorems connect this setup to standard SAT semantics.  Translation A
identifies \(\mathrm{SAT}\in P\) with decision currentization: the SAT
decision bit is itself a current observation on \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\).  Translation
B identifies decision currentization with currentization of the
canonical witness producer of the autonomous lift \(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), using
SAT self-reducibility and closure of current observables under
post-processing, finite products, and composition.

The structural hypothesis \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) of
\citet{TsiokosHiddenness2026} says that this canonical witness producer
is not a lawful current observable on \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\).  Under that
hypothesis, the four-step contradiction chain gives
\(\mathrm{SAT}\notin P\); combined with \(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\) from the
standard verifier package, the framework accepts
\(P^{\mathrm{SB}}\neqNP^{\mathrm{SB}}\) at recognition grade.  Outside the framework, the
result is the conditional theorem: formed-SAT closure carrying
\(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) under \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\) implies \(P\neq NP\).

The same closure records also tag \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), in the audit-closure
register of \citet{Tsiokos2026AOR}, as a carrier-attached
cascade-stable AOR package under \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\).  This is packaging
of the same conditional theorem.  The hypothesis further localizes to
one residual: the canonical lexicographic SAT-branching readout is not
a lawful current observable on the standard fixed-presentation
polynomial current carrier.  A scoped Class-B Irremovability theorem
rules out one removal route: no basis-generated Class-B
carrier-feature method can remove that residual, except by leaving the
basis or importing a target-equivalent lower bound.

The paper does not claim an unconditional standard-ZFC separation of
\(P\) and \(NP\), derivability of \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) from framework
primitives, circumvention of the classical barriers in their native
senses, absolute irremovability of \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\), or any AOR claim
outside the stated formed-SAT, standard-basis scope.

inside Six Birds Theory, a typed framework for closure formation in
mathematical structures.  For SAT, the framework supplies a saturated
SAT layer \(\Tsat\) --- a typed carrier of polynomial-time SAT
computations together with their audit data --- observed through a
lawful polynomial-time instrument \(\Ipoly\) that declares which
observations on the layer count as \emph{current}.  Two translation
theorems connect this setup to standard SAT semantics.  Translation A
identifies \(\mathrm{SAT}\in P\) with decision currentization: the SAT
decision bit is itself a current observation on \(\Tsat\).  Translation
B identifies decision currentization with currentization of the
canonical witness producer of the autonomous lift \(\OmegaSAT\), using
SAT self-reducibility and closure of current observables under
post-processing, finite products, and composition.

The structural hypothesis \(\CSLSATHidden\) of
\citet{TsiokosHiddenness2026} says that this canonical witness producer
is not a lawful current observable on \(\Tsat\).  Under that
hypothesis, the four-step contradiction chain gives
\(\mathrm{SAT}\notin P\); combined with \(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\) from the
standard verifier package, the framework accepts
\(\PSB\neq\NPSB\) at recognition grade.  Outside the framework, the
result is the conditional theorem: formed-SAT closure carrying
\(\CSLSATHidden\) under \(\Ipoly\) implies \(P\neq NP\).

The same closure records also tag \(\Tsat\), in the audit-closure
register of \citet{Tsiokos2026AOR}, as a carrier-attached

one residual: the canonical lexicographic SAT-branching readout is not
a lawful current observable on the standard fixed-presentation
polynomial current carrier.  A scoped Class-B Irremovability theorem
rules out one removal route: no basis-generated Class-B
carrier-feature method can remove that residual, except by leaving the
basis or importing a target-equivalent lower bound.

This paper proves a conditional separation between \(P\) and \(NP\)
inside Six Birds Theory, a typed framework for closure formation in
mathematical structures.  For SAT, the framework supplies a saturated
SAT layer \(\Tsat\) --- a typed carrier of polynomial-time SAT
computations together with their audit data --- observed through a
lawful polynomial-time instrument \(\Ipoly\) that declares which
observations on the layer count as \emph{current}.  Two translation
theorems connect this setup to standard SAT semantics.  Translation A
identifies \(\mathrm{SAT}\in P\) with decision currentization: the SAT
decision bit is itself a current observation on \(\Tsat\).  Translation
B identifies decision currentization with currentization of the
canonical witness producer of the autonomous lift \(\OmegaSAT\), using
SAT self-reducibility and closure of current observables under
post-processing, finite products, and composition.

The structural hypothesis \(\CSLSATHidden\) of
\citet{TsiokosHiddenness2026} says that this canonical witness producer
is not a lawful current observable on \(\Tsat\).  Under that
hypothesis, the four-step contradiction chain gives
\(\mathrm{SAT}\notin P\); combined with \(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\) from the
standard verifier package, the framework accepts
\(\PSB\neq\NPSB\) at recognition grade.  Outside the framework, the
result is the conditional theorem: formed-SAT closure carrying
\(\CSLSATHidden\) under \(\Ipoly\) implies \(P\neq NP\).

The same closure records also tag \(\Tsat\), in the audit-closure
register of \citet{Tsiokos2026AOR}, as a carrier-attached
cascade-stable AOR package under \(\CSLSATHidden\).  This is packaging
of the same conditional theorem.  The hypothesis further localizes to
one residual: the canonical lexicographic SAT-branching readout is not
a lawful current observable on the standard fixed-presentation
polynomial current carrier.  A scoped Class-B Irremovability theorem
rules out one removal route: no basis-generated Class-B
carrier-feature method can remove that residual, except by leaving the
basis or importing a target-equivalent lower bound.

The paper does not claim an unconditional standard-ZFC separation of
\(P\) and \(NP\), derivability of \(\CSLSATHidden\) from framework
primitives, circumvention of the classical barriers in their native
senses, absolute irremovability of \(\CSLSATHidden\), or any AOR claim
outside the stated formed-SAT, standard-basis scope.

This is the scope of the paper.  It does not prove an unconditional
standard-ZFC separation of \(P\) from \(NP\).  Its headline judgment is
framework-relative and recognition-grade; outside the framework, what
is established is the conditional theorem just described.  Nor does
the paper claim to bypass natural proofs, algebrization, or
relativization in their native settings.  The construction works at a
different layer: typed observable saturation over a SAT-specific
history carrier.  Finally, the paper does not claim that

structural recognition source supplied by \citet{TsiokosHiddenness2026}.

\label{def:pvnp:history-carrier}
The \emph{SAT history carrier} \(H^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\) is the all-input,
machine-indexed collection of SAT histories generated over the audited
SAT shells.  At finite stage \(N\), a history in \(\HsatN{N}\) is a
finite typed trace
\[
  h=(\varphi,e,p_{e},I_{e},\operatorname{trace}_{Q},
     \sigma_{L},\operatorname{Cont}_{M},\operatorname{Audit}_{h}),
\]
where \(\varphi\) is an encoded SAT instance of size at most \(N\),
\(e\) is a deterministic polynomial-time transducer index, \(p_{e}\)
is its time certificate, \(I_{e}\) is the package interface,
\(\operatorname{trace}_{Q}\) is the current trace produced by the
autonomous run, \(\sigma_{L}\) is the autonomous lift state,
\(\operatorname{Cont}_{M}\) is the predictive continuation record, and
\(\operatorname{Audit}_{h}\) is the history-local audit record.
\footnote{The SAT history carrier is realized in Lean by the SAT
history carrier declaration listed in \Cref{app:formalization}, with
the finite-stage form exposed as a free argument; see
\Cref{app:formalization} for the narrowing-disclosure discipline.}

\label{def:pvnp:lawfulness-discipline}
A candidate current observable on \(H^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\) is \emph{lawful} when it
satisfies the following five clauses.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Machine indexing.}  The observable is realized by a
  declared deterministic polynomial-time transducer drawn from
  \(K_{\mathrm{poly}}\), with an associated machine index.

\label{thm:pvnp:e-q-closure-properties}
The saturated current-observable family \(E^{!}_{Q}\) has the following
closure properties.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Post-processing.}  If \(f\inE^{!}_{Q}\) has codomain
  \(Y\), and \(g:Y\to Z\) is a deterministic polynomial-time function
  with a declared polynomial budget in the input length, then
  \(g\circ f\inE^{!}_{Q}\).

  \item \emph{Finite products.}  If
  \(f_{1},\ldots,f_{k}\inE^{!}_{Q}\) have codomains
  \(Y_{1},\ldots,Y_{k}\), and the family is fixed-stage in the audit
  sense, at a common stage \(N\), then the product observable
  \[
    h\longmapsto (f_{1}(h),\ldots,f_{k}(h))
  \]
  belongs to \(E^{!}_{Q}\), with codomain
  \(Y_{1}\times\cdots\times Y_{k}\).

  \item \emph{Composition.}  Suppose \(f\inE^{!}_{Q}\) has codomain
  \(Y\), the values \(f(h)\) are encoded SAT instances or other
  admitted input encodings, and \(g\inE^{!}_{Q}\) is a current
  observable defined on histories of the resulting instances.  Then
  the suitable polynomial-time composition \(g\star f\) belongs to
  \(E^{!}_{Q}\).  This composition is through the lawful transducer
  interfaces, not through identity on the history carrier: the
  realizing transducer is the composition of the two underlying
  transducers, with combined time, visibility, replay, and audit
  records.
\end{enumerate}

The Class-B analysis rests on two theorem-grade facts about the
standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier.  The first says
that lawful current observables separate encoded inputs.  The second
says that separately lawful current observations can be paired without
leaving the saturated current-observable family.

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-Presentation Orbit Collapse]
\label{thm:pvnp:orbit-collapse}
For the standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier, the
common kernel of all lawful saturated current observables is the
diagonal:
\[
  \bigcap_{F\inE^{!}_{Q}}\ker(F)=\Delta_{X}.
\]
Equivalently, if \(x\neq y\) are distinct encoded inputs in the carrier,
then there is a lawful current observable \(F\inE^{!}_{Q}\) such that
\[
  F(x)\neq F(y).
\]
\end{theorem}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
A feature is \emph{basis-generated} when it is built from
\(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{fix}}\) by finitely many applications of the
allowed closure operations: quotienting, orbiting, transporting,
holonomy or gluing-class formation, pairing, products, polynomial
post-processing, resource filtration, and presentation refinement.  Each
basis-generated feature is assigned a normal class.  The quotient class
\(Q\) records an equivalence relation that the proposed Class-B law
requires every lawful current observable to respect.  The joint-access
class \(J\) records a tuple of separately current observables whose
joint access is alleged to be inadmissible.  The positive-closure class
\(C\) records a construction yielding new current observables from
current ones.  The presentation-refinement class \(P\) records a
refinement of the carrier by presentation data; it supplies breaker
data, not an obstruction.  The time-filtration class \(T\) records a
feature indexed by polynomial resource strata.  The Basis Combination
Closure theorem in the next subsection proves that these five classes
are exhaustive for basis-generated features.  The formal inductive
definition of basis generation, together with the normal-class
assignment, is deferred to \Cref{app:class-b-definitions}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:pvnp:basis-combination-closure}
Let \(\Phi\) be a finite basis-generated feature of the standard
fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier.  Then \(\Phi\) lies in
one of the five normal classes \(Q,J,C,P,T\).  Moreover, the following
class consequence holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\(Q\).] If \(\Phi\) is a quotient feature, then any equivalence
  relation respected by every \(F\inE^{!}_{Q}\) is the diagonal; orbit
  collapse forces the feature to be trivial.
\item[\(J\).] If \(\Phi\) is a joint-access feature, then any finite
  tuple of separately current observables admits a jointly current
  product observable; pairing closure kills the alleged obstruction.
\item[\(C\).] If \(\Phi\) is a positive-closure feature, then it
  constructs new current observables from current observables and does
  not exclude a target.
\item[\(P\).] If \(\Phi\) is a presentation-refinement feature, then
  it supplies breaker or refinement data rather than an invariance
  obstruction.
\item[\(T\).] If \(\Phi\) is a time-filtration feature, then it is
  either fixed-stratum only, with no obstruction at the full carrier
  \(E^{!}_{Q}=\bigcup_k E^{[k]}\), or it is target-equivalent at the
  full polynomial union.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: Conditional on pseudorandom function generators of the required strength, no such natural property proves the strong circuit lower bounds needed for P versus NP .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The Razborov--Rudich natural-proofs barrier
\citep{RazborovRudich1997NaturalProofs} rules out a broad class of
combinatorial lower-bound methods.  In that setting a natural property
of Boolean functions is constructive, large, and useful against the
circuit class under attack.  The carrier-level fact is
pseudorandomness: a large constructive property useful against all easy
functions would distinguish pseudorandom functions from truly random
functions.  Conditional on pseudorandom function generators of the
required strength, no such natural property proves the strong circuit
lower bounds needed for \(P\) versus \(NP\).  Subsequent work has
refined the largeness and constructivity conditions
\citep{Chow2011AlmostNaturalProofs} without removing the barrier in its
intended scope.

required strength, no such natural property proves the strong circuit
lower bounds needed for \(P\) versus \(NP\).  Subsequent work has
refined the largeness and constructivity conditions
\citep{Chow2011AlmostNaturalProofs} without removing the barrier in its
intended scope.

\label{def:pvnp:aor-instance:object}
Let \(\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{PvNP}}\) be the SAT scope consisting of the
saturated SAT layer \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), the lawful polynomial-time current
instrument \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\), the saturated current and predictive observable
families \(E^{!}_{Q}\) and \(E^{!}_{M}\), the quotients \(Q^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\) and
\(M^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), the comparison map \(\pi^{!}\), the autonomous lift
\(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), the visibility relation \(\operatorname{Vis}^{!}\), the
currentization predicates \(\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{dec}}_{Q}\) and \(\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{wit}}_{Q}\),
the recognition source \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\), the standard SAT verifier
package, the Class-B basis \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{fix}}\), and the
\(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\) judgment package.

The AOR instance object
\[
  C_{\mathrm{PvNP}}(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}},I_{\mathrm{poly}},\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}})
\]
has the following typed fields.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item The carrier is \(H^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), read through the finite-stage
        carriers described in \Cref{def:pvnp:history-carrier} and the
        saturated aggregate of \Cref{def:pvnp:saturated-closure}.
  \item The current observations are the lawful polynomial-time
        observables \(E^{!}_{Q}\) of \Cref{def:pvnp:e-q-saturation}
        under the instrument \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\) of \Cref{def:pvnp:i-poly}.
        The predictive observations are \(E^{!}_{M}\).
  \item The current and predictive quotients are \(Q^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\) and
        \(M^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), with comparison map \(\pi^{!}\), as in
        \Cref{def:pvnp:q-saturated,def:pvnp:m-saturated,def:pvnp:comparison-map}.
  \item The routes are the polynomial-time post-processing, finite
        product, and composition operations of
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:e-q-closure-properties}, together with the
        self-reduction route used in Translation Theorem~B.
  \item The source records are the standard \(\mathrm{SAT}\in P\)
        bridge used in Translation Theorem~A, the self-reduction
        package used in Translation Theorem~B, the standard verifier
        package for \(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\), and the recognition source
        \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) supplied by \citet{TsiokosHiddenness2026}.
  \item The hidden-state record is the autonomous lift \(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}}\)
        of \Cref{def:pvnp:omega-sat}, together with the visibility
        relation \(\operatorname{Vis}^{!}\) of \Cref{def:pvnp:vis-bang}.
  \item The target records are decision currentization
        \(\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{dec}}_{Q}(\mathrm{SAT})\), witness currentization
        \(\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{wit}}_{Q}(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}})\), the localized fixed-branch
        residual
        \(\mathrm{Br}^{\mathrm{lex}}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\notinE^{!}_{Q}\),
        and the judgment proposition \(P^{\mathrm{SB}}\neqNP^{\mathrm{SB}}\).
  \item The residual statuses are the discharges recorded in
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:aor:mechanical-records},
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:aor:recognition-source-discharge},
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:aor:translation-discharge},
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:aor:class-b-scope-fence}, and
        \Cref{thm:pvnp:aor:judgment-package}.
  \item The nonclaim register is the register of \Cref{sec:scope},
        including the absence of an unconditional standard-ZFC
        theorem, the absence of a claim to circumvent classical
        barriers in their native formulations, the non-derivation of
        \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\), and the scoped nature of Class-B
        Irremovability.
\end{enumerate}

Positively, the paper claims the following.  The saturated SAT layer
construction, including \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), \(E^{!}_{Q}\), \(M^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\),
\(Q^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), is standard mathematics expressed in
the framework's typed vocabulary.  The closure properties of
\(E^{!}_{Q}\) are the current-observable closure rules needed by the
translation theorems.  Translation A identifies standard
\(\mathrm{SAT}\in P\) with \(\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{dec}}_{Q}(\mathrm{SAT})\), and
Translation B identifies \(\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{dec}}_{Q}(\mathrm{SAT})\) with
\(\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{wit}}_{Q}(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}})\).  Conditional on the structural
recognition source \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\), the four-step contradiction
gives \(\mathrm{SAT}\notin P\).  The BirdInt judgment records
\(P^{\mathrm{SB}}\neqNP^{\mathrm{SB}}\) at \emph{recognition grade} under the standard Six Birds
closure assumption.  Read as ordinary mathematics, the result is the
conditional theorem
\[
  \text{formed-SAT closure carrying \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) under \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\)}
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  P\neq NP.
\]
The paper also proves the Six Birds Class-B Irremovability barrier on
the standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier
(\Cref{thm:pvnp:irremovability-scoped}).  The localization in
\Cref{sec:recognition-source} identifies the concrete residual on
which the barrier acts:
\(\mathrm{Br}^{\mathrm{lex}}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\notinE^{!}_{Q}\).

\label{nonclaim:pvnp:standard-zfc-pneqnp}
This paper does not claim a standard-ZFC unconditional separation of

\(\neg\operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{wit}}_{Q}(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}})\), and no separation of standard
\(P\) from \(NP\) is proved.
