expanded_source_wording_tex:
The paper has proved three linked results.  First, it constructs the
saturated SAT layer \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), the lawful polynomial-time current
instrument \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\), and the saturated current-observable family
\(E^{!}_{Q}\), then proves Translation Theorem A and Translation Theorem
B.  Conditional on the structural recognition source
\(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\), the four-step contradiction gives
\(\mathrm{SAT}\notin P\); combined with the standard verifier-package
fact \(\mathrm{SAT}\in NP\) \citep{Cook1971TheoremProving}, this yields
the framework-relative \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\) judgment \(P^{\mathrm{SB}}\neqNP^{\mathrm{SB}}\) at
\emph{recognition grade}.  Outside the framework, this is the conditional
theorem that formed SAT closure carrying \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) under
\(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\) implies \(P\neq NP\).
Second, \Cref{sec:recognition-source} makes the structural source
concrete by localizing \(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) to the fixed-branch residual
\[
  \mathrm{Br}^{\mathrm{lex}}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\notinE^{!}_{Q},
\]
the assertion that the canonical lexicographic SAT-branching readout is
not a lawful current observable on the fixed-presentation carrier.
Third, \Cref{sec:class-b-barrier} proves the Six Birds Class-B
Irremovability barrier: no basis-generated Class-B carrier-feature law
on the standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier removes
\(\Gamma_{\textsc{csl-sat-hidden}}\) except by leaving the fixed basis or importing a
target-equivalent lower bound.  That barrier rests on Fixed-Presentation
Orbit Collapse (\Cref{thm:pvnp:orbit-collapse}) and polynomial
pairing closure, organized through Basis Exhaustiveness
(\Cref{thm:pvnp:basis-exhaustiveness}), Basis Combination Closure
(\Cref{thm:pvnp:basis-combination-closure}), and the scoped
Irremovability theorem (\Cref{thm:pvnp:irremovability-scoped}).  It
is analogous in role to Baker--Gill--Solovay relativization,
Razborov--Rudich natural proofs, and Aaronson--Wigderson algebrization
\citep{BakerGillSolovay1975Relativization,RazborovRudich1997NaturalProofs,AaronsonWigderson2009Algebrization},
but methodologically distinct and internal to Six Birds.

\label{def:pvnp:six-mechanisms}
The saturated SAT shell carries the following six mechanisms.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(P_{1}\), \emph{machine update}.  This is the deterministic
  polynomial-time transducer class admitted on the SAT layer, namely
  the class \(K_{\mathrm{poly}}\) declared in the audited shell.
  Update is by lawful polynomial-time machine action on encoded SAT
  instances.

  \item \(P_{2}\), \emph{admissibility}.  This is the set of encoded
  SAT instances admitted at the current finite stage.  Admissibility is
  determined by the finite-stage restriction of the audited shell's
  instance database, together with the type-correctness and
  no-smuggling checks imposed by the lawfulness discipline.

  \item \(P_{3}\), \emph{timescale}.  This is the polynomial budget
  declared by the lawful instrument \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\), including the local
  clock and the time certificate recorded by each lawful current
  observable.

  \item \(P_{4}\), \emph{lens selection}.  This is the visibility lens
  of the audited shell, determining which projection of histories is
  exposed to current observation, and which wider projection is used
  for predictive observation.

  \item \(P_{5}\), \emph{packaging}.  This is the \(Q/M\) quotient and
  continuation packaging: the SAT-saturated current and predictive
  quotients \(Q^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\) and \(M^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), together with the comparison map
  \(\pi^{!}\) on the history carrier \(H^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\).

  \item \(P_{6}\), \emph{audit}.  This is the audit ledger of the
  audited shell, including the machine-index record, time certificate,
  replay log, and gate predicates declared in the audit interface.  The
  closed audit record is part of the saturated SAT layer \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), and
  the seven gates \(G_{1}\)--\(G_{7}\) are listed in
  \Cref{app:gate-audit}.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: This appendix records the seven-gate audit used by the lawfulness discipline in . A lawful current observable in E^ ! _ Q is not merely a polynomial-time transducer; it carries audit data certifying that the transducer has not imported the SAT bit, a witness, an external verifier, or other hidden information. The seven gates below are the typed check predicates attached to that audit data. Each gate is represented in the audit record by the same four-part schema. First there is a check predicate, a typed assertion about the candidate observable or the saturated layer on which it acts. Second there is a status saying whether the check passes. Third there is an evidence record witnessing the status. Fourth there is an implication from the passed check to the corresponding no-smuggling or no-overreading property. The same schema is used for G_ 1 – G_ 6 and for the seventh gate.

conclusion: Every lawful current observable in E^ ! _ Q , acting on the saturated SAT layer T^ ! _ SAT , passes the following seven gate checks with the typed evidence records carried in its lawfulness data. G_ 1 , no SAT oracle smuggling. The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle for the SAT decision predicate. The status passes by construction: the audited shell admits ordinary deterministic polynomial-time transducers, not SAT-oracle machines. The evidence is the audit ledger recording the absence of oracle commitments. The implication is that the observable's computation does not implicitly use the SAT bit as input. G_ 2 , no witness oracle smuggling. The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle for a satisfying-witness producer . The status passes by construction, and the evidence is again the audit ledger of the admitted transducer. The implication is that satisfying assignments are not pre-loaded into the observable or made available as hidden input. G_ 3 , no external verifier oracle smuggling. The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an external NP-verifier oracle. The status passes by the same audit evidence: verifier behavior must be realized by the declared polynomial-time computation itself. The implication is that the observable cannot test whether an assignment satisfies a formula by an undeclared oracle call. G_ 4 , no hidden B -bit smuggling. The check predicate says that the visibility lens does not encode a hidden bit, such as a disguised SAT bit, into the Q -visible package data . The status passes by visibility bookkeeping. The evidence is the visibility-lens record attached to the current instrument. The implication is that the Q -visible projection does not encode predictive or witness-side data. G_ 5 , no time-certificate smuggling. The check predicate says that the polynomial time certificate is honest: the observable does not exceed its declared polynomial budget by hiding deferred evaluation or unrecorded subcomputation. The status passes by the time-certificate clause of the lawfulness discipline. The evidence is the certificate itself, together with the replay record. The implication is that the observable's polynomial budget is the budget actually audited. G_ 6 , no scope violation. The check predicate says that the observable's domain is the all-input replay convention's instance set, not a favorable subfamily of SAT instances. The status passes by the all-input replay convention. The evidence is the replay record. The implication is that the observable cannot be a partial decider presented as a total current observable. G_ 7 , no overreading suppression. The check predicate says that the observable does not suppress overreading of its own audit data: the lawfulness record is faithful to the actual computation being audited. The status passes by the Foundations-III no-overreading-suppression theorem . The evidence is the audit witness field. The implication is that the audit ledger's records cannot be falsified or selectively hidden at audit time.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:pvnp:gate-audit}
Every lawful current observable in \(E^{!}_{Q}\), acting on the
saturated SAT layer \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), passes the following seven gate checks
with the typed evidence records carried in its lawfulness data.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(G_{1}\), \emph{no SAT oracle smuggling}.  The check
  predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle
  \citep{BakerGillSolovay1975Relativization} for the SAT decision
  predicate.  The status passes by construction: the audited shell
  admits ordinary deterministic polynomial-time transducers, not
  SAT-oracle machines.
  The evidence is the audit ledger recording the absence of oracle
  commitments.  The implication is that the observable's computation
  does not implicitly use the SAT bit as input.

  \item \(G_{2}\), \emph{no witness oracle smuggling}.  The check
  predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle for a
  satisfying-witness producer \citep{FeigeShamir1990WitnessHiding,GoldwasserMicaliRackoff1989KnowledgeComplexity}.  The status passes by construction, and
  the evidence is again the audit ledger of the admitted transducer.
  The implication is that satisfying assignments are not pre-loaded
  into the observable or made available as hidden input.

  \item \(G_{3}\), \emph{no external verifier oracle smuggling}.
  The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an
  external NP-verifier oracle.  The status passes by the same audit
  evidence: verifier behavior must be realized by the declared
  polynomial-time computation itself.  The implication is that the
  observable cannot test whether an assignment satisfies a formula by
  an undeclared oracle call.

  \item \(G_{4}\), \emph{no hidden \(B\)-bit smuggling}.  The
  check predicate says that the visibility lens does not encode a
  hidden bit, such as a disguised SAT bit, into the \(Q\)-visible
  package data
  \citep{GoguenMeseguer1982SecurityPolicies,SabelfeldMyers2003InformationFlow}.  The status passes by visibility bookkeeping.  The
  evidence is the visibility-lens record attached to the current
  instrument.  The implication is that the \(Q\)-visible projection
  does not encode predictive or witness-side data.

  \item \(G_{5}\), \emph{no time-certificate smuggling}.  The
  check predicate says that the polynomial time certificate is honest:
  the observable does not exceed its declared polynomial budget by
  hiding deferred evaluation or unrecorded subcomputation.  The status
  passes by the time-certificate clause of the lawfulness discipline.
  The evidence is the certificate itself, together with the replay
  record.  The implication is that the observable's polynomial budget
  is the budget actually audited.

  \item \(G_{6}\), \emph{no scope violation}.  The check predicate
  says that the observable's domain is the all-input replay
  convention's instance set, not a favorable subfamily of SAT
  instances.  The status passes by the all-input replay convention.
  The evidence is the replay record.  The implication is that the
  observable cannot be a partial decider presented as a total current
  observable.

  \item \(G_{7}\), \emph{no overreading suppression}.  The check
  predicate says that the observable does not suppress overreading of
  its own audit data: the lawfulness record is faithful to the actual
  computation being audited.  The status passes by the Foundations-III
  no-overreading-suppression theorem
  \citep{TsiokosFoundationsIII2026}.  The evidence is the audit
  witness field.  The implication is that the audit ledger's records
  cannot be falsified or selectively hidden at audit time.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{definition}[Class-B carrier-property law]
\label{def:pvnp:class-b-law}
A \emph{Class-B carrier-property law} is a theorem of the form
\[
  \Phi(\mathcal C) \Longrightarrow
  \neg \exists O\in\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}\,:\,T(O),
\]
where \(\mathcal C\) is a Six Birds carrier, \(\Phi(\mathcal C)\) is
an intrinsic feature of that carrier, and the impossibility conclusion
follows from the feature itself.  The feature is not an external
recognition source, is not a restatement of the target, and is not a
claim-discipline restriction on how the target is allowed to be
asserted.
\end{definition}

Class-B laws are contrasted with Class-A claim-discipline laws.
Class-A laws, such as no-overread, adequacy, and quotientality, act on
the structure of the claim being made.  Class-B laws act on the
carrier: they try to derive an impossibility from a property of the
computational substrate.  The formalization records the intrinsic
feature condition, the non-recognition-source condition, the
non-claim-discipline condition, and the carrier-feature impossibility
conclusion as explicit fields of the corresponding typed record.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:pvnp:normal-classes}
The five \emph{normal feature classes} are \(Q,J,C,P,T\).
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(Q\), the \emph{quotient class}, consists of equivalence
  relations \(R\subseteq X\times X\) such that the proposed Class-B
  law requires \(R\subseteq\ker(F)\) for every \(F\inE^{!}_{Q}\).
  Equivalently, every lawful current observable is required to be
  constant on \(R\)-classes.

  \item \(J\), the \emph{joint-access class}, consists of finite
  tuples \(F_1,\ldots,F_n\inE^{!}_{Q}\) of separately current
  observables whose joint access \((F_1,\ldots,F_n)\) is alleged not
  to lie in \(E^{!}_{Q}\).

  \item \(C\), the \emph{positive-closure class}, consists of
  constructions that yield new current observables from current ones
  by composition, pairing, products, or polynomial-time
  post-processing.

  \item \(P\), the \emph{presentation-refinement class}, consists of
  refinements of the carrier by presentation data.  These refinements
  supply breaker data rather than invariance constraints.

  \item \(T\), the \emph{time-filtration class}, consists of features
  indexed by polynomial resource strata \(E^{[k]}\), either at a fixed
  \(k\) or uniformly across all \(k\).
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: A basis-generated feature expression is built from B_ fix by finitely many applications of the following closure operations: quotienting, orbiting, transporting, holonomy or gluing-class formation, pairing, finite products, polynomial-time post-processing, resource filtration, and presentation refinement. This is the standard closure-operator construction on a basis of generators , restricted to the operations admitted by the carrier package. Transport has three flavors: route-equivalence transport, record-carrying transport, and resource-indexed transport. The normal-class assignment is a total function normalClass:\ basis-generated expressions\ \ Q,J,C,P,T\ . The diagonal primitive, quotienting, orbiting, transport-by-route, and holonomy or gluing-class formation land in Q . The polynomial-closure primitive, pairing, finite products, and polynomial-time post-processing land in C . The time-filtration primitive, transport-by-resource, and resource filtration land in T . The presentation primitive, transport-by-record, and presentation refinement land in P . Joint-access expressions land in J precisely when they assert obstruction to finite joint access of separately current observables.

\label{def:pvnp:basis-generated}

polynomial-time post-processing, resource filtration, and presentation

basis of generators \citep{DaveyPriestley2002LatticesOrder}, restricted

\label{lem:pvnp:quotient-meet-join}
Let \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) be equivalence relations on \(X\), and suppose
that both are respected by every lawful current observable
\(F\inE^{!}_{Q}\).  Define
\[
  R_{\times}=R_1\cap R_2,
  \qquad
  R_{\vee}=\operatorname{EqCl}(R_1\cup R_2).
\]
Then \(R_{\times}\) is an equivalence relation respected by every
\(F\inE^{!}_{Q}\), and \(R_{\vee}\) is an equivalence relation respected
by every \(F\inE^{!}_{Q}\).  Moreover, by fixed-presentation orbit
collapse,
\[
  R_{\times}=R_{\vee}=\Delta_X .
\]

\label{lem:pvnp:time-stratum}
Let \(E^{[k]}\) denote the family of observables with time bound
\(O(n^k)\), with
\[
  E^{!}_{Q}=\bigcup_k E^{[k]} .
\]
A time-stratum feature has two possible statuses.  At a fixed
stratum, an exclusion \(T\notin E^{[k]}\) does not imply
\(T\notinE^{!}_{Q}\), since \(T\) may lie in \(E^{[\ell]}\) for some
\(\ell>k\).  Uniformly over all strata,
\[
  \bigl(\forall k,\ T\notin E^{[k]}\bigr)
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  T\notinE^{!}_{Q} .
\]
For \(T=\mathrm{Br}^{\mathrm{lex}}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), the uniform
statement is exactly the sharpened recognition residual.

conclusion: This paper gives a conditional Six Birds closure of the Riemann hypothesis by moving the question from classical analytic number theory to a formed-layer trace setting. The substrate is the saturated completed Selberg trace closure of the completed Riemann zeta function, equipped with the functional-equation involution and with a typed ledger of nontrivial zeros. A translation theorem T shows that the anti-invariant zero ledger of the completed zeta shell vanishes, =0 , if and only if every typed nontrivial zero has real part 1/2 . The conditional landing chain uses the Selberg-class instance of Self-Dual Trace Confinement supplied by : its recognition source gives domination records whose vanishing trace forces =0 , and theorem T converts that ledger collapse into the critical-line statement. Stated in the audit-closure language of , the same conditional chain is recorded as a local refinement-stable audited-operational-realisability instance, ^ ref _ S_ RH , whose typed-zero-ledger readout is the critical-line statement. Outside Six Birds, the result is the conditional theorem _ SDTC-Selberg RH on the typed zero ledger. This is not an unconditional proof of the Riemann hypothesis in standard ZFC. The shell's admissibility is a standing Foundations-II hypothesis, and the real-part coordinate of a typed zero is a representation parameter identified with the classical real part by construction-parameter assignment. The development is formalized in Lean as a mathlib-free mechanization (Appendix ).

This paper gives a conditional Six Birds closure of the Riemann
hypothesis by moving the question from classical analytic number
theory to a formed-layer trace setting.  The substrate is the
saturated completed Selberg trace closure of the completed Riemann
zeta function, equipped with the functional-equation involution and
with a typed ledger of nontrivial zeros.  A translation theorem T
shows that the anti-invariant zero ledger of the completed zeta
shell vanishes, \(A_{Z}(\zeta)=0\), if and only if every typed nontrivial
zero has real part \(1/2\).  The conditional
landing chain uses the Selberg-class instance of Self-Dual Trace
Confinement supplied by \citet{TsiokosSDTC2026}: its recognition
source gives domination records whose vanishing trace forces
\(A_{Z}(\zeta)=0\), and theorem T converts that ledger collapse into the
critical-line statement.
Stated in the audit-closure language of \citet{TsiokosAOR2026},
the same conditional chain is recorded as a local
refinement-stable audited-operational-realisability instance,
\(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\in\mathrm{RefStableAOR}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{RH}}}\),
whose typed-zero-ledger readout is the critical-line statement.

Outside Six Birds, the result is the conditional theorem
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC}\text{-}\mathrm{Selberg}}\Rightarrow
\mathrm{RH}\) on the typed zero ledger.  This is not an unconditional
proof of the Riemann hypothesis in standard ZFC.
The shell's admissibility is a standing Foundations-II hypothesis, and
the real-part coordinate of a typed zero is a representation parameter
identified with the classical real part by construction-parameter
assignment.  The development is formalized in Lean as a mathlib-free
mechanization (Appendix~\ref{app:formalization}).

The paper's scope is correspondingly narrow.  The main result is
conditional on \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC\text{-}Selberg}}\); no unconditional RH claim in standard
ZFC is made, and \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC\text{-}Selberg}}\) is not claimed to be derivable
from framework primitives.  The conditional theorem takes a value of
the recognition source as an explicit hypothesis.  The
real-part coordinate of a typed zero is represented by a parameter;
under construction-parameter assignment when the shell is
instantiated, this parameter is identified with the classical real
part of a nontrivial zero of \(\zeta\).  Deriving this identification
from analytic-number-theoretic infrastructure is left as a future extension.
Admissibility of \(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\) under the seven Foundations-II schemas is
carried as an audit witness in the shell, not derived here.  The
classical RH programs named above are neither refuted nor
circumvented in their native sense: they aim at unconditional RH
within their classical substrates, while the present paper
establishes a conditional formed-layer result on the typed Selberg
trace shell.  The generalized Riemann hypothesis lies outside the
scope; the construction is instantiated for \(L=\zeta\) only.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The V-Differential classification organizes such structural laws by
the determining-state information the formed layer may expose.  A
determining state is the internal state through which observable
behavior is required to factor; in a trace-state-only column, the
layer may expose trace observables on a typed positive cone but not
a richer witness that would solve the target problem directly.  For
the RH closure, the visible currency is \(A_{Z}(\zeta)\), the order
\(\preceq\), and the trace functional \(\trace\); the admissible
content has the form of trace domination records
\[
  A_{Z}(\zeta) \preceq B_n,
  \qquad
  \trace B_n \to 0,
\]
not a hidden list of zero locations.  \citet{TsiokosSDTC2026}
identifies Self-Dual Trace Confinement, \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC}}\), as the
V-Differential trace-state-only law for involutive self-dual formed
closures; the present paper is the worked single-substrate
application of that apparatus to \(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\), conditional on the
Selberg-class recognition source.

\label{def:rh:fe-involution}
The functional-equation involution on the complex plane is
\[
  J_{L}(s) = 1-\bar{s}.
\]
Equivalently, if \(s=x+iy\), then
\[
  J_{L}(s) = 1-x+iy.
\]
Thus \(J_{L}\) is reflection across the vertical line
\(\Real(s)=1/2\).

source_wording_tex:
\label{def:rh:fe-involution}
The functional-equation involution on the complex plane is
\[
  \JL(s) = 1-\bar{s}.
\]
Equivalently, if \(s=x+iy\), then
\[
  \JL(s) = 1-x+iy.
\]
Thus \(\JL\) is reflection across the vertical line
\(\Real(s)=1/2\).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:rh:nontrivial-zero-ledger}
Let
\[
  \Lambda_{\zeta}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)
\]
denote the completed Riemann zeta function
\citep{TitchmarshHeathBrown1986,Edwards1974}.  The nontrivial-zero
ledger of \(\Lambda_{\zeta}\) is the typed multiset
\[
  Z_{\zeta}^{\mathrm{nt}}
    =
  \bigl\{\,(\rho,m_{\rho}) :
      \rho\in\mathbb{C},
      \Lambda_{\zeta}(\rho)=0,
      0<\Real(\rho)<1,
      m_{\rho}>0
  \,\bigr\}_{\mathrm{multi}},
\]
where \(m_{\rho}\) is the positive integer multiplicity of \(\rho\)
as a zero of \(\Lambda_{\zeta}\).  The associated atomic ledger measure is
\(\mu_{L}(\{\rho\})=m_{\rho}\).

multiplicity.

\begin{theorem}[RH AOR-instance theorem\footnote{Verified in the Lean formalization against the local refinement-stable AOR predicate over the assembled-carrier fields; the partial alignment relative to the full audit-closure refinement-stable characterisation of \citet{TsiokosAOR2026} is recorded in App~\ref{app:formalization}.}]
\label{thm:rh:aor-instance}
Under the discharges recorded in
\Cref{thm:rh:aor-mechanical-records,thm:rh:aor-recognition-discharge,thm:rh:aor-gamma-bridge-discharge,thm:rh:aor-auditL-discharge,thm:rh:aor-dc-master-import-discharge,thm:rh:aor-real-coordinate-discharge,thm:rh:aor-translation-interface-discharge}, the saturated completed
Selberg trace shell is a local refinement-stable AOR instance on the
RH scope:
\[
  \mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\in
  \mathrm{RefStableAOR}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{RH}}}.
\]
Consequently, at the record level of this AOR instance, the typed zero
ledger of \(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\) has no nontrivial zeros off the fixed locus
\(\Fix(J_{L})\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The definition-side rows provide the carrier, target, role, and
presentation records.  The recognition source provides the
domination-record source.  Its structural-coherence assumptions carry
the abstract DC conclusion to the shell equality \(A_{Z}(\zeta)=0\).  The
\(\mathrm{Audit}_{L}\) field supplies the admissibility
status of the shell.  The master theorem of \citet{TsiokosSDTC2026}
is an accepted typed-cone import.  The real-coordinate presentation
residual and the admissibility-as-hypothesis residual are both
explicitly statused rather than suppressed.  Translation theorem T
then converts \(A_{Z}(\zeta)=0\) into the statement
\[
  \forall\,\rho\inZ_{\zeta}^{\mathrm{nt}},\quad \Real(\rho)=\frac12.
\]
Thus every listed residual in the local wrapper for
\(\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{RH}}\) is either zero, bridged, approved,
carried by construction, or registered as outside the stronger
analytic scope.  This is the AOR-membership reading of
\Cref{thm:rh:conditional}; it does not upgrade the conditional chain
to an unconditional analytic theorem.
\end{proof}

The main result is a Six Birds-native conditional theorem under the
shell-side closure hypothesis recorded by the Foundations-II
admissibility field of \(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\), together with the recognition source
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC\text{-}Selberg}}\).  Outside the Six Birds framing, it reads as
\[
  \Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC\text{-}Selberg}} \Longrightarrow \mathrm{RH}.
\]
That is, given the Selberg-class recognition source, the conditional
landing chain gives RH on the typed zero ledger of \(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\).  This
paper does not claim a standard-ZFC unconditional proof of the
Riemann hypothesis.  Every later use of ``RH'' in this paper should
therefore be read either as the typed-ledger statement under the
construction-parameter identification, or as the conclusion of this
conditional implication.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The SDTC structural law used in this paper is the involutive
self-dual member of that family \cite{TsiokosSDTC2026}.  Its
apparatus is the duality-confinement membrane theorem: given a
separating anti-invariant readout and a vanishing trace domination
sequence, the anti-invariant ledger collapses.  In the RH instance,
the recognition source \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC\text{-}Selberg}}\) supplies the domination
records for \(A_{Z}(\zeta)\), and the bridge theorem
\Cref{thm:rh:dc-master-applied} applies the
\cite{TsiokosSDTC2026} master theorem to \(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\).  The present
paper is therefore the worked single-substrate application of the
SDTC apparatus on the saturated Selberg trace shell, conditional on
the Selberg-class recognition source.  The unconditional analytic
content of any one of the broader formed-layer tracks is not derived
from a common primitive calculus; it is closure content of its formed
layer, supplied as recognition source.  This is why the parallels are
useful but not load-bearing: they show the paper is following a
stable formed-layer pattern inside the Six Birds program, while the
actual RH argument still depends only on the RH-specific shell, the
SDTC apparatus of \citet{TsiokosSDTC2026}, and the Selberg-class
recognition source.

We apply the adequacy-residual calculus of
\citet{Tsiokos2026XiCompanion} and the layer-dissolving membrane
endpoint of \citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller} to the smooth-data
three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes Cauchy problem.  The
argument fixes the Bradshaw--Grujic / Beale--Kato--Majda dissolving
readout \(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\), measures the physical-native adequacy residual
\(\XiRes_C(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\midL^{\mathrm{phys}})\), and propagates it along the doubling
Bradshaw--Grujic stages through the audited source-admission ledger
\(\Omega_{\mathrm{src}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{pr}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{visc}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{tail}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{str}}\).  A no-go family rules
out packing, sparseness, marker-only, and metric-shadow shortcuts; a
Gevrey radius-window gate \(\lambda_J\rho\gtrsim\log\lambda_J\) isolates
the half-log endpoint obstruction; and a Littlewood--Paley transport
map \(S_j\colon L^2(P_j)\to H^{-s}\), \(s\ge q-\varepsilon\), restores
summable predictive propagation.  Under the closure bundle
\(R_1,\ldots,R_9\) and the typed-context discipline, every
divergence-free initial datum \(u_0\in H^{\gamma_0}\) with
\(\gamma_0>5/2\) on the accepted smooth-data channel therefore
satisfies \(T_{\max}(u_0)=\infty\).  The same closure records are then
recast as an AOR-instance membership witness for the smooth-data
carrier, using the audit-closure meta-theory of
\citet{Tsiokos2026AOR}.  This gives the audit-closed-carrier reading
its record-level meaning inside the declared AOR discipline; the
recasting is presented under the carrier-attached discharge-assignment
discipline of the AOR
meta-theory, and a data-bearing strengthening of the discharge-record
fields is outside the present scope.  We make no unconditional
Clay--Millennium claim, no generic critical-Besov data claim, no
criterion-native rewriting of \(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\), and no claim of regularity
independent of the audit records.

We apply the adequacy-residual calculus of
\citet{Tsiokos2026XiCompanion} and the layer-dissolving membrane
endpoint of \citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller} to the smooth-data
three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes Cauchy problem.  The
argument fixes the Bradshaw--Grujic / Beale--Kato--Majda dissolving
readout \(\DBG\), measures the physical-native adequacy residual
\(\XiRes_C(\DBG\mid\Lphys)\), and propagates it along the doubling
Bradshaw--Grujic stages through the audited source-admission ledger
\(\Omsrc=\Omtr+\Ompr+\Omvisc+\Omtail+\Omstr\).  A no-go family rules
out packing, sparseness, marker-only, and metric-shadow shortcuts; a
Gevrey radius-window gate \(\lambdaJ\rho\gtrsim\log\lambdaJ\) isolates
the half-log endpoint obstruction; and a Littlewood--Paley transport
map \(\LPtr\colon L^2(P_j)\to H^{-s}\), \(s\ge q-\eps\), restores
summable predictive propagation.  Under the closure bundle
\(R_1,\ldots,R_9\) and the typed-context discipline, every
divergence-free initial datum \(u_0\in H^{\gamma_0}\) with
\(\gamma_0>5/2\) on the accepted smooth-data channel therefore
satisfies \(\Tmax(u_0)=\infty\).  The same closure records are then
recast as an AOR-instance membership witness for the smooth-data
carrier, using the audit-closure meta-theory of
\citet{Tsiokos2026AOR}.  This gives the audit-closed-carrier reading
its record-level meaning inside the declared AOR discipline; the
recasting is presented under the carrier-attached discharge-assignment
discipline of the AOR
meta-theory, and a data-bearing strengthening of the discharge-record
fields is outside the present scope.  We make no unconditional
Clay--Millennium claim, no generic critical-Besov data claim, no
criterion-native rewriting of \(\DBG\), and no claim of regularity
independent of the audit records.

conclusion: The paper is organized as follows. recalls the adequacy-residual calculus from and the layer-dissolving membrane endpoint from , and specializes both to the Navier–Stokes carrier. fixes the carrier, the fixed readout D^ BG , the physical-native family L^ phys , the BG-windowed exact package, and null-mode legality. records the six imported PDE results and rules out the criterion-native shortcut (NG1). develops the source-admission ledger Omega_ src and the stage-to-stage recurrence for the physical-native residual along the doubling stages. states the remaining no-go family NG2–NG10, excluding scalar-energy, packing, sparse-shadow, marker-only, metric-shadow, moving-window, half-log endpoint, available-analyticity, and raw-nonlinearity shortcuts. develops the Gevrey radius-window branch and the Littlewood–Paley transport rescue. assembles R_1, ,R_9 and concludes the framework-deliverable regularity theorem. recasts the closure records as the AOR-membership witness for the smooth-data carrier. closes with the external interpretation and the locked nonclaim boundary.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The paper is organized as follows.  \Cref{sec:xi-membrane} recalls the
adequacy-residual calculus from \citet{Tsiokos2026XiCompanion} and the
layer-dissolving membrane endpoint from
\citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}, and specializes both to the
Navier--Stokes carrier.  \Cref{sec:ns-carrier} fixes the carrier, the
fixed readout \(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\), the physical-native family \(L^{\mathrm{phys}}\), the
BG-windowed exact package, and null-mode legality.  \Cref{sec:imports}
records the six imported PDE results and rules out the criterion-native
shortcut (NG1).  \Cref{sec:adequacy-cascade} develops the
source-admission ledger \(\Omega_{\mathrm{src}}\) and the stage-to-stage recurrence
for the physical-native residual along the doubling stages.
\Cref{sec:no-go} states the remaining no-go family NG2--NG10,
excluding scalar-energy, packing, sparse-shadow, marker-only,
metric-shadow, moving-window, half-log endpoint, available-analyticity,
and raw-nonlinearity shortcuts.  \Cref{sec:gevrey-lp} develops the
Gevrey radius-window branch and the Littlewood--Paley transport rescue.
\Cref{sec:main-theorem} assembles \(R_1,\ldots,R_9\) and concludes
the framework-deliverable regularity theorem.
\Cref{sec:ns-aor-instance} recasts the closure records as the
AOR-membership witness for the smooth-data carrier.
\Cref{sec:status} closes with the external interpretation and the
locked nonclaim boundary.

conclusion: For each Bradshaw–Grujic stage J and time t∈[0,T_ (u_0)) , the dissolving readout is a linear map DBG_ J,t : E_ J,t → Z_J , where Z_J is the finite-dimensional response space of windowed Fourier values at frequency scale lambda_J(t) . The readout evaluates the windowed observable on P_ J(t) appearing in the Bradshaw–Grujic continuation criterion: typically an L^p or L^∈fty windowed norm of the vorticity or velocity. expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:ns:bg-readout}
For each Bradshaw--Grujic stage \(J\) and time
\(t\in[0,T_{\max}(u_0))\), the \emph{dissolving readout} is a
linear map
\[
  \DBG_{J,t}\colon E_{J,t}\to Z_J ,
\]
where \(Z_J\) is the finite-dimensional response space of
windowed Fourier values at frequency scale
\(\lambda_J(t)\).  The readout evaluates the windowed
observable on \(P_{J(t)}\) appearing in the
Bradshaw--Grujic continuation criterion: typically an
\(L^p\) or \(L^\infty\) windowed norm of the vorticity or
velocity.  The right-support constraint
\(\DBG_{J,t}=\DBG_{J,t}\cdot P_{J(t)}\) records that
\(\DBG_{J,t}\) sees only the active shell at stage \(J\).

\label{def:ns:bg-package}
At each Bradshaw--Grujic stage \(j\), the \emph{BG-windowed
exact package} \(\Gamma_j\) collects the admissible
BG-window probes (the relevant components of
\(\Lphys_{J,t}\) and the windowed value of \(\DBG_{J,t}\)
on the active shell \(P_j\)) together with the structural
constraints they must preserve:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item the divergence-free condition \(\nabla\cdot u=0\);
  \item the Helmholtz-projected carrier
    \citep{Galdi2011} on which the probes act;
  \item the boundary arrangement relating \(P_j\) to
    \(P_{j+1}\);
  \item the doubling relation
    \(\lambda_{j+1}=2\lambda_j\).
\end{enumerate}
The package is \emph{exact} in the sense of
\citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}: it transports the audited
sub-problem from one BG window to the next without
altering the energy, response, or residual information.

\label{def:ns:null-mode-legal-ns}
The \emph{NS carrier} \((E_{J,t},C_{J,t},L^{\mathrm{phys}},D^{\mathrm{BG}})\) is
\emph{null-mode legal} when the physical-native probes and
the dissolving readout both vanish on the audit kernel:
\[
  \Lphys_{J,t}\big|_{\Ker C_{J,t}}=0,
  \qquad
  \DBG_{J,t}\big|_{\Ker C_{J,t}}=0 .
\]
Equivalently, both families descend to the legal energy
quotient \(E_{J,t}/\Ker C_{J,t}\), on which the audit form
is positive definite and the adequacy residual
\(\Xi_{C_{J,t}}(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\midL^{\mathrm{phys}})\) of
\citet{Tsiokos2026XiCompanion} is well-defined.  Null-mode
legality is built into the carrier by construction; it is
not a regularity assumption to be verified after the
residual has been formed.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:ns:source-admission-ledger}
The \emph{source-admission ledger} is the positive
operator-valued sum
\[
  \Omega_{\mathrm{src}} = \Omega_{\mathrm{tr}} + \Omega_{\mathrm{pr}} + \Omega_{\mathrm{visc}} + \Omega_{\mathrm{tail}} + \Omega_{\mathrm{str}} ,
\]
with five positive semidefinite components
\[
  \Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omega_{\mathrm{pr}}\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omega_{\mathrm{visc}}\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omega_{\mathrm{tail}}\succeq 0,\qquad
  \Omega_{\mathrm{str}}\succeq 0,
\]
hence \(\Omega_{\mathrm{src}}\succeq 0\).  The summands record the
contributions entering the dissolving response space at each
stage from, respectively:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item the nonlinear transport \((u\cdot\nabla)u\) as a Schur
    block on the active shells (\(\Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}\));
  \item the pressure \(\nabla p\) after the Helmholtz/Leray
    projection (\(\Omega_{\mathrm{pr}}\));
  \item viscosity \(\nu\Delta u\) as a damping block on each
    shell (\(\Omega_{\mathrm{visc}}\));
  \item the high-frequency tail capturing the interaction of
    visible shells with discarded shells \(j>J\)
    (\(\Omega_{\mathrm{tail}}\));
  \item vortex stretching \((\omega\cdot\nabla)u\) tested
    against the physical-native probes (\(\Omega_{\mathrm{str}}\)).
\end{enumerate}
Each summand is owned by an imported PDE record from
\Cref{sec:imports}: \(\Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}\) and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pr}}\) by the
Littlewood--Paley / Bony--Chemin--Danchin commutator and
Helmholtz-projection estimates
(\Cref{def:ns:lp-bcd-import}); \(\Omega_{\mathrm{visc}}\) by the viscous
damping at scale \(\lambda_J(t)\) from \(\nu\Delta\);
\(\Omega_{\mathrm{tail}}\) by the Sobolev/Besov embedding combined with
the BG-window cutoff (\Cref{def:ns:sobolev-besov-embedding-import});
and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{str}}\) by the vortex-stretching estimate against
the physical-native probes.

This section records the no-go family constraining attempts to pay
the residual ledgers of \Cref{sec:adequacy-cascade}.  Each no-go
excludes a category of shortcut payment that uses data of the wrong
type.  The no-gos do not pay any ledger; they restrict admissible
payments so that the Gevrey radius-window and Littlewood--Paley
transport rescue of \Cref{sec:gevrey-lp} carries the remaining
analytic obligation.  The criterion-native circularity result NG1 was
recorded in \Cref{sec:imports}; here we record NG2--NG10.

\begin{theorem}[No-go NG2: scalar energy / enstrophy category error]
\label{thm:ns:no-go-scalar-energy}
Quadratic scalar budgets such as kinetic energy \(\|u\|_{L^2}^2\),
enstrophy \(\|\nabla u\|_{L^2}^2\), or any positive scalar functional
that is quadratic in the carrier variable, are not lawful native Schur
probes.  The adequacy residual
\[
  \Xi_C(D\mid L)=K_{DD}-K_{DL}K_{LL}^{\dagger}K_{LD}
\]
is defined for a linear native probe family \(L:E\to Y\).  A quadratic
scalar functional is not such a family, so
\(\Xi_C(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\mid\text{scalar quadratic})\) is not a well-formed object
of the Schur-complement calculus until a lawful linear native family has
been declared and audited.
\end{theorem}

Quadratic scalar budgets such as kinetic energy \(\|u\|_{L^2}^2\),
enstrophy \(\|\nabla u\|_{L^2}^2\), or any positive scalar functional
that is quadratic in the carrier variable, are not lawful native Schur
probes.  The adequacy residual
\[
  \Xi_C(D\mid L)=K_{DD}-K_{DL}K_{LL}^{\dagger}K_{LD}
\]
is defined for a linear native probe family \(L:E\to Y\).  A quadratic
scalar functional is not such a family, so
\(\Xi_C(\DBG\mid\text{scalar quadratic})\) is not a well-formed object
of the Schur-complement calculus until a lawful linear native family has
been declared and audited.
\end{theorem}

conclusion: Thus the half-log Gevrey budget under Bradshaw–Grujic frequency-doubling fails the summable predictive-propagation hypothesis unless an additional decay record is supplied.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:ns:no-go-half-log-endpoint}
On the available half-log analyticity lane alone, the staged residual
budget has the form
\[
  B_j
  =
  C_B\,2^{2pj}\bigl(1+\mu\sqrt{L_j}\bigr)
  e^{-2c\mu\sqrt{L_j}},
  \qquad
  p=q-\varepsilon,\qquad
  L_j=\log\lambda_J .
\]
For positive constants \(C_B,\mu,c\) and \(p>0\), the stage ratio
satisfies
\[
  \frac{B_{j+1}}{B_j}
  =
  2^{2p}
  \frac{\bigl(1+\mu\sqrt{L_{j+1}}\bigr)
        e^{-2c\mu\sqrt{L_{j+1}}}}
       {\bigl(1+\mu\sqrt{L_j}\bigr)
        e^{-2c\mu\sqrt{L_j}}}
  \longrightarrow 2^{2p}>1 .
\]
Thus the half-log Gevrey budget under Bradshaw--Grujic
frequency-doubling fails the summable predictive-propagation hypothesis
unless an additional decay record is supplied.

conclusion: Raw nonlinear observables, including flux quantities, pressure interactions, vortex stretching, and triad terms, cannot enter the native family L^ phys as Schur-complement probes. Lawful entry requires one of the following: [label=( )] tangent linearization around the audited solution arc, producing a linear probe that may depend on the solution but is linear in the perturbation; interaction lifting to a higher-order linearization, for example by expressing a triad as a linear probe on an augmented carrier that explicitly resolves the interaction; recording the nonlinear quantity as a source-admission entry in Omega_ src , so it is treated as part of the ledger rather than as a native probe.

interactions, vortex stretching, and triad terms, cannot enter the
native family \(L^{\mathrm{phys}}\) as Schur-complement probes.  Lawful entry
requires one of the following:

linear probe that may depend on the solution but is linear in the
perturbation;
\item interaction lifting to a higher-order linearization, for example
by expressing a triad as a linear probe on an augmented carrier that
explicitly resolves the interaction;
\item recording the nonlinear quantity as a source-admission entry in
\(\Omega_{\mathrm{src}}\), so it is treated as part of the ledger rather than as a
native probe.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: Let rho(t) be the spatial analyticity radius at time t , as supplied by the half-log analyticity import, and let C_G>0 be the Gevrey normalization constant. For each derivative order m 0 , BG stage J , and time t , the Gevrey-normalized derivative probe is M_ m,J,t = rho(t)^m C_G^m m! ^m P_ J(t) . The family \ M_ m,J,t \ _ m 0 is a lawful native probe family on the BG-windowed carrier under the half-log analyticity record.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:ns:gevrey-probes}
Let \(\rho(t)\) be the spatial analyticity radius at time \(t\), as
supplied by the half-log analyticity import, and let \(C_G>0\) be the
Gevrey normalization constant.  For each derivative order \(m\ge 0\),
BG stage \(J\), and time \(t\), the Gevrey-normalized derivative probe
is
\[
  \widetilde M_{m,J,t}
  =
  \frac{\rho(t)^m}{C_G^m\,m!}\,\nabla^m P_{J(t)} .
\]
The family \(\{\widetilde M_{m,J,t}\}_{m\ge 0}\) is a lawful native
probe family on the BG-windowed carrier under the half-log analyticity

\label{def:ns:gevrey-probes}
Let \(\rho(t)\) be the spatial analyticity radius at time \(t\), as
supplied by the half-log analyticity import, and let \(\CG>0\) be the
Gevrey normalization constant.  For each derivative order \(m\ge 0\),
BG stage \(J\), and time \(t\), the Gevrey-normalized derivative probe
is
\[
  \widetilde M_{m,J,t}
  =
  \frac{\rho(t)^m}{\CG^m\,m!}\,\nabla^m P_{J(t)} .
\]
The family \(\{\widetilde M_{m,J,t}\}_{m\ge 0}\) is a lawful native
probe family on the BG-windowed carrier under the half-log analyticity
record.

\label{thm:ns:gevrey-dominance}
For the Gevrey-normalized derivative probe
\(\widetilde M_{m,J,t}\), the dominance constant at derivative order
\(m\) has the closed form
\[
  A_m^G(t,J)
  =
  \lambda_J(t)^{q-\varepsilon}\,
  \frac{m!}{\sigma_J(t)^m},
  \qquad
  \sigma_J(t)=\frac{\lambda_J(t)\rho(t)}{C_G}.
\]
Optimizing over \(m\ge 0\) gives, for a positive constant \(c\),
\[
  \inf_{m\ge 0} A_m^G(t,J)
  \lesssim
  \lambda_J(t)^{q-\varepsilon}\sqrt{1+\sigma_J(t)}\,
  e^{-c\sigma_J(t)} .
\]
Consequently the direct radius-window gate is
\[
  \sigma_J(t)\ge \log\lambda_J(t),
\]
up to the harmless normalization constants absorbed into \(c\).  Under
this gate the optimized dominance is smaller than the leading
\(\lambda_J^{q-\varepsilon}\) scaling by an exponential radius-window factor.

\label{thm:ns:lp-transport-rescue}
Let \(S_j:L^2(P_j)\to H^{-s}\) be the LP-transport stage operator with

\[

\label{thm:ns:smooth-data-half-log-transfer}
On the accepted smooth-data subcarrier \(H^{\gamma_0}\) with
\(\gamma_0>5/2\), the half-log analyticity radius satisfies
\[
  \rho(t)\gtrsim \frac{\log\lambda_J(t)}{\lambda_J(t)}

on BG-compatible stages.  This follows by composing the Sobolev/Besov
embedding
\[
  H^{\gamma_0}\hookrightarrow
  \dot B^{-\varepsilon}_{\infty,\infty}
\]
with the half-log analyticity import.  Consequently
\[
  \sigma_J(t)
  =
  \frac{\lambda_J(t)\rho(t)}{C_G}

\]
so the normalized radius-window gate of
\Cref{thm:ns:gevrey-dominance} is met, and the LP-transport rescue of

on \(H^{-s}\) for \(s>q-\varepsilon\).

\begin{definition}[Six Birds closure records \(R_1\)--\(R_9\)]
\label{def:ns:closure-r1-r9}
The Six Birds closure record bundle for the Navier--Stokes carrier is
the tuple
\[
  \mathsf R=(R_1,R_2,R_3,R_4,R_5,R_6,R_7,R_8,R_9),
\]
where the nine entries are the following proof-carrying records.
\begin{enumerate}[label=$R_\arabic*$.]
\item Adequacy orientation: the carrier data
\((E_{J,t},C_{J,t},\Lphys_{J,t},\DBG_{J,t})\) is ordered so that a
smaller residual \(\Xi\) is better.
\item Exact BG-windowed package: \(\Gamma_j\) preserves
divergence-free structure and the mismatch sector on the packaged
carrier.
\item Null-mode legality: \(L^{\mathrm{phys}}\) and \(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\) vanish on
\(\Ker C_{J,t}\) as in \Cref{sec:ns-carrier}.
\item Source-admission acceptance: the recurrence with
\(\Omega_{\mathrm{src}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{pr}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{visc}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{tail}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{str}}\) is accepted on the
cascade of \Cref{sec:adequacy-cascade}.
\item BG frequency-doubling staging: the active scales obey
\(\lambda_{j+1}=2\lambda_j\).
\item Dissolving-side LP transport: \(S_j:L^2(P_j)\to H^{-s}\) with
\(s\ge q-\varepsilon\) is accepted as the typed transport of
\Cref{sec:gevrey-lp}.
\item Half-log analyticity: restart data in
\(H^{\gamma_0}\cap\dot B^{-\varepsilon}_{\infty,\infty}\), with
\(\gamma_0>3/2-\varepsilon\), carries the half-log lower radius on
BG-compatible stages.
\item Paper-grounded PDE imports: Beale--Kato--Majda continuation,
Bradshaw--Grujic frequency-window continuation, Kato local
well-posedness, half-log analyticity, Littlewood--Paley /
Bony--Chemin--Danchin calculus, and the Sobolev/Besov embedding chain
are accepted at their declared status.
\item Nonclaim boundary: there is no criterion-native replacement of
\(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\), no generic Besov claim, no untyped global comparison, and no
closure outside the smooth-data subcarrier without additional records.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\label{thm:ns:aor-r4-discharge}
The source-admission recurrence record $R_4$ of $\mathsf C_{\mathrm{NS}}$ has primary type $\Delta_{\mathrm{source}}$ and forced secondary types $\Delta_{\mathrm{transport}},\Delta_{\mathrm{scale}},\Delta_{\mathrm{target}},\Delta_{\mathrm{role}}$.  Its discharge status decomposes as $(\Delta_{\mathrm{source}},\texttt{budgeted}\text{ per stage})+(\Delta_{\mathrm{transport}},\texttt{zero})+(\Delta_{\mathrm{scale}},\texttt{cross-cascade to }R_6,R_7)$, with the Loewner recurrence as the budgeted witness and the quotient-transport record \Cref{thm:ns:aor-quotient-transport-record} as the zero-transport witness.  $R_4$ is per-stage budgeted; its asymptotic propagation is not standalone, and is paid by the $R_6/R_7$ cross-cascade.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The principal result is
\Cref{thm:ns:framework-deliverable-regularity}: given the closure
records \(R_1,\ldots,R_9\), every divergence-free initial datum
\(u_0\in H^{\gamma_0}\) with \(\gamma_0>5/2\) on the accepted
smooth-data channel satisfies \(T_{\max}(u_0)=\infty\).  The companion
\Cref{thm:ns:in-refstableaor} of \Cref{sec:ns-aor-instance} recasts
the same records as the AOR-membership witness for the smooth-data
carrier \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{NS}}\), so that under the
refinement-stable audit-closure discipline of
\citet{Tsiokos2026AOR} the same conclusion is read as an
audit-closed carrier predicate.  Read together or separately, the
manuscript is not a Clay--Millennium claim.  The owned contribution is
the Navier--Stokes specialisation of these
frameworks:
\begin{itemize}
\item the smooth-data carrier, the fixed dissolving readout, the
physical-native probe family, the BG-windowed exact package, and
null-mode legality (\Cref{sec:ns-carrier});
\item the source-admission ledger and the stage-to-stage recurrence
(\Cref{sec:adequacy-cascade});
\item the no-go family NG1--NG10 excluding shortcut payments
(\Cref{sec:imports,sec:no-go});
\item the Gevrey radius-window branch, LP-transport rescue, and
smooth-data half-log transfer (\Cref{sec:gevrey-lp});
\item the closure record bundle and the conditional-form statement
of \Cref{thm:ns:framework-deliverable-regularity}
(\Cref{sec:main-theorem});
\item the AOR-instance recasting of the same records and its
partial-status disclosure (\Cref{sec:ns-aor-instance}).
\end{itemize}

The residual calculus is imported from
\citet{Tsiokos2026XiCompanion}: the Schur-complement object
\(\Xi_C(D\mid L)\), the projection identity, the optimal residual
identity, exact adequacy, adequacy promotion, the chain rule, the
data-processing identities for post-processing and native coarsening,
and the blind-spot witness characterisation, together with the
typed-context audit discipline.

\label{nonclaim:ns:outside-framework}
Outside the Six Birds closure framework, \Cref{thm:ns:framework-deliverable-regularity} reads as the conditional implication
\[
  \bigl(\mathsf R\text{ holds on the smooth-data carrier}\bigr)
  \Longrightarrow
  \bigl(T_{\max}(u_0)=\infty\bigr).
\]
This paper does not claim:
\begin{enumerate}
\item a standalone Clay--Millennium
solution~\citep{Fefferman2000NavierStokes} independent of the Six
Birds closure discipline;
\item generic critical-Besov data regularity outside the smooth-data
subcarrier \(H^{\gamma_0}\), \(\gamma_0>5/2\), in the sense of
critical-space well-posedness
results~\citep{KochTataru2001,Cannone1995,LemarieRieusset2023};
\item a criterion-native rewriting of \(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\) in place of
physical-native adequacy, as ruled out by
\Cref{thm:ns:no-go-criterion-native};
\item that any single PDE input alone closes the problem, since the
argument uses the full \(R_1,\ldots,R_9\) bundle architecture;
\item engagement with Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg partial
regularity~\citep{CaffarelliKohnNirenberg1982}, which concerns
Leray--Hopf weak solutions~\citep{Leray1934,Hopf1951} on a different
carrier class;
\item an untyped global comparison, since every comparison in the proof
is made inside the typed-context discipline;
\item a full-log analyticity radius theorem, since the paper uses only
the available half-log analyticity import together with the
LP-transport rescue.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: Energy estimates for 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes control L^2 norms but do not prevent highly localized gradient peaks, which is why global regularity is typically reduced to ``peak-channel'' criteria (e.g.\ Beale–Kato–Majda ). We develop a multiscale decision scaffold, inspired by the Six-Primitives/Six-Birds framework, that separates (i) system-agnostic inequality logic, (ii) Navier–Stokes-facing hinge assumptions, and (iii) numerical diagnostics. Operationally, we (A) mechanize in Lean a No-Zeno engine: refinement events are encoded by crossing times, and Zeno cascades are ruled out under work/capacity/divergence hypotheses; (B) mechanize a route-stability polynomial-capacity lemma; and (C) mechanize a discrete no-go theorem: if the feasible interface inputs at a scale admit highly localized tests, then any uniform ICAP-style capacity certificate forces a pointwise positive-gain bound—the discrete analogue of a peak/strain control in the PDE interpretation. Motivated by this obstruction, we propose an SBT-legal variant in which feasibility excludes strong localization, and we operationalize legality as a reproducible certificate based on per-shell anti-localization and channel diagnostics. In numerical demos, typical smooth random seeds pass the certificate with _j _j=O(1) , while intentionally localized shell wavepackets fail immediately (e.g.\ _j _j 10^2 ). These results clarify exactly where a Clay-style proof would require a genuinely new Navier–Stokes inequality (a provable channelization/delocalization-to-anti-localization hinge) and provide a reproducible workflow for testing such hypotheses. We do not claim a proof of Clay regularity, nor do we prove that the legality certificate is preserved under the classical Navier–Stokes flow; PDE-facing implications are stated explicitly as OPEN assumptions.

conclusion: This paper does not claim a solution to the Clay problem.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
This paper does \emph{not} claim a solution to the Clay problem. Instead, it builds a sharp, reproducible \emph{decision scaffold} for a multiscale approach inspired by the Six Birds framework \citep{tsiokos_2026_18365949}. The core idea is to treat scale-elimination not as a modeling choice but as a canonical \emph{packaging} operation: the eliminated degrees of freedom become a causal ``bridge object'' acting on the retained variables through an interface, and the overall dynamics are constrained by an \emph{accounting} law. In Six Birds terms, we rely on six recurring structural moves:
(i) rewrite/coordinate change, (ii) feasibility/gating constraints, (iii) route dependence of reductions, (iv) sectorization/quantization of interaction channels, (v) packaging of eliminated structure into an effective object, and (vi) accounting (passivity-like) inequalities \citep{tsiokos_2026_18365949}. Our repo makes this concrete for Navier--Stokes by defining canonical multiscale objects (dyadic shells, frontier scales, and packaged subgrid operators) and then asking which primitive-shaped lemmas would be sufficient to rule out ``Zeno'' cascades to infinite depth.

conclusion: This does not prove global regularity for all smooth data
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{What we do instead: an SBT-legal Navier--Stokes variant.}
Rather than chasing Clay as stated, we formalize and study a sharpened program: define an operational notion of \emph{SBT-legal} initial data that forbids extreme localization at dyadic scales, motivated by the channelization/anti-localization hinge required to escape the wavepacket obstruction. Concretely, we implement a certificate that measures anti-localization metrics per shell (normalized concentration factors, burst ratios, and effective channel counts), and we show (numerically) that typical smooth random seeds pass while intentionally constructed localized shell wavepackets fail immediately. This does not prove global regularity for all smooth data; it clarifies a precise, testable boundary between ``legal'' and ``illegal'' regimes for the Six Birds program.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:work-cap-div}
Let $w,\mathrm{Cap}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$ be sequences with $\mathrm{Cap}(n)>0$.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{WORK:} $w(n)$ is the ``work quantum'' required to advance from level $n$ to $n+1$.
\item \textbf{CAP:} $\mathrm{Cap}(n)$ is the ``capacity'' available at level $n$ (a bound relating work
to input energy and/or throughput on the crossing interval).
\item \textbf{WORK$\times$CAP inequality:} for all $n$,
\[
w(n)\ \le\ \mathrm{Cap}(n)\,\bigl(t(n+1)-t(n)\bigr).
\]
\item \textbf{DIV:} the ratios $w(n)/\mathrm{Cap}(n)$ have unbounded partial sums:
\[
\forall M\in\mathbb{R},\ \exists n\in\mathbb{N}\ \text{s.t.}\ M \le \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{w(k)}{\mathrm{Cap}(k)}.
\]
\end{itemize}

\begin{theorem}[Route-stability $\Rightarrow$ polynomial capacity]\label{thm:route-capacity}
Assume $C(0)\ge 0$, $e(n)\ge 0$ for all $n$, and the recursion \eqref{eq:route-rec} holds with
the tame bound \eqref{eq:r-tame}. Then for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
\[
C(n)\ \le\ \Big(C(0)+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} e(k)\Big)\,(n+1)^p.
\]
In particular, if \eqref{eq:e-bounded} holds for some $E\ge 0$, then
\[
C(n)\ \le\ (C(0)+E)\,(n+1)^p,
\]
so $C(n)$ cannot grow exponentially in depth.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[Proof idea (one paragraph)]
Iterate \eqref{eq:route-rec}. Each step contributes a multiplicative factor $r(k)$ in front of the
previous capacity, plus an additive mismatch term transported forward by later $r(\cdot)$ factors.
Using \eqref{eq:r-tame}, the transported factors telescope to $(n+1)^p$, yielding the stated bound.
\end{remark}

conclusion: a uniform ICAP certificate cannot bypass the traditional bottleneck unless feasibility quantitatively excludes localization
expanded_source_wording_tex:
This section isolates a structural obstruction in the ``capacity certificate'' route.
Roughly: an ICAP-style inequality is an \emph{extremal} (worst-case) gain bound.
If the feasible interface inputs at scale $j$ are rich enough to contain highly localized tests
(the discrete analogue of wavepackets), then ICAP forces a \emph{pointwise} bound on the
positive-gain functional of the bridge.
In the Navier--Stokes interpretation, that pointwise gain corresponds to a classical
``peak/strain'' channel.
Therefore, a uniform ICAP certificate cannot bypass the traditional bottleneck unless feasibility
\emph{quantitatively excludes localization}.

source_wording_digest: This section isolates a structural obstruction in the ``capacity certificate'' route. Roughly: an ICAP-style inequality is an extremal (worst-case) gain bound. If the feasible interface inputs at scale j are rich enough to contain highly localized tests (the discrete analogue of wavepackets), then ICAP forces a pointwise bound on the positive-gain functional of the bridge. In the Navier–Stokes interpretation, that pointwise gain corresponds to a classical ``peak/strain'' channel. Therefore, a uniform ICAP certificate cannot bypass the traditional bottleneck unless feasibility quantitatively excludes localization.

This section isolates a structural obstruction in the ``capacity certificate'' route.
Roughly: an ICAP-style inequality is an \emph{extremal} (worst-case) gain bound.
If the feasible interface inputs at scale $j$ are rich enough to contain highly localized tests
(the discrete analogue of wavepackets), then ICAP forces a \emph{pointwise} bound on the
positive-gain functional of the bridge.
In the Navier--Stokes interpretation, that pointwise gain corresponds to a classical
``peak/strain'' channel.
Therefore, a uniform ICAP certificate cannot bypass the traditional bottleneck unless feasibility
\emph{quantitatively excludes localization}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Definition vs.\ diagnostic.}
Throughout, ``SBT-legal'' is used in two explicit senses.
\emph{Analytically}, it denotes a restricted variant/theory in which feasibility at each scale excludes
wavepacket-like concentration (a hypothesis on admissible interface signals, not a theorem about
classical Navier--Stokes).
\emph{Operationally}, we implement a certificate that tests this exclusion at a chosen resolution and
time window; in this paper we use it primarily as an initial-data filter and as a controlled
LEGAL-vs-ILLEGAL diagnostic.
We do not claim that passing the certificate at $t=0$ implies it remains true for later times under
the classical PDE flow; that invariance problem is recorded as an OPEN hinge in
Section~\ref{sec:discussion}.

This section states the paper's main proposal: rather than claiming Clay regularity, we define an SBT-legal (restricted) variant of Navier–Stokes in which feasibility (P2) excludes localization in a quantitative way, and we provide a reproducible certificate to test this legality on initial data (and diagnostically along short runs). The obstruction in Theorem~\ref{thm:icap-no-go} is driven by the existence of feasible inputs
that can localize (basis tests / wavepackets). Anti-localization in the sense of
\eqref{eq:antiloc} is a quantitative way to forbid such tests: if $\eta_j\to 0$, then at high $j$
no feasible shell input can carry most of its $L^2$ mass inside a single ball $B_j(x_0)$.
This is the minimal ``escape hatch'' that can bypass the wavepacket implication
``ICAP $\Rightarrow$ peak bound''.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{lem:channel-antiloc}
Fix a finite index set of channels $\rho$ with $|\rho|=m$ and a finite spatial index set $\iota$
(modeling a discrete grid). Let $B\subset \iota$ represent a cell/ball at scale $j$.
Assume channel shapes $\psi_r:\iota\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfy the delocalization bound
\[
\sum_{i\in B} \psi_r(i)^2 \;\le\; \kappa\,\mu(B)\qquad \text{for all }r\in\rho,
\]
where $\kappa\ge 0$ and $\mu(B)\ge 0$ is the reference ``cell mass'' (e.g.\ volume fraction).
Then for any coefficients $a:\rho\to\mathbb{R}$ the synthesized field
$u(i)=\sum_{r\in\rho} a_r\,\psi_r(i)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:finite-channel-antiloc}
\sum_{i\in B} u(i)^2
\;\le\;
m\,\kappa\,\mu(B)\,\sum_{r\in\rho} a_r^2.
\end{equation}
In particular, if the channel family is orthonormal in $\ell^2(\iota)$ so that
$\|u\|_{\ell^2}^2=\sum_r a_r^2$, then $u$ is $\eta$-anti-localized on $B$ with
$\eta = m\,\kappa\,\mu(B)$.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
We now define an operational notion of ``SBT legality'' for initial data, intended as an
\emph{admissibility restriction} for a modified research question (not the Clay problem):
\emph{do SBT-legal initial data evolve without Zeno cascades, and hence avoid blow-up within
the No-Zeno scaffold?}

\begin{definition}[Operational SBT-legality certificate (initial data)]
\label{def:spt-legal-cert}
Given a dyadic decomposition $u_0=\sum_j (u_0)_j$, define $L_j(u_0)$ by \eqref{eq:local-energy-fraction}.
Let $f_j$ denote the baseline volume fraction at scale $j$ (uniform reference).
Define the normalized concentration factor
\[
\kappa_j(u_0) \;:=\; \frac{L_j(u_0)}{f_j}.
\]
We say $u_0$ is \emph{SBT-legal at thresholds} $(\kappa_\star,\mathrm{burst}_\star,m_\star)$
if the certificate computed by the script
\nolinkurl{python/scripts/ns_spt_legal_certify.py}
returns PASS, which in practice checks configurable bounds on:
(i) $\max_j \kappa_j$,
(ii) a burst ratio statistic over time windows if evolution is enabled,
and optionally (iii) an effective channel count $m_{95}$ from PCA/SVD diagnostics.
\end{definition}

We now define an operational notion of ``SBT legality'' for initial data, intended as an
\emph{admissibility restriction} for a modified research question (not the Clay problem):
\emph{do SBT-legal initial data evolve without Zeno cascades, and hence avoid blow-up within
the No-Zeno scaffold?}

\begin{definition}[Operational SBT-legality certificate (initial data)]
\label{def:spt-legal-cert}
Given a dyadic decomposition $u_0=\sum_j (u_0)_j$, define $L_j(u_0)$ by \eqref{eq:local-energy-fraction}.
Let $f_j$ denote the baseline volume fraction at scale $j$ (uniform reference).
Define the normalized concentration factor
\[
\kappa_j(u_0) \;:=\; \frac{L_j(u_0)}{f_j}.
\]
We say $u_0$ is \emph{SBT-legal at thresholds} $(\kappa_\star,\mathrm{burst}_\star,m_\star)$
if the certificate computed by the script
\nolinkurl{python/scripts/ns_spt_legal_certify.py}
returns PASS, which in practice checks configurable bounds on:
(i) $\max_j \kappa_j$,
(ii) a burst ratio statistic over time windows if evolution is enabled,
and optionally (iii) an effective channel count $m_{95}$ from PCA/SVD diagnostics.
\end{definition}

conclusion: Finally, we show the certificate rejects intentionally localized ``wavepacket-like'' initial data. We construct an ILLEGAL initial condition by placing most of the shell energy into a localized blob in a single dyadic band (see python/src/nswave/illegal_initial_conditions.py ). The LEGAL baseline is a standard band-limited random initial condition used in our demos. Bandlimiting alone does not prevent spatial concentration: the ILLEGAL example is band-limited by construction yet fails the certificate with a large . [t] ∈cludegraphics[width=0.92 ] ../python/artifacts/paper/ns_spt_illegal_vs_legal.png LEGAL vs.\ ILLEGAL initial data under the same SBT-legality certificate. The LEGAL baseline passes with _j _j O(1) , while an intentionally localized shell ``wavepacket'' fails immediately with a very large concentration factor (e.g.\ _j _j 10^2 in the included demo). This illustrates that SBT-legality is a substantive restriction: it rules out strongly localized high-frequency initial conditions that trigger the wavepacket obstruction.

conclusion: We do not prove that SBT-legality is preserved by Navier–Stokes evolution, nor that every smooth initial datum is SBT-legal. The point is sharper: within this scaffold, bypassing the ICAP no-go requires an anti-localization/channelization hinge, and we can (i) state that hinge precisely, (ii) mechanize the finite-dimensional inequality logic it relies on, and (iii) provide reproducible diagnostics and certificates that test it on concrete initial conditions.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Determinism scope.}
Our determinism checks verify byte-identical \texttt{.npz} outputs when rerunning in a fixed
software environment (same code, dependencies, and backend behavior). We do not claim bitwise
identity across arbitrary BLAS/FFT backends or thread schedules; for cross-platform reruns we
recommend pinning threads (e.g.\ \texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=1}, \texttt{MKL\_NUM\_THREADS=1})
and using tolerance-based numeric comparisons where appropriate.

conclusion: What this paper does not claim.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{What this paper does \emph{not} claim.}
We do not prove the Clay 3D Navier--Stokes global regularity theorem.
All PDE-specific hinge claims that would be required for a Clay claim are stated explicitly
as OPEN assumptions elsewhere in the repository. Our emphasis is on (i) making the lemma chain
explicit and auditable, and (ii) showing precisely where and why the ``obvious'' ICAP/capacity
route collapses into a classical peak/strain channel unless one adds a genuine feasibility
restriction that excludes wavepacket-like localization.

conclusion: This does not claim that legality is preserved under Navier–Stokes evolution
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{What we do instead: an ``SBT-legal'' variant.}
Given the above obstruction, the only viable bypass within this scaffold is to restrict feasibility
so that localized wavepacket tests are \emph{not} admissible. We formalize this as an anti-localization
hinge and show that it can follow from finite-channel delocalized feasibility in a discrete model.
We then propose an operational certificate (computed by scripts in this repository) that checks
anti-localization-style metrics for initial data (Section~\ref{sec:spt-legal}).
This does not claim that legality is preserved under Navier--Stokes evolution; rather, it proposes
a concrete restricted theory where the No-Zeno engine becomes meaningful without smuggling in a
classical supremum regularity hypothesis.

conclusion: Boolean logic is usually treated as a formal starting point. We ask instead when a substrate actually earns a logic layer. In the Six Birds emergence calculus—P1 operator rewrite, P2 gating/constraints, P3 protocol holonomy, P4 sectors/invariants, P5 packaging, and P6 accounting/audit—we define a logic layer as an audited closure of packaged predicates under induced dynamics. This yields two complementary views. In the feasibility view, propositions are definable feasible sets and connectives are their stable closure operations. In the operator view, bits are packaged equivalence classes and gates are macro-updates induced by the underlying dynamics. We implement quantitative diagnostics for both views: metastability, route mismatch, closure defect, gate error, conditional entropy, unretained input information, and entropy-production audits. Across controlled finite Markov laboratories we obtain four main results. First, parity/XOR-type variables are unusually robust coarse variables: the parity lens beats the median random binary partition across the full tested grid. Second, NOT, AND, and reversible XOR embeddings exhibit distinct closure regimes under noise, staging, and timescale stress. Third, when a reversible CNOT embedding is coarse-grained to an erased XOR output, closure degrades sharply and unretained input information increases by more than eightfold relative to the retained view. Fourth, a minimal unsupervised discovery pipeline recovers stable bits and reconstructs a NOT gate directly from transition structure. The result is a falsifiable criterion for when a system has logic at a layer—and for which logic it has—without treating logic as fundamental.

conclusion: Fix a microstate space Z , a lens f : Z → X , and an evaluation window tau . A logic layer at (f,tau) consists of a nontrivial family B ⊆ Sigma_f of binary packaged predicates together with induced macro-updates such that: Stability. Each b ∈ B is metastable on the timescale tau . Closure. The relevant micro-updates descend to macro-operators on the packaged variables with small closure defect. Feasibility semantics. Each b ∈ B is the indicator of a stable feasible set, and the connective operations required at the layer remain definable there. Auditability. Persistence, route agreement, and information loss are measurable by explicit diagnostics. conclusion: Definition is intentionally stricter than merely being able to label states by zero and one. A candidate bit must remain stable long enough to matter, must support a descended operator calculus, and must survive audit. This is why the six primitives are complementary rather than redundant. P5 packages the carrier; P4 keeps it from dissolving immediately; P2 makes it semantically meaningful; P1 determines whether an effective operator vocabulary can be stabilized; P3 detects route dependence and protocol residue; P6 determines what must be paid to maintain the whole arrangement. The criterion is also intentionally broader than classical Booleanity. Complement and negation appear naturally when the relevant complements remain definable and stable at the lens. But nothing in Definition forces every layer to have those complements available at low cost. For that reason we speak of a logic layer rather than a Boolean layer. The finite laboratories studied in this paper are classical-looking enough to realize NOT, AND, and XOR cleanly, but the framework itself is meant to diagnose which closures a layer actually supports rather than to decree them in advance.

conclusion: Figure is the empirical anchor for the title claim of the paper. The parity-sector laboratory is designed around controlled leakage between the even- and odd-parity sectors of a two-bit system, so the natural candidate coarse variable is the parity bit a b . We compare that lens against two alternatives defined on the same underlying four macrostates: the familiar Boolean predicate a b , and the median of a family of balanced random binary partitions. The comparison is intentionally closure-based rather than purely predictive. The plotted quantity is route mismatch (RM), so smaller values mean that the proposed binary variable is better aligned with the induced coarse dynamics. conclusion: Certifying multiscale anti-localization only at t=0 is not useful unless legality is forward-closed; we lack general, mechanizable conditions under which SPT-legality propagates under time evolution. \label{rem:stable-synthesis}
The inequality \eqref{eq:frame-bounds} is a stability condition for the \emph{synthesis} map $a\mapsto \Gamma_j a$.
In classical frame theory, this corresponds to the channels forming a \emph{Riesz sequence} (equivalently, $\Gamma_j$ is injective and coefficients are stable), rather than an arbitrary redundant frame.
In particular, $\alpha_j>0$ forces $m_j\le \dim(H_j)$.
We adopt this strong form because our legality envelopes are stated in terms of the coefficient norm and are representation-independent only when coefficients are unique (or otherwise canonically selected).
Extending the theory to redundant dictionaries would require fixing a coefficient-selection rule (e.g.\ minimal $\ell_2$-norm coefficients) and replacing $\alpha_j$ by a pseudoinverse stability constant; we do not pursue this here.

or, in operator form,

(I-E)\,\Phi_t\,E = 0 \qquad \text{for all } t \text{ in the lifespan.}

We prove Theorem~\ref{thm:t-spt-01}.
Fix a trajectory $u(t)\in H$ on its lifespan and assume $u_j(0)\in\mathcal{F}_j$ for all depths $j$.
By the system slot HL-SPT-INV (exact feasibility invariance, \eqref{eq:HL-INV}), it follows that
\[
u_j(t)\in \mathcal{F}_j \qquad \text{for all times $t$ in the lifespan and all depths $j$.}
\]
For each fixed $t$ and each depth $j$ with $u_j(t)\neq 0$, we may therefore apply the static feasibility bound (Theorem~\ref{thm:t-spt-00}) to the feasible vector $v=u_j(t)\in\mathcal{F}_j$ to obtain
\[
\kappa_j(u_j(t)) \;\le\; K^{\mathrm{feas}}_j.
\]
Taking the maximum over depths yields
\[
\max_{0\le j\le J_{\max}}\kappa_j(u_j(t))
\;\le\;
\max_{0\le j\le J_{\max}} K^{\mathrm{feas}}_j
\;=\;
K^{\mathrm{pred}}_{\mathrm{glob}},
\]
where the last equality is the definition \eqref{eq:Kpred-global}.

source_wording_tex:
We prove Theorem~\ref{thm:t-spt-01}.
Fix a trajectory $u(t)\in H$ on its lifespan and assume $u_j(0)\in\mathcal{F}_j$ for all depths $j$.
By the system slot HL-SPT-INV (exact feasibility invariance, \eqref{eq:HL-INV}), it follows that
\[
u_j(t)\in \mathcal{F}_j \qquad \text{for all times $t$ in the lifespan and all depths $j$.}
\]
For each fixed $t$ and each depth $j$ with $u_j(t)\neq 0$, we may therefore apply the static feasibility bound (Theorem~\ref{thm:t-spt-00}) to the feasible vector $v=u_j(t)\in\mathcal{F}_j$ to obtain
\[
\kappa_j(u_j(t)) \;\le\; K^{\mathrm{feas}}_j.
\]
Taking the maximum over depths yields
\[
\max_{0\le j\le J_{\max}}\kappa_j(u_j(t))
\;\le\;
\max_{0\le j\le J_{\max}} K^{\mathrm{feas}}_j
\;=\;
K^{\mathrm{pred}}_{\mathrm{glob}},
\]
where the last equality is the definition \eqref{eq:Kpred-global}.
This is exactly \eqref{eq:t-spt-01-bound} and implies SPT-legality with threshold $K_\kappa=K^{\mathrm{pred}}_{\mathrm{glob}}$ as stated in \eqref{eq:t-spt-01-K}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:fm-mode}
Consider a family of depths with $|\mathcal{C}_j|\to\infty$ (hence $f_j\to 0$).
Suppose there exist depths $j$ for which the feasible set is all of the band, $\mathcal{F}_j=H_j$ (e.g.\ $\Gamma_j$ is surjective, which is possible when $m_j\ge \dim(H_j)$).
Then for each such $j$ there exists a feasible vector $v\in\mathcal{F}_j$ with
\[
\kappa_j(v)=\frac{1}{f_j}.
\]
Consequently, any fixed legality threshold $K_\kappa$ independent of $j$ fails for sufficiently deep $j$.

More generally, even in the best-case artifact regime where $\kappa^{\mathrm{emp}}_0(j)$ and $\mathrm{cond}(\Gamma_j)$ remain bounded, the feasibility envelope in T-SPT-00 scales linearly in $m_j$:
\[
\sup_{v\in\mathcal{F}_j\setminus\{0\}}\kappa_j(v)
\;\lesssim\;
\kappa^{\mathrm{emp}}_0(j)\,\mathrm{cond}(\Gamma_j)\,m_j,
\]
so if $m_j$ grows without bound with depth then the best available legality bound also grows without bound.

\label{prop:ng-ledger}
Fix a depth $j$.
Assume the feasible set $\mathcal{F}_j$ contains two orthonormal vectors $\psi_{\mathrm{uni}},\psi_{\mathrm{loc}}\in \mathcal{F}_j$ such that
\[
\kappa_j(\psi_{\mathrm{uni}})=1,
\qquad
\kappa_j(\psi_{\mathrm{loc}})=\frac{1}{f_j}.
\]
Define an energy-preserving evolution in the two-dimensional subspace $\mathrm{span}\{\psi_{\mathrm{uni}},\psi_{\mathrm{loc}}\}$ by
\[
u(\theta)=\cos\theta\,\psi_{\mathrm{uni}}+\sin\theta\,\psi_{\mathrm{loc}}.
\]
Then $\|u(\theta)\|^2\equiv 1$ for all $\theta$, but $\kappa_j(u(\theta))$ can be made arbitrarily close to $1/f_j$.
In particular, there exists $\theta$ such that
\[
\kappa_j(u(\theta)) \ge 0.9/f_j.
\]

\label{prop:ng-dist}
Fix a depth $j$.
For any target leakage ratio $r\in(0,1)$ and any target threshold fraction $\rho\in(0,1)$ (e.g.\ $\rho=0.9$), there exists a multiscale state $u\in H$ and a decomposition
\[
u = v + w,
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{$v$ is SPT-legal}) for every depth $\ell$, $\kappa_\ell(v_\ell)\le 2$ (in particular $v$ is legal for $K_\kappa=2$).
\item (\emph{$w$ is globally tiny}) $\|w\|/\|v\| \le r$.
\item (\emph{$w$ is deep and localized}) $w_\ell=0$ for $\ell\neq j$, and $w_j$ is supported in a single cell of $\mathcal{C}_j$.
\item (\emph{Deep-band illegality}) the deep component satisfies
\[
\kappa_j(u_j)\ge \rho/f_j.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Thus, even when the global leakage ratio $\|w\|/\|v\|$ is arbitrarily small, the deep-band legality audit can be violated by a factor on the order of $1/f_j$.

source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:ng-dist}
Fix a depth $j$.
For any target leakage ratio $r\in(0,1)$ and any target threshold fraction $\rho\in(0,1)$ (e.g.\ $\rho=0.9$), there exists a multiscale state $u\in H$ and a decomposition
\[
u = v + w,
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{$v$ is SPT-legal}) for every depth $\ell$, $\kappa_\ell(v_\ell)\le 2$ (in particular $v$ is legal for $K_\kappa=2$).
\item (\emph{$w$ is globally tiny}) $\|w\|/\|v\| \le r$.
\item (\emph{$w$ is deep and localized}) $w_\ell=0$ for $\ell\neq j$, and $w_j$ is supported in a single cell of $\mathcal{C}_j$.
\item (\emph{Deep-band illegality}) the deep component satisfies
\[
\kappa_j(u_j)\ge \rho/f_j.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Thus, even when the global leakage ratio $\|w\|/\|v\|$ is arbitrarily small, the deep-band legality audit can be violated by a factor on the order of $1/f_j$.

\label{prop:toy-ladder-leakage}
Assume the artifact slots HL-SPT-DELOC, HL-SPT-FRAME, and HL-SPT-MODE hold so that $K^{\mathrm{pred}}_{\mathrm{glob}}$ is finite.
There exist choices of depth $j_\star$ (with small $f_{j_\star}$), injection time $t_\star$, and off-feasible cell-localized $w_{\mathrm{inj}}$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the global leakage ratio $\|\eta w_{\mathrm{inj}}\|/\|u(t_\star)\|$ can be made arbitrarily small, yet
\item the post-injection state violates legality:
\[
\kappa_{j_\star}(u_{j_\star}(t_\star^+)) \;>\; K^{\mathrm{pred}}_{\mathrm{glob}}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Thus legality is not forward-closed without HL-SPT-INV (or without a robust substitute such as HL-SPT-ROBUST$\infty$), in agreement with Prop.~\ref{prop:fm-inv}.
